c0d16197592de19a5f6b.translation: 你的意思我明白了。有什么东西卖吗？

b3f313c50e242648f5ce.source: We'll leave you to your travels.

1b72bd7fdbea908b54e9.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{The merchant grins.%SPEECH_ON%I'm glad you have asked for I do at times tire of dealing with the Viziers' feathery liveries. The blackguards and blaggards.%SPEECH_OFF%He snaps his fingers and points at you with fatherly sincerity.%SPEECH_ON%Conversation quickly becomes confabulation. As my father used to say, business is balladry. And we all need a bit of poetry in the dullness of our lives.%SPEECH_OFF%He nods and speaks with a tone you know he uses upon his fellow merchants.%SPEECH_ON%I have an expectation with the Viziers, but being robbed or losing items is also an expectation of this expectation. Upon this, I do have things to offer, which if agreed upon, will be 'stolen' from me at your expense. But you can only have one of these availabilities: a Handgonne for but 2,500 crowns, or a Fire Lance for a mere 500 crowns. You may have only one of the two on offer.%SPEECH_OFF%}
1b72bd7fdbea908b54e9.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{商人咧嘴笑了。%SPEECH_ON%问得好，我有时也实在厌烦与维齐尔那些穿得花里胡哨的仆从打交道。尽是无赖恶棍。%SPEECH_OFF%他打个响指，像长辈般诚恳地朝你一指。%SPEECH_ON%话匣子一开，闲谈便能成故事。我父亲常说，做生意就像唱歌谣。日子这么乏味，人人都需要一点诗意。%SPEECH_OFF%他点点头，换上你一听便知是与同行谈买卖时的语气。%SPEECH_ON%我答应过给维齐尔们交货，不过路上遭抢、遗失些货物，也在他们的预料之中。因此，我手头确实有东西可供出售。只要谈妥，您付钱，这些货便算从我手里“遭了窃”。但两样只能选一样：一支手铳，2,500克朗；或者一支火矛，只要500克朗。两样货，只能拿一样。%SPEECH_OFF%}

86af8cbf6fc8981eab63.source: We'll take the handgonne for 2,500 crowns.

1ded6684860a7e9bde88.source: The firelance at 500 crowns for sure.

2f0b746030cd48c58ec4.source: For that price, none are of interest.
2f0b746030cd48c58ec4.translation: 这个价，哪件我都没兴趣。

7103e9112b094eea8245.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{You and the merchant come to an agree upon the items. After you make an exchange of coin and goods, he gets back up on his camel and thumbs his nose at you.%SPEECH_ON%I'm so sorry to have been stolen from, this has truly been an awful day. Woe, the Viziers will be just as sad as I am.%SPEECH_OFF%The merchant sits sidesaddle again and begins to feast on his berries and nuts. He doesn't take up his reins, yet the camels seem to move as though on command.%SPEECH_ON%May your path be ever Gilded, Crownling, and may my abrogated goods provide you the shine you seek.%SPEECH_OFF%}
7103e9112b094eea8245.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{你与商人谈妥了货物的价钱。一手交钱，一手交货后，他重新爬上骆驼，冲你做了个拇指抵鼻的鬼脸。%SPEECH_ON%唉，我竟然遭了贼，今天可真糟糕。哎呀，维齐尔们想必也会跟我一样难过。%SPEECH_OFF%商人又侧身坐好，大吃浆果和坚果。他没有拉缰绳，骆驼却像听见号令般迈步前行。%SPEECH_ON%愿你的前路永沐金光，克朗客。也愿这些脱手的货物，给你带来所求的光辉。%SPEECH_OFF%}

a80596a46e6a3079d0e1.source: And may you find shine as well.

a8e1709a4d76393ca623.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{The merchant puts his hands out as though you are robbing him.%SPEECH_ON%It is no matter that you do not wish to have my goods, truly.%SPEECH_OFF%He crosses his legs to sit sidesaddle once more and the camels immediately begin to move as though this was their command. The merchant talks as he eats his nuts and berries.%SPEECH_ON%May your path be ever Gilded, Crownling, and may the Viziers of these deserts put you to good use.%SPEECH_OFF%}
a8e1709a4d76393ca623.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{商人摊开双手，仿佛你要抢他似的。%SPEECH_ON%不想买我的货，也没关系，真的。%SPEECH_OFF%他再次交叠双腿，侧身坐好，骆驼便立刻迈步，像是把这动作当作了命令。商人边吃坚果与浆果，边说道：%SPEECH_ON%克朗客，愿你的前路永蒙镀金者光照，也愿这片沙漠的维齐尔们善用你的本领。%SPEECH_OFF%}

25c77d9be5d4786e0193.source: I hope they do as well.

485bf534b15e384203c9.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{You nod and wish the man good luck in his travels. He bows respectively.%SPEECH_ON%May your path be ever Gilded, Crownling.%SPEECH_OFF%}
485bf534b15e384203c9.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{你点点头，祝他旅途顺利。他恭敬地鞠躬。%SPEECH_ON%克朗客，愿你的前路永蒙镀金者光照。%SPEECH_OFF%}

ac29b22ea7bd0077edb0.source: Our fate will lead us here again in time.
ac29b22ea7bd0077edb0.translation: 时机一到，命运还会引我们回来。

ae23077f0e984fe9ee68.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_152.png[/img]{Venturing into the vestibule of the ancient Oracle is like stepping into someone else's dream. Men and women listlessly shift around its pillars, the timid scratch of shoes across stone faintly filling the air, and day or night the architectural curvature brings a pale and somber shadow to its strange halls as though it were permitted eternity beneath the moon herself.

People of all religions come to the Oracle with a shared sense of awe. Nobody knows which priestly being once dwelled there, nor what clerical colors they donned. Despite these mysteries, many believe that by sleeping inside the Oracle one can harness visions of their own future. An admirable faith to have, though you find it ironic these ethereal meanings must be sought by using the faithful's hands and feet to get there. For now, an impoverished and clustered tent city has glommed onto the Oracle's edges. It is a decrepit end for those who have so buoyed themselves to hope they've made themselves refugees of reality.}
ae23077f0e984fe9ee68.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_152.png[/img]{踏进这座古老神谕殿的前厅，仿佛闯进了别人的梦。男男女女无精打采地在柱间挪动，鞋底小心翼翼地蹭过石面，细微的声响飘在空气里。无论白昼还是黑夜，这座建筑弯曲的轮廓总为怪异的殿堂罩上一层苍白、阴郁的暗影，仿佛月亮亲自准许它永世沐浴在自己的光下。

信奉各路神明的人都怀着同样的敬畏来到这里。没人知道，曾有怎样的祭司居于此地，又身披何种颜色的祭服。尽管谜团重重，许多人仍相信，只要睡在神谕殿里，就能在梦中窥见自己的未来。这份信仰令人钦佩。不过，在你看来，要探求如此缥缈的奥义，信徒却得先靠自己的双手双脚赶到这里，实在有些讽刺。如今，一片拥挤、贫穷的帐篷聚落依附在神谕殿周围。那些将全部身家性命都寄托于希望的人，最终成了逃避现实的难民，在这破败之地落了脚。}

32a6740a116df746498e.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_173.png[/img]{The shine and shimmer is so bright you almost think the Gilder Himself has ordained you a proper visit - unfortunately or fortunately, what you've stumbled across is actually a great gilded dome protruding ever so slightly from the sands. Immediately, you test if you can pull some of the gold away, but it has no give. %randombrother% calls you over to a slab of stone which is gapped. Perhaps a belltower at one point? Light fades quick and you can see very little inside. Above the entryway a relief depicts men pulling carts of scrolls.

 There's a set of words repeatedly scrawled across the relief. None of the languages look remotely familiar to anything you've ever heard or seen. It takes a bit of time until you can find a hurriedly etched translation left by someone approximal to your era: 'the Library, the Labyrinth of the Night, the Labyrinth of the Mind, Leave here as you would Leave a Dream, Tread here as you would Tread a Dream, Leave to Dwell upon the Horror of not Knowing, Enter to be One with Knowing, and in Knowing the Dream, Know the Nightmare'.%SPEECH_ON%Fair bit ominous, captain, but if you wanna go down in there we got the rope and torches to see to it.%SPEECH_OFF%%randombrother% tells you this, and the look on his face suggests he's hoping you decline the proposition.}
32a6740a116df746498e.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_173.png[/img]{光芒闪耀得如此明亮，你几乎以为镀金者本尊安排了一场亲临。可惜——也许是幸好——你发现的其实是一座硕大的镀金穹顶，只从沙中露出一小截。你立刻试着抠点黄金下来，可表面纹丝不动。%randombrother%叫你去看一块留着缺口的石板，也许这里曾是钟楼？光线很快便沉入黑暗，里面几乎看不清。入口上方的浮雕描绘着人们拉着满载卷轴的货车。

浮雕上反复刻着一段话，所用语言没有一种与你见过、听过的相似。你找了一阵，终于发现一份匆忙刻下的译文，显然出自与你年代相近的人：“藏书之馆，夜之迷宫，心之迷宫。离此地，如离梦；行此地，如行梦。离去者，长居无知之恐怖；进入者，与知融为一体。而知梦者，必知梦魇。”%SPEECH_ON%团长，听着挺不吉利。不过你要想下去，我们有绳子和火把，够用了。%SPEECH_OFF%%randombrother%这样告诉你，脸上的神情却分明盼着你拒绝这个提议。}

2dbc960ac312f4d9f481.source: Let's not disturb what rests here.
2dbc960ac312f4d9f481.translation: 别惊扰长眠于此的东西。

1e3e25d11e0b804b79fe.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_89.png[/img]{The climb down is a perilous one, the dark so thick you can't even see your own boots. But eventually you hit a marbled floor and quickly light up some torches. You find yourself in a massive hall around which spiral rows and rows of bookcases. Every shelf is adorned with piles of scrolls, many dwelling within glass enclosures. The shelves are stacked upon each other and seem to ascend to the very ceiling from which you descended. Rolling ladders rest at each level, but even further up runs a floating mezzanine with metal chutes stationed here and there. It seems as though once upon a time one was meant to pass these scrolls up and down, though now everything is rusted, and the mezzanine has collapsed in parts.

 %randombrother% calls your attention. He points to an enormous scroll flattened behind a sheet of glass. Drawings sprawl over the paper, and upon closer inspection it appears they are blueprints for seemingly everything: the human body, the bodies of many animals, castles, towers, windmills, ships, weapons and armor, boots and gloves, alignments of the stars, and a great number of drawings of things which you have never seen before, things which don't make sense.%SPEECH_ON%Captain, this place is not meant for us. The languages, the halls, we should go.%SPEECH_OFF%One of the sellswords expresses the mood in the air. You have absolutely trespassed to a place few have gone before. And if they have gone before, where are they? A place like this surely can't stay hidden, right?}
1e3e25d11e0b804b79fe.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_89.png[/img]{向下攀爬十分危险，黑暗浓得连自己的靴子都看不见。不过，你们终于踩上大理石地板，赶紧点起火把。眼前是一座巨大厅堂，周围一排排书架盘旋排列。架上堆满卷轴，许多还封在玻璃罩内。书架层层叠起，仿佛一直升到你们下来的天顶。每一层都靠着可滑动的梯子，更高处还有一圈悬空夹层，金属滑槽散布其间。看来，往昔的人们曾用它们上下传递卷轴，如今却已锈蚀殆尽，夹层也有部分坍塌。

%randombrother%叫你过去，指着一张平铺在玻璃后面的巨大卷轴。图画铺满纸面，细看之下，仿佛万事万物的图样都收录其中：人体、许多动物的身体、城堡、高塔、风车、船只、武器与盔甲、靴子与手套、星辰的排列，还有许多你从未见过、根本无法理解的东西。%SPEECH_ON%团长，这地方不该是我们来的。那些文字，这些厅堂……我们走吧。%SPEECH_OFF%一名佣兵说出了众人心中的不安。你们无疑闯进了一个罕有人至的地方。可若以前有人来过，他们又去了哪里？这样的地方，真能一直不为人知吗？}

294675702f2cf1b281a4.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_89.png[/img]{%SPEECH_START%Interlopers in the Library.%SPEECH_OFF%The voice scratches along the marbled floor and rises up to meet your ears and continues on, the word 'Libraryyy' slithering into the dark behind you. Suddenly, a number of the glass cases begin to glow, the phylacteries holding some sort of ethereal energy, and as the light widens it unveils the torso of a black skeleton, its body captured in air. The ribcage holds a book, hooked into place by the sickly folds of its own ribs as a spider would clutch a meal. The skull of the creature stares at you with peerless sockets.%SPEECH_ON%Your kind has already stolen from me, now you dare profane these halls again?%SPEECH_OFF%The phylacteries grow brighter and in turn the skeleton's torso grows flesh, weeds of vein and the pulp of skin blossoming outward to cover bone. But it is only the torso which is ensconced. You stare at the phylacteries and they are brimming with energy now, and in staring you can see the ghostly faces smearing along the glass like streaks of rain. You hear a loud clap and turn back to see the Loremaster in full, its eyes aflame with white fire, its limbs skinny yet with smoky muscles winding around its frame, and its lower half is pluming with black ash as it glides forward. The brighter the glass bulbs get, the stronger and faster it becomes!}
294675702f2cf1b281a4.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_89.png[/img]{%SPEECH_START%有外人闯入藏书馆。%SPEECH_OFF%声音沿着大理石地面刮过，升到耳畔，又继续向后延伸，拖长的“藏书馆——”滑进你身后的黑暗。突然，几只玻璃容器开始发光，那些命匣里蕴藏着某种虚幻的能量。光芒扩散，照出一具悬在空中的黑色骷髅躯干。它的肋骨以病态的弧度弯折，像蜘蛛抱住猎物一样，将一本书钩在胸腔里。骷髅用空洞的眼窝盯着你。%SPEECH_ON%你们这类人已经偷过我的东西，如今还敢再次亵渎这座殿堂？%SPEECH_OFF%命匣愈发明亮，骷髅的躯干也随之生出血肉。血管如杂草蔓延，皮肉向外绽开，覆盖骨骼，可被包裹的只有躯干。你望向命匣，它们已盈满能量。凝视之下，还能看见鬼魂的面孔沿玻璃滑过，仿佛一条条雨痕。一声巨响传来，你回头，只见博学者已完整显现：双眼燃着白火，四肢瘦削，烟雾般的肌肉却缠绕骨架；下半身翻涌着黑灰，向前飘来。玻璃球越亮，它便越强，也越快！}

6694907c313abc82961d.source: Fight for your lives! Fight like you've never fought before!
6694907c313abc82961d.translation: 想活命就拼吧！拿出这辈子最大的本事！

0e01d934b78047c90f88.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_89.png[/img]{The Lorekeeper collapses onto the ground a pile of ash and the phylacteries slowly fade back to dark. You walk over with torch in hand. Its black skull resides atop the book that once dwelled in its chest.%SPEECH_ON%Captain, I don't think we should be touching anything here.%SPEECH_OFF%You ignore one of your men and pick the book up. Its leather covering is stitched together, and as you look closer you can see the flesh of ears and noses encompassing the cover. Immediately, the bones of the slain undead scratch across the marbled floor. One zips between your legs and flies into the pile of ash. A dull white fire alights inside the socket of the skull. That's more than enough for you: with a quick command, you get the men to climb back up the rope, yourself the last to leave. As you near the light of the earth above, you take one moment to stare back down and - the black skull is already in your face! It floats alone, eyes burning white, capturing your sight in a cone of fire you cannot understand, and as you stare into it you can hear the voices of your men fade away. The skull floats alone, and you almost feel the urge to let the rope go. The skull speaks to your mind:%SPEECH_ON%It is but one of its gifts, Interloper, and you are not the first to have it. There are many who have taken it, and in the many there is but one end, the one who awaits us all!%SPEECH_OFF%The skull's fire snuffs out and it drops away into the dark where you hear a brief clatter. The voices of your men rush back in, louder than ever and you look up to see %randombrother%'s hand. Grabbing hold, they pull you out. As you exit, the entrance sinks into the sand, and all you have of the place is a strange, fleshen book filled with writings you cannot ever hope to decipher.}
0e01d934b78047c90f88.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_89.png[/img]{典籍守护者坍落在地，化作一堆灰，命匣也渐渐黯淡下去。你举着火把走近。漆黑的头骨搁在一本书上，那书先前还嵌在它胸膛里。%SPEECH_ON%团长，我觉得这里的东西最好都别碰。%SPEECH_OFF%你没理会弟兄的劝告，将书捡起。皮革封面缝缀而成，细看之下，竟能辨出包在上面的耳朵与鼻子。立刻，死去亡灵的骨骸开始刮擦大理石地面。一根骨头从你双腿间窜过，飞进灰堆。头骨眼窝里，燃起暗淡的白火。这已足够让你下定决心：一声急令，弟兄们沿绳索向上爬，你留到最后。快接近地面光亮时，你低头回望了一瞬——那漆黑头骨已贴到你面前！它独自悬浮，眼中白火燃烧，用一道你无法理解的锥形火光攫住你的目光。凝视火焰时，你听见弟兄们的声音逐渐远去。头骨孤零零地飘着，你几乎想要松开绳索。它直接向你的心智开口。%SPEECH_ON%闯入者，这不过是它赐下的一份礼物，你也并非第一个得到它的人。许多人曾将它带走，可无论多少人，终局都只有一个——那个等待着我们所有人的存在！%SPEECH_OFF%头骨中的火焰熄灭，随即坠入黑暗，只留下一声短促的碰撞。弟兄们的呼喊猛然涌回，比先前更加响亮。你抬头，看见%randombrother%伸来的手，紧紧抓住，被众人拉了出去。刚一脱身，入口便沉入沙中。你从这里带走的，只有一本怪异的人皮书，书中文字，是你永远也别想破译的。}

11ce49ccdceacbcf57d1.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_173.png[/img]The men run and hastily climb up again.%SPEECH_ON%Perhaps another time?%SPEECH_OFF%One sellsword says. %randombrother% nods.%SPEECH_ON%Another time, aye. Maybe a time far away from now, when I'm out retired and farkin' whoors, then y'all can dip down into the darkness and go gallivanting with dead wizards. Does that time work for y'all?%SPEECH_OFF%
11ce49ccdceacbcf57d1.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_173.png[/img]弟兄们拔腿就跑，匆忙爬了上来。%SPEECH_ON%不如下次再说？%SPEECH_OFF%一个佣兵提议。%randombrother%点头。%SPEECH_ON%对，下次。最好是很久以后，等老子退了休，正忙着嫖妓，你们再钻进那片黑里，找死巫师寻开心。这个时候各位觉得合适吗？%SPEECH_OFF%

0a30b76792b123e87537.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_53.png[/img]{The surviving man scrambles away from you. He's muttering something. You can't hear it, but the language is clear nonetheless: he knows who you are, and what you are. | The battle over, you find one survivor in the field. He's a little scraped up but could be of use. | %SPEECH_ON%Slaving shit, do your worst.%SPEECH_OFF%Despite being the last man standing, the northerner's still got some fight in him. He may do well in the %companyname%. | You find the last man standing, hurt but alive. He's a northerner and would look good in chains. Perhaps fetch a solid price in the south, or serve as fodder on the frontlines? | The northern troop has been cut down to its last, a pale man who seems to not dwell long in defeat.%SPEECH_ON%Southern shits, your 'Gilder' can suck my balls. C'mon, give me a weapon, I'll show you how a northerner dies!%SPEECH_OFF%You can't help but like his gusto. Instead of serving worms in the grave, perhaps he could serve the company as one of the indebted?}
0a30b76792b123e87537.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_53.png[/img]{幸存的男人连滚带爬地躲着你，嘴里不住嘟囔。你听不清他说什么，但他的意思再明白不过：他知道你是谁，也知道你是做什么的。 | 战斗结束后，你在战场上发现一名幸存者。他受了点皮外伤，应该还派得上用场。 | %SPEECH_ON%贩奴的杂种，有什么手段尽管来吧。%SPEECH_OFF%尽管只剩他一个人还站着，这北方人仍不肯服软。放在%companyname%里，他或许能干得不错。 | 你找到最后一个活口。他受了伤，但还没死。这北方人戴上镣铐应该挺合适。或许能在南方卖个好价钱，也可以送到前线当炮灰？ | 这支北方部队只剩最后一人。他面色苍白，却似乎没打算在战败的沮丧中沉浸太久。%SPEECH_ON%南方的狗东西，叫你们那“镀金者”来舔老子的卵蛋吧。来啊，给老子把武器，让你们看看北方人怎么死！%SPEECH_OFF%你倒有些喜欢他的这股劲头。与其让他去坟里喂蛆，不如把他收为负债者，让他为战团效力？}

b07daf411c39e633af38.source: Take him as an indebted to the Gilder so that he may earn his salvation.
b07daf411c39e633af38.translation: 将他收为镀金者的负债者，让他有机会挣得救赎。

e630710ec3d9f755c0c6.source: We have no use for him.

3a48574a7fc457f765d6.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_53.png[/img]{The surviving man scrambles away from you. He's muttering something. You can't hear it, but the language is clear nonetheless: he knows who you are, and what you are. | The battle over, you find one survivor in the field. He's a little scraped up but could be of use.}
3a48574a7fc457f765d6.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_53.png[/img]{幸存的男人手脚并用地往后退，嘴里嘟囔着什么。你听不清，可意思却再明白不过：他知道你是谁，也知道你是什么样的人。 | 战斗结束后，你在场上找到一个幸存者。他受了些轻伤，或许还能派上用场。}

51f78680927722220ec1.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_53.png[/img]{The surviving man scrambles away from you. He's muttering something. You can't hear it, but the language is clear nonetheless: he knows who you are, and what you are. | The battle over, you find one survivor in the field. He's a little scraped up but could be of use. | The lone bandit survivor yells out for the old gods as you weigh a chain in your hand, wondering how it will fit around his neck. | %SPEECH_ON%Is this the penalty for banditry?%SPEECH_OFF%The northerner asks as you weigh a chain in your hand. You're still not sure yet of how you'll handle him, but answer anyway.%SPEECH_ON%This isn't punitive at all, it's merely business.%SPEECH_OFF% | The bandit tries to hide, but as the last survivor he's about as easy to spot as a white rabbit on a bloodslaked battlefield. He yells out that the old gods wouldn't abide by men such as yourself. You shrug.%SPEECH_ON%The old gods aren't standing where I am, now are they?%SPEECH_OFF%And you hold out the chain, sizing it with his neck.%SPEECH_ON%But I wonder, how much would you give up, to swap spots with one of your gods, hm?%SPEECH_OFF%}
51f78680927722220ec1.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_53.png[/img]{幸存的男人连滚带爬地躲着你，嘴里不住嘟囔。你听不清他说什么，但他的意思再明白不过：他知道你是谁，也知道你是做什么的。 | 战斗结束后，你在战场上发现一名幸存者。他受了点皮外伤，应该还派得上用场。 | 唯一幸存的强盗大声呼唤旧神，而你掂着手里的锁链，琢磨它套在他脖子上是否合适。 | %SPEECH_ON%这就是当强盗的惩罚？%SPEECH_OFF%北方人问道，你正掂量着手里的锁链。你还没决定如何处置他，不过还是答了一句。%SPEECH_ON%这根本不是惩罚，只是生意。%SPEECH_OFF% | 强盗想躲起来，可作为最后一个活口，他就像血染战场上的白兔一样显眼。他大喊，说旧神绝不会容忍你这样的人。你耸耸肩。%SPEECH_ON%可站在这里的是我，又不是旧神，对吧？%SPEECH_OFF%你伸出锁链，对着他的脖子比了比。%SPEECH_ON%不过我倒想知道，要是能跟你信奉的某位神换个位置，你愿意付出多少代价，嗯？%SPEECH_OFF%}

6724b84af8837c2c6a51.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_172.png[/img]{The surviving man scrambles away from you. He's muttering something. You can't hear it, but the language is clear nonetheless: he knows who you are, and what you are. | The battle over, you find one survivor in the field. He's a little scraped up but could be of use. | You hold the chain out to the nomad, sizing his head from a distance in the swing of its closed gate.%SPEECH_ON%Sometimes in the sands, a man may come across those he should not have trifled with. Sometimes he walks away.%SPEECH_OFF%You grasp the chain firmly.%SPEECH_ON%Sometimes he just walks.%SPEECH_OFF% | The sands shift and slide as the wounded nomad tries to escape. You easily put a boot on him and hold him down, your other hand sizing up his neck with the slave chain. | The nomad prays for forgiveness.%SPEECH_ON%By parting our shadows, the shine of the Gilder brighten the both of us!%SPEECH_OFF%You hold up a chain and tell him not every shadow is born a part of us.}
6724b84af8837c2c6a51.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_172.png[/img]{幸存的男人连滚带爬地躲着你，嘴里不住嘟囔。你听不清他说什么，但他的意思再明白不过：他知道你是谁，也知道你是做什么的。 | 战斗结束后，你在战场上发现一名幸存者。他受了点皮外伤，应该还派得上用场。 | 你朝那游牧民伸出锁链，晃着合拢的颈圈，隔空比了比他的脑袋。%SPEECH_ON%在沙漠里，人有时会碰上不该招惹的对手。有时候，他能安然走开。%SPEECH_OFF%你攥紧了锁链。%SPEECH_ON%有时候，他只能被牵着走。%SPEECH_OFF% | 受伤的游牧民挣扎着想逃，身下的沙子不断滑落。你轻轻松松一脚将他踩住，另一只手提着奴隶的锁链，在他脖子旁比量起来。 | 游牧民祈求你开恩。%SPEECH_ON%让我们的影子各奔东西，愿镀金者的光辉照亮你我！%SPEECH_OFF%你举起锁链，告诉他，有些影子可不是生来就跟在自己身后的。}

3569781021d4dc74f04c.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_172.png[/img]{The surviving man scrambles away from you. He's muttering something. You can't hear it, but the language is clear nonetheless: he knows who you are, and what you are. | The battle over, you find one survivor in the field. He's a little scraped up but could be of use. | %SPEECH_ON%The Gilder wouldn't have it.%SPEECH_OFF%He is the last of the southern troop, a wounded pitiful man begging for his life. You hold up the chain.%SPEECH_ON%Just because this is on you does not mean your path is shadowed, fellow traveler. Just means mine is a little bit brighter.%SPEECH_OFF% | %SPEECH_ON%Ah, please don't!%SPEECH_OFF%You have your boot on the last of the southern troop, and you are sizing him up to join the indebted. He begs for his life, or for freedom, and eventually to simply die free. You shake your head.%SPEECH_ON%Gold cannot live or die, traveler, it is merely weighed. Heavy. Or light. My considerations do not concern you. You beg about something you lost the moment you crossed paths with me.%SPEECH_OFF% | The last of the southern troop is at your feet. He's praying to the Gilder to bring light to his path. Unfortunately, the only one with say here is yourself, and you've got a spot in chains for the man if you wish him to 'join' the %companyname%.}
3569781021d4dc74f04c.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_172.png[/img]{幸存的男人连滚带爬地躲着你，嘴里不住嘟囔。你听不清他说什么，但他的意思再明白不过：他知道你是谁，也知道你是做什么的。 | 战斗结束后，你在战场上发现一名幸存者。他受了点皮外伤，应该还派得上用场。 | %SPEECH_ON%镀金者不会允许的。%SPEECH_OFF%他是这支南方部队最后的活口，一个受了伤、苦苦求饶的可怜人。你举起锁链。%SPEECH_ON%同路人，戴上这个，不代表你的道路就蒙了阴影，只代表我的路又亮了一点。%SPEECH_OFF% | %SPEECH_ON%啊，求你，别这样！%SPEECH_OFF%你一脚踩住南方部队最后的活口，打量着他是否适合加入负债者。他先求活命，再求自由，最后只求能自由地死去。你摇摇头。%SPEECH_ON%旅人，黄金无所谓生死，只论轻重。重，或轻。我盘算什么，与你无关。你现在苦苦哀求的东西，早在遇上我的那一刻，就已经失去了。%SPEECH_OFF% | 南方部队最后的活口伏在你脚下，祈求镀金者照亮他的道路。可惜，此地真正说了算的，只有你。只要你想让他“加入”%companyname%，锁链里便有他的位置。}

5354991c941fd5949ebb.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_145.png[/img]{The surviving man scrambles away from you. He's muttering something. You can't hear it, but the language is clear nonetheless: he knows who you are, and what you are. | The battle over, you find one survivor in the field. He's a little scraped up but could be of use. | Ah, the last survivor. He's a large man, the barbarian, and could perhaps do well for you. In chains, of course. | The %companyname% rarely comes across stock such as these northern barbarians. With one last survivor left on the field, you ponder if taking him as an indebted would be to your benefit. | The last barbarian standing. He speaks to you in a language you'd never have the time to learn. Grunts, growls, things which other languages would take for threats, but here you know he is articulating something of import. But, all you have to respond with is the chain, and this barbarian might just make a very good indebted for the %companyname%.}
5354991c941fd5949ebb.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_145.png[/img]{幸存的男人连滚带爬地躲着你，嘴里不住嘟囔。你听不清他说什么，但他的意思再明白不过：他知道你是谁，也知道你是做什么的。 | 战斗结束后，你在战场上发现一名幸存者。他受了点皮外伤，应该还派得上用场。 | 啊，最后一个活口。这蛮族汉子身材魁梧，或许能成为一把好手，为你效力。当然，得先给他戴上镣铐。 | %companyname%很少遇上这些北方蛮族这样的人货。战场上只剩最后一个活口，你琢磨着，把他收为负债者是否划算。 | 最后一个还站着的蛮族。他用一种你这辈子都没工夫学的语言对你说话。哼声、低吼，放在别的语言里都像是在威胁人，但你明白，他此刻正努力说些要紧的事。不过，你能给他的回答只有锁链。这个蛮族或许会成为%companyname%手下相当好用的负债者。}

1b0f93d3847b848ab2db.source: Lost a battle and was taken a captive

feadfb188b02af2f1efb.source: Formerly a soldier loyal to noble lords, his company was slaughtered by your men and %name% was taken as an indebted. It didn't take much to break his spirit and force him to fight for you.
feadfb188b02af2f1efb.translation: %name%曾是忠于贵族领主的士兵。你的手下屠灭了他的队伍，将他收为负债者。没费多少力气，他便屈服了，被迫为你而战。

8cd231590d1f12ab332f.source: %name% was taken as an indebted after barely surviving a battle against your men. His spirit was broken and he was forced to fight for you, so that he may pay his debt to the Gilder.
8cd231590d1f12ab332f.translation: 与手下交战后，%name%勉强捡回性命，却被你收为负债者。他的意志被摧垮，被迫为你作战，以偿还欠镀金者的债。

639c5299714a393649a5.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{A lone merchant approaches with a wagon pulled by a camel. Large jugs rattle against one another in the bed of his cart, with ropes of dried moss hanging between the lids of each one. He rears up on the camel and swings his legs to one side of the animal's withers, tapping his own boot with a jockey switch.%SPEECH_ON%Hello there, travelers, I pray that your road to the coin has been gilded well. Mine has, though I'm afraid we have seemingly crossed paths at a time when my peculiar shines rank in rare number. I've but a few goods left, all of the drinking sort. 50 crowns per jug. Interested?%SPEECH_OFF%}
639c5299714a393649a5.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{一个独行商人赶着骆驼拖曳的货车走来。大罐在车厢中相互碰撞，罐盖之间垂着搓成绳状的干苔藓。他在驼背上坐直身子，将双腿转到骆驼肩侧，用短鞭轻敲自己的靴子。%SPEECH_ON%你们好，旅人。愿各位的发财路都铺满金光。我倒是一路顺遂，不过，恐怕各位来得不巧，我那些稀奇货色已所剩无几。只余几样，全是能喝的。每罐50克朗，有兴趣吗？%SPEECH_OFF%}

2f521b744ddfc8791ba9.source: We'll take all the jugs for 150 crowns.

e8e35a1a3c8fccd1aab3.source: For 50 crowns, we'll just take one.

9f53f7652744a2242e50.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{You exchange for everything he's got to which the merchant happily obliges. When he leaves, his camels are barren and seem to have a skip in their step after carrying a load for so long. The drink in the jugs is a mixture of water and other additives which will ensure good, long lasting taste. A refreshing beverage to have in an otherwise hellish wasteland.}
9f53f7652744a2242e50.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{你买下了他的全部货物，商人欣然答应。离开时，骆驼背上空空如也，卸下长久压身的重负，连脚步都仿佛轻快起来。罐中的饮品以水调制，加入了其他配料，滋味宜人，也耐存放。在这地狱般的荒原上，算得上难得的清爽。}

1ef6a04ad3837209d4ce.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{The merchant nods and you exchange crowns for one of the jugs. Despite only having a single jug of the drink, it will provide a refreshing respite from the hellish heat of the desert.}
1ef6a04ad3837209d4ce.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{商人点头，你付出克朗，换来一罐饮品。虽只有一罐，仍能让人暂时从沙漠地狱般的酷热中得到一丝清凉。}

902f9e484c29ffa29511.translation: 痛快地喝了个够，神清气爽

837cdca07186016c5060.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{You come across a line of men being marched in chains. Their leader remarks that they are a part of the 'indebted,' but one of the men, clearly a northerner, yells out that they're merchant mariners who have been captured by pirates. The supposed manhunter at the head of this troop laughs.%SPEECH_ON%Don't believe his lies, traveler, those who are deeply indebted to the Gilder fear the long journey to redemption. He'd rather die and face hellfire than trouble himself with salvation. Is there nothing more human than that?%SPEECH_OFF%}
837cdca07186016c5060.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{你遇到一列戴着锁链行进的人。领头者称他们是“负债者”，可其中一个明显是北方人的男人大喊，他们其实是遭海盗俘虏的商船水手。队首这个所谓的捕奴者笑了。%SPEECH_ON%旅人，别信他的谎话。深欠镀金者之债的人，都害怕漫长的赎罪之路。他宁肯死后面对地狱烈火，也不愿费力拯救自己。还有什么比这更像人性呢？%SPEECH_OFF%}

f13d3dbb197ea42d35ac.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{You draw your sword and demand the 'indebted' be set free. The manhunter looks around, incredulous.%SPEECH_ON%Kind traveler, I am merely obeying the laws of the Gilder. These men have debts to pay, and hellfire awaits the ones who shall go unremitted.%SPEECH_OFF%Shaking your head, you tell him you won't repeat yourself. He sighs and goes about unshackling the men. Most immediately take off running, however one stays behind. But he's not there to join you, he stays with the manhunter, holding his wrists out.%SPEECH_ON%Please, let me into the Gilder's light.%SPEECH_OFF%Another man also stays behind, but mostly to convene with you. He announces himself with clear intentions: he'll join and fight for the %companyname%.%SPEECH_ON%If I've debts to pay off, it's with you, sir.%SPEECH_OFF%}
f13d3dbb197ea42d35ac.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{你拔剑，要求释放这些“负债者”。捕奴者难以置信地看看四周。%SPEECH_ON%好心的旅人，我不过是在遵从镀金者的律法。这些人有债要偿，无法赎清的人，等着他们的便是地狱烈火。%SPEECH_OFF%你摇摇头，告诉他，自己不会再说第二遍。他叹了口气，开始替众人解开镣铐。大多数人立刻拔腿就跑，却有一个留了下来。他并不是要加入你，而是待在捕奴者身旁，主动伸出双腕。%SPEECH_ON%求您，让我沐浴镀金者的光辉。%SPEECH_OFF%另有一人也没走，却是为了与你说话。他自报来意，明确表示愿意加入%companyname%，为战团作战。%SPEECH_ON%先生，真要说欠了谁的债，那也是欠您的。%SPEECH_OFF%}

4795ccdc802c95d1db2b.source: I hope you know how to use a weapon.

a1a76d15c3a36b2a455b.source: You're free, but you'll have to find your way back home on your own.
a1a76d15c3a36b2a455b.translation: 你自由了，不过得自己找路回家。

2e6e099f687d890f7532.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{%fisherman% the fisherman steps forward.%SPEECH_ON%Wait, I know this man! He's not indebted to no one, we used to sail together many winters ago.%SPEECH_OFF%The sailor nods.%SPEECH_ON%Yes, yes that's right!%SPEECH_OFF%The manhunter looks over, then walks forward and frees the sailor.%SPEECH_ON%I am no stranger the circumstances and complexities of the Gilder and can see the machinations of his designs. No doubt he wanted these two to meet. Please, have the man, and his salvation shall be true.%SPEECH_OFF%The manhunter continues on with his train of captured men. One turns to you.%SPEECH_ON%Real shame we don't farkin' know each other, yeah?%SPEECH_OFF%}
2e6e099f687d890f7532.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{渔夫%fisherman%走上前。%SPEECH_ON%等等，我认识这人！他谁的钱都不欠，很多年前我们还一起跑过船。%SPEECH_OFF%水手连忙点头。%SPEECH_ON%对，对，没错！%SPEECH_OFF%捕奴者望了过来，随后上前解开水手的束缚。%SPEECH_ON%镀金者的安排曲折深奥，我对此并不陌生，也看得出祂在其中的谋划。毫无疑问，祂是想让这两人重逢。请带走他吧，愿他由此获得真正的救赎。%SPEECH_OFF%捕奴者继续押着俘虏们上路。其中一个转头看向你。%SPEECH_ON%咱俩他妈的怎么就不认识呢，真可惜，是吧？%SPEECH_OFF%}

afbbb22dc743ce340ea7.source: Welcome. I hope you know how to use a weapon.

d510934f0c7616b48fb1.source: You'll have to find your way back home on your own.

bd2d7da3ce19af6060af.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{You rattle a chain and bring a few of your indebted forward. Flexing your indebted-wrangling cred, you tell the manhunter that you've experience in these matters and you can tell these unruly sailors will find a moment to ambush and kill him.%SPEECH_ON%Hand them over to me and I will pursue their salvation accordingly. Keep them in your stead, and the Gilder Himself will not be able to protect you from the evil which lies in their hearts.%SPEECH_OFF%The manhunter thinks for a time, then nods in agreement.%SPEECH_ON%You're right. This was a good haul, but the Gilder shall see my deeds have already been enough and my intents true. Take them for yourself and may the Gilder shine sublimity upon your life and theirs.%SPEECH_OFF%}
bd2d7da3ce19af6060af.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{你抖响锁链，把手下几个负债者带到前面，向捕奴者显摆自己管束这些人的本事。你告诉他，自己对此颇有经验，一眼就看得出，这群桀骜不驯的水手迟早会找机会偷袭，将他杀死。%SPEECH_ON%把他们交给我，我自会引导他们赎罪。要是继续留在你身边，就算镀金者亲自出手，也护不住你，挡不了他们心里的恶念。%SPEECH_OFF%捕奴者想了一会儿，点头赞同。%SPEECH_ON%你说得对。这一趟收获虽好，但镀金者定能看见，我所做的已然足够，心意也确实真诚。你带走他们吧。愿镀金者的崇高光辉照耀你与他们的一生。%SPEECH_OFF%}

25a3fabeaf84b5837a92.source: The Gilder is most benevolent to let you pay off your debt.
25a3fabeaf84b5837a92.translation: 镀金者慈悲为怀，准你偿清自己的债。

7a359812e6ebf7594df2.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{The manhunter bows briefly.%SPEECH_ON%May your road be ever gilded, traveler.%SPEECH_OFF%He continues on his way while the supposed sailor yell out that they're not even from these lands, that they don't know anything about this 'Gilder' they're indebted to in the first place.}
7a359812e6ebf7594df2.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_157.png[/img]{捕奴者略一鞠躬。%SPEECH_ON%旅人，愿你的前路永蒙镀金者光照。%SPEECH_OFF%他继续赶路，那些自称水手的人却大喊着，说他们根本不属于这片土地，连自己欠债的这个“镀金者”是谁都不知道。}

d4f223a6dd4042e4e2bf.source: Let these men go free at once!

59b6ed715332b0ec638e.source: It looks like %fisherman% has something to say on the matter.

576787b1f3130087ca9b.source: Hand over the indebted to me and I will pursue their salvation accordingly.
576787b1f3130087ca9b.translation: 把负债者交给我，我会妥善安排他们的救赎。

0904a7703ecd1a60b796.source: Be on your way then, manhunters.

e85f20de2c014ecee99e.source: You rescued %name% from a life in slavery after he was taken by pirates operating out of the city states.
e85f20de2c014ecee99e.translation: %name%遭来自城邦的海盗俘虏，是你将他从奴役生涯中救了出来。

f26b66e9fdf32e2fb67e.source: Heard rumors of you freeing indebted

8d74a39c68f044b9b623.source: Got saved from a life in slavery by
8d74a39c68f044b9b623.translation: 得救并摆脱奴役，救他的人是

ba4404acbb4bf933c8ed.source: %name% was working the seas as a sailor when pirates of the city states boarded his vessel and took him as captives along with his crew. By some happenstance, he made his way into your care to work off his debt to the Gilder.
ba4404acbb4bf933c8ed.translation: %name%原是海上水手，城邦海盗登上他的船，将他与船员一并俘虏。几番辗转，他落到你手下，为偿还欠镀金者的债而服役。

5b1f8ab4a795bb0f3db0.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_12.png[/img]{%nonhistorian% enters your tent.%SPEECH_ON%Captain, come quick, there's something wrong with %historian%!%SPEECH_OFF%You hurry to the scene. %historian% is bowled over the Lorekeeper's book like an ancient man shielding the first flame. He's clenching the fleshen covers, hands shaking, and he looks up at you with bloodshot eyes.%SPEECH_ON%I know what it says, captain, I know what it says!%SPEECH_OFF%You crouch down and the man backs off, shaking his head.%SPEECH_ON%No. No! It's about the end! The end of all things! We're... we're merely tools to get there, don't you understand? Everything we do, everything anybody does, is a means to the ultimate end: the death of all beings. Our very existence gives it power, without us, it can rest again. But so long as there is existence, it cannot sleep!%SPEECH_OFF%You shake your head and ask what he means. The man turns the book around and there's a page that is entirely black, yet he points his finger to a spot on it as though you were meant to read a sentence there.%SPEECH_ON%This is no book, captain, it is instruction, on how to raise the spirits of the dead.%SPEECH_OFF%You ask who could have such knowledge, and %historian% grins madly.%SPEECH_ON%There is no 'who', there is no 'what'! It is a tool of undoing, put into this world by the one that calls itself Davkul!%SPEECH_OFF%You tell the men to shelter him as he has clearly lost his mind. One of the sellswords brings you %historian%'s translations of the book, but they're just scribbles, no less unintelligible than their source.%SPEECH_ON%Even if we could understand a word of it, even if we could use it, I don't think we should. See, and just between us, but that page he showed you? It had text on it earlier. And I mean in the very moment you were walking up. I could see the words, I could see the symbols. But at some point, the ink, the ash, whatever it was, it spread over the page entirely. It's as if we're not meant to have this knowledge.%SPEECH_OFF%It's quite possible, but there's a darker realization spreading over your mind: %historian% is meant to have this knowledge, but his limited understanding is not for your benefit, but merely a tool in the machinations of something else entirely. You are only being shown as much as you need and no more...}
5b1f8ab4a795bb0f3db0.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_12.png[/img]{%nonhistorian%走进你的帐篷。%SPEECH_ON%团长，快来，%historian%不对劲！%SPEECH_OFF%你匆忙赶去。%historian%蜷身伏在典籍守护者的书上，像远古之人护着世间第一簇火。他紧攥人皮封面，双手颤抖，抬起布满血丝的眼睛望你。%SPEECH_ON%我知道上面写什么了，团长，我知道了！%SPEECH_OFF%你蹲下，他却后退，连连摇头。%SPEECH_ON%不，不！说的是终结！万物的终结！我们……我们不过是抵达终点的工具，你不明白吗？我们做的一切，所有人做的一切，都在通往最终的结局：一切生灵的死亡。我们的存在本身就在给它力量，没有我们，它便能重新安息。可只要还有东西存在，它就无法入睡！%SPEECH_OFF%你摇头，问他什么意思。那人将书转过来，一整页漆黑，却仍用手指着其中一处，仿佛你该在那里读到一句话。%SPEECH_ON%团长，这不是书，是指引，教人如何唤起亡者之灵。%SPEECH_OFF%你问，谁会掌握这样的知识，%historian%却疯狂地咧嘴笑了。%SPEECH_ON%没有“谁”，也没有“什么”！这是毁灭的工具，是那个自称达夫库尔的存在放进这个世界的！%SPEECH_OFF%他显然已经失去理智，你叫弟兄们安顿好他。一名佣兵拿来%historian%对书的译文，可那不过是胡乱涂画，和原文一样无法辨认。%SPEECH_ON%就算能读懂一个字，就算真能派上用场，我也觉得不该碰。听着，这话只跟你说，他刚才给你看的那页，先前是有字的。就是你走过来的那一刻，我还看得见文字，看得见符号。可不知什么时候，墨水、灰烬，或者不管那是什么，突然铺满了整页。就像我们本不该掌握这些知识。%SPEECH_OFF%很有可能。然而，一个更阴暗的念头正在你心中蔓延：%historian%本来就该掌握这些知识，可他有限的领悟，并不是为了帮你，而是某个全然不同的存在施行诡计的工具。你能看见的，只有它需要你看见的那些，仅此而已……}

He's clenching the fleshen covers, hands shaking, and he looks up at you with bloodshot eyes.%SPEECH_ON%I know what it says, captain, I know what it says!%SPEECH_OFF%You crouch down and the man backs off, shaking his head.%SPEECH_ON%No. No! You are only being shown as much as you need and no more...}

c9385572e923b6fc259e.source: Has seen the end of things

ec1ca7441b720e8c4462.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{You come across an old man in the street. He wouldn't be particularly remarkable, except for the fact that he is owner of a particularly nice set of equipment. A bit worn and torn, but nice. And, of course, the fact he's an elder and hasn't had these items stolen from him is evidence of something else going on here.%SPEECH_ON%The Crownling stares, the Crownling wonders.%SPEECH_OFF%The man says as he bites in a loaf of bread. He looks up at you.%SPEECH_ON%My name is %retired%. I once fought in the arenas, but retired five years ago. Not by choice, mind. I was tasked with throwing a match, but instead I cut the opponent's head off. Said opponent was the son of a Vizier. This particular detail was not shared with me at the time. Those five years I spoke of? Spent them in a dungeon.%SPEECH_OFF%}
ec1ca7441b720e8c4462.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{你在街上遇见一个老人。本来没什么值得留意，偏偏他手里有一套相当精良的装备，虽有些破损磨耗，仍是好东西。而一个上了年纪的人，竟没被人抢走这些家当，本身就另有意味。%SPEECH_ON%克朗客在打量，克朗客在琢磨。%SPEECH_OFF%老人咬着面包，抬眼望向你。%SPEECH_ON%我叫%retired%，以前在角斗场里打过，五年前退了下来。可不是自愿的，先说清楚。有人让我故意输一场，我却把对手的脑袋砍了。那对手是位维齐尔的儿子，偏偏这点细节，当时没人告诉我。我刚才说的五年？全在地牢里过了。%SPEECH_OFF%}

9ea3815c6f5342f3ef4b.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{You tell him that you'd have use for him in the %companyname%. He laughs.%SPEECH_ON%Fighting days are a bit beyond me. I'm looking to sell this armor at cost and leave this city forever.%SPEECH_OFF%He tilts armor forward.%SPEECH_ON%You won't find equipment like this anywhere. All I ask is 1,000 crowns for it, a gladiator's harness the likes of which you'd be hard pressed to find in any ordinary blacksmith's shop.%SPEECH_OFF%}
9ea3815c6f5342f3ef4b.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{你告诉他，%companyname%用得上他的本领。他笑了。%SPEECH_ON%我已经过了打打杀杀的年纪。现在只想把这副护甲按成本卖掉，然后永远离开这座城。%SPEECH_OFF%他将护甲往前一倾。%SPEECH_ON%这样的装备可不是什么地方都有。我只要1,000克朗。这副角斗士护身带，寻常铁匠铺里可难得一见。%SPEECH_OFF%}

2c4a7b0eeb864ef60019.source: We'll take the armor for 1,000 crowns.

6b823d7677261f66ff60.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{You hand him the gold and he gives you the armor. He weighs the purse of crowns.%SPEECH_ON%I suppose this will be enough to retire away on. The weapons are better left to me. This is not a particularly safe land, after all, and even an old man as dangerous as myself might need protection.%SPEECH_OFF%He's right about that. You wish him well and put the armor into inventory.}
6b823d7677261f66ff60.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{你交出金币，他交给你护甲，掂了掂那袋克朗。%SPEECH_ON%我想，这些够我找个地方养老了。武器还是留给我吧。这地方毕竟不太平，就算我这样的危险老头，也得有点防身的家伙。%SPEECH_OFF%这话倒没错。你祝他往后顺遂，将护甲收入仓库。}

e2dd7a4d587ea23bc639.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{%gladiator% laughs.%SPEECH_ON%Friend, I was once a gladiator. Come with us and treat the whole world as your arena. I know you have that itch. I know it's somewhere down in there. Find it. That glee of the kill. That energy from victory. Share it with us, a band of battle brothers.%SPEECH_OFF%The elder gladiator stares at his equipment. His reflection stares back, albeit muddled and warbled from dirt and dents. He nods.%SPEECH_ON%You're right. What in the Gilder's name am I thinking? I've been piss poor and pissed on and pissed off for far too long. If your company will have me, then I shall end my days going out the way I lived it: killing!%SPEECH_OFF%}
e2dd7a4d587ea23bc639.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{%gladiator%笑道。%SPEECH_ON%朋友，我也当过角斗士。跟我们走，把整个世界都当作你的角斗场吧。我知道你还手痒，心底那股劲儿还在。把它找回来。杀敌的快意，取胜的热血，与我们这帮并肩作战的弟兄一同分享。%SPEECH_OFF%老角斗士看着自己的装备。装备上倒映着他的脸，只是被污垢和凹痕映得模糊扭曲。他点点头。%SPEECH_ON%你说得对。镀金者在上，我到底在想什么？我穷得叮当响，受尽欺负，憋了一肚子气，这样的日子早就过够了。只要你们肯收留，我就要像活着时一样，在杀戮中迎来最后一刻！%SPEECH_OFF%}

12592d9fef764d6ff4a3.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{You welcome the man aboard. He gets to his feet.%SPEECH_ON%I'd like to fight with my own gear, but I'm not partial to it. After all, I was just trying to sell it, right? Give me what you think is best and point me in the right direction. I'll show them what the Wolf of Arena Alley has to show!%SPEECH_OFF%}
12592d9fef764d6ff4a3.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{你欢迎他入伙。他站起身来。%SPEECH_ON%我想用自己的装备打仗，不过也不强求。毕竟刚才还想把它卖了，对吧？你觉得什么合适就给我什么，再指个方向。我会让他们见识竞技场后巷之狼的本事！%SPEECH_OFF%}

c57fe8da5de00cf30a42.source: Wolf of Arena Alley? Ah, alright.
c57fe8da5de00cf30a42.translation: 竞技场后巷之狼？啊，好吧。

f62a6afafd8115e6c9a7.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{The gladiator sits back down.%SPEECH_ON%Well, what the fuck was all that big bravado speech for?%SPEECH_OFF%%gladiator% apologizes, throwing you a glare between words whlie the rest of the company laughs.}
f62a6afafd8115e6c9a7.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{角斗士重新坐下。%SPEECH_ON%那刚才那一通豪言壮语，他妈的到底算什么？%SPEECH_OFF%%gladiator%一边道歉，一边抽空瞪你，其余弟兄都笑了起来。}

26b820f6102334b55122.source: Perhaps %gladiator% can convince you to join us.

60c07a91ce9973d4b0fc.source: %name%, also known as Wolf of Arena Alley, is a retired gladiator, but an active sellsword. He's been earning crowns by killing for a long time, and it shows both in his experience and his age.
60c07a91ce9973d4b0fc.translation: %name%人称“竞技场后巷之狼”，已从角斗场退役，如今却仍是个现役佣兵。他靠杀人挣克朗已有许多年，这一点，既写在经验里，也写在年纪上。

75fd49f1abb977a16aac.source: Had a good laugh at a retired gladiator
75fd49f1abb977a16aac.translation: 被一名退役角斗士逗得大笑

bd334fb48d5eb0bd2054.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_170.png[/img]{You come across a sparse group of nomads arguing with a troop of the Vizier's men. Between them is another group of what look like the sort of women that would be in the Vizier's harem. As you draw near all sides pause and stare at you. A lieutenant of the Vizier's troop waves you off.%SPEECH_ON%This does not concern you, Crownling.%SPEECH_OFF%But, perhaps trying to invite you into the event, the nomads explain: the women consist of 'indebted', those whose service is owed to another for failures or transgressions. In this case, they owe services to the Vizier. However, they have escaped and the nomads, who find the concept of indebtedness to be heresy, have taken them in.%SPEECH_ON%Hey, Crownling! Don't listen to a word of that nomad's poison! And nomad, these women come with us, or you ALL die here.%SPEECH_OFF%}
bd334fb48d5eb0bd2054.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_170.png[/img]{你遇见一小群游牧民，正与维齐尔的一队手下争执。两拨人之间，还有一群看着像是维齐尔后宫侍妾的女人。你一走近，各方都停下来望着你。维齐尔军中的副官挥手赶人。%SPEECH_ON%克朗客，这事与你无关。%SPEECH_OFF%游牧民却像是有意拉你介入，解释起缘由：这些女人是“负债者”，因过失或罪行而欠下为人服役的债，在这里，她们该服侍的是维齐尔。不过，她们逃了出来，而游牧民认为所谓“负债”之说是异端邪说，便收留了她们。%SPEECH_ON%喂，克朗客！别听那游牧民的毒言毒语！还有你们，游牧民，要么让这些女人跟我们走，要么你们所有人都死在这里！%SPEECH_OFF%}

90ec8d0a8fdab19f239d.source: I'd rather not get involved in this.

12f2c9dbee1b17881bd8.source: The women belong to the Vizier.

020243b39ffc92331732.source: The women are free to go wherever they choose.
020243b39ffc92331732.translation: 这些女人想去哪儿，就有权去哪儿。

5348bc54cb2169fc8c75.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_170.png[/img]{You draw your sword and tell the Vizier's men to get lost, hoping it works because any violence with them will not be without a good amount of bloodshed. Thankfully, they retreat. The lieutenant bows mockingly.%SPEECH_ON%The womenfolk are free, but with their debts to the Gilder left unpaid, they shall burn in pits of burning sand, a hell from which there will never be escape!%SPEECH_OFF%Laughing, you thank him for the imagery. The nomads also thank you, as do the freed harem though it's more with their eyes than anything. One nomad hands you a gift of treasures.%SPEECH_ON%We carry these not for us, but for when we occasion upon travelers such as yourself. We do not seek comforts in material things, not in this world. And do not trust that man of the Vizier. He lies. The Gilder shall see us all in sublimity when it is our time to come.%SPEECH_OFF%}
5348bc54cb2169fc8c75.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_170.png[/img]{你拔出剑，喝令维齐尔的手下滚开，心里只盼这招能管用，毕竟真与他们动手，必然少不了一场血战。所幸，他们退了。副官讥讽地鞠了一躬。%SPEECH_ON%这些女人是自由了，可欠镀金者的债尚未偿清，她们终将在炽热的沙坑中焚烧，永世不得逃出地狱！%SPEECH_OFF%你笑着谢他描述得如此生动。游牧民也向你道谢，获救的侍妾们同样如此，只是更多用的是眼神。一个游牧民送来一份财宝。%SPEECH_ON%我们带着这些，并非为了自己，而是留待遇见您这样的旅人时相赠。至少在这个世界，我们不求物质的安逸。也别信维齐尔那手下的话，他在撒谎。等时辰到了，镀金者会在祂的荣光中接纳我们所有人。%SPEECH_OFF%}

e3911a314e1843578509.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_170.png[/img]{You know a good payday when you see one, and by payday you mean an ambassador of a Vizier. Drawing your sword, you jump between the nomads and the women, telling the former to back off and return to the deserts. The nomads draw bows and raise spears, but their leader quiets them.%SPEECH_ON%No, the interloper has intervened in a manner he finds most suitable, and certainly the Gilder has chosen him as an arbiter in this matter for good reason. Take the women, then, and the dispute is settled.%SPEECH_OFF%The Vizier's men gather the harem back into their ranks. A heavy bag is brought to you by the lieutenant.%SPEECH_ON%Payment, Crownling. This was not your task, but that does not mean it carries no reward. You have saved these indebted women from the Gilder's hellfire. May our generosity be a constant reminder going forward, yes?%SPEECH_OFF%}
e3911a314e1843578509.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_170.png[/img]{你一眼就能认出挣钱的好机会——眼前这位维齐尔的使者就是。你拔剑跃到游牧民与女人之间，叫前者退开，回沙漠去。游牧民张弓举矛，首领却止住了他们。%SPEECH_ON%不。这位外来者已按他认为妥当的方式介入。镀金者选他裁决此事，必有缘由。那就带走这些女人吧，争端到此为止。%SPEECH_OFF%维齐尔的手下把侍妾们重新拢进队伍，副官则给你送来一只沉甸甸的钱袋。%SPEECH_ON%克朗客，这是酬劳。此事虽非你的差事，却不代表没有赏钱。你把这些负债的女人从镀金者的地狱烈火中救了出来。往后，还望你常记着这份慷慨，如何？%SPEECH_OFF%}

6547edd3451cf683afa9.source: We look forward to further business with your master.
6547edd3451cf683afa9.translation: 盼着以后还能和你主人做生意。

a21830aba5814a4a0508.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_170.png[/img]{You shake your head and wish the women the best in the matter, but it's resolved before you can even leave: the nomads back off and the Vizier's men take them away. When you ask the nomads why they gave up so quick, their leader states that you must have been an arbitrator sent by the Gilder Himself, and if this is what you chose then so be it. Seems the nomads never had a chance at beating those professional soldiers and you were their last hope.}
a21830aba5814a4a0508.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_170.png[/img]{你摇头，祝那些女人好运。可还没等你离开，事情就结束了：游牧民退下，维齐尔的人将女人们带走。你问游牧民为何这么快放弃，首领说，你一定是镀金者亲自派来的仲裁者；既然你如此裁定，他们也只能接受。看来，游牧民根本打不过那些职业士兵，而你就是他们最后的希望。}

b5aacd9b59439c0bfc9c.source: You aided in the escape of a Vizier's harem
b5aacd9b59439c0bfc9c.translation: 你帮助一位维齐尔的姬妾逃走

50dd323c7dfb923ba621.source: You helped to return a Vizier's harem
50dd323c7dfb923ba621.translation: 你帮助一位维齐尔追回姬妾

43b2d49062beb579712c.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_64.png[/img]{While on the path, you come across a man sitting beside the path. He's clad in some beaten armor and there's an even more beaten weapon in his lap. He regards you with the limpest of waves.%SPEECH_ON%Evening. If you ain't sellswords, then I never set my pa's pants afire.%SPEECH_OFF%That seems to be an interesting tale in and of itself, but you instead ask the man what he's doing in the middle of the road. More important, you ask this rather able-bodied fella if he's looking for work.%SPEECH_ON%A job? No. I don't need one. I already done that sword-selling bit and I'm done with it. You know what, here.%SPEECH_OFF%He starts undoing his armor and throws it on the ground before you.%SPEECH_ON%Take it. I've no need for that life anymore. Take the weapon, too. I'm leaving all this shite behind. You should, too, but I knew ya won't. Not before it's too late, anyway. I'm walking the earth until my feet are ground into nubs. As for yourself, godspeed.%SPEECH_OFF%And just like that, the stranger goes.}
43b2d49062beb579712c.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_64.png[/img]{赶路时，你遇见一个坐在路边的男人。他穿着一身破甲，膝上搁着把更破的武器。他朝你有气无力地挥了挥手。%SPEECH_ON%晚上好。你们要不是佣兵，那我就没烧过我爹的裤子。%SPEECH_OFF%这话背后似乎有段有趣的故事，不过你还是问起他为什么坐在路中央。更要紧的是，这人看着还挺健壮，你问他是否想找份活干。%SPEECH_ON%找活？不。我不需要。我也干过卖命的行当，现在干够了。这样吧，给你。%SPEECH_OFF%他开始解下盔甲，扔在你面前的地上。%SPEECH_ON%拿去吧。我再也不想过那种日子了。武器也拿走。这些破事，我全都要丢下。你也该收手，可我知道你不会。至少等你想收手时，肯定已经晚了。我要走遍天下，直到把两只脚都磨秃。至于你，愿神保佑吧。%SPEECH_OFF%话音刚落，这陌生人就起身走了。}

2a231f12787203804275.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_64.png[/img]{%peddler% the peddler, always having a good nose for gold, asks if the man earned any crowns while working as a sellsword. When the stranger nods, the peddler notes that if that's true then he can always 'buy' his way back into the life. The sellsword thinks for a minute, then nods again.%SPEECH_ON%You know what? That's right. So long as I've got the crowns, I've still got a lifeline back to that damned business. Here, take it.%SPEECH_OFF%The retiring, and ostensibly soon-to-be-hermit, fishes into his pockets and happily throws you a sack of crowns like a man ridding himself of an old burden.}
2a231f12787203804275.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_64.png[/img]{小贩%peddler%向来对金钱嗅觉灵敏，便问那人，当佣兵这些年可曾攒下克朗。陌生人点头，小贩随即指出：既然如此，他随时还能花钱买回过去的生活。那佣兵想了片刻，再次点头。%SPEECH_ON%你知道吗？没错。只要还有克朗，就还有根线，把我牵回那该死的行当。来，拿去吧。%SPEECH_OFF%这个准备退隐、看来很快就要当隐士的人，摸索口袋，愉快地朝你抛来一袋克朗，仿佛终于卸下了一副陈年重担。}

87b6ac431ac0b024ead0.source: We'll put these to good use.
87b6ac431ac0b024ead0.translation: 我们会让这些东西派上用场。

e82ff031b3c3940b52ba.source: %terrainImage%{The desert is not home to much of anything beyond the sands. So it is rather particular when you come across a lone tree setting out by itself, and even more stranger that hanging from a branch is a fat beehive with a cloud of workers swarming around its bulbous shape. Even at some distance, you can see the golden ember of their honey glistening...}
e82ff031b3c3940b52ba.translation: %terrainImage%{沙漠除了沙，什么都难得一见。所以，前方孤零零立着一棵树，已够稀奇；更稀奇的是，枝头还挂着硕大的蜂巢，工蜂如云，在鼓胀的巢身四周飞舞。隔着一段距离，你都能看见蜂蜜闪着金色余烬般的光……}

58d09092acd13db1d5e3.source: %terrainImage%{%chosen% confidently walks up toward the tree and the bees seem shunted away by his very presence. The noise of their fluttering thickens with angry vibrations, but otherwise they take no further offense. He carefully scoops some of the honey into a jar and then eases back and steps away. He returns to the company.%SPEECH_ON%Easy peasy beehive squeezy, lads.%SPEECH_OFF%}
58d09092acd13db1d5e3.translation: %terrainImage%{%chosen%自信满满地走向大树，蜂群仿佛单凭他的气势便被逼退。振翅的嗡鸣变得愤怒而密集，却没有进一步攻击。他小心将蜂蜜舀进罐里，缓缓后退，离开大树，回到战团。%SPEECH_ON%弟兄们，取蜜这点活，伸手就有得。%SPEECH_OFF%}

a79c27979fee3c2eacfa.source: Buzz all you want, this honey is ours!
a79c27979fee3c2eacfa.translation: 随你们怎么嗡嗡，这蜂蜜归我们了！

920ea0f9107c423a605f.source: %terrainImage%{%chosen% laces his fingers and cracks the knuckles with a long stretch.%SPEECH_ON%Like stealing candy from a baby.%SPEECH_OFF%He walks up to the tree and stands beneath the hive. He poses and points up at it, laughs, then turns his hands up and - much to the shock of everyone - just grabs the entire beehive. The bees instantly swarm the sellsword and he drops the hive and sprints away, a cloud of angry buzzing chasing him down a sand dune. He rolls and rolls, his screams issuing out whenever he flies out of the sand, and then he lands at the bottom and a wash of sand covers him and spares him from further bee stings. You wait a while before retrieving him, lest the bees know your hand in this attempted thievery.}
920ea0f9107c423a605f.translation: %terrainImage%{%chosen%十指交扣，伸了个长长的懒腰，将指关节压得咔咔作响。%SPEECH_ON%这还不跟抢小孩的糖一样容易。%SPEECH_OFF%他走到树下，站在蜂巢正下方，摆着架势朝上一指，哈哈大笑，随后抬起双手，竟在众目睽睽之下直接抱住了整个蜂巢。蜜蜂瞬间一拥而上。他丢下蜂巢，拔腿就跑，一团嗡嗡作响的怒蜂紧追不舍，将他赶下沙丘。他一路翻滚，每次从沙里翻出来，就发出一声惨叫。最后，他跌到坡底，被涌下的沙子盖住，总算躲过了继续挨蜇的命运。你等了一阵才去把他挖出来，免得蜜蜂认出你也是这场未遂偷窃的同谋。}

e7e1ccd6ff319b4f0205.source:
%terrainImage%{You're sure %wildman% the Wildman has seen a hive or two in his time estranged to the forests. He grunts and points at the beehive and then at himself. You nod. He grunts again and goes up the sand dune to the tree while you watch from a safe distance. When he stands beneath the hive, he hoots again, cupping his hand over his mouth to make sure you hear him. He points at the beehive. You nod again and point aggressively at the hive. It's the only beehive for miles, what could possibly be so confusing about this? 

 The Wildman turns toward the beehive. He cocks an arm back. That... that is not what you wanted to see. He sizes up the beehive, tongue out, eyes slimmed. You rush forward, yelling at him, but he's already honed in. He launches a fist and absolutely obliterates the bees. Honeycombs stickily flail around his wrist as though his hairy arm were an impromptu maypole. The Wildman casually walks back down the sand dune. As he nears, you see bees crawling all over his face and stinging away like the pissed off savages that they are, but he doesn't seem to even sense their presence. He holds out the crunchy remains of his honeyed demolition as though he held the heart of a ferocious beast.}
e7e1ccd6ff319b4f0205.translation:
%terrainImage%{你确信，荒野人%wildman%独自在森林里生活时，多少见过几个蜂巢。他哼了一声，指指蜂巢，又指指自己。你点头。他又哼一声，爬上沙丘，朝树走去，你则留在安全的距离外看着。站到蜂巢下方后，他拢起手掌对着嘴，又叫了一声，确保你听得见，再次指向蜂巢。你又点头，用力朝蜂巢比划。方圆几里就这么一个蜂巢，这有什么好弄不明白的？ 

 荒野人转向蜂巢，把一条胳膊往后一抡。那……那可不是你想看的。他伸出舌头，眯起眼，瞄准蜂巢。你赶忙冲过去大喊，可他已经锁定了目标。一拳轰出，蜂巢顿时稀烂。黏糊糊的巢片缠在他手腕上晃来晃去，仿佛那条毛茸茸的胳膊临时成了挂满彩带的五月柱。荒野人若无其事地走下沙丘。等他靠近，你看见蜜蜂爬得他满脸都是，正像一群暴怒的蛮子般拼命蜇他，他却似乎根本感觉不到。他递出那堆沾满蜂蜜、碎得脆生生的残骸，仿佛手里捧着一头凶兽的心脏。}

a7194e1d72572202df96.source: Looks like %wildmanfull% wants to go for it.

13552be0676e71c2d5a7.source: Let's go. Nothing good can come of this.

6f74c82f68710c54de31.source: Enjoyed some honey in the desert

d853f4f8bcb80766d91a.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{A sword eater is dancing around a plaza of %townname%. He holds out a blade about as thick as your pinky.%SPEECH_ON%As the Gilder sees me, I will eat this steel!%SPEECH_OFF%The man announces his intent, and follows through promptly: he arches his back, pinches the blade, and glides it into his mouth and onward and inward, his mouth puckering around the steel as though he were slurping noodles. The crowd at first gasps, but then the swallower gives two thumbs up and the onlookers cheer.}
d853f4f8bcb80766d91a.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{一个吞剑艺人在%townname%的广场上蹦跳，亮出一柄约你小指粗细的剑。%SPEECH_ON%请镀金者作证，我要吞下这块钢铁！%SPEECH_OFF%话音刚落，他便兑现了宣告：向后仰身，捏住剑刃，将它送进嘴里，一寸寸继续深入，嘴唇裹住钢铁，活像在吸面条。人群先是惊呼，随后艺人竖起双手拇指，围观者顿时欢呼起来。}

78c313c9e4a8ffc8a7b8.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{You toss the man a few crowns. He pulls out his sword and places its tip upon his pate. The crowd cheers again. Grinning, the man talks as he balances the sword.%SPEECH_ON%I see your banner, Crownling. I'm no warrior, but I am a traveler and well enough speaker. Though I seek to impress for personal gain, I will on occasion make sure to put in a kind word for your company of coin-seeking misfits.%SPEECH_OFF%The swallower throws his arms wide and nods quickly. The blade plummets from his skull and falls deftly into his sheathe at his hip. Again, the crowd roars with delight and you can't help but think this entertainer is a man of his word.}
78c313c9e4a8ffc8a7b8.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{你抛给那人几枚克朗。他抽出剑，将剑尖立在头顶，人群再次欢呼。他咧嘴笑着，一边稳住长剑，一边说话。%SPEECH_ON%克朗客，我记住你们的旗帜了。我不是战士，不过走南闯北，也还算会说话。虽说卖弄本事是为了自己挣钱，但得空时，我一定替你这群为钱奔命的怪人说几句好话。%SPEECH_OFF%吞剑艺人张开双臂，猛地点了下头。长剑从头顶坠下，巧妙地落入腰间的剑鞘。人群又一次爆发出欢呼，你也不由觉得，这艺人应当是个守信的人。}

5dc3dac4e26d6115b198.source: My sword is not so sharp, yet the ladies can't even do that?
5dc3dac4e26d6115b198.translation: 我的“剑”没这么锋利，姑娘们怎么连这都办不到？

e2ba19d6c93a3a76773e.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{You hand %wildman% a few crowns and tell him to tip the entertainer. He grunts and heads over, then you realize that wasn't just any sellsword you beckoned, but %wildman% the wildman! Before you can stop him, he pushes the sword swallower over. There are cries, screams, and blood gargling death throes, but the crowd sweeps in front of the action and blocks the view. The way it is relayed to you is that the blade came out the swallower's front with straps of esophagus or stomach hanging off it. You know this, because the wildman made sure to bring back the sword himself and you had to have it cleaned.

 How exactly he retrieved the blade during those moments of carnage is beyond you, though you imagine he escaped the ferocity of the crowd by sheer will, determination, and complete absence of moral judgments which frightens men of normal sensibilities. You ask a few of the sellswords to hide the wildman away as he'll need to lay low for a while.}
e2ba19d6c93a3a76773e.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{你递给%wildman%几个克朗，让他去给那艺人一点赏钱。他哼了一声便走过去。你这才意识到，刚才随手叫来的可不是随便哪个佣兵，而是荒野人%wildman%！你还来不及阻止，他就把吞剑人推倒了。现场顿时哭喊四起，夹杂着鲜血堵住喉咙的临死咯咯声，但涌上前的人群挡住了你的视线。后来有人告诉你，剑从吞剑人的身体前方穿了出来，上面还挂着几缕食道或胃囊。你知道这话不假，因为荒野人特地把那把剑带了回来，你还得找人把它洗干净。

 他究竟是怎么在那一片血腥混乱中取走剑的，你无从得知。想来他是凭着蛮横的意志、决心，以及那种足以让正常人胆寒的、毫无道德顾忌的劲头，才冲出了愤怒的人群。你叫几个佣兵把荒野人藏起来，他得避避风头。}

006a4f4bb4b5e6780756.source: Good job, but also bad job.

0731892d0892b2bc323f.source: Bravo! Here's a few coins for you.

dadc812a45d6b1e15aa3.source: Bravo! Give that guy a few coins from me, %wildman%.

7011a0dbf9c81e78287a.source: Interesting way to earn a living.
7011a0dbf9c81e78287a.translation: 这谋生的手段倒有意思。

e6f084684c965753b9af.source: Local entertainers spread the word about you
e6f084684c965753b9af.translation: 当地艺人传扬了你的名声

e95bbb6bc99cd82d2afb.source: Rumor is that a local entertainer was killed by one of your men
e95bbb6bc99cd82d2afb.translation: 据传，你的一名部下杀死了当地艺人

b15cc7a9113920881468.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{A man has approached the camp. You leave your tent to find him standing with his hands atop a golden spear, the shaft of which branches out with sharpened points. As threatening as the weapon looks, a pair of water jugs and golden curios have weighted it with other purposes. The man himself throws back a cloak to reveal a very peculiar and pale face that has not a single hair upon the flesh. He introduces himself with flawless articulation.%SPEECH_ON%Hello stranger, my name is Yuchi Eveohtse. I'm looking for two things in these lands, one of which I've come to understand is in your possession. It is a profound text on the nature, no, the existence of death. I believe one of your men has already unlocked a partial set of its mysteries and, at this point, it is of little further use to you.%SPEECH_OFF%%translator% nods, stating that as long as he stares at the pages, he can make nothing more of it and doubts anyone can. Yuchi whistles and you look back at him. The man holds out three fingers.%SPEECH_ON%In exchange for the book, I've one of these to offer: either a golden shield the faithful of these lands call the Gilder's Embrace, my two jugs which, when imbibed, will strengthen a man in ways beyond your imagining, or, being that you are mercenaries, a sum of 50,000 crowns.%SPEECH_OFF%}
b15cc7a9113920881468.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{一个男人来到营地。你走出帐篷，见他双手搭在一杆金色长矛上，矛杆伸出几根尖锐的分枝。这兵器看着虽唬人，上面却挂着两只水壶和一些金色小玩意，兼作了别的用途。男人掀开斗篷，露出一张极其古怪、苍白且没有一丝毛发的脸。他吐字清晰，做起了自我介绍。%SPEECH_ON%你好，陌生人。我叫尤奇·埃沃茨。我在这片土地上寻找两样东西，据我所知，其中一样就在你手中。那是一本论述死亡本质——不，论述死亡之存在的深奥著作。我想，你的一位手下已经解开了其中一部分奥秘，而到了这一步，它对你们便没什么进一步的用处了。%SPEECH_OFF%%translator%点头，说自己无论盯着书页看多久，都再也读不出更多东西，也不相信别人能做到。尤奇吹了声口哨，你回头看他。男人竖起三根手指。%SPEECH_ON%作为交换，我可以让你从三样报酬中选一样：一面金色盾牌，此地的信徒称它为“镀金者的拥抱”；我的这两只水壶，喝下其中的东西，便能获得超乎你想象的力量；或者，既然你们是佣兵，就给你们50,000克朗。%SPEECH_OFF%}

b3a6f3ec426977ed5be4.source: We trade the book for the golden shield.

c1573c9dde541f816d5e.source: We trade the book for the two jugs.
c1573c9dde541f816d5e.translation: 用这本书换那两罐东西。

a5068b751f282fda189d.source: We trade the book for 50,000 crowns.

5601bce5ef0e9c2328c6.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{A man has approached the camp. You leave your tent to find him standing with his hands atop a golden spear, the shaft of which branches out with sharpened points. As threatening as the weapon looks, a pair of water jugs and golden curios have weighted it with other purposes. The man himself throws back a cloak to reveal a very peculiar and pale face that has not a single hair upon the flesh. He introduces himself with flawless articulation.%SPEECH_ON%Hello stranger, my name is Yuchi Eveohtse. I'm looking for two things in these lands, one of which I've come to understand is in your possession. It is a profound text on the nature, no, the existence of death.%SPEECH_OFF%The man holds out three fingers.%SPEECH_ON%In exchange for the book, I've one of these to offer: either a golden shield the faithful of these lands call the Gilder's Embrace, my two jugs which, when imbibed, will strengthen a man in ways beyond your imagining, or, being that you are mercenaries, a sum of 50,000 crowns.%SPEECH_OFF%}
5601bce5ef0e9c2328c6.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{一个男人来到营地。你走出帐篷，见他双手搭在一杆金色长矛上，矛杆伸出几根尖锐的分枝。这兵器看着虽唬人，上面却挂着两只水壶和一些金色小玩意，兼作了别的用途。男人掀开斗篷，露出一张极其古怪、苍白且没有一丝毛发的脸。他吐字清晰，做起了自我介绍。%SPEECH_ON%你好，陌生人。我叫尤奇·埃沃茨。我在这片土地上寻找两样东西，据我所知，其中一样就在你手中。那是一本论述死亡本质——不，论述死亡之存在的深奥著作。%SPEECH_OFF%男人竖起三根手指。%SPEECH_ON%作为交换，我可以让你从三样报酬中选一样：一面金色盾牌，此地的信徒称它为“镀金者的拥抱”；我的这两只水壶，喝下其中的东西，便能获得超乎你想象的力量；或者，既然你们是佣兵，就给你们50,000克朗。%SPEECH_OFF%}

d34f8017ce040c217dd9.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{Yuchi bows for the briefest moment and when he stands he is holding a shield. At first glance, it appears to be nothing more than steel with ornate gildings around the edges, but suddenly an orb of yellow light cycles around the outer rim, dancing around and around.%SPEECH_ON%They call it the Gilder's Embrace for the God's very divinity is said to be partitioned within its framing. See, if you were to turn this against your enemies, the light would grow to such blinding rays that your foes shall not see. And as you can tell, the light now is dull, for we are not enemies, stranger.%SPEECH_OFF%The man holds out his hand. You give him the book, and he gives you the shield. He does not even stare at the book, simply stows it away and gathers up his spear. You ask him what he intends to do with the text. He smiles.%SPEECH_ON%Who knows. Maybe I will simply return it, hm? Or maybe not.%SPEECH_OFF%}
d34f8017ce040c217dd9.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{尤奇短暂地鞠了一躬，直起身时，手中已多了一面盾。乍看不过是面钢盾，边缘饰有精美镀金纹样，可忽然间，一团黄色光球沿盾缘游走，循环不息。%SPEECH_ON%人们称它为“镀金者的拥抱”，据说盾框中寄存着那位神明的一缕神性。只要将它朝向敌人，光便会化作耀眼射线，让对方无法视物。而您也看到了，此刻光芒柔和，因为我们并非敌人，陌生人。%SPEECH_OFF%他伸出手。你交出书，他便将盾交给你。他连看也没看那书，径自收起，拿上长矛。你问他打算拿书做什么，他微微一笑。%SPEECH_ON%谁知道呢。也许只是把它还回去，嗯？也许不会。%SPEECH_OFF%}

d706d943bce7b67bd0a8.source: What was the second thing you came for?
d706d943bce7b67bd0a8.translation: 你此行的第二件事是什么？

3cb25b41ad9cb535f88a.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{Yuchi tips his gilded spear forward. It sharpness is incredible, like something a blacksmith may dream of but never manifest by any mortal hand. The pair of jugs slide off and he catches them by their straps and holds them out. You give him the book and he lets go of the jugs. Not wanting to be poisoned, you ask that he take a drink of both jugs which he does so willingly. Wiping his mouth, he nods.%SPEECH_ON%I'm quite partial to its flavors and its effects, please do not waste anymore of it on your suspicions and hesitancies.%SPEECH_OFF%The man stows the book somewhere into his cloak, picks up his gear, and begins to walk away. You ask what he plans to do with the text. He smiles.%SPEECH_ON%Who knows. Maybe I will simply return it, hm? Or maybe not.%SPEECH_OFF%}
3cb25b41ad9cb535f88a.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{尤奇将镀金长矛向前一倾。矛尖锋锐得不可思议，仿佛是铁匠梦寐以求、凡人双手却永远造不出的东西。两只壶滑下来，他抓住系带，将壶递出。你把书交给他，他便松手交出壶。你不想中毒，要求他每壶都喝一口，他欣然照办。擦过嘴，他点头说道。%SPEECH_ON%我很喜欢它的滋味与功效，还请别再因疑虑和犹豫浪费它了。%SPEECH_OFF%那人将书藏进斗篷，拿好行装，转身离开。你问他打算拿书做什么，他微微一笑。%SPEECH_ON%谁知道呢。也许只是把它还回去，嗯？也许不会。%SPEECH_OFF%}

451c5dd4b6cae745fcff.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{Yuchi nods.%SPEECH_ON%Give me the book and bring me your warchest.%SPEECH_OFF%You throw him the text and then have the company's treasury brought before the man. He holds out both arms of his cloaks and slowly tips them forward. Crowns stream out of the sleeves seemingly without end and then on an instant the man tips both arms up.%SPEECH_ON%Your %reward% crowns should be there.%SPEECH_OFF%You have the coin counted and it is the exact amount. You look up to say he's quite lucky, but the man is already picking up his things and preparing to leave.%SPEECH_ON%Take care, stranger.%SPEECH_OFF%Before he goes, you ask what he plans to do with the text. He smiles.%SPEECH_ON%Who knows. Maybe I will simply return it, hm? Or maybe not.%SPEECH_OFF%}
451c5dd4b6cae745fcff.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{尤奇点点头。%SPEECH_ON%把书给我，再把你们装钱的箱子搬来。%SPEECH_OFF%你把书抛给他，又让人把战团的钱箱抬到面前。他伸出罩在斗篷下的双臂，缓缓向下倾斜。克朗便从袖口里源源不断地流出，仿佛永无止境。随后，他忽然抬起双臂。%SPEECH_ON%你要的%reward%克朗，应该都在这里了。%SPEECH_OFF%你让人点过钱，数目分毫不差。你抬头想说他蒙得真准，他却已经在收拾东西准备离开。%SPEECH_ON%保重，陌生人。%SPEECH_OFF%临走前，你问他打算拿这本书做什么。他微微一笑。%SPEECH_ON%谁知道呢。也许只是把它还回去，嗯？也许不会。%SPEECH_OFF%}

eec858cdd4f75aa49c4b.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{Yuchi turns around.%SPEECH_ON%Hm?%SPEECH_OFF%You explain that he said he had come to these lands looking for two things. One was the book, what was the other? He smiles.%SPEECH_ON%There is a town in these parts by the name of Dagentear. The town is no more, but something that lived there still wanders. A being they call the 'Wight.' I wish to find it and speak with it.%SPEECH_OFF%When you ask for more information he simply parts with a graceful bow.%SPEECH_ON%Thank you for your gentle dealings, stranger.%SPEECH_OFF%}
eec858cdd4f75aa49c4b.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_174.png[/img]{尤奇转过身。%SPEECH_ON%嗯？%SPEECH_OFF%你解释，他说过来此地寻找两样东西，一样是书，另一样是什么？他笑了。%SPEECH_ON%这一带有座叫Dagentear的镇子。镇子已经没了，可曾住在那里的一样东西仍在游荡。人们叫它“尸妖”。我想找到它，和它谈谈。%SPEECH_OFF%你再追问，他却只是优雅地鞠躬告别。%SPEECH_ON%陌生人，多谢你以礼相待。%SPEECH_OFF%}

6ae3cbd7ac8af87b5e7b.source: I hope we did the right thing giving him that book...
6ae3cbd7ac8af87b5e7b.translation: 但愿把书交给他是对的……

b1e695e093f3f8ba73c3.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{You come across a man wandering the desert with a family of younger men by his side. He welcomes you to a campfire and asks if you'd like to hear tales of the desert and of the south in general.}
b1e695e093f3f8ba73c3.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_171.png[/img]{你遇见一个在沙漠中行走的男人，身旁跟着一群年轻家人。他邀你在篝火旁坐下，问你想不想听些关于沙漠与南方的故事。}

9c483f0f5576d61f8bfd.source: Happy to join you at the campfire.
9c483f0f5576d61f8bfd.translation: 很乐意和你一起围火歇息。

8f51e72f44cb494f6e6d.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]{The man goes on to talk about the Ancient Empire - at least what he is aware of it.%SPEECH_ON%It's hard to say exactly what it was, you know? And it is hard to say what exactly came before. I had gotten a glimpse into the libraries of %randomcitystate% and was rather astonished and what I was able to find. You know what the oldest texts we have are? Ancient texts. Do you know what these ancient texts write about? Other ancient texts. We have no idea how far back our timeline really goes. We just exist in the here and now, and perhaps one day in the future our progeny will come to find that we are the mystery, and those that were mysteries to us?%SPEECH_OFF%He scissors his fingers through the air.%SPEECH_ON%Gone.%SPEECH_OFF% | He prods the campfire with an iron poker.%SPEECH_ON%They say that the Ifrits are manifestations of man's cruelty. That when we are evil to one another there is a force, some unseen force, which we are pressing against. When we attack and slaughter on a larger scale, this force is bent across the entire seam, but when we do ill against one individual, to such horrible ends, it is when this force snaps. And a hole is made, and out of that hole comes a correction. A correction which we call the Ifrit. A correction that will seek to make amends, by literally mending these invisible forces with the corpses of those who dared to open them in the first place.%SPEECH_OFF%The man sets the iron poker aside. He smiles somberly.%SPEECH_ON%So it is said, anyway.%SPEECH_OFF% | Despite being an old man, he crosses his legs with the limberness and agility of a younger fellow. He's no doubt sat before many a campfire. He speaks as warmly as the flames before you.%SPEECH_ON%I've been around these sands for many summers. But my sons, who I have outlasted, I must sadly say, they would ask, how do we go on about telling the time from one season to the next? To which marker do we signify the years?%SPEECH_OFF%A wrinkly finger is raised, and it points further above. He winks at you.%SPEECH_ON%The stars. They wheel across the sky in patterns one can recognize if one is willing to pay attention. I also imagine that those stars may be beings of another aether, another unimaginable place. Perhaps somewhere we will go when we die, but this is hearsay, of course, and just between us musing travelers, yes?%SPEECH_OFF% | The man sips at a drink from a cup of unknown make and material. He smells the drink and sips it again before setting it down and stretching out.%SPEECH_ON%You know, I somewhat look forward to the end of my Gilded path. It has been good to me, all these years, but I can tell that I stride between the withers of this horrible world and the sooner I can make my leave the better. I have the notion that if I stick around too long then the world is going to find out I slipped by, receipt in hand, and have been getting away with a good life while I supposedly got suffering on the docket.%SPEECH_OFF%You ask him why he thinks this. He shrugs.%SPEECH_ON%Instinct. You got it too, Crownling, this I have no doubt. After all, how do you make it so far when others, just like you, trundle into terrors and horrors and, eventually, death? There's a ticker somewhere in this world, a great accountant, perhaps it is the Gilder, perhaps it is something else, but life is not meant for unending good. At some point, eventually, there's gonna be one big, bad moment.%SPEECH_OFF% | Once you settle down, the old man leans back as though you were an old friend and begins to talk.%SPEECH_ON%It's interesting to me to see you here, Crownling, dressed in the regalia of brigandage as it were. Here are, simple men in simple times. But I take it you're as aware of a much greater past as I am. The sense that there was a long, long time of events that came before us.%SPEECH_OFF%You nod. It seems obvious. The man nods back.%SPEECH_ON%That is good. It shows an inquisitive nature to your side, even just in recognizing that there was much that walked these sands before us both. Many... many do not even take this into consideration. They live in the here and now. In some ways, I envy them. How it must be to exist as oneself and only oneself with the whole world beneath your feet.%SPEECH_OFF%He lays back and stares up at the sky.%SPEECH_ON%I think most people don't really believe they'll die.%SPEECH_OFF% | You set down and the old man leans back with a book in hand that is part scrolls and part binding. He reads, occasionally looking up. You have no idea if he's speaking from the text or if his nature is capable of holding two different studies at once.%SPEECH_ON%Did you know how it is the Ancient Empire was felled? They say it was a great blast from the earth itself.%SPEECH_OFF%He mimics with his hands an explosion from the sands.%SPEECH_ON%A volcano. But that seems far too simple, doesn't it? One volcano wipes out the entire empire?%SPEECH_OFF%You remark that the best sellsword you have could be crippled with a small nick to the back of his heels. No longer able to walk well, turn, pivot, or put weight on his feet, he'd fall apart from the bottom up. The old man stares at you.%SPEECH_ON%Hmm, that may be right then. Perhaps this volcano obliterated what little grasp this empire had on its own control. After that... who knows what happened. Chaos, presumably. That sweet little thing.%SPEECH_OFF% | You set down and the man begins to speak almost immediately.%SPEECH_ON%I've heard rumors of a cult running about. Something about 'Davkul'. Well, I will say this: they're an earnest sort by the sounds of it.%SPEECH_OFF%You ask if he has any knowledge beyond just rumors. He shrugs.%SPEECH_ON%Only that is a cult of death and it did not originate here. At least, you'll never hear a southerner admit to this Davkul creation starting here. No, no, must have been those scoundrels to the north to come up with such a gruesome idea as this death god.%SPEECH_OFF%He grins whimsically. You take it he has no real skin in the game with this topic and only threw it out there to see your response. | %SPEECH_ON%Yes yes, have a seat already.%SPEECH_OFF%You sit down and the man begins speaking immediately.%SPEECH_ON%One of the strange natures of the desert is that will both preserve and erase all things. Do you understand what I mean? If you were to die, the sands would swallow you whole, but you, your body, would never really disappear. It would be submerged. If we were to start clawing our way into the desert around us we would surely find bodies and treasures and some say even entire cities.%SPEECH_OFF%You wave off the notion, but the man raises a finger.%SPEECH_ON%Tsk tsk tsk, don't be so dismissive, Crownling. This is a hungry world and, may my path be Gilded, it is entirely possible that all these cities we know today will soon be gone.%SPEECH_OFF%}
8f51e72f44cb494f6e6d.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]{那人继续谈起远古帝国，至少，是他所知的那些。%SPEECH_ON%很难说清，它究竟是什么样，你懂吗？更难说清，在它之前又有什么。我有幸翻阅过%randomcitystate%的藏书，发现的东西着实令我震惊。你知道，我们现存最古老的文献是什么吗？古代文献。而那些古代文献写的又是什么？更古老的文献。我们根本不知道，历史能往前追溯多久。我们只活在此时此刻。也许未来某天，子孙会发现，我们成了谜。而那些对我们而言已是谜的存在呢？%SPEECH_OFF%他用两根手指在空中做了个剪断的动作。%SPEECH_ON%没了。%SPEECH_OFF% | 他用铁钎拨弄篝火。%SPEECH_ON%听说，沙魔是人类残酷之心的显化。我们彼此作恶时，会压迫某种力量，一种看不见的力量。大规模进攻、屠戮，会让这力量沿着整道接缝弯曲；可若把极其可怕的恶行，全施在一个人身上，这力量就会绷断。于是，破口出现，从中走出一种修补。我们称这种修补为沙魔。它会来弥合裂隙，真正拿那些胆敢撕开无形力量之人的尸体，把缺口补起来。%SPEECH_OFF%那人放下铁钎，露出沉静的笑。%SPEECH_ON%反正，传说是这么讲的。%SPEECH_OFF% | 虽然年老，他盘起双腿时，却仍像年轻人般柔韧敏捷。想必，他已坐过无数篝火旁。说话的语气，也如眼前火焰一般温暖。%SPEECH_ON%我在这片沙地，度过了许多个夏天。我的儿子们——遗憾的是，他们都走在了我前头——曾问，我们怎么分辨时节轮换？又该凭什么标记岁月？%SPEECH_OFF%一根皱巴巴的手指抬起，指向更高处。他朝你眨眼。%SPEECH_ON%星辰。只要肯留心，就能认出它们巡行天空的规律。我也常想，那些星星也许是另一个天界、另一个无法想象之地的生灵。也许，我们死后会去那里。不过，当然，这只是传言，只是咱们两个爱胡思乱想的旅人私下聊聊，对吧？%SPEECH_OFF% | 那人从一只材质、制法都不明的杯中抿了一口，闻闻饮料，又抿一口，才放下杯子，舒展身体。%SPEECH_ON%你知道，我有些期待走到镀金之路的尽头。这些年，它待我不薄，可我感觉，自己正从这可怖世界的肩背之间偷偷经过，越早离开越好。总觉得，若逗留太久，世界就会发现，我拿着凭据溜了过去，明明账上记着该受苦，却一直偷享着好日子。%SPEECH_OFF%你问，为何这样想。他耸肩。%SPEECH_ON%直觉。克朗客，你也有，我毫不怀疑。不然，与你相仿的人都踉跄着走进恐惧、惨剧，最终走向死亡，你又凭什么走到这么远？世间某处，有个记账的，一位大账房。也许是镀金者，也许是别的什么，可人生并不是注定永远顺遂的。总有一天，总有一个时候，会遇上一次真正的大灾祸。%SPEECH_OFF% | 你刚坐稳，老人便向后一靠，仿佛面对一位老友，开始谈天。%SPEECH_ON%克朗客，在这里见到你，穿着这一身仿佛劫匪的行头，让我觉得有趣。我们只是寻常时世里的寻常人。可我想，你和我一样，知道曾有过远比眼下宏大的过去。知道在我们之前，已经发生过漫长、漫长岁月里的许多事。%SPEECH_OFF%你点头，这似乎显而易见。老人也点头回应。%SPEECH_ON%很好。哪怕只是承认，在我们踏上沙地前，已有许多生灵走过，也能说明你有一颗好奇的心。许多人……许多人连这都不曾想过。他们只活在当下。有些时候，我真羡慕他们。只作为自己而存在，也仅仅是自己，脚下却是整个世界，那会是什么滋味？%SPEECH_OFF%他躺下，仰望天空。%SPEECH_ON%我想，大多数人并不真相信，自己会死。%SPEECH_OFF% | 你坐下，老人向后靠着，手里拿着一本半像卷轴、半像装订书的东西。他读着，偶尔抬头。你不知道，他是在念书上的话，还是天生便能同时思索两个问题。%SPEECH_ON%你知道远古帝国是怎么灭亡的吗？听说，是大地本身的一次猛烈爆发。%SPEECH_OFF%他用双手比画出沙地炸开的模样。%SPEECH_ON%火山。可这未免太简单了，不是吗？一座火山，就毁了整个帝国？%SPEECH_OFF%你说，手下最好的佣兵，也可能因脚跟后面一道小伤而残废。从此走不稳、转不了身、挪不开步，双脚也撑不住重量，整个人便从根基开始垮掉。老人望着你。%SPEECH_ON%嗯，也许是这样。或许，那座火山摧毁了帝国对自身仅存的一点掌控。之后……谁知道呢。大概是混乱吧，那甜美的小东西。%SPEECH_OFF% | 你刚坐下，老人几乎立刻开口。%SPEECH_ON%听说有个教派在四处活动，叫什么“达夫库尔”。嗯，我只能说，听起来是些很认真的人。%SPEECH_OFF%你问，除了传言，他是否还知道别的。他耸肩。%SPEECH_ON%只知道他们崇拜死亡，而且不是从这里起源的。至少，绝不会有南方人承认，达夫库尔这套东西起源于此。不，不，肯定是北边那些坏种，才想得出死亡之神这么可怕的主意。%SPEECH_OFF%他露出俏皮的笑。你觉得，他对这个话题并无切身利害，不过是随口一提，想看你的反应。 | %SPEECH_ON%是，是，快坐吧。%SPEECH_OFF%你一坐下，老人便立即开口。%SPEECH_ON%沙漠有个奇妙的本性，它既保存万物，也抹去万物。懂我的意思吗？若你死了，沙子会把你整个吞下，可你，你的身体，其实从不会真正消失，只是被埋住。若我们开始挖掘四周的沙漠，一定能找到尸体、宝藏，甚至有人说，还有整座城市。%SPEECH_OFF%你挥手表示不信，老人却竖起一根手指。%SPEECH_ON%啧，啧，啧，克朗客，别这么不当回事。这是个饥饿的世界，愿我的道路得以镀金。如今我们熟知的所有城市，很可能不久后就全没了。%SPEECH_OFF%}

ceacf51419e69603f8e8.source: May your path be ever gilded.

e9bf3763ad31e76f6fb7.source:
{[img]gfx/ui/events/event_05.png[/img]{%anatomist% is sitting near to the campfire. Almost too close. You pull him back a ways so he doesn't burn himself. He looks up, his face dotted with pustules and slathered in the grease of ones which have already popped.%SPEECH_ON%I'm beginning to wonder if I made a great mistake in drinking that potion.%SPEECH_OFF%He scoots back toward the flames, and there's a sense in his eyes that he wants to pitch himself into it. You can't do much for him, mostly because he looks awfully gross at the moment and you'd rather not touch him again. | You find %anatomist% standing beside the company wagon with a sleeve unfurled and his finger picking at some strange markings there. Curious, you ask if they are birthmarks. The anatomist turns, shaking his head. He lifts up his shirt to show that these markings are all over his body, mottling the flesh with unsightly colors which look rough to the touch, like scabs that cannot be peeled.%SPEECH_ON%The potion I drank did this and I know not what to with myself.%SPEECH_OFF%You nod and tell him it'll surely get better. He sighs and simply lowers his shirt and looks away. | %anatomist% stands over a bucket of water, looking at his darkened reflection in it. He sighs. You ask how he is doing, and he turns to reveal horrific rashes and boils upon his skin.%SPEECH_ON%I am not doing so well, to be honest. The concoction I imbibed seems to have had a gravely ill-effect on me, though I am being perhaps a little giving with my vocabulary there. I will survive, but it has wounded me in ways that are not just of the skin and the body, but of the mind. I thought myself distanced from such matters, but now, seeing my horrible face...I am in a state of perpetual unease.%SPEECH_OFF%You grab his shoulder and give it a squeeze, then pat him on the back and make some recommendations like he should drink some water and of course to not feel bad. You weren't ever that great at consoling other men, much less ones suffering from terrible maladies sprung from scientific madness. | %anatomist% the anatomist is in a despondent state. The potion he made, and was in such a hurry to drink, has resulted in his entire body being overcome with maladies ranging from rashes to boils to what appear to be unusual spasms and plenty of snot from the nose. You assure him that he will get better, but his horrific appearance is taking a toll on him. | The strange concoctions %anatomist% the anatomist has been making, are strange concoctions that he has also been drinking. Unsurprisingly, the effects have not been good: rashes, infections, smells, hair falling out, and more. While on the outside he proclaims that what he is doing is in the name of science, you can tell that all these maladies and disfigurations are debilitating to the man's morale. You can only hope he gets better with time. | Matters of science, which are far outside your understanding, always do seem to come with risks. You remember as a child that your friend took the risk of swinging out on a rope into a river, and by happenstance you all found out just how much weight a branch can hold while in the throes of Fall.

Now, it seems %anatomist% the anatomist is finding out the debilitating nature of drinking one of his bizarre potions. He is overwhelmed with rashes and infections, and for some reason he is a siren to ants, who for who knows what reason now love to crawl on him at all hours of day and night. Hopefully, with time, these maladies will depart, and hopefully take the damned ants with them. | You always knew the anatomists to be a bit wrong in the head, but the way they've been creating potions and drinking them has really floored you. Water alone can be poisonous if sipped from the wrong cup, nevermind wholesale concoctions which are distilled in the mire of whatever scientific notions the anatomists are carrying that day. Naturally, it isn't long until one of the eggheads, %anatomist%, falls ill. He is still capable of moving and day-to-day tasks, but the giant warts and leaking pustules makes him a horror to look at, and though he may see himself distanced from society, you've little doubt that walking around looking like a rag that's mopped up pigshite is healthy for the mind and spirit.
