The horse owner springs to his feet.%SPEECH_ON%Well shit, sir, we was just gonna whip him good. Why'd you go and kill him for?%SPEECH_OFF%He pauses then waves a dismissive hand.%SPEECH_ON%Shit. Shit, man. Well, alright. We'll just all depart in our own way and say nothing of what happened here. Ain't that right fellas?%SPEECH_OFF%The rest of the men nod.%SPEECH_ON%'Course. I ain't ruining my life over some filly fiddler. Good going, sellsword, stupid sword swingin' sumbitch.%SPEECH_OFF%
56be6fd6b2a1b8484d27.translation: %terrainImage%你拔出刀，割断绳索，把那人放了下来。他却头朝下摔在地上，脖子发出令人牙酸的脆响，当场折断。身体随之塌下，双腿别扭地翻压在自己胸前。这姿势，恐怕连他这性癖古怪的家伙也没尝试过。马主人腾地站起身。%SPEECH_ON%见鬼，先生，咱们不过想狠狠抽他一顿，你干吗直接把人杀了？%SPEECH_OFF%他顿了顿，随即挥手作罢。%SPEECH_ON%操，真他妈的。好吧，咱们各走各的，谁也别提这里发生的事。对吧，伙计们？%SPEECH_OFF%其他人纷纷点头。%SPEECH_ON%当然。为了个糟蹋母马的家伙，犯不着把自己一辈子搭进去。干得好啊，佣兵，你这个只会乱挥剑的蠢货。%SPEECH_OFF%

1329e0fc77b498a9afb3.source: %terrainImage%%flagellant% steps forward and takes the horse owner's whip. He bends it and runs the leather through his hands. Nodding, he calls it a 'fine tool' for a good whipping, but that the men were going about it 'all the wrong way.' He points at the wounds on the man's back.%SPEECH_ON%See these streaks? They're thin and barely opened. Don't let the amount of blood fool you, these are superficial. Here, let me show you a good hiding.%SPEECH_OFF%The flagellant drop the whip's strings, twirls them around for a moment, then strikes. The hanging man cries out. A wound opens and gapes from the tip of one rib clear across his back to the tip of another. You can see the muscle and fat bubbling beneath. %flagellant% strikes again, and again, and again. Blood splashes the flagellant as he works and the horse-porker has long since passed out. Eventually, one of the men gets to his feet and takes the whip back.%SPEECH_ON%Th-that's enough. You fellas get on and go, alright? Farkin' hell...%SPEECH_OFF%Another man cuts the filly fiddler down and tends to his new, quite serious wounds. %flagellant% wipes his brow and admires his handiwork.%SPEECH_ON%Mmhmm, that's how it's done.%SPEECH_OFF%
1329e0fc77b498a9afb3.translation: %terrainImage%%flagellant%走上前，接过马主人的鞭子，折了折，又让皮条从手中滑过。他点头，说这是件适合施鞭的“好工具”，可这些人的用法“全错了”。他指着那人背上的伤。%SPEECH_ON%看见这些印子了吗？又细又浅，皮肉几乎没破。别被血多骗了，这都是皮外伤。来，我让你们看看，什么才叫挨顿好打。%SPEECH_OFF%苦修者垂下鞭梢，转了几圈，随即挥出。被吊着的人惨叫起来，背上裂开一道豁口，从一侧肋骨尖横贯到另一侧，下面的肌肉和脂肪都翻了出来。%flagellant%又抽一鞭，再一鞭，再一鞭。鲜血溅到苦修者身上，那个亵弄母马的家伙早已昏了过去。终于，一人站起来，夺回鞭子。%SPEECH_ON%够、够了。你们走吧，继续赶路，好不好？他娘的……%SPEECH_OFF%另一人割断绳索，将那家伙放下来，照料起他新添的重伤。%flagellant%擦擦额头，欣赏自己的手艺。%SPEECH_ON%嗯哼，这才叫对路。%SPEECH_OFF%

a7b820f9c0144ec5ad77.source: %terrainImage%%butcher% asks if the horse is still around. Its owner nods.%SPEECH_ON%Aye, freshly dead, freshly soiled by that prick. Why?%SPEECH_OFF%The butcher asks if he can take it off his hands. The owner shrugs.%SPEECH_ON%Yours if you want it. Though you'd best be careful cutting around the bits he touched with his own bits.%SPEECH_OFF%Before anymore can be said, %butcher% has the man take him to the horse corpse to, well, butcher it. The company gets some questionable meat to eat.
a7b820f9c0144ec5ad77.translation: %terrainImage%%butcher%问那匹马还在不在。马主人点头。%SPEECH_ON%在，刚死，也刚被那混账糟蹋过。怎么？%SPEECH_OFF%屠夫问能否把马交给他。主人耸肩。%SPEECH_ON%想要就拿去。不过他拿自己的家伙碰过的地方，下刀时可得留神。%SPEECH_OFF%话还没说完，%butcher%已让主人领他去找马尸，准备……宰肉。战团因此添了些令人起疑的口粮。

5a15d2274fe4100e4858.source: Not sure I want that in our stocks.
5a15d2274fe4100e4858.translation: 我可不确定要不要把那东西放进我们的储备里。

a6bff6b07549fcca0f93.source: %flagellantfull%, you look like you have something on your mind.

330c01cebd12cbdc90cd.source: You found %name% being whipped for 'involving' himself with a dead horse. Hopefully that past is, er, behind him now.
330c01cebd12cbdc90cd.translation: 你遇见%name%时，他正因与一匹死马有了些“瓜葛”而挨鞭子。只盼那段过去如今真的，呃，被他抛在身后了。

70582b508f88ed521a3f.source: Satisfied his needs with a dead horse
70582b508f88ed521a3f.translation: 拿一匹死马满足了自己的欲望

1036a365bd1392e93e45.source: Put his unique skills to good use
1036a365bd1392e93e45.translation: 让独门本领派上了用场

99ed73f3c8531cc653d8.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]During a short rest, your men managed to catch a man that tried to make off with some of your supplies. His clothes are but rags and he looks more skeleton than man. What are you going to do with him?
99ed73f3c8531cc653d8.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]短暂休息时，弟兄们抓住了一个想偷走物资的人。他衣服破得只剩布条，形销骨立，比起人，更像一副骷髅。你打算如何处置他？

e16d0b2b9d98cc211ef1.source: Give that poor guy some food and water.
e16d0b2b9d98cc211ef1.translation: 给这可怜人一点吃的和水。

7cb1cef070b73082996e.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]Under the cloak of night some thief managed to nick some of your supplies. He will probably offer them back to you in the next settlement...
7cb1cef070b73082996e.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]有个贼趁着夜色偷走了你们的一些物资。到了下一个聚落，说不定他就会把东西再卖给你……

05af48195b1637828f3d.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]%randombrother% gives the thief a proper beating with a short cane. The shaft lands viciously hard and you can hear the sound of the blows passing through the man's almost hollow frame. He wilts and turns and tries hard to get away, but the sellsword is persistent in meting out the punishment. When it's all said and done, you leave the beaten man behind, wimpering and clutching the dirt between his frail fingers.
05af48195b1637828f3d.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]%randombrother%拿短棍狠狠教训了盗贼一顿。每一下都打得凶，声音穿过那副几乎空空的骨架。他蜷缩、扭动，拼命想躲，可佣兵始终不肯停手。惩罚结束，你们把挨打的人留在原地，任他呜咽着，用纤弱的手指抓紧泥土。

a07940860b1de030da95.source: Let this be a lesson to you!

c023002eaecea82ed732.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]Feeling bad for the feeble man, you decide to give him some water and food. He almost snatches the meal away from you and drives his famished face into it. The thief thanks you between every bite.
c023002eaecea82ed732.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]你可怜这个虚弱的人，决定给他一些水和食物。他几乎是从你手里抢过饭，立刻埋头狼吞虎咽，每吃一口，都要道一声谢。

34be2555b9d43b76e88d.source: Not everyone will be this lenient...
34be2555b9d43b76e88d.translation: 可不是谁都这么宽宏大量……

faba72ff43c31f52c60e.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img] You tell the men to get back to marching. The thief wipes his mouth and stands up, wobbling as his weak legs take a few steps after you. He asks if maybe he could join the company. He'll give his life for you, if he must, just anything to not have to steal anymore.
faba72ff43c31f52c60e.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]你叫弟兄们继续行军。盗贼抹抹嘴，站起身，虚弱的双腿摇晃着跟了几步，问自己能否加入战团。只要不用再偷东西，叫他做什么都行，必要时，他愿为你卖命。

8b2502ce0faf8ef11701.source: Well, fine, you might as well join us.

5dc779a9405bb3d0e21b.source: We need fighting men, not underfed thieves.
5dc779a9405bb3d0e21b.translation: 我们需要能打的人，不需要饿得半死的贼。

dd0782d12910041625b1.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]As the thief cowers, you draw your sword. He begs for mercy as his mirrored face ripples over the blade's fuller and edges. You raise the weapon. The man screams out that he'll work for you, that he'll work for free, anything to spare his life. You hesitate, your sword still lingering in the air.
dd0782d12910041625b1.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]盗贼瑟缩着，你拔出剑。他哀求饶命，脸映在剑槽与刃口上，扭曲晃动。你举起武器，他尖叫着说愿替你做事，分文不取也行，只求活命。你迟疑了，剑仍悬在半空。

d957862ff89a0372fd91.source: Die with some dignity at last.

85717d5ac052e5b96725.source: Fine. I'll spare your life  if you work for me.
85717d5ac052e5b96725.translation: 好，你替我做事，我就饶你一命。

7c0cef5fc5f2255097b2.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%The punishment for thievery is death.%SPEECH_OFF%You plunge the sword down, cutting off the thief's last words with a quick stab into his chest. He seizes up, speechless save for the scratching of his thin hands grabbing that which is killing him, and then he falls back, dead within moment. You retrieve your weapon and clean it off in the nook of your elbow. The dead man's head turns to a side as blood pools quietly beneath him.
7c0cef5fc5f2255097b2.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_33.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%偷盗者，死。%SPEECH_OFF%你一剑向下刺入盗贼胸口，截断了他的遗言。他浑身僵住，再也说不出话，只有干瘦的双手抓挠着夺命剑锋的声音。随后，他向后倒下，片刻便断了气。你抽回武器，夹在臂弯擦净。死者的头歪向一旁，鲜血在身下悄悄汇成一滩。

56f80b5795e9ee5ebcf2.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_05.png[/img]You lower your weapon and the man crawls to you and hugs your legs. He kisses your feet until you draw away.

To get things straight, you give him a long list of orders and how it is to work in the company. You also give him a contract which he signs with a jagged 'x'. A few of the brothers then spend the rest of the day teaching him the ropes and introducing him to the rest of the company. By night's end, it seems like he's already beginning to fit in. By next morning, you wake to see a great number of supplies are missing and the new man is nowhere in sight. It appears that, although you stayed the thief's execution, he went on ahead and stole things anyway. Let that be a lesson to you.
56f80b5795e9ee5ebcf2.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_05.png[/img]你放低武器，那人便爬过来抱住你的双腿，不停亲吻你的脚，直到你抽身避开。

为了把规矩讲清，你详细说明了命令与纪律，以及在战团里该如何行事。你还给他一份契约，他用一个歪扭的叉号签了名。接下来一整天，几个弟兄都在教他熟悉差事，领他认识其他人。夜深时，他似乎已经开始融入战团。可到了第二天早晨，你醒来却发现大批物资不翼而飞，新人也没了踪影。看来，你虽饶了这个贼的性命，他却照偷不误。这下你可该长记性了。

0394b3341918cd86ca2b.source: Felt for a thief killed by you

3aba15ec2f96fb7406db.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_19.png[/img]While training, %clumsyguy%, not being the most dexterous fellow, manages to hurt himself with his own weapon.
3aba15ec2f96fb7406db.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_19.png[/img]训练时，手脚不怎么灵巧的%clumsyguy%竟被自己的武器弄伤了。

3c6257d6b8c25819e849.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]Traveling, you like to keep your men fresh with the occasional training exercise. Unfortunately, while practicing a riposte, %clumsyguy% managed to stick himself in the foot. The man appears even more hurt by the embarrassment.
3c6257d6b8c25819e849.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]旅途中，你喜欢偶尔安排训练，让弟兄们保持身手。可惜，%clumsyguy%练习反击时，竟一剑扎中了自己的脚。看他的样子，丢脸似乎比伤口更疼。

89204f85746ef4c0698b.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]While doing inventory, you ask %clumsyguy% to carry over a quiver of arrows. The short, simple journey ends with the man tripping over a rock and turning himself into a pincushion.
89204f85746ef4c0698b.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]清点物资时，你让%clumsyguy%搬来一袋箭。短短几步、简单至极的差事，却以他被石头绊倒、把自己扎成针垫告终。

fae7208a852b78a86295.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]You find a rather drunk %clumsyguy% nursing the side of his face. %otherguy1% explains that the idiot tried to dance over a series of rocks, only to fall and bash himself in the face. Great.
fae7208a852b78a86295.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]你发现喝得酩酊大醉的%clumsyguy%正捂着半边脸。%otherguy1%解释，这傻子想踩着一串石头跳舞，结果摔了下来，把脸磕了。真行。

713b539701c0c0a27b90.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]While %otherguy1% and %otherguy2% train, %clumsyguy% comes in between them, lecturing on how to do it properly while at the same time not watching where he's going. A wayward wooden sword crosses paths with his face and a moment later the idiot is unconscious.
713b539701c0c0a27b90.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]%otherguy1%与%otherguy2%正在训练，%clumsyguy%走到两人中间，一边讲解正确招式，一边却不看路。一柄偏了方向的木剑恰好迎上他的脸，下一刻，这傻子便不省人事。

04834e24502503d77926.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]It appears %clumsyguy% got a little too much to drink before partaking in today's sparring. As the story was explained to you, the drunkard mistakened a tree for an enemy combatant. He then, again as the story goes, proceeded to charge said tree, knocking himself out in the process.
04834e24502503d77926.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]看来%clumsyguy%参加今天的对练前，多喝了几杯。据人禀报，这酒鬼把一棵树当成了敌人，随后——据说确实如此——向那棵树发起冲锋，把自己撞晕了。

8a23dcb35175b646e65e.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%Man is treated to war the day he is born. It is his mother who is with him for that first battle, and to his mother whom he calls in his last. If only the evil we see in others could be seen in ourselves, then the call to swords might fall on deaf ears. How sad that men are so uncomfortable looking inward, and how sad that when the call for swords is made our ears hear better than ever.%SPEECH_OFF%
8a23dcb35175b646e65e.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]你们围火而坐，天南地北地聊了许多。旅人走后很久，有几句话仍留在你脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%人降生那天，便迎来第一场战斗。陪他打这一仗的是母亲，而最后一仗里，他呼唤的仍是母亲。若我们能在自己身上看见指责他人的那些恶，号召拔剑的声音，也许就无人理睬。可悲啊，人们如此不愿审视内心；更可悲的是，刀剑一响，我们的耳朵却比任何时候都灵。%SPEECH_OFF%

39719fe8416b339d8173.source: T'was my call to answer, traveler.
39719fe8416b339d8173.translation: 旅人，那是我该担起的事。

4fa07efa4faf05b52b17.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%I'd found myself nearing the top of a mountain a few months ago. Highest I've ever been! Traveled there in the company of an expedition. Some man smarter than I reckoned it might be worthwhile so he could point his big glasses to the skies. Anyway, I looked down at the land and could see what had been done to it. Cities and towns and roads, little moles of gritty patchwork. Wagons scuttling like ants, selling what could be pilferaged from this man or this animal or this land. Holes in the forests where trees used to be.%SPEECH_OFF%
4fa07efa4faf05b52b17.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]你们围坐在火堆旁，东拉西扯地聊着。可旅人的一些话，即使在他离开很久之后，仍留在你的脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%几个月前，我跟着一支探险队，爬到快接近山顶的地方。那是我这辈子去过的最高处！有个比我聪明的人觉得值得跑一趟，好把他那大镜筒对准天空。总之，我往下看，才看清这片土地被折腾成了什么样。城市、村镇、道路，像一片片粗糙拼凑的补丁，又像长在地上的小痣。货车跟蚂蚁似的爬来爬去，贩卖着从人、牲畜或土地上搜刮来的东西。森林里满是空洞，原先长在那里的树都没了。%SPEECH_OFF%

2ab01c0ff497dc30d65e.source: Man has certainly made an impression.

58cc4a459a077976df05.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%Thank you for offering the fish, sirs, but I will have to turn it down. Let me explain. Just the other day I tried diggin' a hole for m'kin as he'd passed away as folks requiring holes in the earth tend to do. T'was a distant cousin that stood close. Lived next door, actually. Feller died of illness, something we don't know of, but none but he got so I guess we is alright. He was all green when he passed. Y'all know what that might have been?%SPEECH_OFF%
58cc4a459a077976df05.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]你们围坐在火堆旁，东拉西扯地聊着。可旅人的一些话，即使在他离开很久之后，仍留在你的脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%诸位，多谢你们请我吃鱼，可我还是不吃了。听我解释。就在前几天，我给一个亲戚挖坑来着，因为他死了——毕竟，要在地里挖坑安置的人，多半都是死了。他是个远亲，住得却很近，就在隔壁。他得病死的，谁也说不清是什么病。不过只有他一个人得了，我想咱们应该没事。他走的时候，全身都绿了。你们可知道，那会是什么病？%SPEECH_OFF%

f33cb9383ae053de2fb8.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%No? Damn. Well anyway, I dug his grave for him, as he surely wasn't going to do it himself. I got far into the ground when I come across a big ol' stone. Pick hit it hard, broke the shaft in two and made chalk of my pickaxe. I said horseshit, I've gone too far to stop here so get out of the way, stone! But that rock had bones in it. Not on it, in it. Strange looking ones, but bones nonetheless. Death is remarkably familiar from an outsider's perspective.

Anyway, the skull seemed to be looking at me, judging me, saying 'what is it you think yer doing here?' So I got up out of that hole and ran to m'home, my cousin's remains yoked over my shoulders like I'd stolen them. I was bothered. Couldn't sleep. Felt like I was laying over what must've been hundreds of fellers right then, some so old they'd taken shape with rocks of all things. Dead fellers. All the way down. Nothing but dead, all the way down I say! And I didn't know what to do and I suppose it still bothers me now if it ain't obvious.%SPEECH_OFF%
f33cb9383ae053de2fb8.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%没有？见鬼。总之，我替他挖坟，反正他也不可能自己动手。我挖得挺深，碰上了一大块老石头。镐子重重砸上去，柄断成两截，镐头也碎成了粉。我骂了声狗屎，都挖到这份上了，还能就此打住？石头，给我让开！可那块石头里有骨头。不是石头上，是石头里面。样子古怪，但的确是骨头。站在旁观者的位置看，死人这回事还真是熟悉得吓人。

总之，那颗头骨像是在盯着我，审视我，仿佛在问：“你以为自己在这里干什么？”于是我爬出坑，把表亲的尸身扛在肩上，像做贼似的一路跑回家。我心里发毛，睡不着觉，总觉得自己正躺在几百个死人的上头，其中有些老得连骨头都跟石头长到一块儿去了。死人。一路往下都是。往下全是死人，我告诉你，全是！我当时真不知道该怎么办。就算我不说，你也该看得出，这事到现在还在折磨我。%SPEECH_OFF%

3982774bf9e2a6e1a182.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%Later on I decided I wouldn't bury m'cousin. Instead, I burned his remains and threw the heap of what was left stewing and smoking into'a'pond. Said to m'self, 'cousin, you ain't gonna be no rock'.

But the other day I found them bones washed ashore, and there was a fat bellied fish caught in the ribs. Caged himself there on account of good eats, I guess. I picked that fish up and held it, and my cousin I s'pose, in my hand. T'was limp. Bugeyed as fish are without their watery lids. But then a dog ran by and took it from me. Gobbled it right quick for it knew the nature of its crime, I think. That's where a piece of my cousin ran off to. Dodged the earth on account of the hungry rocks only to be eaten by a squire of a fish that served itself to a righteous dog of all things. So now you know why I don't eat fish no more.%SPEECH_OFF%
3982774bf9e2a6e1a182.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%后来，我决定不埋那亲戚了。我把尸体烧掉，将余下那堆还冒烟发烫的东西扔进池塘，心里说：“亲戚啊，你可不会变成石头。”

可前些天，我发现骨头被冲上了岸，肋骨里卡着一条大肚子鱼。我猜它贪吃，自己钻进去，反倒把自己关住了。我把鱼捡起来，捧在手上——这么说，我那亲戚也算在里面。鱼软塌塌的，没了水遮眼，眼珠跟所有鱼一样鼓着。忽然一条狗跑过来，从我手里抢走它，三两口就吞了。我想，它也知道自己做的是贼事，才吃得那么快。我那亲戚的一部分，就这样跑远了。为躲那些饥饿的石头，没让他入土，结果却被一条小喽啰似的鱼吃了，那鱼又把自己献给一条正气凛然的狗。喏，现在你明白，我为什么再也不吃鱼了。%SPEECH_OFF%

fbac618ab0773324dd20.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%I took part in the eastern campaigns. Drove the supply wagons, carrying untold numbers of armor, weapons, horses, foods, you name it. Hell, that's an age ten years past now, I believe. T'was the last time men truly stood together, and I suppose the last time the greenskins did the same. No mystery that when the two forces met they shattered against one another. Now we dwell in a time of chaos and rumor and superstition and idle talk amongst strangers.%SPEECH_OFF%
fbac618ab0773324dd20.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围坐在火堆旁，东拉西扯地聊着。可旅人的一些话，即使在他离开很久之后，仍留在你的脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%我参加过东征，赶补给车，运过数不清的盔甲、武器、马匹、粮食，你能想到的都有。见鬼，算来都是十年前的事了。那是人类最后一次真正团结起来，我猜，也是绿皮最后一次如此。两股力量撞在一起，把彼此撞得粉碎，也就没什么奇怪了。如今的世道，只剩混乱、传言、迷信，还有陌生人之间这些闲聊。%SPEECH_OFF%

bdfc2f4dc34b7fa1d3f2.source: May you find peace on the roads, traveler.
bdfc2f4dc34b7fa1d3f2.translation: 旅人，愿你在路途中找到安宁。

c2a6f0e0d1aab1185921.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%Ten years ago I fought in the Battle of Many Names. Orc against man. The end of a war that struck its name across an entire age. I rode with the cavalry, if you want to know. Southern flank in the mud and swamp and aye, neither are well fit for horseriding but our commander was having none of that. An orc drove a polearm through that commander's horse, and on through the commander himself. Taking horses into that muck.. a terrible idea. I heard the northern flank fared better, but it's no matter. Neither side won that damned fight.%SPEECH_OFF%
c2a6f0e0d1aab1185921.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围坐在火堆旁，东拉西扯地聊着。可旅人的一些话，即使在他离开很久之后，仍留在你的脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%十年前，我打过众名之战。兽人与人类交锋，那是一场将名字刻进整个时代的战争的终局。要问我在哪儿，我跟着骑兵，在南翼，全是烂泥和沼泽。没错，都不适合跑马，可指挥官根本不听。后来一个兽人用长柄武器刺穿了他的坐骑，又捅穿了他本人。把马骑进那种烂泥地……真是个糟透了的主意。听说北翼打得好些，但也没什么意义。那场该死的仗，谁也没赢。%SPEECH_OFF%

d836be8a24e6bad2be8e.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%Ever seen a greenskin cleave a horse's head off? Quite the sight. But I've also seen a horse kick an orc's teeth out and bury him in mud with stomping madness. We forget, I think, that the horse is more akin to fancy a war than we are. Frightful, curious animals, sure, but violent. They say, left to themselves they oft kill one another, kill each other's children and their children's children. It's a damned thing that women love us both.%SPEECH_OFF%
d836be8a24e6bad2be8e.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围坐在火堆旁，东拉西扯地聊着。可旅人的一些话，即使在他离开很久之后，仍留在你的脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%见过绿皮一刀砍掉马头吗？那场面可真够瞧的。不过我也见过马踢飞兽人的牙，再发疯似的踩踏，把它踩进泥里。我想，咱们总是忘记，马兴许比人还好斗。它们确实胆小，又爱好奇，可也凶狠得很。听说放着不管，它们常会彼此残杀，杀对方的崽子，连崽子的崽子都不放过。偏偏女人就喜欢咱们这两种东西，真是见鬼。%SPEECH_OFF%

9630c43147668879a0fb.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%Ah, the Battle of Many Names. Aye, I took part. Vanguard. Front and center. No, I do not wish to talk about it.%SPEECH_OFF%
9630c43147668879a0fb.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]你们围火而坐，天南地北地聊了许多。旅人走后很久，有几句话仍留在你脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%啊，众名之战。对，我参加了。先锋，正面最前排。不，我不想谈。%SPEECH_OFF%

9458c491a635db8e67b9.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%The Battle of Many Names? Who did not take part in that? Half the world was on the march then, I swear it. I stood with the infantry. Footman to a lord, to be precise. Protected him well until the orcs released their berserkers. After that, everybody sought to protect themselves, a job which proved quite difficult. I used to lie about how I made it out. Now I don't. The truth is my lord had his face crushed by a chain and his mount flipped and fell atop me, its poor heart struck dead in fright.%SPEECH_OFF%
9458c491a635db8e67b9.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围坐在火堆旁，东拉西扯地聊着。可旅人的一些话，即使在他离开很久之后，仍留在你的脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%众名之战？谁没打过？我敢说，那时候半个世界都在行军。我在步兵里，确切地说，是跟着一位领主步行作战的侍卫。一直护得挺好，直到兽人放出狂战士。那之后，人人都只能顾着自保，而这活儿也着实不好干。以前我总编瞎话，说自己如何逃出生天，如今不编了。实情是，我家领主被铁链砸烂了脸，他那匹可怜的马活活吓得心脏停跳，翻倒下来，正压在我身上。%SPEECH_OFF%

194004da0ed223ecc767.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] The traveler pauses, staring into the campfire. He prods the edge of it with a stick.%SPEECH_ON%That's the last thing I remembered as far the fightin' was concerned. I eventually woke to the rains coming up to my nose. Nearly drowned me in my dozing. I wiggled my way out from under the horse and crawled to god knows where. Orcs and men lay everywhere, dead, dying, drowning. Lots of screaming. Couldn't tell who or what it was coming from. I remember the mud. I remember it clutching at me. A maiden, strong-armed like an ox, saved me from it. She threw me on a cart and the last thing I saw was the battlefield and, I'm sorry. I must stop. Thank you for having me for the night.%SPEECH_OFF%
194004da0ed223ecc767.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 旅人停了下来，望着篝火，用木棍拨了拨火堆边缘。%SPEECH_ON%那场仗，我能记起的就到这里。后来醒过来，雨水已经漫到鼻子，差点让我在昏睡中淹死。我从马尸底下挣出来，往前爬，天知道爬向哪里。到处躺着兽人和人，有的死了，有的快死了，有的正被水淹死。惨叫声不断，分不清是人还是别的什么。我记得那泥，记得它死死拖着我。后来，一个力气大得像牛的姑娘把我救了出来，扔上一辆小货车。我最后看见的还是战场，还有……抱歉，我说不下去了。谢谢你们今晚收留我。%SPEECH_OFF%

c6938b18c5c101f25f12.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%I led a company in the Battle of Many Names. It was a righteous affair. Man against orc! Oh, what a sight. Half of my men died on those fields, but their sacrifice saved the whole land! I look fondly on those times. What man doesn't?%SPEECH_OFF%
c6938b18c5c101f25f12.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]你们围火而坐，天南地北地聊了许多。旅人走后很久，有几句话仍留在你脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%众名之战时，我带着一支队伍。那是场正义之战，人类对抗兽人！啊，何等景象。我手下一半人死在那片战场，可他们的牺牲救了整片大地！想起那些日子，我心里就暖和。哪个男人不是如此？%SPEECH_OFF%

b3309412c8e1d455e542.translation: 陌生人，这是个高尚的故事。

2684673257dc1d952b3b.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%Out in %randomtown% they had a father up for trial. He'd murdered two brothers on account of knocking his cart over. And then apparently the taste of it had him murdering some more. All told, he took the lives of at least seven people. Naturally, they hanged the man. But I ran into his son the other day and he told me the hanging was merely some clerical mistake. His father was an upstanding man, not the least bit self-serving and the people he killed had it coming. What's more curious, this youngin' is now mayor! Now, the way I remember it the man slaughtered seven folks outright. Just like that! But last time I was in town they'd moved his long-necked bones to a proper cemetery and I'll be damned if I didn't see some flowers on the tombstone. Not sure what to make of these things.%SPEECH_OFF%
2684673257dc1d952b3b.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围着火堆闲坐，天南海北地聊了不少。不过，旅人说的几句话，即使他走了很久，仍留在你脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%%randomtown%那边，曾经审过一个当爹的。他杀了一对兄弟，就因为人家碰翻了他的货车。后来大概是杀出了滋味，又接着杀人。算下来，至少有七条人命。那当然得把他吊死。可前几天，我碰见了他的儿子，那小子竟说，他爹被绞死，只是文书上弄错了。他爹为人正直，半点私心也没有，那些被杀的人全是活该。更怪的是，这年轻人如今竟当上了镇长！我记得清清楚楚，那人就是把七个人杀了，说杀就杀！可上次进城，我发现他们把那具脖子吊长了的尸骨迁进了正经墓地，墓碑上甚至还摆着鲜花，骗你我是狗。这些事，我真不知道该怎么想。%SPEECH_OFF%

25fff76f0c3fcaa5bb33.source: People try to see the best in themselves.
25fff76f0c3fcaa5bb33.translation: 人们总想把自己往好处想。

78aa90ed1550134a24d6.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%You ain't the only mercenary company out here. I'm sure you know that, and I don't mean to sound threatening, but I only wish to tell ya something.

A couple weeks past some two or three companies of men, standing like your own, met at a crossroads and apparently the path wasn't big enough for all of 'em, so they fought. If any survived, it wasn't enough to carry off those who didn't. I like your men. They is good people. But please do be careful out there. Killing raiders and brigands and the gods know what else isn't the only thing you'll be doing. You kill in a market of competitors, sellsword.%SPEECH_OFF%
78aa90ed1550134a24d6.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围坐在火堆旁，东拉西扯地聊着。可旅人的一些话，即使在他离开很久之后，仍留在你的脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%世上可不止你们这一支佣兵团。我相信你知道，也不是想吓唬你，只是有件事想说说。

前几周，有两三支跟你们差不多的战团，在十字路口碰上了。大概那条路容不下所有人，于是就打起来。就算有人活下来，剩下的人手也不够抬走死者。我喜欢你的弟兄，他们都是好人。可出门在外，千万小心。杀劫掠者、强盗，还有诸神才知道的其他东西，并不是你们唯一会干的事。佣兵，杀人也是一门有同行抢饭吃的生意。%SPEECH_OFF%

473c8029089dc45763c9.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%A boy stole my lunch the other day, but he'd done not do anything but stand there and eat it in front of me. I said, 'give me back my lunch ya scamp', but he said no. I reached for it but his scrawny legs proved to be more cat than chicken. I said, no, I asked why he'd done have to eat it in front of me. This was torture, you see. He said 'because I'm hungry'. I told 'im, 'I'm hungry too, now give it back'. Naturally, he done said no. And so naturally when he'd done turned around I cracked him with a stone and that slackened his speed a bit and I got m'lunch back. 

 But then yonder comes a footman of the mayor who says don't do that. I asked 'im why not, he said 'because that's the mayor's boy'. My punishment was nothing, but I was warned t'not do it again. I told 'im, I said, 'tell the boy to not steal again!'. And they said they had, and that I was more likely to yield to a command than he and that's t'way it t'was. Farkin' small towns, I swear on m'sack those places are more billy than hill.%SPEECH_OFF%
473c8029089dc45763c9.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围着火堆闲坐，天南海北地聊了不少。不过，旅人说的几句话，即使他走了很久，仍留在你脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%前些天，有个男孩偷了我的午饭，可他偷完哪儿也不去，就站在我面前吃。我说：“小兔崽子，把午饭还我。”他说不。我伸手去抢，才知道那两条细腿不像鸡腿，倒像猫腿，灵活得很。我说——不，我是问他，为什么非要当着我的面吃？你明白，这就是折磨人。他说：“因为我饿。”我告诉他：“我也饿，还给我。”他当然又说不。所以他一转身，我也就顺手拿石头砸了他一下。这下他跑不快了，我把午饭拿了回来。 

 可紧接着，镇长的一个随从走过来，叫我不准这么干。我问为什么，他说：“因为那是镇长的儿子。”倒没罚我什么，只是警告别再有下次。我说：“那你叫他别再偷啊！”他们说，已经叫过了，可我比那孩子更可能听话，所以事情就得这么办。该死的小镇，我拿卵蛋发誓，这些地方简直比山沟还土！%SPEECH_OFF%

b02de51d74727351e39e.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%Death was strange on the battlefield of Many Names. Orcs don't kill like men do, they make it fast. They leave you little wait between the now and the then. I got a good look at their handiwork after it was all said and done. Men strewn in pieces. Whole parts, legs, arms, bodies split in seams most unnatural. Instant death. Swing, head gone! And the body crumples and stiffens. Most of the dead looked like that, like they'd just been scared and sat frozen in their embarrassment. Most looked nothing like men at all. A man should look asleep when he's dead, you know?%SPEECH_OFF%
b02de51d74727351e39e.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围坐在火堆旁，东拉西扯地聊着。可旅人的一些话，即使在他离开很久之后，仍留在你的脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%众名之战的战场上，死法很古怪。兽人杀人不像人类，它们下手快，不让你在生死之间等上多久。等一切结束，我好好见识了它们的手段。人被砍得七零八落，整条腿，整条胳膊，身体从根本不该裂开的地方分成几截。当场毙命。一下，脑袋就没了！身子倒下，僵在那里。大多数死人都是那副样子，像刚被吓了一跳，还没缓过那股窘迫就定住了。大多数甚至都不成人形。你知道吗，人死了，就该像睡着一样。%SPEECH_OFF%

374b1caf5eca23a15cc3.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]He continues.%SPEECH_ON%A few received the courtesy of a slow death, of a pause to get ready and make themselves comfortable and find peace, to curl up into a ball and depart this place in a similar shape to how they'd come in. But I will say one man, taken apart at the beltline, managed to hang on. I found him myself. I told him to close his eyes because I thought if he went to sleep maybe death'd wake up. But he didn't go to sleep. He just kept breathing, and talking. Talking about this chicken he had as a boy, and how he got upset when his father slaughtered it. Talked about a girl, and then a wife and a mother. Talked about two mothers, actually.%SPEECH_OFF%The man pauses, staring into the campfire. He looks up at you.%SPEECH_ON%I did not know half a man could live for so long.%SPEECH_OFF%
374b1caf5eca23a15cc3.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]他继续说道。%SPEECH_ON%有些人倒受了慢慢死去的优待，能有片刻准备，让自己舒服些，寻得平静，蜷成一团，以近似来到世上时的姿态离开。可有一个人，齐腰断成两截，居然还撑着。是我亲自找到他的。我叫他闭上眼，想着他若睡去，死神也许就会醒来。可他不睡，只是不停呼吸，不停说话。说起小时候养的鸡，父亲宰了它，自己有多难过。说起一个姑娘，然后是妻子，还有母亲。其实，他说到了两个母亲。%SPEECH_OFF%那人停下来，望着篝火，随后抬眼看你。%SPEECH_ON%我从不知道，半个人也能活那么久。%SPEECH_OFF%

771990e312c20c2ba94a.source: May you find peace in your travels, stranger.
771990e312c20c2ba94a.translation: 陌生人，愿你在旅途中找到安宁。

e62184436f3e4139f69a.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler does speak some words which reside within your mind long after he's gone.%SPEECH_ON%I saw'r man cut down by lightning a few months ago. %randomname% was his name. He had a lumber mill for a mouth, a wooden bite from side-to-side. Termites for teeth we used to say! Anyway, I'd found his head aflame, grinning hot fire back at me, his flesh curled down in strips of black and purple. The ground around him was scorched, smoke drifting around and little fires crackling. But he was still alive. So I ran off to get some help when I heard a horrid noise behind me. Damned lightning struck him again! Smote by the gods through and through.%SPEECH_OFF%
e62184436f3e4139f69a.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围坐在火堆旁，东拉西扯地聊着。可旅人的一些话，即使在他离开很久之后，仍留在你的脑海里。%SPEECH_ON%几个月前，我见过一个人被雷劈倒。他叫%randomname%。他那张嘴简直是个锯木厂，满口上下都是木头假牙，咱们总说，他长的是一嘴白蚁！总之，我发现他时，他脑袋上正烧着火，冲我咧嘴一笑，嘴里也是热焰。皮肉焦黑发紫，成条地卷了下来。周围地面烧焦了，烟气飘着，几簇小火噼啪作响。可他还活着。我便跑去找人帮忙，谁知身后又传来一声巨响。该死的雷居然又劈中了他！诸神这是非要把他劈个透啊。%SPEECH_OFF%

bc8373f27ed50a26edf1.source: Well, may he rest in peace.

bb1027f1cfe1d5a14e9c.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. The traveler speaks of some idle news.%SPEECH_ON%They hanged some lady in %randomtown%. Didn't see her drop, but I did see her swing. They said she stove a man's head in while he slept. What a wench.%SPEECH_OFF%
bb1027f1cfe1d5a14e9c.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]你们围火而坐，旅人说起一桩闲闻。%SPEECH_ON%他们在%randomtown%绞死了个女人。我没看见她落下去，倒看见她挂着晃荡。听说她趁一个男人睡觉，把他的脑袋砸烂了。好个狠娘们。%SPEECH_OFF%

ef7edb30883c6295daa4.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. The traveler speaks of a crime and its punishment.%SPEECH_ON%Out in %randomtown% they hanged a boy for killin' a merchant. Said he threw a stone at the trader to knock him off his cart. He then ran over to steal his things, but the stoned man wasn't knocked out, so he drew his dagger and the boy drew his and I guess the boy was the one left standing when it was all said and done, o'course, he now just be left swinging. Talk of the execution say he kicked good and long, wouldn't stop kicking even after he was dead. Maybe his cold feet were lookin' for warmth.%SPEECH_OFF%
ef7edb30883c6295daa4.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] 你们围坐火边，旅人讲起一桩罪案及其刑罚。%SPEECH_ON%%randomtown%那边绞死了个男孩，说他杀了个商人。他拿石头把商人从货车上砸下来，跑去抢东西，可那人没昏，拔出了匕首，男孩也拔刀。等打完，站着的只剩男孩。当然，如今就剩吊着晃了。听看行刑的人说，他蹬了好久的腿，死了还在蹬。也许是脚冷，想找点暖和吧。%SPEECH_OFF%

73ad26b8f7c500dd2b97.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. Much talk is made about this or that, but the traveler gets a little skittish and you ask what is on his mind.%SPEECH_ON%I've heard rumors of graveyards turning up earth-empty. They hanged a man out in %randomtown% for gravedigging, unfortunately they kept finding deadless graves anyway. Now, I'm no superstitious man, but the way I hear it the dead're stepping out of the ground.%SPEECH_OFF%
73ad26b8f7c500dd2b97.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]你们围火而坐，聊着杂事。旅人渐渐有些不安，你问他在想什么。%SPEECH_ON%听说有些坟墓挖开后，里面空了。%randomtown%还为盗墓绞死过一个人，可空坟照样不断出现。我不是迷信的人，不过听那意思，是死人自己从地里爬出来了。%SPEECH_OFF%

c8615a31eb9cc14e686c.source: It's just hearsay. You have nothing to fear.
c8615a31eb9cc14e686c.translation: 不过是传言，没什么好怕的。

80a44a2842a41c559d5f.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] %SPEECH_ON%Whew. Yeah I suppose you is right. Dead walking the earth? Ha! I'll leave such ideas to the children.%SPEECH_OFF%
80a44a2842a41c559d5f.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%呼，你说得也是。死人还会爬起来走路？哈！这种故事，留给小孩信吧。%SPEECH_OFF%

6099934a61468b73cf3e.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] %SPEECH_ON%May the old gods have mercy for if my damned mother-in-law walks the earth she'll certainly have none for me.%SPEECH_OFF%
6099934a61468b73cf3e.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%愿旧神发发慈悲。要是我那该死的丈母娘又爬出来走动，她肯定不会对我慈悲。%SPEECH_OFF%

b80f196cefadb329b14c.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] You sit about a fire. The rather unfortunate looking man stares into the fire as he talks.%SPEECH_ON%I hear the rich folk have got these things that let them see what they look like. Mirrors! Aye, that's the name. Wish I had one. I hadn't seen my own face in.. well, ever. Maybe a bit of a look when staring into a pond, I guess.%SPEECH_OFF%
b80f196cefadb329b14c.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]你们围火而坐。那男人长相颇为不幸，盯着火说道：%SPEECH_ON%听说富人有种东西，能照出自己长什么样。镜子！对，就叫这个。我也想有一面。我的脸自己已经……唔，其实从来没看清过。也许盯着池塘时，算是瞧见过一点吧。%SPEECH_OFF%

db23748e10347f8db0aa.source: Some things are best left unseen.
db23748e10347f8db0aa.translation: 有些东西，还是别看见的好。

f313d7e8c1657858d9da.source: We got a mirror right here.
f313d7e8c1657858d9da.translation: 我们这里正好有面镜子。

2699b5e4063afd7f4a47.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] The man's brow furrows.%SPEECH_ON%Oh yeah thanks, sellsword, that makes me feel so much better. Farkin' cunt.%SPEECH_OFF%
2699b5e4063afd7f4a47.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]那人皱起眉头。%SPEECH_ON%哦，真谢谢你啊，佣兵，这话可让我舒坦多了。你这该死的狗东西。%SPEECH_OFF%

a4320f4c35ef74b26a24.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img] The man stares into the mirror like he was watching his own death. He rubs his chin and turns his head, desperately looking for some angle that won't disappoint.%SPEECH_ON%I'll be damned if my mother ain't the biggest liar that ever walked the earth. Look at that ugly mug!%SPEECH_OFF%He hands the mirror back and can't help but laugh at his unfortunate visage.%SPEECH_ON%Well, I suppose I no longer have to wonder why the womenfolk run from me.%SPEECH_OFF%
a4320f4c35ef74b26a24.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]那人盯着镜子，仿佛看见自己的死相。他摸摸下巴，转动脑袋，拼命想找个不那么令人失望的角度。%SPEECH_ON%我娘准是天底下最大的骗子。瞧这张丑脸！%SPEECH_OFF%他把镜子还来，忍不住为自己这副不幸的尊容笑出声。%SPEECH_ON%好吧，往后也不用再纳闷女人为什么都躲着我了。%SPEECH_OFF%

14ce15cb5eaf0109aa8b.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_92.png[/img]While camping beside the road, a colorful wagon trundles on up with a sort of clanking, jingling musical immodesty. You didn't think it a particularly big cart, but about fifteen men and women inexplicably pour out of its back. Painted faces, musical instruments, juggling balls, longswords for swallowing, wine jugs for firebreathing, the troupe of entertainers fan out and demonstrate mini-talent shows as though you'd already paid for their services. When they finish, they clap, stomp their feet, and freeze before you, hands out, smiles across their faces. A white-faced mime ironically speaks.%SPEECH_ON%What say you, travelers, care for a show? A mere %payment% crowns to entertain you all evening!%SPEECH_OFF%
14ce15cb5eaf0109aa8b.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_92.png[/img]你们在路边扎营时，一辆色彩鲜艳的货车晃晃悠悠地驶来，叮当哐啷，闹得像一支毫不知收敛的乐队。车子看着不大，后头却不可思议地涌出约十五个男男女女。花脸、乐器、杂耍球、吞剑用的长剑、喷火用的酒壶，这群艺人一字散开，各显绝活，仿佛你已经付了钱。演完，他们拍手、跺脚，然后齐齐定住，伸着手，满面笑容。一个涂白脸的哑剧演员竟开了口。%SPEECH_ON%旅人们，怎么样，要不要看场戏？只需%payment%克朗，就能让各位痛快一整晚！%SPEECH_OFF%

1fa7bfa70e862c56c823.source: Sure, we'll pay for a show.

ee3cdd063765c1feb635.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]%entertainer% steps forward and picks up some of the troupe's tools of trade. He tests them out, impressing the entertainers with how well he's able to use their own equipment. The mime asks if perhaps they could play a couple of tunes with him. He nods and joins the entertainers, putting on a show that's for the ages. When it's all over, the troupe is so impressed that they try and recruit the man. You tell them that ain't happening and %entertainer% nods.%SPEECH_ON%My time is with the %companyname% now, but I appreciate the compliment.%SPEECH_OFF%You ask how much for the show, but the troupe leader shakes his head.%SPEECH_ON%No need. It was a pleasure playing with him. We've not put on a show like that in some time and the practice will do us well.%SPEECH_OFF%
ee3cdd063765c1feb635.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]%entertainer%走上前，拿起剧团的几件家伙什试了试。借来的道具在他手里竟使得如此娴熟，艺人们都看呆了。哑剧演员问，能否与他合演几曲？他点头加入，众人献上一场足以长久流传的好戏。演完后，剧团佩服得想把他招走。你告诉他们，这不可能，%entertainer%也点头道。%SPEECH_ON%如今我效力于%companyname%，不过，多谢各位赏识。%SPEECH_OFF%你问演出要收多少钱，团长却摇摇头。%SPEECH_ON%不必了。能和他同台，实在痛快。我们很久没演过这么精彩的一场了，这番切磋，对大家都大有益处。%SPEECH_OFF%

148aba4c96222f0b0f4d.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]Before the troupe can start, %nobleman% the nobleman gets up and asks if they know of a particular song from his days in the court.%SPEECH_ON%They used to sing it when I was a little lad. It's been years since I've heard it.%SPEECH_OFF%The mime, again breaking character, grins and loudly proclaims that they know it. He snaps his fingers and the musicians of the group pick up their instruments. When they start, the tune is instantly catchy. It's a stringed and horn orchestration, played alongside a large woman singing from both heart and belly. She is a tempest of a singer, bringing both the quiet and ferocity of a large storm's coming and going, and her lyrics are that of incredible heroism of yore.

 After the troupe finishes, you ask how much you owe them. The mime shakes his head.%SPEECH_ON%No, sir, payment is not necessary. It's been awhile since that got requested and it was a pleasure to play it for you.%SPEECH_OFF%
148aba4c96222f0b0f4d.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]剧团还没开始表演，贵族%nobleman%便站起来，问他们会不会唱一首自己从前在宫廷里听过的歌。%SPEECH_ON%我小时候，他们常唱这首。已经好多年没听过了。%SPEECH_OFF%哑剧演员又一次忘了自己的本行，咧嘴大声说他们会唱。他打了个响指，乐师们纷纷拿起乐器。乐曲一响，旋律便立刻抓住了人。弦声与号角交织，一位身材丰腴的女人以发自胸腹的浑厚嗓音，倾情歌唱。她的歌声如同风暴，将暴雨来去前后的宁静与猛烈都带了出来，唱的是往昔那些惊世骇俗的英雄壮举。

 演出结束后，你问该付多少钱。哑剧演员摇摇头。%SPEECH_ON%不必，先生，不用付钱。已经很久没人点这首歌了，能为你们演奏，我们也很高兴。%SPEECH_OFF%

0b806bfebcf6d9509b2a.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_60.png[/img]You order the troupe raided. The mime, this time actually in character, holds up his hands and mouths 'what?'. But the playfulness is wiped away when %randombrother% walks up and plants a punch right on his chin. The mime goes down with a catlike cry, mewling in the mud as he nurses his jaw.

The rest of the company knocks the troupe around while raiding their wagon for goods. A juggler gets kicked right in the balls and a singer has her throat chopped by %randombrother2%'s hand. The sword swallower tries to hide his sword the only place he knows where, but a mercenary retrieves it with a rather painful unsheathing. The firebreather drinks the entirety of his jug then asks if you want to take that, too. You have him gut-punched for his snark.

 When it's all said and done, there really isn't much to take as beating up jesters isn't the most profitable business. At least with a busted mouth maybe the mime will do his job better.
0b806bfebcf6d9509b2a.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_60.png[/img]你下令抢劫剧团。这一回，哑剧演员倒还记得自己的身份，举起双手，无声地做出“什么？”的口型。可%randombrother%上前一拳砸在他下巴上，顷刻间打散了那点诙谐。他像猫一样尖叫着倒下，捂着下巴，在泥地里哀鸣。

其余弟兄一边殴打剧团成员，一边翻上货车搜刮。耍杂技的被一脚踢中卵蛋，女歌手则挨了%randombrother2%一记手刀，正中喉咙。吞剑人想把剑藏进自己最熟悉的地方，可一名佣兵又用极其痛苦的方式把它“拔”了出来。喷火艺人喝光整壶东西，问你是不是连这也想拿走。你让人往他肚子上揍了一拳，好教他别耍嘴皮子。

 到头来，其实也没什么可抢的，揍一群逗乐的艺人毕竟算不上赚钱的买卖。至少嘴巴打坏了，那哑剧演员没准能把本行干得更好些。

160181775fa3c953a338.source: Learn to mime, you creepy prick.
160181775fa3c953a338.translation: 去学哑剧吧，你这瘆人的混蛋。

dc40bdc55459243989bb.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]You pay for a show which the troupe puts on quite well. The jesters crack out some jokes, the jugglers juggle which is sorta old-hat but whatever, singers sing, swords get swallowed, fire 'breathed', and the mime, well, he's godawful and you actually hope he dies.

 When it's all said and done, you do feel like you got your money's worth and the men are happy.
dc40bdc55459243989bb.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]你付钱看了场演出，剧团演得颇好。丑角讲笑话，杂耍艺人耍把戏——虽有些老套，也就随它了——歌手唱歌，还有吞剑、喷火。至于那个哑剧演员，唉，烂透了，你甚至真希望他赶紧死了算了。

总之，散场时你觉得钱花得值，弟兄们也很开心。

350df624d95a229d7cd8.source: You look like you have something on your mind, %noblefull%.

2d12804451abe0978585.source: How about you just hand over your valuables?
2d12804451abe0978585.translation: 不如把你们的值钱东西交出来？

4ba6334883c1e8926620.translation: 欣赏了巡回剧团的表演

97b001e3fc6b277c0f3a.source: Enjoyed beating up a traveling troupe
97b001e3fc6b277c0f3a.translation: 痛打巡回剧团后感到痛快

f08cac36ae78c08e7d08.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]You meet a monk on the roads and with him is a donkey-pulled cart, the poor draught animal carrying its head low in mute exhaustion. Broomstraw and virid moss are strung up to one side of the cart, both twisting eagerly in the very winds that dried them, and some pots and pans clatter like rustic windchimes as the modest wares come to a bumbling stop. A barrel totters on the edge of the cart's bed and a couple of bees sway to keep up, poking and prodding at its cracks with thirsty curiosity.

The monk lifts a wool hat up out of his face but the lip of it folds back down over his eyes. He takes it off altogether and passes a sleeve across his brow. Carrying a jolly smile, he seems not at all disturbed by the veritable living armory standing before him.%SPEECH_ON%Evening gents. Don't s'pose yer the kind to march b'neath a lord's banner. Y'look like sellswords t'me.%SPEECH_OFF%
f08cac36ae78c08e7d08.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]你在路上遇见一个修士，赶着驴拉的小货车。可怜的牲口累得低垂脑袋，一声不吭。车侧挂着扫帚草和青苔，在将它们吹干的风里不住扭转。货车摇摇晃晃地停下，锅碗碰撞，像一串乡野风铃。车板边缘一只酒桶晃悠着，几只蜜蜂跟着飞来，渴切而好奇地探寻桶身的缝隙。

修士抬起遮脸的羊毛帽，帽檐却又折下来盖住眼睛。他索性摘掉帽子，用袖子抹过额头。面前这位简直像座会走路的兵器库，他却毫不在意，脸上带着愉快的笑。%SPEECH_ON%诸位，晚上好。看着不像替哪个领主扛旗的，依我看，各位是佣兵吧。%SPEECH_OFF%

e0ef8fe7df6edb8ff9e1.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%Aye, I was thinkin' you'd ask. This here is Bessie, a cow's name for a donkey's arse. Don't worry, she won't kick ye. She's all hawed-out, see? What she carry, well, that's beer. For men yonder, so that they may drink to men above. If ye don't mind, or if ye don't mind m'business, I'd like to get on where I be going.%SPEECH_OFF%The monk picks up the reins of his jenny as he readies to start moving.
e0ef8fe7df6edb8ff9e1.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]%SPEECH_ON%对，就知道你会问。这位叫贝西，给驴起了个奶牛的名儿。别担心，她不会踢你，连叫都叫累啦。驮的是什么？啤酒。给那边的人喝，好向天上的人敬一杯。若你不介意，或者至少别管我的事，我还想继续赶路呢。%SPEECH_OFF%修士拎起母驴的缰绳，准备动身。

0b1a855b3010d9da8d47.source: How many crowns for a round of beer?
0b1a855b3010d9da8d47.translation: 请大家喝一轮啤酒，要多少克朗？

9ad711b2bcb01ebb9e1b.source: We earned this by keeping the roads safe - take the beer, men!
9ad711b2bcb01ebb9e1b.translation: 我们保了道路平安，这酒是应得的。弟兄们，拿酒！

c82038069b81d06eac85.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]You hold your hand up, stopping the monk before he can get going again. He sighs, slowly lowering the reins out of his hand. Feeling as though he may be getting the wrong impression, you quickly ask if maybe he has beer to spare for your men. You are more than willing to pay. The monk looks back at his stock for a moment, then turns around.%SPEECH_ON%Aye. I give yer men a sip for a crown or two. Don't mind the bees 'round the top, they'll scurry when you come, but if you scurry when they scurry, they'll scurry after ya. Strange little gits.%SPEECH_OFF%You ask the man how much he wants.%SPEECH_ON%I'd wager ten crowns a head will do. I'm no business man, though, I might be takin' advantage of m'self here.%SPEECH_OFF%
c82038069b81d06eac85.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]你抬手拦住修士，不让他继续赶路。他叹了口气，慢慢放下缰绳。你觉得他可能误会了，赶紧问是否有多余的啤酒可以卖给弟兄们，你愿意付钱。修士回头看了一眼车上的存货，又转过来。%SPEECH_ON%行啊。一两个克朗，给你们尝上几口。别管桶口那些蜜蜂，你们一靠近，它们就散；可它们一散，你们要是也跟着乱窜，它们可就追着你们跑了。古怪的小东西。%SPEECH_OFF%你问他到底要多少钱。%SPEECH_ON%我看每人十克朗就成。不过我不是生意人，这价钱兴许还亏待了自己呢。%SPEECH_OFF%

a350559834d145bc8cad.source: A round for the whole company!

3468dd5dd266d075f874.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]You agree to pay the man what he's asked for and he opens his arm in invitation. Your men pop the lid off the cask and dip their cups in. They come to sit in the shade, sipping tankards and exchanging beers. The monk bids you a good farewell and the men all lift their cups to him in a loud, increasingly slurred cheer.
3468dd5dd266d075f874.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]你答应照价付钱，他张开手臂，示意请便。弟兄们揭开酒桶盖，伸杯舀酒，随后坐到阴凉处，端着大杯啜饮，互相敬酒。修士向你道别，众人纷纷举杯，响亮的欢呼也越来越含糊。

ab292295f98a5a22671c.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]You hold your hand up, stopping the monk before he can get going again. He sighs, slowly lowering the reins out of his hand. Feeling as though he may be getting the wrong impression, you quickly ask if maybe he has beer to spare for your men. You are more than willing to pay. The monk looks back at his stock for a moment, then turns around.%SPEECH_ON%Aye. Damn it to hells if the gods wouldn't be happy with yer money crossin' m'palms. If ye fight the good fight, then I bid you to take some for free, but not all of it of course.%SPEECH_OFF%You thank the monk for his generosity and order you men to be modest with their drinking. As a few brothers circle around to the cask, the monk throws his hands up.%SPEECH_ON%Don't mind the bees 'round the top, they'll scurry when you come, but if you scurry when they scurry, they'll scurry after ya. Strange little gits.%SPEECH_OFF%
ab292295f98a5a22671c.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]你抬手拦住修士，不让他继续赶路。他叹了口气，慢慢放下缰绳。你觉得他可能误会了，赶紧问是否有多余的啤酒可以卖给弟兄们，你愿意付钱。修士回头看了一眼车上的存货，又转过来。%SPEECH_ON%行啊，你们的钱交到我手里，诸神保准高兴得很。不过，你们若为正义而战，我就请你们免费喝些。当然，可不能全喝光。%SPEECH_OFF%你谢过修士的慷慨，吩咐弟兄们喝得节制些。几个人围到酒桶旁时，修士举起双手。%SPEECH_ON%别管桶口那些蜜蜂，你们一靠近，它们就散；可它们一散，你们要是也跟着乱窜，它们可就追着你们跑了。古怪的小东西。%SPEECH_OFF%

e924533c48a122e6e1b3.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]As the cart waddles by, you take the pommel of your sword and bash it against the cask of beer, popping the lid off the top and sending a number of bees into a frenzy. The monk lets go of the reins as he looks back at you.%SPEECH_ON%T'was afraid you'd do that.%SPEECH_OFF%The man disappears beneath a punch, his body twisting as he falls to the ground. A few brothers converge on him for some good kicks while others lift the beer and take it to some shade. You dip a mug into the cask for a drink then lift it to the monk writhing on the ground.%SPEECH_ON%Bottom's up lads, and let us not forget to thank our generous friend over there!%SPEECH_OFF%The monk turns over, eyes wincing as they rapidly blink. He's clutching his back with one hand while using the other to slowly get up. With a bent posture, he takes the reins of the donkey and starts forward. He tries to slip his hat back on but it falls away and he doesn't bother to go after it. The man grows small in the distance, blurred by horizon and alcohol alike, and then he is gone.

The men all lift their cups to you in a loud, increasingly slurred cheer.
e924533c48a122e6e1b3.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_40.png[/img]小货车晃悠悠地经过，你用剑柄猛砸酒桶，掀飞桶盖，也惊得几只蜜蜂乱成一团。修士松开缰绳，回头看你。%SPEECH_ON%我就怕你会这么做。%SPEECH_OFF%一记拳头将他打翻在地，身体扭着栽了下去。几个弟兄围上来狠狠踢打，另一些则把麦酒搬到阴凉处。你将杯子浸进桶里舀了一杯，喝上一口，又朝地上扭动的修士举起杯。%SPEECH_ON%弟兄们，干杯！别忘了感谢那边慷慨的朋友！%SPEECH_OFF%修士翻过身，痛得眯着眼，不停眨动。他一手捂着后背，另一手撑地，慢慢爬起来。随后，他弓着身子，牵住驴的缰绳，继续往前走。他试着把帽子戴回头上，可帽子又掉了，他也没再去捡。那人在远处越走越小，地平线和酒意一同模糊了他的身影，最后，他消失不见。

弟兄们纷纷朝你举杯，大声欢呼，话音随着酒意越来越含糊。

1c173551e148cdfda2b7.source: %townImage%Entering %townname%, it isn't long until %troublemaker% is bothering the locals. He's slapping buckets out of their hands and kicking women into the mud. When an old man confronts him, the sellsword draws out his weapon. Other peasants beg that you put a stop to this at once.
1c173551e148cdfda2b7.translation: %townImage%刚进%townname%不久，%troublemaker%就开始欺负当地人，打翻人家手里的水桶，把女人踹进烂泥。一个老人出面理论，佣兵却拔出了武器。其他农民恳求你立刻制止他。

49c3f49b00145bd4dc1d.source: I don't have time for this.

c591050b9d4979ee54ac.source: You need to stop this, %troublemaker%. It reflects badly on the company.
c591050b9d4979ee54ac.translation: %troublemaker%，收手吧。你在败坏战团的名声。

3e3bc8b6985f46fc4d75.source: Put the peasants in their place and search their homes for valuables!
3e3bc8b6985f46fc4d75.translation: 让那些农民认清自己的身份，再去他们家搜值钱的东西！

af6223f8191fe53e2a82.source:
%townImage%You shrug. %troublemaker% doesn't run the old man through, but he does threaten to, raising the weapon on high. When the old man cowers, the sellsword delivers a punch that knocks the elderly right out, his teeth peppering the muck like spits of white rain. This brings a few jeers from the villagers, but they know not to contest your presence any further.

A few men drag the elder away while children boo and women hiss. One child even runs up to the sellsword, pointing at him as he yells 'he's a bad man.' %troublemaker% shrugs as he sheathes his weapon.%SPEECH_ON%And yet the bad man still stands. Would you also like a taste of the mud, little one?%SPEECH_OFF%The kid quickly runs off.
af6223f8191fe53e2a82.translation:
%townImage%你耸耸肩。%troublemaker%并未真把老人刺穿，却高举武器，作势要动手。老人吓得缩起身，佣兵便一拳打去，将他当场打昏。牙齿像一阵白雨，零落撒进泥里。村民们发出几声嘘骂，却也明白，不能再反对你们待在这里。

几个男人把老人拖走，孩子们喝倒彩，女人们愤愤咒骂。一个孩子甚至跑到佣兵面前，指着他大喊“他是坏人”。%troublemaker%收起武器，耸了耸肩。%SPEECH_ON%可这坏人还好端端站着呢。小家伙，你也想尝尝泥巴的滋味？%SPEECH_OFF%孩子赶紧跑开了。

b477ed34efc19c7f2e91.source: Now on to things that actually matter...
b477ed34efc19c7f2e91.translation: 现在，说点真正要紧的事……

b46e46e82dfea10ca9c7.source:
%townImage%As %troublemaker% raises his weapon on high, you grab him by the forearm and bring it back down. He swings around, looking at you sternly. The cowering old man backs off, soon collected by caretakers that shuttle him back inside before he gets himself hurt.

A few other peasants linger around, watching with keen interest. You tell the sellsword to back down. He's paid to fight who you deem he should fight, not a bunch of peasants who are minding their own.

 As %troublemaker% glances around, you realize you've left him no 'out' that will save face. In his eyes, there is a look that says he's about to kill you. It'd be the end of him, but he'd go out with his suicidal pride intact. But the look fades, and embarrassment and humiliation take its place. He sheathes his weapon, spits, and remarks that he was only having some fun.
b46e46e82dfea10ca9c7.translation:
%townImage%%troublemaker%高高举起武器，你一把抓住他的前臂，压了下来。他猛地转身，冷冷地盯着你。瑟缩的老人往后退，很快被照料他的人扶住，赶在受伤前带回屋里。

还有几个农民留在附近，兴致勃勃地看着。你命令佣兵住手。他领钱，是来打你指定的敌人，不是欺负一群安分过日子的农民。

 %troublemaker%环视四周，你这才意识到，自己没给他留下任何保全面子的台阶。他眼神里有一股杀意，仿佛下一刻就要杀你。那样他必死无疑，却能带着这份不要命的傲气去死。不过，这道目光渐渐消退，取而代之的是尴尬与屈辱。他收起武器，啐了一口，嘟囔着自己不过是找点乐子。

71a7ef8ea7b95de13ee9.source: Save it for when we're paid to do this.
71a7ef8ea7b95de13ee9.translation: 等有人出钱雇我们干这事时再说。

3f39ee5ac4950b367f15.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_30.png[/img]You look at the peasant who hailed you down.%SPEECH_ON%Who are you, peasant, to tell me or my men what to do?%SPEECH_OFF%The man takes a step back, stammering something about 'only trying to help.' Laughing, you tell your men to take what they want. If this village has no respect for the authority of armed men, then you will have to teach them that respect.

Women scream and bundle up their children as the order leaves your tongue. They run off and a few men join them. Other men stay behind, protecting their homes, but the %companyname% makes quick work of their modest defenses. Your mercenaries are soon pillaging each and every home, taking what they can with roaring laughter. Today is a good day.
3f39ee5ac4950b367f15.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_30.png[/img]你望着那个出声叫住你的农民。%SPEECH_ON%你算什么东西，也配教我和我的弟兄做事？%SPEECH_OFF%那人退了一步，结结巴巴地说，自己“只是想帮忙”。你笑了，告诉弟兄们，想拿什么就拿什么。既然这个村子不懂得敬畏手握刀剑的人，你就亲自教会他们。

命令刚出口，女人们便尖叫着抱起孩子逃走，一些男人也跟着跑了。其余人留下保卫家园，可他们那点抵抗，很快就被%companyname%击垮。佣兵们放声大笑，挨家挨户洗劫，能拿多少就拿多少。今天真是个好日子。

de497e5e931be0bb7b86.source: %townImage%%peacekeeperfull% places himself between %troublemaker% and the old man. He shakes his head 'no' in a very modest fashion, but you can't help but notice that his swordhand is also on the pommel of his weapon. The troublemaking sellsword briefly seems to consider cutting the man down, but then a smile snaps across his face. He laughs as he sheathes his weapon.%SPEECH_ON%Only having a bit of fun, my brother.%SPEECH_OFF%The peasants slowly start going about their business again, but they are wary and stare side-eyed at your men for the rest of your duration in %townname%.
de497e5e931be0bb7b86.translation: %townImage%%peacekeeperfull%站到%troublemaker%与老人之间，温和地摇头制止。不过，你也注意到，他握剑的手正按在剑首上。惹事的佣兵似乎短暂考虑过砍倒他，随后脸上忽然绽出笑容，一边笑，一边收剑。%SPEECH_ON%弟兄，我就是逗个乐。%SPEECH_OFF%农民们慢慢恢复各自的营生，却仍心怀戒备。你们留在%townname%的这段时间里，他们始终斜眼盯着弟兄们。

1a577503f0dba3a91196.source:
%townImage%%peacekeeperfull% steps in between %troublemaker% and the old man. The troublemaking sellsword laughs and sheathes his weapon. He turns back to the rest of the company, grinning and shaking his head, but you notice that this smile quickly fades. Before you can say anything, %troublemaker% wheels a fist back around and knocks %peacekeeper% out cold.

 Well, that's one way to mollify a mercenary.
1a577503f0dba3a91196.translation:
%townImage%%peacekeeperfull%挡在%troublemaker%与老人之间。惹事的佣兵笑着收起武器，转向其余弟兄，咧嘴摇头。可你注意到，那笑容很快便消失了。还没来得及说话，%troublemaker%已经反手一拳，将%peacekeeper%打得当场昏厥。

好吧，这也算让一个佣兵安静下来了。

b969d802f75375c3a3f1.source: I might have to do something about discipline in this company.
b969d802f75375c3a3f1.translation: 看来得整顿一下战团的纪律了。

8d488d2548e336a07eb7.source: %peacekeeperfull%, see if you can calm %troublemaker% with your wisdom.
8d488d2548e336a07eb7.translation: %peacekeeperfull%，拿出你的智慧，看看能不能劝住%troublemaker%。

83ea510d88307bdbd76e.source: One of your men caused havoc in town
83ea510d88307bdbd76e.translation: 你的一个手下在镇上惹出了乱子

9534d2a161b6f8fdb0d6.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_50.png[/img]%juggernaut% carries a brand of courage one part fearless, one part craziness. His urgency to throw himself against his enemies is inspirational, if no doubt foolish to a mind of reason and rationality. But this is the %companyname%, a band of men who are drawn to the simple life of sword and coin. %juggernaut%'s indomitable nature in this struggle of kill or be killed has rubbed off on a few of the sellswords.
9534d2a161b6f8fdb0d6.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_50.png[/img]%juggernaut%的勇气，一半是无畏，一半是疯狂。他总急不可待地扑向敌人，在理智者看来固然愚蠢，却也鼓舞人心。毕竟，这是%companyname%，一群被刀剑与钱币的简单生活吸引来的男人。在这场不是杀人就是被杀的挣扎中，%juggernaut%那股不屈的劲头也感染了几名佣兵。

6a005ec95b73e9f0ceaf.source: This would be a mad world if all men were like him.
6a005ec95b73e9f0ceaf.translation: 人人都像他，这世道就疯了。

86c7b816e1cb35c119f5.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_16.png[/img]{Men of the road, %walker1% and %walker2% share stories of their travels with one another. You don't really understand what's so rich about walking about, but the two men do bond over their tales and that's good enough for you. | %walker1% and %walker2% have seen much of the world. They've spent years on the road, and now they're telling tales of those years to one another.

Their appreciation for each other rises, and your appreciation for not listening to boring travel stories also increases. | Most men find the task of walking about to be pretty simple, but men who do little else but walk about find more interest in the affair. Unsurprisingly, %walker1% and %walker2% have come to bond of their tales of... walking around.}
86c7b816e1cb35c119f5.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_16.png[/img]{常年在路上讨生活的%walker1%与%walker2%，正互相讲述旅途中的见闻。你不太明白，走来走去到底有什么好聊的。不过两人确实因此亲近了不少，这对你来说就够了。 | %walker1%和%walker2%见识过世上许多地方。他们在路上走了多年，如今正互相讲述那些年的故事。

两人愈发欣赏彼此，而你也愈发庆幸，自己不必听那些无聊的游记。 | 大多数人觉得，走路不过是件再简单不过的事。可那些除了走路几乎什么也不干的人，却能从中找出不少乐趣。于是，%walker1%和%walker2%果然因为互相讲述……四处走路的经历，而成了朋友。}

342a0bf4372fe8dc3cba.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]A series of barks followed by muted growling interrupts your work. You leave your tent to see that the two wardogs, %randomwardog1% and %randomwardog2% are fighting. They've locked their jaws onto the nape of each other's necks. A few brothers try to intervene, but every time they do the wardogs briefly separate and snap at the humans as if to say this fight is between them and them only.
342a0bf4372fe8dc3cba.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]一阵吠叫，接着是压低的咆哮，打断了你的工作。你走出帐篷，发现两条战犬%randomwardog1%与%randomwardog2%正在厮咬，彼此死死咬住后颈。几个弟兄试着干预，可每次一上前，狗便短暂分开，转头咬向人，仿佛在说：这是它们之间的事，谁也别插手。

1cd19ec0318ca68f2fae.source: Let the hounds sort it out themselves.

a5951c92b2c8c26ae572.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]You elect to stand back and let nature take its course. Once the dust settles, you step forward to see how everything shook out.
a5951c92b2c8c26ae572.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]你决定退在一旁，顺其自然。尘埃落定后，才上前查看结果。

b165acc53db799c53749.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]You yell at %otherbrother% to separate the two wardogs. He takes up a long stick and lowers it into the furred and furious melee. The dogs yelp as the metal comes between them. One takes hold of the pole-handle and rips it forward, dragging the brother into the fray. Man and beast blur together as all three fight for their own survival, each taking turns at fighting off the other. As the dust settles, you take stock of who or what is still standing.
b165acc53db799c53749.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]你大喊，让%otherbrother%把两条战犬分开。他拿起长杆，探进那团暴怒的毛球。金属伸进两狗之间，它们顿时尖叫。一条狗咬住杆柄猛地一拽，把弟兄也拖进了厮斗。人与兽滚作一团，三个都在拼命求生，轮番抵挡另外两个。等尘土散开，你才看清，究竟还有谁、还有什么站着。

5319f7f8cf3e6108e0a6.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]Unfortunately, both dogs passed away. They died with bloodied fur clenched in their jaws, each one sharing a sum of both victory and defeat. You have %randombrother% bury the bodies lest their smell attract even angrier beasts.
5319f7f8cf3e6108e0a6.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]可惜，两条狗都死了。断气时，嘴里还咬着对方沾血的毛皮，谁都赢了一半，也输了一半。你让%randombrother%埋掉尸体，免得气味招来更凶的野兽。

f6736c71ec86dcbf1dcf.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_27.png[/img]The battle over, you have %randombrother% take a look at the wardogs. They growl as he approaches, but that's all they got to muster for the fight has been kicked out of them. He reports on a few broken teeth and they each got a bit of a limp, but they ain't lame. In time, they'll be good as new for fighting. Hopefully, just not fighting one another...
f6736c71ec86dcbf1dcf.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_27.png[/img]厮斗结束，你让%randombrother%去看看战犬。他一靠近，狗便低吼，可也只剩这点力气，打架的劲早耗光了。他回来报告：断了几颗牙，两条狗都略有跛行，却未落下残疾。过些时日，它们就又能生龙活虎地上阵。只盼到时别再互咬……

04be3a3bd44246bdc78c.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]One wardog limps off from the melee, leaving behind a dead mutt. That the winner did not even eat or try to eat the loser shows all you need to know about these animals' namesake. You have %randombrother% take care of the survivor while a few other brothers bury the body of the departed.
04be3a3bd44246bdc78c.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_37.png[/img]一条战犬跛着腿离开，留下一具狗尸。胜者连吃掉败者的念头都没有，便足以说明它们为什么叫战犬。你让%randombrother%照料活下来的那条，其他几个弟兄则埋葬了死去的狗。

e938151d8b792082eb52.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]%otherbrother% manages to separate the two wardogs before they kill one another. Unfortunately, he paid a price heavy with bites and scratches. He'll survive, but you can't help but notice that he's very skittish and wary of the dogs now.
e938151d8b792082eb52.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_34.png[/img]%otherbrother%总算赶在两条战犬咬死对方前，将它们分开。可惜代价不轻，满身都是咬伤与抓痕。他死不了，不过你不难看出，如今他对狗格外紧张、戒备。

03bc07534d2b4bf96a6b.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_27.png[/img]You order %houndmaster% the houndmaster to do something. He nods and steps forward, calmly walking between the two fighting dogs. They bark and snap at each other, but both pause to eye the man coming in. One growls, but does in fact sit down. The other backs up, its tail wagging furiously, but there's still fire in its eyes. The houndmaster crouches down and pets them both on the head. One mutt lowers itself, and the other follows suit.

 The man slowly brings the dogs together, practically touching noses, and then whispers to them both. Slowly, but surely, the bestial energy leaves the dogs and their softened dispositions seem more fit for watching children than fighting in a mercenary band. The houndmaster gets back up and the dogs happily follow him. He nods.%SPEECH_ON%Just a small row between dogs, heh.%SPEECH_OFF%He walks off while the rest of the company looks on slackjawed, as if they'd just watched some kind of procession of druidic sorcery.
03bc07534d2b4bf96a6b.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_27.png[/img]你命令驯犬师%houndmaster%想想办法。他点头上前，从容地走到两条缠斗的狗之间。它们仍冲彼此吠叫撕咬，却都停了一下，打量这个走进来的男人。一条低吼着，却还是坐了下来；另一条往后退，尾巴摇得飞快，眼里却仍冒着火。驯犬师蹲下，分别摸了摸它们的脑袋。一条狗伏低身子，另一条也跟着照做。

 他缓缓把两条狗领到一起，让它们几乎鼻尖相触，接着低声对它们说起话。渐渐地，两条狗身上的凶性确实褪了下去，温顺得更像是照看孩子的家犬，而非跟着佣兵团厮杀的战犬。驯犬师站起身，两条狗欢快地跟在他身后。他点点头。%SPEECH_ON%狗之间的一点小口角罢了，嘿。%SPEECH_OFF%他走开了，战团其余人仍看得目瞪口呆，仿佛刚目睹了一场德鲁伊的施法仪式。

30cbe64b3d8ad5c60c46.source: A master of his craft, indeed.

2bfe8f95b9e20a81e291.source: %houndmaster%, you are a houndmaster, handle this!

1a7adeca8abcf03765ca.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_87.png[/img]The battle over, you look around at the destruction it had wrought. %deadbrother% is on his back, staring blankly at the skies with glazed eyes. Other brothers litter the battleground. They are ill-shaped, ragged, fractured and fragmented and soon fermented. It is a collectively cruel end. And now the flies are gathering, dotting the dead like skittering moles. They copulate on cold skin with shameless abandon and set about burrowing the next brood in the still-warm gore. %randombrother% walks up and asks what it is you wish to do with the bodies.
1a7adeca8abcf03765ca.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_87.png[/img]战斗结束，你环顾留下的惨状。%deadbrother%仰面躺着，失神的双眼茫然望天。其他弟兄散落战场，身躯扭曲、破碎、支离，接下来便要腐烂。这是他们共同迎来的残酷结局。苍蝇已经聚来，在死者身上爬动，像一颗颗游走的黑痣。它们肆无忌惮地在冰冷皮肤上交配，将下一窝后代埋进尚温的血肉。%randombrother%走上前，问你打算如何处置遗体。

b20fd35c808e1bb459ee.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_87.png[/img]You take a look up at the skies. Crows and archcrows circle overhead. They squall and sqwuak and bicker amongst one another as they await your departure. Sheathing your sword, you nod at the battleground.%SPEECH_ON%Loot the bodies. Leave the dead to the birds.%SPEECH_OFF%
b20fd35c808e1bb459ee.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_87.png[/img]你抬头望天，乌鸦与巨鸦盘旋其上，嘶叫争吵，等着你们离开。你收剑入鞘，朝战场点头。%SPEECH_ON%搜走尸体上的东西。死人留给鸟。%SPEECH_OFF%

eae4b6a229b55029573a.source: Tis a hungry world, after all.
eae4b6a229b55029573a.translation: 这世道，终究什么都吞得下。

99b3284d6b9eee5a8214.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_28.png[/img]You nod toward the dead.%SPEECH_ON%Those were some fine men and fine men get a fine burial. We'll honor them just as we should: a good hole to sleep in, crowns which they can spend in the next world, and a feast to celebrate. I'd expect the same to be done for me!%SPEECH_OFF%The surviving men cheer and begin preparations.
99b3284d6b9eee5a8214.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_28.png[/img]你朝死者点了点头。%SPEECH_ON%他们是好弟兄，好弟兄就该有场好葬礼。咱们按应有的礼数送他们：挖个好坑安睡，留些克朗去另一个世界花，再摆一顿酒席纪念。换成我，也盼你们这么办！%SPEECH_OFF%活着的弟兄齐声应和，开始准备。

32e5135eaf76de15732e.source: Now we can leave them to find their final rest.
32e5135eaf76de15732e.translation: 现在，可以让他们安息了。

4953a3b0e434965ea34a.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_28.png[/img]You assign the duty of burials to %gravedigger%, a man well-practiced for this particular trade. It doesn't take him long to shovel perfectly squared holes into the ground. He wraps the bodies in linens before carefully placing them into their final rests. When it's all said and done, the graves lay across the ground as though they were an earthly fenceline knocked astray. Each mound of dirt has a stake before it with the dead brother's name carved into the wood. %gravedigger% stands his shovel and tents his hands on the handle. He nods at his work.%SPEECH_ON%They're in deep.%SPEECH_OFF%The man spits.%SPEECH_ON%Only thing after 'em now be the worms. Hope that don't bother ya - but anywhere a man goes once he's dead there be a mouth in need of new feed. Lest you burn the bodies, I s'pose, but they say even then the spirits have their licks. Snortin' smoke is a spirit's spice or some such thing.%SPEECH_OFF%Picking up his shovel, the gravedigger turns and leaves as though both his work and words were but dreams upon dreams.
4953a3b0e434965ea34a.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_28.png[/img]你把安葬的差事交给%gravedigger%，他对这门行当很是熟悉。没多久，他就在地上挖出几个方方正正的坑。他先用亚麻布裹好尸身，再小心地将他们放进最后的安息之所。一切办妥后，坟冢横列在地上，仿佛一排歪倒的土栅栏。每座土堆前都立着木桩，上面刻着死去弟兄的名字。%gravedigger%竖起铲子，双手交搭在铲柄上，看着自己的活计点了点头。%SPEECH_ON%埋得够深了。%SPEECH_OFF%他啐了一口。%SPEECH_ON%现在能找上他们的，也就剩虫子了。但愿你别介意——人死之后，不管去了哪儿，总有张嘴等着吃点新鲜的。我想，除非把尸体烧了。不过听说就算烧了，鬼魂也能分上一口。吸几口烟，对它们来说就跟尝香料似的，反正差不多这个意思。%SPEECH_OFF%掘墓人提起铲子，转身离去，仿佛他刚做的事、说的话，都不过是梦中之梦。

e29ce44c0fed1dae5ea8.source: Well... may they rest in peace.

bc77aa9f4b8eb61a50d7.source: Dismayed that fallen comrades were left to rot on the battlefield
bc77aa9f4b8eb61a50d7.translation: 因阵亡的战友被遗弃在战场上腐烂而悲痛

c8e9fc899c773dba5b55.source: Glad to see fallen comrades receive a fine farewell
c8e9fc899c773dba5b55.translation: 欣慰于阵亡的战友得到了体面的送别

84c277b9ab60af41aa8b.source:
%townImage%Civilization is no place for a wildman like %wildman% and he quickly proves it.

Apparently, the damned man went crazy while in a shop and trashed the whole place. As the story goes, he just walked in and started taking things, not quite understanding the social norms of paying for goods. The shop owner then came after him with a broom, trying to shoo the man out of his store. Believing the broom a monster, the wildman proceeded to go completely crazy. Judging by the reports, it was quite the commotion, up to and including shite throwing.

Now the shop owner is in your face demanding compensation for the damage done. Apparently he's wanting %compensation% crowns. Behind him, a few town militia stand with very watchful eyes.
84c277b9ab60af41aa8b.translation:
%townImage%文明社会容不下%wildman%这样的荒野人，而他很快就亲自证明了这一点。

据说，这家伙在商店里发了疯，把店砸了个稀烂。事情的起因是，他一进门就直接拿东西，根本不懂买货要付钱的规矩。店主拿起扫帚追赶，想把他轰出去。荒野人却把扫帚当成了怪物，彻底失控。照旁人的说法，当时闹得鸡飞狗跳，连扔粪这样的事都干出来了。

现在，店主正堵在你面前，要求赔偿损失，开价%compensation%克朗。他身后站着几个镇民兵，警惕地盯着你。

3a8e410436fbc5932d20.source: Fine, the company will cover the damages.

f98994b1eacc88f771da.source: Fine, the company will cover the damages - but %wildman% will work it off.
f98994b1eacc88f771da.translation: 行，战团先赔损失，不过%wildman%得干活抵债。

21820e3d4dc8834963a0.source: %townImage%You push the shop owner away, telling him that you owe nothing. When he jumps forward again, your hand deftly moves to the pommel of your sword, stopping the man in one swift motion. He raises his hands up, nodding as he backs off. A few townspeople see this and skirt by, trying to avoid your gaze. The militiamen notice, but they seem uncertain on whether to take action or not.
21820e3d4dc8834963a0.translation: %townImage%你推开店主，告诉他自己一分钱也不欠。他再次扑上前时，你的手迅速按住剑首，只一个动作就让他刹住脚。他举起双手，边点头边后退。几个镇民看见这一幕，绕着走开，尽量避开你的目光。民兵也注意到了，却似乎拿不准要不要出手。

df86edcd48842c16899d.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_01.png[/img]You go and see the shop. The wildman truly did a number on the place. And it reeks of his... scent. It would be a bad look for the company to not handle this issue with great care. You agree to pay for the damages, something most mercenary bands would not have done. This act of kindness does not slip the townspeople by.
df86edcd48842c16899d.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_01.png[/img]你去店里看了看。荒野人确实把这里折腾得够呛，还留下满屋他的……气味。若不妥善处理，会很伤战团名声。你答应赔偿损失，这是大多数佣兵团不会做的事。镇民们把这份善意看在了眼里。

71d14b4227d62051bfac.source:
%townImage%Surveying the damage, you agree to compensate the businessman. But this isn't your fault, it's the wildman's. You dock his pay: for some time to come, the mercenary's earnings will be halved. Furthermore, you take what earnings he's made and hand them over to the shop owner. It doesn't even begin to cover the damages, but it's a start. One man is left happy, and another quite disgruntled.

You tell the wild cretin that now he'll think twice about smearing shit all over someone else's walls. But the wildman doesn't seem to understand you. He just understands that the gold he once owned has been given to someone else, and he eyes its departure with sadness and bottled anger.
71d14b4227d62051bfac.translation:
%townImage%查看过损失后，你答应赔偿店主。不过，闯祸的是荒野人，又不是你。你扣了他的薪水：接下来一段日子，他的工钱减半。此外，你还把他已经挣到的钱拿来，交给了店主。这点钱离赔足损失还差得远，但好歹算个开头。一个人满意了，另一个却满腹怨气。

你告诉这野蛮的蠢货，下回往别人墙上抹屎之前，总该多想一想了。可荒野人似乎根本听不懂。他只明白，原本属于自己的金子给了别人，便满怀悲伤与压抑的怒气，目送它们离开。

4707920acec0abb7d99d.source: Don't look at me like that, you know what you did.
4707920acec0abb7d99d.translation: 别这么看着我，你知道自己干了什么。

189d1c205289b08bd71f.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_141.png[/img]While leaving town, you hear a bark over your shoulder. But it is from no dog: you turn 'round to find a number of militiamen converging on the road, fanning out from homes and shops. They say you did that businessman wrong and they won't be having your kind in a place like this no more. You can either pay up right now, or they'll take it from you by force.
189d1c205289b08bd71f.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_141.png[/img]离镇时，身后响起一声厉喝，却不是狗叫。你转身，只见一群民兵从房屋和店铺间涌出，在路上聚拢。他们说，你亏待了那位店主，这地方再也容不下你们这种人。要么现在赔钱，要么他们动手来拿。

b6192c11fb332058bfbc.source: A shame it had to come to this.
b6192c11fb332058bfbc.translation: 真遗憾，竟闹到了这一步。

75e18faecfb270c37e9b.source: Fine. I did not wake up this morning looking to slaughter innocents.
75e18faecfb270c37e9b.translation: 好吧，我今早起来可没打算屠杀无辜。

37bb337d77dba43d6a22.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_141.png[/img]The men before you are weak and frail, a force cobbled together out of the meek and downtrodden. Nowhere in their ranks is the actual businessman you had trouble with. While you admire their tenacity, you can't quite bring yourself to slaughter half a town over a rather small affair. You reach to your side, drawing a few gasps from the poorly armed crowd of men, only to return your hand with a purse in its palm. A deal is struck and the compensation is paid. The townspeople are relieved, though a few of the men are not so happy about backing down from a fight.
37bb337d77dba43d6a22.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_141.png[/img]面前这些人瘦弱不堪，是一群受尽欺压的老实人勉强拼凑起来的队伍。真正跟你起冲突的那个商人，反倒不在其中。你钦佩他们的韧性，却实在不愿为这么点小事屠掉半个镇子。你伸手摸向腰侧，装备简陋的人群里顿时响起几声惊呼，可你收回手时，掌中只有一个钱袋。双方谈妥，赔偿付清。镇民们松了口气，不过，你有几个手下对这次退让颇为不满。

36612196d3fcee53b739.source: You refused to pay for damages caused by one of your men
36612196d3fcee53b739.translation: 你拒绝赔偿手下造成的损失

142273e20c8c4ae91907.source: You killed some of the militia

cff27809c104ffa8f6a8.source: The company backed down from a fight
cff27809c104ffa8f6a8.translation: 战团在冲突面前选择了退让

7e0d00d371fdd1337e28.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_25.png[/img]While trying not to lose your temper at just how many low-hanging branches are catching you in the face, %otherguy% hurries to your side and says %wildman% the wildman has run off. You turn round to see the rest of the men looking as confused as you are. Holding your fist up to quiet the company, the forest returns your order of silence with muted chirps of distant birds and the buzz of a bee or wasp somewhere unseen. Shaking your head, you decide to continue the march.

A few hours later, the wildman jumps out of a bush you were about to cleave with a machete. He's got an armful of random items in hand. Where he got these things, you've no idea, but you have the men sift through the findings. %wildman% returns to rank as though nothing happened at all. You glance at the man and catch him staring at a butterfly on his finger. When you glance at him again, the butterfly is gone and the man is swallowing something. %otherguy% gives you a report on what he brought.
7e0d00d371fdd1337e28.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_25.png[/img]低垂的树枝一次又一次刮到你脸上，你正强压着火气，%otherguy%匆匆赶到身边，说荒野人%wildman%跑没影了。你回头一看，其余弟兄也和你一样茫然。你举起拳头，示意战团安静。回应这道命令的，只有远处微弱的鸟鸣，以及不知藏在哪儿的一只蜜蜂或黄蜂的嗡嗡声。你摇摇头，决定继续行军。

几个小时后，你正要挥砍刀劈开一丛灌木，荒野人突然从里面跳了出来，怀里抱着一堆杂七杂八的东西。你完全不知道他从哪儿弄来的，不过还是叫弟兄们清点一下。%wildman%若无其事地回到队列。你瞥了他一眼，见他正盯着停在手指上的蝴蝶。再看时，蝴蝶已经不见了，他正在往下咽什么东西。%otherguy%过来向你汇报了他带回的物件。

624245fda07ccdd2d80b.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_25.png[/img]You take a rest at the base of an enormous tree. Somehow, the sun manages to sear a path through the forest canopy and blind your eyes. Getting up to move, you run into %wildman% the wildman. He's offering you a handful of various questionables: mushrooms, flower petals, berries. With a grunt, he ushers them toward your face.
624245fda07ccdd2d80b.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_25.png[/img]你在一棵大树下歇息。太阳不知怎的，硬是穿过浓密树冠，刺得你睁不开眼。你起身想换个地方，却碰上荒野人%wildman%。他递来一把可疑的东西：蘑菇、花瓣、浆果，样样都有。低哼一声，他又把它们往你脸前凑了凑。

da2508780c58d3f83006.source: Sure, %wildman%, I'll take some of those.

19fcc01568032f29b20e.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_25.png[/img]Surprisingly, the bits of forest foods are actually quite good. Sweet, but not too sweet, and with a hint of oak. You thank teh weeldman fore his gift. He rises hyyy into the skies, the skies of all things, shaking what are noww braanches you had earlier mistakenly assumed were human arms of humane purposes. Cats rain from his mouth as he speaks. His tongue is a leenguage of marbled letters, floating before his lips innn.. innn... in great sighs for sentences. Feeling good about his graces, you give him a weave, a wave of yer hand, but find yer fingers are also hands, something you had not noticed in the befores. A shock to your beliefs, yer memories of childhood flooded with fleeting feet rocking yer crib, yer domain, yer castle. All lies. All of it! Blackness comes. The darkness smiles.

You awake on the ground, %otherguy% gently dabbing a rag of water over your forehead.%SPEECH_ON%He's back! You alright?%SPEECH_OFF%You can't quite remember what happened, but your mind is desperately telling you not to ask. You simply nod in response and get the men back to marching.
19fcc01568032f29b20e.translation:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_25.png[/img]出乎意料，这些林间小食竟相当美味。甜，却不腻，还带着一丝橡木的气息。你向那荒、荒野人道了个谢，谢他的礼物。他升得高——高起来，升到天上，偏偏就是天上，摇着如今成了树枝的东西；你先前竟误以为那是人的胳膊，会干人该干的事。他开口说话，猫从嘴里下雨般落出来。他的舌头是一种由大理石字母组成的语、语言，在唇前飘着，在……在……一声声长叹里连成句子。你觉得他这番恩赐很好，便向他挥、挥了挥手，却发现手指也全是手，这是从前的从前里从没注意过的事。你的认知猛地崩裂，童年记忆汹涌而来，闪过的一只只脚摇着你的摇篮、你的领地、你的城堡。全是假的，全都是！漆黑降临。黑暗微笑。

你在地上醒来，%otherguy%正拿湿布轻轻擦着你的额头。%SPEECH_ON%他醒了！你还好吧？%SPEECH_OFF%你记不清出了什么事，可脑子正拼命劝你别问。你只点点头，便叫弟兄们继续赶路。

70b2e31b1b3587df0ffb.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_04.png[/img]You find %wildman% the wildman stacking his crowns into towers. He leans back from his moneyed manifestations with a wide grin, but then suddenly launches forward, knocking the towers over like a child would their blocks. He laughs maniacally as the coins scatter. The man playing with his money is a curious sight. Perhaps the wildman has no real conception of what crowns are good for? If so, maybe... maybe you could take them back?
70b2e31b1b3587df0ffb.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_04.png[/img]你发现荒野人%wildman%正拿克朗垒塔。他退后欣赏这些金钱造物，咧嘴大笑，随后又突然扑上前，像孩子推积木一样将塔撞倒，任硬币四散，笑得近乎癫狂。拿钱这么玩，倒也稀奇。或许他根本不懂克朗有什么用？真要如此，也许……也许你能把钱拿回来？

b1e1ae866896b429acb3.source: Let's see if he'll trade it all away for something else.
b1e1ae866896b429acb3.translation: 看看他肯不肯拿这些钱全换成别的东西。

773ab3a1966d9157cde6.source: Better to leave the man and his crowns alone.
773ab3a1966d9157cde6.translation: 还是别打他和他那些克朗的主意了。

227469f7b8753ab3b5ad.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_04.png[/img]You crouch down.%SPEECH_ON%Hey there %wildman%. Mind if I take one of these?%SPEECH_OFF%Carefully, you pick up a coin and measure the wildman's reaction. He shrugs and grunts as if to say 'it's yours'. You take another crown. And then another. The wildman glares at you, but you slowly produce a stick with a frilly bow tied to the top. Its whirly nature captures the wildman's eye. When he reaches out for it, you draw it back and shake your head. You then point at the crowns, and then at the stick.%SPEECH_ON%One for the other, yes?%SPEECH_OFF%The wildman looks at his crowns, mulling them over like an accountant, but you know his thoughts are far more chaotic than that. Suddenly, he growls and pushes his crowns forward and takes the stick away from you. Looks like the trade is done.
227469f7b8753ab3b5ad.translation: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_04.png[/img]你蹲下身。%SPEECH_ON%嘿，%wildman%，我拿一枚，可以吧？%SPEECH_OFF%你小心捡起一枚钱币，观察荒野人的反应。他耸耸肩，哼了一声，像在说“归你了”。你又拿一枚克朗，再拿一枚。荒野人瞪着你，你却慢慢取出一根棍子，顶端系着花哨的蝴蝶结。花结转动，吸引了他的目光。他伸手要拿，你便收回，摇摇头，再指指克朗，又指指棍子。%SPEECH_ON%拿这个换那个，懂吗？%SPEECH_OFF%荒野人看着钱，像个账房先生般权衡起来，可你知道，他脑子里的念头可比那混乱得多。忽然，他低吼一声，把钱推过来，夺走你手中的棍子。看来，交易完成了。

6e50bdc56de53d3733ef.source:
[img]gfx/ui/events/event_06.png[/img]You crouch down and look at the mess of crowns.%SPEECH_ON%Those are real shiny, huh?%SPEECH_OFF%The wildman grunts and tries to shoo you away. Resisting, you pick up a crown. His hands drop and he jerks his head up, glaring at you. Slowly, you put the coin down and then produce a stick with a string wrapped around its top. His stare slackens, the sturdy stick a slick treat to the unkempt wildman. You motion that you'll give it to him in exchange for the crowns. He takes the stick. You take the crowns.

 But when the wildman plays with the string, it falls off and blows away in the wind. He cries out, then stares murderously at you, yourself standing there with both arms barreled to try and hold all the crowns. The wildman screams. You drop the crowns and run as fast as you can.
