Ironically, he hates the notion of you being a father figure to him, and you always tell him you'd never father a son so ugly to begin with. You keep in touch to this day.
3898807f3f169b024db1.translation: %name%从一开始就跟着你，退役时也一样：你离开后不久，他便退出了战团。但他还没过够刀口舔血的日子，于是又为另一支战团而战——他自己的战团。在你的带领下，他学到了许多，如今的成就让你像看着儿子出息一样骄傲。有趣的是，他最讨厌你摆出父亲般的架势，而你总会回敬一句：自己才生不出这么丑的儿子。直到今天，你们仍保持着联系。

578791b9e5829f19f759.source: With you from the start, %name% was as loyal as he was talented. He stayed with the company for a time before eventually leaving to forge out a path for himself. The other day, you received a letter from the mercenary stating that he had started his own company and was in dire need of help. Unfortunately, the message was dated to nearly a full year ago. When you investigated the existence of his company, you learned that it had been completely annihilated in a battle between nobles.
578791b9e5829f19f759.translation: %name%从一开始就跟着你，本领出众，忠心也同样可贵。他在战团又待了一阵，最终离开，去闯自己的路。前几天，你收到他的一封信，说自己已经建立了战团，眼下急需援助。可惜，信上的日期已经是将近一年前了。你打听那支战团的下落，才得知他们早已在一场贵族之间的战斗中全军覆没。

f0c1b3dab76bd3c22654.source: %name% is not known to be a big talker, but he has every right to be. {He's saved the lives of both %2h% and %ranged%. | He once spared you from an orc's wicked chain. | An assassin would have killed you in a pub were it not for this man. | A misfired crossbow nearly took out your eye - hadn't %name%'s shield been there to stop it. | He once pushed two men off a cliff using only his shield and two strong legs. | He learned how to fight from his father, a vanguard at the Battle of Many Names. | Sacrificing his family's heirloom - an old shield of wood and studded iron - he saved your life. | A man of rather consistent heroism, he pulled a drunken %2h% from a pub fire. | Faced with a horde of goblins, he used his shield and strength to push a hole in their lines, opening the way for %2h% and %ranged% to kill them all.} With quick whirls and whips of his shield, the man's deflected all manner of mortal danger. Although rather quiet, you've found %name%'s place in a shield-wall to be rather indispensable.
f0c1b3dab76bd3c22654.translation: %name%向来话不多，但他完全有资格夸夸自己的本事。{他救过%2h%和%ranged%的命。 | 他曾把你从兽人挥来的铁链下救出来。 | 要不是他出手，你早就被酒馆里的一名刺客杀了。 | 一支误射的弩矢险些夺走你的一只眼睛，幸亏%name%的盾牌及时挡住了它。 | 他曾只凭一面盾牌和两条有力的腿，将两个人推下悬崖。 | 他的武艺传自父亲——众名之战中的一名先锋战士。 | 他毁掉了家传的一面钉铁木盾，却救下了你的命。 | 他总能做出英勇的壮举，曾把喝得烂醉的%2h%从失火的酒馆里拖出来。 | 面对一大群地精，他凭盾牌和蛮力冲破敌阵，为%2h%和%ranged%打开了缺口，让他们将敌人斩尽杀绝。}那面盾牌在他手中腾挪翻转，挡下过种种致命威胁。尽管%name%不爱说话，你早已明白，盾墙中少不了他的身影。

a0bef469b57406d464ec.source: Brooding and at times suicidal, it's no surprise that %name% is frequently found diving into battle with nothing more than a large two-hander. {Clothed in murderous intent, you once saw him cleave a man in two - top to bottom. | It is said that he once cleaved a warrior orc in two, leaving the trunk of its legs still standing. | The man is known to ignore the fragility of his own mortality just to end the life of another. | He thrives being in the thick of battle where he can swing his weapons with little regard for safety or accuracy. | Supposedly, he once won a jousting tournament, but had to flee after bedding a watching nobleman's wife. | The man is not a murderer, but he would have made a fine one. | Seemingly unstoppable at times, you are glad to have the man on your side. | In a fit of bloodthirsty rage he once impaled two goblins on one pike. | A strong brute, you once saw %name% kill someone just on his backswing.} He'll use any weapon you give him, but %name% has a proclivity towards those that can make calamitous ruin out of a man's body.
a0bef469b57406d464ec.translation: %name%沉默阴郁，有时甚至像在求死，因此常常只带一柄巨大的双手武器就冲进战场，也就不足为奇了。{你曾见他杀气腾腾，一刀将人从头到脚劈成两半。 | 据说他曾把一名兽人战士拦腰斩断，下半身却还直挺挺地立着。 | 为了结束别人的性命，他向来不把自己的血肉之躯当回事。 | 他在乱战深处如鱼得水，尽情挥舞武器，全不顾安危，也不怎么在乎准头。 | 据说他曾在骑枪比武中夺冠，却因睡了一位观赛贵族的妻子，不得不逃之夭夭。 | 他不是个杀人狂，不过真要当起来，一定是个出色的杀人狂。 | 他有时简直势不可挡，你很庆幸他站在自己这边。 | 一次杀红了眼时，他曾用一根长枪串起两只地精。 | 这家伙力大如牛，你曾见%name%只在回收武器时顺势一挥，便取了一人的性命。}你给什么武器，他都能用，不过%name%尤其偏爱那些能把人砍得惨不忍睹的家伙。

fd4a056225f22822eaf3.source: %name% is one of the more talented marksman you've encountered in your travels. {After he saved your life with an arrow into the heart of a would-be assassin, you hired the man on the spot. | Learning of the man was easy - you just had to find the winner of a local shooting competition. | He once won an archery contest that had over a hundred participants from all the lands. | It is said that he can split an arrow - mid-flight. | You found the man on a farm where, obviously, you thought his shooting talents were going to waste. | A poacher, a bowyer, an archer, the man's skills have gotten plenty of use. You suspect he readily accepted your offer for mercenary work just to say 'he's done it all'. | You once saw him shoot the moon, but that may have been some sort of trick. | A clever bowman, he once loosed two arrows simultaneously to kill a charging set of brigands.} While he has a fondness for killing from afar, %name%'s no slouch in close-quarters combat.
fd4a056225f22822eaf3.translation: 在你旅途中遇到的射手里，%name%算是最有天赋的几人之一。{他一箭射穿了企图刺杀你的凶手的心脏，救下你的性命，你当场就雇了他。 | 想找到他很容易，只需打听当地射击比赛的冠军是谁。 | 他曾在一场汇集各地百余名参赛者的射箭比赛中夺冠。 | 据说他能劈开一支箭——还在半空飞着的箭。 | 你在一座农场发现了他，显而易见，他的射术在那儿完全是浪费。 | 偷猎者、制弓匠、弓箭手，他的本事在许多行当里都派过用场。你怀疑他痛快答应来当佣兵，只是为了日后能说一句“我什么都干过”。 | 你曾见他射中过月亮，不过那也许是某种障眼法。 | 这个机灵的弓手曾同时射出两支箭，杀死了一对迎面冲来的强盗。}虽然喜欢在远处取敌性命，%name%的近身格斗也绝不含糊。

127fdd857b68b5026e72.source: Who this man once was no longer matters. He now bears the mark of Davkul on his forehead and while his lips do not yet know the words of his newfound religion, they speak of the cult's fascination in a familiar tongue. Darkness, he says, is coming.
127fdd857b68b5026e72.translation: 这个男人过去是谁，已经不重要了。如今，他额头上烙着达夫库尔的印记，虽然还不熟悉新信仰的祷词，却已用熟悉的语言述说起教团令人着迷之处。他说，黑暗就要降临。

38cbcac7f0aea775e201.source: The only thing swift about a cripple is his expected demise in a real battle.
38cbcac7f0aea775e201.translation: 残疾人唯一迅速的，恐怕就是他在真正战斗中丧命的速度。

c31dd121325acabaed1a.source: It's shocking that a man of %name%'s stature survived at all, but the cripple did retire from the %companyname% with a sizeable stack of crowns. He runs an orphanage these days, spending his crowns to help the world's broken and abandoned children. That, or it's just a front for cheap labor. Can't be too sure these days.
c31dd121325acabaed1a.translation: 以%name%的身体状况，能活下来就已令人惊讶，可这残疾人竟带着一大笔克朗从%companyname%退役了。如今他经营着一家孤儿院，拿积蓄帮助那些伤残或被遗弃的孩子。又或者，这只是招揽廉价劳力的幌子。如今这世道，谁说得准呢。

7bbe44a35eb3d51b9911.source: When you left the %companyname%, there was one thing you were almost certain of: that damned cripple, %name%, wouldn't last long. Despite all odds, he did survive. Long enough in fact to retire himself, albeit departing with about as many crowns as he had when he joined up. You've no idea what became of him, but surely he's dead by now. Surely, right?
7bbe44a35eb3d51b9911.translation: 你离开%companyname%时，有一件事几乎可以断定：%name%那个该死的残废撑不了多久。可他偏偏活了下来，甚至还熬到了退役，虽然走时口袋里的克朗和来时差不多。后来他怎么样了，你一无所知，不过现在肯定已经死了吧。肯定的，对吧？

b74203876059e5ccd9d4.source: Is always content with being in reserve
b74203876059e5ccd9d4.translation: 担任后备队员时始终安于现状

6ef2da531b22a36f3528.source: %name% {hobbles toward you like a mangy dog | greets you with a hand missing numerous fingers | smiles at you with a toothless grin | carries the slouching posture of a man with a broken back | wobbles on two very stiff, possibly even wooden legs | uses a cane to walk toward you | crawls toward you at first, but then rises to his feet with all the grace of a drunk on church steps | has bones that creak and croak with every step | carries an arm in a sling, and has a cane standing in support for one of his legs | has a smashed nose and two blackened eyes | looks like someone tried to scalp and burn him alive | has flesh that smells partly cooked, his eyes wincing with every step he takes toward you | is missing two ears, though the holes still hear | reeks of shit and urine | is missing one eye, and the other wanders severely | has two lazy eyes and a crooked, gap-filled smile}. He explains that {he was once a mason, but that he was attacked by a madman for trying to replicate his work | he once donned armor as a knight, but that cruel fate has taken all of that from him | once upon a time he was a nobleman, but his poor vocabulary suggests this may be a lie | he was a peddler once, but the sale of a lobo-rail ended with him at the mercy of an angry town mob | he dabbled in cultism, but when he bailed they punished him for it | he was once a monk, but {cultists attacked his church | a spat with other monks had him severely punished | brigands attacked him for crucifying one of their own} | he used to brawl for lords, but a beatdown by other fighters left him crippled | he used to wander the land for jousting tournaments, but a bad tourney ended with him horribly crippled | he used to rob graves, but when he got caught a parishioner broke more of his bones than he knew a skeleton even had | he dabbled in {the arcane arts | necromancy} but, made obvious by his near-deathly state, that experiment was shortlived | he was once a successful gambler, but as it turns out not paying back your debts is bad for business - and your bones | he once sang as a minstrel, but when his voice gave out mid-song a lord had him brutally tortured | he used to catch rats for a living, but apparently a giant rat paid him a vengeful visit in the night | he once served a lord, but after dropping a plate of food he was sent to the dungeons where he was promptly forgotten for years | he once killed a man, sure, but that he deserved a better fate than the irreversible torture he received as punishment | he used to hunt witches, but a cruel mistress tricked him into drinking a concoction which crippled his very bones | he once deserted an army and, obviously, got caught | he used to juggle for royalty until he accidentally fell down some steps in the middle of a stunt. The steps proved rather edgy against his bones, it seems | he was born with a horrific deformity | his father brutally attacked him for not living up to his image | his mother scarred him with endless torture | his siblings tortured him all his life}. {The man looks so weak you can almost see his mortal coil flapping in the wind. | Hiring him would almost certainly be the man's doom. How merciful! | You don't want to be seen as hiring just anybody, but if this guy is a nobody, does that still count as 'anybody'? | You've seen dead people who look better than this man. | This guy is wolf-lunch on two legs. | The good news is that if he comes back from the dead he shouldn't be too hard to put down a second time. | Dreams and inanimate objects are more threatening than this poor git. | To be honest, you'd rather hire a child, but apparently people look down on that so here we are instead. | And you thought %randombrother% smelled bad. | Hiring a man such as this would send anyone's moral compass spinning. | Oh c'mon, look at him! Are the %companyname% really that in need of warm bodies? | Hiring this man just wouldn't be right. Whelp, here goes. | A pair of crutches has more value than this poor man. | This man is in such a sorry state he can play dead standing up.}
6ef2da531b22a36f3528.translation: %name%{像条癞皮狗一样，一瘸一拐地朝你走来 | 用一只缺了好几根手指的手向你致意 | 朝你咧嘴一笑，嘴里一颗牙也没有 | 耷拉着身子，仿佛脊梁已经折断 | 晃晃悠悠地站在两条僵硬的腿上，那两条腿说不定根本就是木头做的 | 拄着手杖向你走来 | 起初是朝你爬过来的，随后才挣扎起身，那姿态活像个醉倒在教堂台阶上的酒鬼 | 每走一步，骨头就嘎吱嘎吱地响 | 一条胳膊吊在布带里，另一边还得靠手杖撑住一条腿 | 鼻梁塌陷，两只眼睛乌青 | 看上去像被人剥过头皮，还险些活活烧死 | 皮肉散发着半熟的气味，每朝你走一步，都会疼得眯起眼睛 | 两只耳朵都没了，不过耳洞还能听见声音 | 浑身散发着屎尿的恶臭 | 缺了一只眼，另一只也斜得厉害 | 两眼无神，笑起来嘴歪牙缺}。他解释说，{自己原本是个石匠，只因想仿造一个疯子的作品，就遭到了对方的袭击 | 自己也曾披甲为骑士，可残酷的命运夺走了他的一切 | 自己曾是贵族，不过他言辞粗鄙，这话恐怕不真 | 自己曾是个小贩，却因兜售“狼轨车”，落到了镇上一群愤怒的暴民手里 | 自己曾混迹邪教，后来想退出，便遭到他们的惩罚 | 自己曾是一名修士，后来却因{邪教徒袭击教堂 | 与其他修士争吵而遭受重罚 | 将一名强盗钉上十字架，遭到其同伙报复}而落得这般下场 | 自己曾替领主打拳取乐，后来被别的拳手一顿毒打，成了残废 | 自己曾四处参加骑枪比武，直到一场糟糕的赛事将他伤成了这样 | 自己曾以盗墓为生，被逮住后，一个教徒打断了他全身的骨头，比他原以为人身上能有的骨头还多 | 自己曾涉猎{奥术 | 死灵术}，可从眼下这副半死不活的模样来看，那场试验显然没能持续多久 | 自己曾是个常胜的赌徒，后来才明白，欠债不还既伤财，也伤筋动骨 | 自己曾是一名吟游诗人，有一回唱到一半失了声，一位领主便命人对他施以酷刑 | 自己曾靠捕鼠为生，不过似乎有只巨鼠在夜里登门报了仇 | 自己曾侍奉一位领主，却因摔了一盘食物被关进地牢，随后便被忘在里面好几年 | 自己确实杀过人，但也不该受到那般酷刑，落下一辈子治不好的伤 | 自己曾猎杀女巫，却被一个狠毒的女人骗着喝下药水，连骨头都废了 | 自己曾从军中逃跑，结果嘛，显然是被逮住了 | 自己曾为王族表演杂耍，直到某次耍把戏时不慎摔下台阶。看来那些台阶的棱角，可比他的骨头硬多了 | 自己生来就有严重的畸形 | 父亲嫌他不成器，对他施以毒打 | 母亲无休止地折磨他，留下了满身伤疤 | 兄弟姐妹从小到大都在虐待他}。{他虚弱得仿佛一阵风就能将魂吹走。 | 雇下他，几乎就等于送他去死。真是慈悲啊！ | 你不想让人觉得自己什么人都收，不过要是这家伙压根算不上个“人”，还算“什么人”吗？ | 你见过的死人都比他气色好。 | 这家伙就是一份长了两条腿的狼食。 | 好消息是，万一他死后又爬起来，再放倒一次应该不难。 | 一个梦，甚至一件不会动的东西，都比这可怜虫更有威胁。 | 说实话，你宁可雇个孩子。可惜大家似乎对此颇有微词，所以只好考虑眼前这位了。 | 你原先还以为%randombrother%身上的味道够难闻了。 | 雇用这样的人，换了谁都得好好掂量掂量自己的良心。 | 拜托，看看他！%companyname%真的已经缺人缺到只要还喘气就行了吗？ | 雇这个人实在说不过去。唉，算了，还是雇吧。 | 一副拐杖都比这可怜人更有用。 | 他这副惨样，站着都能装死。}

Are the %companyname% really that in need of warm bodies? | Hiring this man just wouldn't be right. Whelp, here goes. | A pair of crutches has more value than this poor man. | This man is in such a sorry state he can play dead standing up.}
aa156f58c587d95c943f.translation: %name%{像条癞皮狗一样，一瘸一拐地朝你走来 | 用一只缺了好几根手指的手向你致意 | 朝你咧嘴一笑，嘴里一颗牙也没有 | 耷拉着身子，仿佛脊梁已经折断 | 晃晃悠悠地站在两条僵硬的腿上，那两条腿说不定根本就是木头做的 | 拄着手杖向你走来 | 起初是朝你爬过来的，随后才挣扎起身，那姿态活像个醉倒在教堂台阶上的酒鬼 | 每走一步，骨头就嘎吱嘎吱地响 | 一条胳膊吊在布带里，另一边还得靠手杖撑住一条腿 | 鼻梁塌陷，两只眼睛乌青 | 看上去像被人剥过头皮，还险些活活烧死 | 皮肉散发着半熟的气味，每朝你走一步，都会疼得眯起眼睛 | 两只耳朵都没了，不过耳洞还能听见声音 | 浑身散发着屎尿的恶臭 | 缺了一只眼，另一只也斜得厉害 | 两眼无神，笑起来嘴歪牙缺}。他解释说，{自己原本是个石匠，只因想仿造一个疯子的作品，就遭到了对方的袭击 | 自己也曾披甲为骑士，可残酷的命运夺走了他的一切 | 自己曾是维齐尔，不过他言辞粗鄙，这话恐怕不真 | 自己曾是个小贩，却因兜售“狼轨车”，落到了镇上一群愤怒的暴民手里 | 自己曾混迹邪教，后来想退出，便遭到他们的惩罚 | 自己曾替骄奢淫逸的商人打拳取乐，后来被别的拳手一顿毒打，成了残废 | 自己曾在角斗场搏杀，直到一场糟糕的比赛将他伤成了这样 | 自己曾以盗墓为生，被逮住后，一个教徒打断了他全身的骨头，比他原以为人身上能有的骨头还多 | 自己曾涉猎{奥术 | 死灵术}，可从眼下这副半死不活的模样来看，那场试验显然没能持续多久 | 自己曾是个常胜的赌徒，后来才明白，欠债不还既伤财，也伤筋动骨 | 自己曾靠捕鼠为生，不过似乎有只巨鼠在夜里登门报了仇 | 自己曾侍奉%randomcitystate%的一位维齐尔，却因摔了一盘食物被关进地牢，随后便被忘在里面好几年 | 自己确实杀过人，但也不该受到那般酷刑，落下一辈子治不好的伤 | 自己曾猎杀女巫，却被一个狠毒的女人骗着喝下药水，连骨头都废了 | 自己曾从军中逃跑，结果嘛，显然是被逮住了 | 自己曾为富人表演杂耍，直到某次耍把戏时不慎摔下台阶。看来那些台阶的棱角，可比他的骨头硬多了 | 自己生来就有严重的畸形 | 父亲嫌他不成器，对他施以毒打 | 母亲无休止地折磨他，留下了满身伤疤 | 兄弟姐妹从小到大都在虐待他}。{他虚弱得仿佛一阵风就能将魂吹走。 | 雇下他，几乎就等于送他去死。真是慈悲啊！ | 你不想让人觉得自己什么人都收，不过要是这家伙压根算不上个“人”，还算“什么人”吗？ | 你见过的死人都比他气色好。 | 这家伙就是一份长了两条腿的狼食。 | 好消息是，万一他死后又爬起来，再放倒一次应该不难。 | 一个梦，甚至一件不会动的东西，都比这可怜虫更有威胁。 | 说实话，你宁可雇个孩子。可惜大家似乎对此颇有微词，所以只好考虑眼前这位了。 | 你原先还以为%randombrother%身上的味道够难闻了。 | 雇用这样的人，换了谁都得好好掂量掂量自己的良心。 | 拜托，看看他！%companyname%真的已经缺人缺到只要还喘气就行了吗？ | 雇这个人实在说不过去。唉，算了，还是雇吧。 | 一副拐杖都比这可怜人更有用。 | 他这副惨样，站着都能装死。}

ac196f30af88899b5a2c.source: %name% joined your party during the undead scourge. Little is known about him and he almost never talks save for the occasional grunt while swinging his sword. His language seems to be codified into one simple structure: killing creatures of evil.
ac196f30af88899b5a2c.translation: %name%在亡灵天灾期间加入了你的队伍。你对他知之甚少，除了挥剑时偶尔哼一声，他几乎从不开口。他似乎只懂一种语言：斩杀邪恶生物。

729f6aed040e74c65ac9.source: Cultists have a resolve to spread further their cult that is second to few.
729f6aed040e74c65ac9.translation: 邪教徒传播信仰的决心，少有人能够比拟。

7bae28bf71523059ecd9.source: The cultist, %name%, left the company with a band of cloaked converts. You know not what became of him, but every so often you have dreams in which he appears. He's often standing by himself in a great void and there is always someone, or something, lingering in the black beyond. Every night, this image gets a little more clear, and each night you find yourself staying up later and later just to avoid dreaming at all.
7bae28bf71523059ecd9.translation: 邪教徒%name%带着一群披斗篷的新信徒离开了战团。你不知道他后来怎么样了，却时不时会在梦里见到他。他总是独自站在一片无边的虚空中，而更远的黑暗里，总有某个人，或某种东西，徘徊不去。每过一夜，那幅景象便清晰几分。你也睡得越来越晚，只为了逃开梦境。

7cd05604f595dc2b8317.source: You heard that %name%, the cultist, left the company at some juncture and went out to spread his faith. There's no telling what became of him, but there was a recent inquisition against unholy faiths and hundreds of 'men in dark cloaks with even darker intentions' were burned at the stake across the realm.
7cd05604f595dc2b8317.translation: 你听说邪教徒%name%在某个时候离开了战团，外出传教。他后来境遇如何无人知晓，不过最近各地展开了异端审判，数百名“披着黑斗篷、心思更加阴暗的人”被送上了火刑柱。

022ec621c2513f103ec4.source: {The man stands with a placard hanging from his neck. | The man's face is wreathed in garish tattoos. He carries a note. | The man hides his face inside a deep cowl, an islanded tip of a nose all that you see in the darkness. He carries a placard around his neck. | Clothed in rags, it is strange the man neither sweats nor shakes in heat or cold. He clutches a scroll as if it protects him from the very elements. | Scripture is written across his arm in scars, the coda of madness. | The stranger writes in the dirt as quick as a man who has done it a thousand times. His message is clear to see. | The man stands with a tome nestled behind a crooked arm. He hands it to you. Opening it, the leather feels like none you've ever touched before. There is only one passage inside, written over and over.} It reads: "Ph'nglui mglw'nafh Davkul R'lyeh wgah'nagl fhtagn. Nn'nilgh'ri, nn'nglui. Sgn'wahl sll'ha ep'shogg." Hmm... quaint.
022ec621c2513f103ec4.translation: {那人站在原地，脖子上挂着一块牌子。 | 那人脸上布满刺眼的文身，手里拿着一张字条。 | 那人把脸藏在深深的兜帽里，黑暗中只露出孤零零的鼻尖，脖子上还挂着一块牌子。 | 那人衣衫褴褛，奇怪的是，无论冷热，他既不流汗，也不发抖。他紧攥着一卷文书，仿佛它能替自己挡住风霜寒暑。 | 那人手臂上以伤疤刻满经文，如同一曲疯狂的终章。 | 陌生人飞快地在泥地上写着字，熟练得仿佛已经写过千遍。他写下的文字清晰可见。 | 那人站在那里，弯着胳膊夹住一册厚书，随后将它递给你。你翻开书，皮革的触感是从未有过的。里面只有同一段文字，反反复复写满了每一页。}上面写着：“芬格鲁伊·姆格尔乌纳夫·达夫库尔·拉莱耶·乌格哈纳格尔·弗坦。恩尼尔格里，恩恩格鲁伊。斯格恩瓦尔·斯尔哈·埃普肖格。”嗯……真有些古怪的趣味。

4c6296e6872feb28841f.source: Daytalers are used to all kinds of physical work, but don't excel in any.
4c6296e6872feb28841f.translation: 短工做惯了各类体力活，但没有哪一门格外出众。

6a59244e5407edb41a59.source: %name% the daytaler retired from fighting and, well, he keeps working with his hands. Now he's back to laying bricks and carrying hay instead of slaying beasts and crushing heads. He took all his mercenary money to purchase a bit of land and settle down. While not the richest man, word has it that there is hardly a happier man in the realm.
6a59244e5407edb41a59.translation: 短工%name%退出了战斗，依旧靠双手过活，只是如今砌砖搬草，不再屠兽碎颅。他拿当佣兵攒下的全部积蓄买了块地，安顿下来。虽不算富有，听说整个王国却难找出比他更快活的人。

b54ea6911ef14c9a5485.source: %name% retired from fighting while he still had most of his fingers and toes intact. He went back to working for the nobility. Last you heard he was out {south | north | east | west} building a great tower for some nobleman. Sadly, you also heard that tower collapsed halfway through its construction with many workers going down with it.
b54ea6911ef14c9a5485.translation: 趁手指脚趾还大多齐全，%name%便退出了战斗，回去替贵族做工。最后听说，他在{南边 | 北边 | 东边 | 西边}替某位贵族修建一座高塔。遗憾的是，你还听说那座塔建到一半就倒了，许多工人也一同坠了下去。

306ea47e92dbdf6674ba.source: {Working here and there | With no steady work | Working on and off | Doing this and that | Having learned no craft}, %name% is known as a daytaler, someone to ask whenever an extra hand is needed. {Work had been sparse for a while now, so | There was little work to be a had these past weeks, so | %name% wanted to do something he had not done before, so | Despite having no experience in battle, staring too deep into the bottle made him believe that | %name% considered the fighting profession one that doesn't run out of work these days, so | %name% lost his loved one to sickness, as befalls so many these days, and broke down. After weeks blurred by drinking his sorrows away,} a travelling mercenary company seemed a good opportunity {to stay with for a while | to earn some coin | to see a bit of the world | to clear his head | to get him to the next village while filling his pockets}.
306ea47e92dbdf6674ba.translation: {四处揽活 | 没有固定营生 | 有活便干，没活便歇 | 什么杂活都接 | 没学过专门手艺}的%name%是个短工，谁家缺人搭把手，便会来找他。{最近活计稀少，于是 | 这几个星期没多少活可干，于是 | %name%想试试从没做过的事，于是 | 他虽毫无战斗经验，多灌了几杯酒后却觉得 | %name%觉得如今靠打仗吃饭总不愁没活干，于是 | %name%像如今许多人一样，在病疫中失去了挚爱，几近崩溃。借酒浇愁，浑浑噩噩地过了几个星期后，}加入一支路过的佣兵战团似乎是个好机会，{可以先待上一阵 | 可以挣几个钱 | 可以见见世面 | 可以让脑子清醒些 | 可以边挣钱边前往下一个村庄}。

e09f517cc9ea7ffee267.source: {Working here and there | With no steady work | Working on and off | Doing this and that | Having learned no craft}, %name% is known as a daytaler, someone to ask whenever an extra hand is needed. {Work had been sparse for a while now, so | There was little work to be had these past weeks, so | %name% wanted to do something he had not done before, so | Despite having no experience in battle, staring too deep into the bottle made him believe that | %name% considered the fighting profession one that doesn't run out of work these days, so | %name% lost his loved one to sickness, as befalls so many these days, and broke down. After weeks blurred by drinking his sorrows away,} a travelling mercenary company seemed a good opportunity {to stay with for a while | to earn some coin | to see a bit of the world | to clear his head | to get him to the next village while filling his pockets}.
e09f517cc9ea7ffee267.translation: {四处打零工 | 没有固定的营生 | 时有活干、时无活干 | 这也做一点，那也做一点 | 没学过什么手艺}，%name%是个短工，谁家缺个帮手，都会想到找他。{最近一直没多少活可干，于是 | 过去几周几乎找不到活干，于是 | %name%想试试从没干过的事，于是 | 虽然毫无作战经验，几杯酒下肚，他便觉得 | %name%觉得如今这世道，靠打仗吃饭总不会缺活干，于是 | %name%的挚爱被疾病夺走，和如今许多人一样。他为此彻底崩溃，借酒浇愁，浑浑噩噩地熬过几个星期后，}一支途经此地的佣兵战团似乎成了不错的去处，{可以跟着待上一阵 | 可以挣几个钱 | 可以出去见见世面 | 可以让脑子清醒些 | 可以一边填满钱袋，一边搭伴去下一个村子}。

83c3baab387e467f8561.source: Deserters have received some martial training, but usually aren't eager to put it to use.
83c3baab387e467f8561.translation: 逃兵受过一些军事训练，却通常不太愿意将其派上用场。

2231212f740c49782a66.source: %name% the deserter continued fighting for the %companyname%, ever striving to redeem his name. Word has it that during a brutal fight with orcs, he dove headfirst into a crowd of greenskins, surfing across the top of their shocked heads. His heroism rallied the men to an incredible victory and he lives out his days getting toasted in every bar he enters.
2231212f740c49782a66.translation: 逃兵%name%继续为%companyname%征战，始终想洗清自己的污名。据说，在一次与兽人的惨烈厮杀中，他一头扑进绿皮群中，踩着那些惊愕的脑袋一路冲了过去。这番壮举鼓舞了弟兄们，助他们赢下了一场不可思议的胜利。如今，他走进哪家酒馆，都有人为他举杯。

6d6920a605f621ad6e4e.source: You heard %name% the deserter actually renewed his title and fled a battle the %companyname% had with some greenskins. Goblins caught him out in the woods and turned his head into a goblet for an orc warlord.
6d6920a605f621ad6e4e.translation: 你听说逃兵%name%又一次不负其名，在%companyname%与绿皮交战时临阵脱逃。地精在林中抓住了他，把他的脑袋做成了献给兽人军阀的酒杯。

af376d7a11827dc5989a.source: {%name% used to be a common soldier in a lord's army, but suffering loss after loss, | Once a watchman on the outskirts of %randomtown%, %name% watched all his friends die to the beasts that lurk there. After so many losses | When two lords quarreled over a petty matter of who owned a local pond, %name% was conscripted to help settle the matter. Being a nobody, it was clear his life was of little value. One slaughter later, | While employed in a lord's professional army, a horrible disease fell upon %name% and his comrades. Fearing its wrath, | While on a lengthy military campaign, %name% felt that there was too much marching and too little spoils to be had. So} he {stuck his weapons in the ground and walked off. | waited until night to desert his outfit. | and several others disbanded in protest. | volunteered for a patrol and, at the first opening, abandoned his soldiering career.} {It is no secret that deserters are widely despised - and %name% keeps his head hung low to stay out of others' eyes. | Most deserters spend the rest of their days avoiding the noose, and %name% is no different. | Donning the garb of the everyman, %name% has, for a time, avoided the deserter's punishment. | By total luck, %name% has, thus far, gotten away with his crime.} {But now broke and penniless, he seeks a return to his former field. | Perhaps compelled by lawmen closing in, he now finds himself joining another fighting force. | Unfortunately, he is not a smart man. Lacking the imagination to pursue a safer career, %name% once again returns to fighting. | Feeling guilty about deserting his brothers in the field, he now seeks redemption in fighting for another outfit. But who is to say he won't flee again? | With an empty coin purse from drinking his memories away, he now considers any opportunity to make a living.}
af376d7a11827dc5989a.translation: {%name%原是领主麾下的一名普通士兵，可接连的败仗让他再也忍受不住。 | %name%曾在%randomtown%郊外担任守卫，眼睁睁看着朋友们一个接一个死于潜伏在那里的野兽之口。经历了太多损失， | 两位领主为当地一口池塘的归属争执不休，%name%被征召入伍，去替他们了结这场争端。他只是个无名小卒，没人把他的性命当回事。一场屠戮过后， | %name%曾在领主的常备军中服役，后来，一场可怕的疫病在他和战友之间蔓延。怕染上疾病， | 在一次漫长的远征中，%name%觉得路走得太多，战利品却少得可怜。于是，}他{把武器往地上一插，转身走了。 | 等到夜深人静，逃离了部队。 | 和几名同伴一同离队，以示抗议。 | 主动领了一趟巡逻差事，逮着机会便结束了自己的军旅生涯。}{谁都知道，逃兵遭人唾弃。%name%总是低着头，躲避旁人的目光。 | 大多数逃兵余生都在躲避绞索，%name%也不例外。 | %name%换上平民的衣服，暂时躲过了当逃兵的惩罚。 | 全凭运气，%name%的罪行至今还没受到追究。}{如今身无分文，他又想干回老本行。 | 或许是追捕他的执法者步步逼近，他又投身于另一支武装队伍。 | 可惜他脑子不太灵光，实在想不出什么更安全的营生，%name%只好再次拿起武器。 | 他为抛弃战场上的弟兄而内疚，希望为另一支队伍作战来赎罪。可谁敢保证他不会再次逃跑？ | 他借酒浇愁，把钱袋喝了个精光，如今只要能糊口，什么机会都愿意试试。}

e7411b2cd4bf8431a1b1.source: Disowned nobles often have profited from some training in melee fighting at court.
e7411b2cd4bf8431a1b1.translation: 失势贵族往往在宫廷中受过一些近战训练。

61a1f9180ad1846ba628.source: A noble at heart, the disowned nobleman %name% returned to his family. Word has it he kicked in the doors and demanded a royal seat. An usurper challenged him in combat and, well, %name% learned a lot in his days with the %companyname% and he now sits on a very, very comfortable throne.
61a1f9180ad1846ba628.translation: 被家族除名的贵族%name%骨子里依然高贵，最终返回了故乡。据说他踹开大门，要求夺回自己的尊位。篡位者向他发起决斗——可%name%在%companyname%的日子里学到了太多本事，如今已坐上一张极其舒适的宝座。

c38019c1c6102f5785c8.source: A man of nobility at heart, %name% the disowned noble returned to his family home. Word has it an usurper arrested him at the gates. His head currently rests on a pike with crows for a crown.
c38019c1c6102f5785c8.translation: 骨子里仍是贵族的%name%回到了家族宅邸。传闻一个篡位者在大门前将他逮捕。如今他的脑袋插在长矛上，乌鸦便是他的王冠。

be2248b990bed6abaf19.source: {A constant disappointment to a delusional father | A victim of court intrigue involving poison and cake | After openly denouncing his own heritage | After an incestous relationship with his sister came to light | After a coup to dispose his older brother failed | After pride and hubris had him leading his father's army to total defeat | For accidentally killing his oldest brother and heir to the throne on a hunt | As a price to be paid for choosing his allies poorly in a war of succession | For attempting to sell captured poachers as slaves | Caught bedding a fellow nobleman | Discovered to be the head of a child stealing plot that shocked the peasantry | For turning his back on the gods and causing a riot amongst the laymen | Seen with the cultists' book of Davkul tucked under an arm}, %name% {was disowned and cast away from his family's estate, never to return. | was stripped of his titles and exiled from the land. | was forcibly removed from his land and told never to return. | came to see, by the threat of an executioner's axe, that he no longer belonged in the court. | saw the hangman's noose, and only by a clever ploy did he slip it. | was branded with the symbol of shame and cast out from his lands. | was believed to have been involved in one too many conspiracies and was removed from the lands. | was seen as being too ambitious, a dangerous trait amongst the nobility.} {%name% now seeks to redeem himself and live up to the family name. A bit selfish for a mercenary outfit, noble nonetheless. | His posture slumped by scandal, %name%'s resistance to difficulties has diminished. | A skilled fighter he may be, but %name% rarely talks about anyone but himself. | Though quick with a sword, you get the feeling someone like %name% was disowned for a reason. | Down on his luck and essentially broke, %name% ventures in the field of sellswords. | Without title or land, %name% seeks to join the sort of men he used to lord over. | Well-geared this former noble may be, you do notice that the most used piece of equipment %name% has are his boots.}
be2248b990bed6abaf19.translation: {总是让那位妄想成性的父亲失望 | 卷入一桩牵涉毒药与蛋糕的宫廷阴谋 | 公开否认自己的出身 | 与姐妹的乱伦关系败露 | 试图推翻兄长的政变失败 | 因骄傲自大，率领父亲的军队遭遇惨败 | 狩猎时误杀了身为王位继承人的长兄 | 在继承战争中站错了队 | 企图把抓到的偷猎者卖为奴隶 | 被撞见与另一位贵族男子同床 | 被查出是拐卖孩童阴谋的主使，在农民中引起轩然大波 | 背弃诸神，激起平民信众的骚乱 | 被人看见腋下夹着邪教徒的《达夫库尔之书》}，%name%{被家族除名，逐出庄园，永世不得归还。 | 被剥夺头衔，流放出境。 | 被强行赶出领地，勒令永不返回。 | 在刽子手斧头的威胁下，终于明白宫廷里已没有自己的位置。 | 眼看就要套上绞索，幸靠一条妙计才逃了出去。 | 被烙上耻辱的印记，逐出领地。 | 被认为卷入了太多阴谋，最终遭到驱逐。 | 被视为野心过盛之人——这在贵族中是个危险的名声。}{如今，%name%想要洗刷耻辱，无愧于家族之名。对佣兵战团而言，这念头有些自私，不过倒也不失高尚。 | 丑闻压弯了%name%的脊背，也磨去了他承受挫折的韧性。 | %name%也许是个好战士，可他开口谈的几乎永远只有自己。 | 尽管%name%出剑很快，你还是觉得，他被家族逐出并非毫无缘由。 | 倒霉透顶，又几乎身无分文，%name%只好来佣兵这行碰碰运气。 | 没了头衔，也没了土地，%name%如今想加入的，正是昔日受他呼来喝去的那群人。 | 这位前贵族的装备或许不错，不过你注意到，%name%身上用得最多、磨得最狠的，还是那双靴子。}

0be7d30fb0ad09adf3af.source: The fact that eunuchs can't sire children is probably a secondary concern for a mercenary company.
0be7d30fb0ad09adf3af.translation: 阉人无法生育，不过佣兵战团大概不会太在意这件事。

a7f0cec46a031b013266.source: For %name%, some things would just always come up a little short. But that didn't stop the eunuch from enjoying himself. Retiring from the %companyname% with a large pile of crowns, and completely devoid of the allures of women, the man went on to live a wonderful, extremely focused life.
a7f0cec46a031b013266.translation: 对%name%而言，有些地方总是难免短那么一点。不过，这并不妨碍这位阉人享受生活。他带着大笔克朗从%companyname%退役，也不再受女色诱惑，从此日子过得滋润，凡事都能专心致志。

3e16b2f0fbe3729e666f.source: It's said that %name% the eunuch departed from the company shortly after you did. He traveled the lands, broke and broken, wasting his scant crowns on ale and wenches. Insulted by a whore for his cockless nature, the drunken and enraged eunuch stabbed the woman in the eye with a goat horn. 3e16b2f0fbe3729e666f.translation: 据说，阉人%name%在你离开后不久也退出了战团。他四处游荡，穷困潦倒、心灰意冷，把仅有的几个钱全花在酒和女人身上。一名妓女嘲笑他没了命根子，醉醺醺的阉人勃然大怒，用一只羊角刺进了她的眼睛。治安官找来时，他的酒还没醒，仍是一副迷迷糊糊、不知所措的模样。镇民们扒光他的衣服，将他吊死，又肢解了尸体，最后拿去喂了猪。

e80962bc7bc6e6e763b3.translation: 刽子手性情阴沉，习惯了暴力，却很少经历真正的战争。

ab5b6747b9ac56f7d561.source: %name% eventually retired from the company and once again found himself plying the executioner's trade. His considerable decapitation skills only honed further by sellswording, the man has apparently gained such notoriety in his field that the local nobility frequently get into feuds over who may keep him on retainer.
ab5b6747b9ac56f7d561.translation: %name%最终从战团退役，重操刽子手旧业。佣兵生涯让他本就出众的斩首技艺更加精湛。据说他已名声大噪，当地贵族常常为了争相雇用他而闹得不可开交。

d1c564bcbb17bfe2d7ad.source: His skill with the headsman's blade sharpened further by combat, %name% left the company and resumed work as an executioner. The townsfolk found little spectacle in his efficiency, however, and he was soon replaced with a more crowd-pleasing amateur. Left destitute, it wasn't long before the man was found hanging from a tree outside of town.
d1c564bcbb17bfe2d7ad.translation: 战斗进一步磨炼了%name%的斩首本领。他离开战团，重操刽子手旧业。可镇民觉得他下手太利落，没什么看头，很快用一位更会讨观众欢心的生手替换了他。他从此一贫如洗，不久便被发现吊死在城外的树上。

b66d915049e707c5558a.source: {As with many men, %name%'s direction in life was dictated by the family business: executing criminals for the burgomeister of %randomtown%. | As a boy, %name% dreamed of becoming a knight clad in shining armor. As a man, he became an executioner clad in a dark hood. | %name%'s whole family was slain in a bandit raid. Unable to join the manhunt himself, he became an apprentice to the local executioner in the hopes of one day meting out revenge in his own way. | Once a brigand himself, %name% had a change of heart and turned himself in. The local guard offered him a pardon if he agreed to execute any criminals they captured, and he's been in the trade ever since. | With the distant stare of one who has seen much death, and the worn blade of one who has dealt it, it's obvious that %name% is an executioner. | An executioner, %name% is about as cheerful as the gallows he operates.} {Though content with his profession, it made him unpopular. After carrying out the beheading of {a local youth sentenced for stealing from a noble | a beloved whore who slept with the wrong lord | a respected craftsman accused of embezzling}, he was ostracized by the townsfolk. | He always viewed himself as a necessary, if grisly, part of law for the common folk. But when he learned {his employer was making backroom deals with brigands | the local lord was ordering the deaths of the innocent | a man he executed was innocent | of the horrible things the local lord did with the heads of the condemned}, he resigned his post in disgust. | One day he was tasked with killing a strange cultist from distant lands. After he broke a third blade halfway through the strangely cheerful man's neck, he decided it was time to find a new profession. | But one day he woke up and found he could no longer stomach the idea of slaying a man who couldn't fight back. | But eventually he grew unhappy with his role, finding little satisfaction in slaying men after they'd already performed their evil works.} {With few other careers available to him, %name% decided mercenary work seemed the best fit for his talents. | While not a warrior, %name% knows how to handle a blade, and so sellswording was the obvious career change. | With a skillset predominantly based around necklines, %name% decided he could either become a mercenary or a tailor. The former seemed like it paid better, and now here he is. | In need of a new career but with few other skills, %name% decided that mercenary work was sort of like executing with more steps.} {The man stands silently before you, staring wide-eyed and expectant but not saying a word. Ok then. | Less confident in conversation than in killing, he mumbles out a nervous greeting to you and asks about pay. | Not much for words, he grunts expectantly at you. As long as he can kill, you suppose you don't mind the quiet. | He approaches and barks something at you that his heavy hood muffles beyond comprehension. After a few moments of silence he follows up with '...please?' and you realize he's asking to join the company. Oh.}
b66d915049e707c5558a.translation: {和许多人一样，%name%的人生由家业决定：替%randomtown%的镇长处决罪犯。 | 小时候，%name%梦想成为一名身披闪亮铠甲的骑士；长大后，他却成了一个戴着黑兜帽的刽子手。 | %name%的全家在一次强盗袭击中惨遭杀害。他无力亲自参加追捕，便拜当地刽子手为师，盼着有朝一日能用自己的方式报仇。 | %name%曾是强盗，后来回心转意，投案自首。当地卫兵答应，只要他替他们处决抓来的罪犯，就赦免他的罪。他自此便干上了这一行。 | 目光空洞，显然见过太多死亡；刀刃磨损，显然亲手制造过太多死亡。不难看出，%name%是个刽子手。 | 身为刽子手，%name%的神情和他操持的绞刑架一样，半点喜气也没有。}{他对自己的营生还算满意，只是不怎么招人待见。砍下{一名因偷窃贵族财物而获罪的本地青年的脑袋 | 一名人缘极好、却睡错了领主的妓女的脑袋 | 一名受人敬重、却被控侵吞钱财的工匠的脑袋}后，镇民便彻底排斥了他。 | 他一直认为，自己的工作虽血腥，却是维护平民法度所必需的一环。可当他得知{雇主竟在私下与强盗做交易 | 当地领主下令处死无辜之人 | 自己处决过的一人竟是无辜的 | 当地领主拿死刑犯的头颅做的那些骇人勾当}后，便愤然辞职。 | 一天，他奉命处决一个来自远方的古怪邪教徒。那人诡异地满脸喜气，而他的第三把刀也在砍到脖子一半时崩断了。他决定，是时候换个行当了。 | 可有一天醒来，他发现自己再也无法忍受杀死一个无力还手的人。 | 可渐渐地，他对自己的差事不再满意：等人作完恶再杀掉他们，实在没什么值得欣慰的。}{别的出路不多，%name%觉得当佣兵最适合自己的本事。 | %name%虽不是战士，却懂得使刀，因此转行当佣兵便顺理成章。 | %name%的手艺大多围着脖子转，他觉得自己要么当佣兵，要么当裁缝。前者似乎给钱更多，于是他就来了。 | 想另谋生路，又没什么别的手艺，%name%觉得当佣兵无非是多费几道工序的行刑。}{他默默站在你面前，瞪大眼睛，满怀期待，却一言不发。好吧。 | 他杀人时比说话时自在得多，紧张地含糊问了声好，便打听起酬劳。 | 他不善言辞，只朝你满怀期待地哼了一声。只要杀得了敌人，你想自己也不介意他安静些。 | 他走近，冲你嚷了句什么，却被厚重的兜帽闷住，完全听不清。沉默片刻后，他又补了一句“……行吗？”你这才明白，他是想加入战团。哦。}

8c8cbe0b5b467c293e6f.source: {Once an executioner in the many nomad tribes of the South, %name% was banished {for a beheading gone horribly wrong | when it was discovered he'd slain the wrong man | after he faked the death of a friend}. Aimless, he drifted into %randomcitystate% and resumed his trade in service of the viziers. | An executioner, %name% was tasked with beheading, hanging, quartering, and all the other punishments conveyed upon those criminals deemed unworthy of repaying their debts to the Gilder in life, and those who had been given the chance and failed. | %name% worked for %randomvizier% as an executioner, meting out grisly justice to the criminals of the South. | From his distinctive hood, it's clear %name% is an executioner. From his grim affect, it's clear he's been in the trade for some time.} {In the city states, however, even criminals are more valuable alive than dead, and soon he found himself running out of work and out of crowns. | One day he was charged with severing the neck of another headsman who had 'ruined' an execution by allowing the condemned to predict the killing blow and scream. %name% carried out his own task in silence, then decided it was time to find a new line of work. | For many years he was content with his work, but one day he was tasked with {hanging a young boy who had stolen food from the market | beheading a beautiful concubine who had displeased her master | drowning an old man too feeble even to stand}. He performed his duty, but found he no longer had a taste for the profession after that. | Though happy enough in his role, he learned that all of his predecessors had eventually been indebted or executed themselves after displeasing his employer. Seeing the writing on the wall, he began looking for a new line of work.} {Unsure what else to do, %name% decided mercenary work was a good fit for his skillset. | Figuring he'd be no less respected as a Crownling, but better paid, %name% now pursues a sellsword's career. | Accustomed to blood and blades alike, mercenary work is an obvious next step for %name%. | %name% tried his hand at a few occupations before deciding that his particular talents were best suited for the bloody, and well-paid, work of a sellsword.}
8c8cbe0b5b467c293e6f.translation: {%name%曾在南方各个游牧部族中当刽子手，后来因{一次斩首出了可怕的岔子 | 被发现杀错了人 | 帮一个朋友伪造死讯}而被放逐。漫无目的地流落到%randomcitystate%后，他重操旧业，为维齐尔们效力。 | 身为刽子手，%name%负责斩首、绞刑、肢解，以及施加在罪犯身上的种种刑罚。那些人或是被认定不配活着偿还欠镀金者的债，或是得了机会却未能做到。 | %name%替%randomvizier%当刽子手，用血腥的手段惩治南方的罪犯。 | 从那顶醒目的兜帽便能看出，%name%是个刽子手；从那张阴沉的脸便能看出，他干这一行已经很久了。}{然而在城邦，即使罪犯也是活着比死了更值钱。很快，他便没了活干，钱袋也空了。 | 一天，他奉命砍下另一名刽子手的脑袋。那人让死刑犯察觉到杀招将至，惊叫出声，因此被认定“毁掉”了一场行刑。%name%一声不响地完成差事，随后决定另谋生路。 | 多年来，他一直安于这份差事，直到有一天奉命{绞死一个在集市偷食物的小男孩 | 砍下一名惹主人不快的美貌侍妾的脑袋 | 溺死一名虚弱得连站都站不起来的老人}。他履行了职责，却从此对这一行失去了胃口。 | 他原本还算满意自己的职位，后来却得知，前任们最终全都因惹恼雇主而沦为负债者，或被处死。看清自己的下场后，他开始另找出路。}{不知道还能干什么，%name%觉得佣兵很适合自己的本事。 | %name%寻思着，当克朗客也不会比现在更受人轻贱，却能多挣些钱，于是转而投身佣兵行当。 | %name%早已习惯刀刃与鲜血，转行当佣兵显然顺理成章。 | %name%试过几种营生，最后还是觉得，自己这点独门本事，最适合佣兵这份血腥而酬劳丰厚的工作。}

5a8ae857482c9b889407.source: Farmhands are used to hard physical labor.
5a8ae857482c9b889407.translation: 农场帮工早已习惯繁重的体力劳动。

2b43a52de324af424467.source: The former farmhand, %name%, retired from the %companyname%. The money he made was put toward purchasing a bit of land. He spends the rest of his days happily farming and starting a family with way too many children.
2b43a52de324af424467.translation: 曾是农场帮工的%name%从%companyname%退役，用挣来的钱买了一块地。他余生快活地耕种，成家立业，还生了一大群孩子。

f6436f9221a5e20f7c86.source: The former farmhand, %name%, soon left the %companyname%. He purchased a bit of land out {south | north | east | west} and was doing quite well for himself - until noble soldiers hanged him from a tree for refusing to hand over all his crops.
f6436f9221a5e20f7c86.translation: 曾是农场帮工的%name%不久便离开了%companyname%。他在{南边 | 北边 | 东边 | 西边}买了块地，日子过得不错——直到他拒绝交出全部收成，被贵族的士兵吊死在树上。

89f5374a23892889ce3a.source: {Tilling the soil is hard work, requiring the blood and sweat of sturdier men. | Every farm in the land needs a stable of hardy men to work the fields.  | Man puts his sweat into the earth to feed himself, and he feeds himself to put his sweat into the Earth another day. | No matter the weather, a farm needs working. | Pigsties, stables, and ungated pens, these are the dreams and nightmares of farming men. | While some men earn their keep by killing, others look below their own two feet, wondering what crops the soil may hold. | A special breed of men comes out of ranchers and farmers. Sturdy, resolute, hard-working. | With food so needed, there's little wonder why farmers are the most common sort of man in all the land. | A farmer hates to see his land fertilized in blood, but that's becoming more and more common these days. | In war, farms are hotspots for armies. Not just to feed themselves, but to recruit from the stable of strong men who work those lands. | As cities grow and distance themselves from the hinterland, citizens often forget to whom their full bellies owe gratitude.} %name% {is a burly, sweat-sculpted farmhand. | hails from the outskirts of %randomtown% where he drove ploughs and broke horses. | knows a couple kinds of hoes, all of which the farmhand can swing with ease. | grew up on one of the land's many farms. | spent many years harvesting the crops that feed everyone in the land. | worked as a farmhand for a simple homestead. | fell into farming after his boating business went under. | became a farmhand to help feed his dozen kids and two wives. | took up farming as a means to a belly-filled end. | carries the stocky frame best used for planting, harvesting, and surviving winters.} {Unfortunately, it didn't take war and turmoil long to find his farm. | But poor harvests have driven him from the farms. | Sadly, his farm was one of the first to be attacked during these trying times. | Word of coming violence, however, drove him from the peaceful vocation of farming. | Droughts, poorly-timed as ever, have now driven the man from his work. | Unpaid for his labor, he eventually abandoned the farm life. | With more crowns than ever in the killing businesses, the man was easily drawn away from his motley crops. | One day, he realized his strong body had more value chopping heads than milking cows. | After raiders pillaged his crops, he'd had enough, leaving the farm life for good. | After the weather soured his harvest, the farmer decided to choose a vocation not wholly based on the whims of Mother Nature. | Word has it he really did sleep with the farmer's daughter. What a surprise he's no longer on the farm.} {Cornfed and barnbred, %name% stands before you as fit a man you've ever seen. | He misses the cows, true, but %name% should take to the mercenary's tough life with ease. | Growing up on a farm gives a man all the nutrients he'd ever need, and %name% certainly took advantage. | %name% once took a mule kick to the face. Its foot broken, they had to put the animal down. | If men were trees, %name% would never fall down. Or something gracious like that. | Don't let his simple past fool you, %name% could fit right in with any wrestler or fighter. | %name% shares a lot in common with draught animals. Just point him the right way. | Judging by his size, there must have been a lot of meat in that corn %name% spent all his life eating. | %name% is big enough to wring a guy's neck like it was a cow's udder.}
89f5374a23892889ce3a.translation: {耕地是份苦差事，得靠身强力壮的汉子流血流汗。 | 这片土地上的每一座农场，都需要一群健壮的人手下地干活。  | 人把汗水洒进泥土，换来填肚子的粮食，吃饱了，第二天再把汗水洒进泥土。 | 无论天公作不作美，农活总得有人干。 | 猪圈、马厩和敞着口的牲口栏，既装着农夫的美梦，也藏着他们的噩梦。 | 有人靠杀人挣饭吃，也有人低头打量脚下的土地，琢磨着能种出什么庄稼。 | 农场和牧场养育出一种特别的汉子：强壮、坚定、勤劳。 | 人人都得吃饭，农夫成为这片土地上最常见的一类人，自然也就不奇怪了。 | 没有农夫愿意看见鲜血给自己的田地施肥，可这样的事近来越来越多。 | 战时，农场总是军队盯上的地方。不光为了粮食，也为了征走那些在田里劳作的壮汉。 | 城市日益扩张，与乡野渐行渐远，城里人也常常忘了，自己吃饱肚子该感谢谁。}%name%{是个魁梧的农场帮工，一身筋骨都是汗水磨出来的。 | 来自%randomtown%郊外，过去在那里扶犁耕地、驯服烈马。 | 熟悉好几种锄头，每一把都能抡得轻轻松松。 | 在这片土地上再普通不过的一座农场里长大。 | 多年来忙于收割庄稼，养活这片土地上的人们。 | 曾在一处普通农庄当帮工。 | 经营船运的买卖垮了以后，转行下了田。 | 为了养活十二个孩子和两个老婆，当上了农场帮工。 | 干农活没别的讲究，就是图个吃饱。 | 生得粗壮结实，正适合播种、收割，熬过漫长的冬天。}{可惜没过多久，战乱就找上了他的农场。 | 接连歉收，逼得他离开了田地。 | 可悲的是，在这动荡年月里，他的农场是最早遭袭的一批。 | 然而，战火将至的消息使他告别了平静的农耕生活。 | 旱灾来得从来不是时候，这回又把他逼得丢了营生。 | 辛苦劳作却领不到工钱，他最终放弃了田里的生活。 | 杀人的行当越来越赚钱，轻易就把他从那几块杂乱的庄稼地里引了出来。 | 有一天，他忽然明白，自己这身力气用来砍人脑袋，比挤牛奶值钱得多。 | 劫掠者洗劫庄稼后，他受够了，决意再也不种地。 | 坏天气毁了收成，他决定换个不必全看老天爷脸色的营生。 | 听说，他还真爬上了农场主女儿的床。难怪再也没法在那儿干下去。}{吃着粮食、睡着谷仓长大的%name%站在你面前，结实得不能再结实。 | %name%确实想念那些奶牛，不过雇佣兵的苦日子，他应该也能很快适应。 | 在农场长大，营养总不会缺，%name%显然没浪费这份好处。 | 一头骡子曾一脚踢在%name%脸上。骡子的腿骨折了，最后只好把它宰掉。 | 要是人能长成树，%name%肯定永远不会倒。反正大概就是这么句好话。 | 别被%name%平凡的出身骗了，他混进摔跤手或斗士当中也毫不逊色。 | %name%和拉犁的牲口有不少共同之处，给他指对方向就行。 | 看%name%这体格，他吃了一辈子的玉米里，怕是没少掺肉。 | %name%块头大得惊人，拧断别人的脖子，对他来说恐怕和挤牛奶差不多。}

3e6c410c222f74b381f3.source: Fishermen are used to physical labor.
3e6c410c222f74b381f3.translation: 渔夫早已习惯体力劳动。

3aa66657b9a2fe2c8310.source: %name% retired from fighting and returned to his fishing ventures. A huge storm ran up the shores, destroying every skiff and drifter - except that wily fisherman's! The only boat afloat, %name%'s business boomed. He lives a comfortable life waking up to a nice beachfront view every morning.
3aa66657b9a2fe2c8310.translation: %name%告别战场，重操捕鱼旧业。一场巨大的风暴席卷海岸，毁掉了所有小艇和渔船，唯独放过了这个机灵渔夫的船！手里握着唯一还能下水的船，%name%的生意蒸蒸日上。如今他过得十分舒适，每天清晨醒来，都能欣赏美丽的海滨风光。

ac185b245bdb82b305e8.source: With the fighting career going so poorly, %name% decided to retire from the field and return to fishing. He went missing at sea after an enormous storm wrecked the shorelines.
ac185b245bdb82b305e8.translation: 战斗生涯一塌糊涂，%name%决定退出战场，回去捕鱼。一场巨大的风暴摧毁海岸之后，他便在海上失踪了。

bd87511c5c3adf0db5a0.source: {%name% loved the sea and the serenity of fishing alone on the water | Ironically, %name% always hated the water, but became a fisherman after his father and his father's father | %name% was a strong and able fisherman | %name% was content with being a fisherman | %name% always had a lucky hand in finding the best fishing grounds and catching the fattest fish}. As long as there was no storm, he was out there, fishing, day in and out. {Sadly, his fishing cabin burned to the ground while he was out at sea. | But disaster struck as he lost his best friend at sea when a storm suddenly came up, leaving him with a badly damaged boat and no one to sail out with. | But disaster struck when his wife died during childbirth, shattering all what he held dear. | After being unable pay his debts for some time, however, his boat was taken from him by a merciless loan shark. | It was after he strangled his wife in a fit of rage that he lost all interest in the fishing trade. | Much to his dismay, for almost a whole summer most of the fish he caught was already dead and rotten inside. | It was after a priest of the gods told %name% that the life of a fisherman was not what they desired of him, but that they wished for him to spill blood in their name, that he would set his eyes on another trade.} Visiting the tavern one evening, a new opportunity presented itself with the promise of coin for dangerous work.
bd87511c5c3adf0db5a0.translation: {%name%热爱大海，也享受独自在水上捕鱼的宁静 | 讽刺的是，%name%一直讨厌水，却仍像父亲和祖父一样当了渔夫 | %name%是个强壮能干的渔夫 | %name%安于捕鱼为生 | %name%总有好运气，能找到最好的渔场，捕到最肥的鱼}。只要没有风暴，他就日复一日地出海捕鱼。{遗憾的是，一次出海期间，他的渔屋被烧成了灰烬。 | 突如其来的风暴夺去了他最好的朋友，只留给他一艘严重破损的船，再也没人陪他一同出海。 | 妻子死于难产，灾祸摧毁了他珍视的一切。 | 可他迟迟还不上债，冷酷的放贷人便夺走了他的船。 | 一次盛怒之下，他扼死了妻子，此后便对捕鱼彻底失去了兴趣。 | 令他沮丧的是，几乎整整一个夏天，捕上来的鱼大多早已死去，肚子里也已腐烂。 | 一位祭司告诉%name%，诸神不愿他继续捕鱼，而是希望他以诸神之名挥洒鲜血，他这才将目光投向别的行当。}某晚去酒馆时，一个新的机会摆在了他面前：干危险的活，拿相应的报酬。

161146bf62801dc01b11.source: Flagellants have a high resolve in what they do, and a high tolerance for pain, but their work has often left their bodies scarred for life.
161146bf62801dc01b11.translation: 苦修者意志坚定，忍痛能力很强，但他们的修行往往让身体留下终生伤痕。

61ec2e77345509cad0ba.source: One of the more disturbing members of the group, %name% the flagellant at least put aside the whip long enough to bring blades to your enemies. Although he was a capable if not unsettlingly diligent mercenary, it became increasingly obvious that his habits would be the end of him. After another night of harsh personal repudiation, the company found the man unconscious and nearly bleeding out yet again. Hoping to save %name% from himself, they dropped the flagellant off at a monastery where he eventually woke to painful confusion. A kind monk nursed him to health and taught him the ways of peaceful religiosity. To this day, %name% walks the cloisters, giving tempered talks to the young and sparing them from notions of savage spirituality.
61ec2e77345509cad0ba.translation: 苦修者%name%是战团里最令人不安的几个人之一。好在他总能暂时放下鞭子，抽出刀剑对付你的敌人。他确实是个能干的佣兵，勤勉得甚至有些吓人，但也越来越明显：他的那些习惯迟早会要了他的命。又一个严厉自罚的夜晚过后，弟兄们再次发现他昏迷不醒，几乎流干了血。为了让%name%免于死在自己手里，战团将他送进了一座修道院。他最终在那里醒来，浑身疼痛，不知所措。一位善良的修士照料他康复，并教他以平和的方式侍奉诸神。直到今天，%name%仍漫步于回廊之间，温和地教导年轻人，让他们远离以残酷折磨求取救赎的念头。

09e7c57469cd35656e9b.source: With the company rapidly declining, many mercenaries turned to desperate measures. %name% the flagellant was one such measure. Due to chaos and confusion, some men came to believe %name% could lead them to honor and salvation. A handful of survivors broke off from the %companyname% and went mad, joining his cult of savage spirituality. A howling %name% at their helm, the converts wander aimlessly, sulking half-bent across the earth, rinds of raw hides for backs.
09e7c57469cd35656e9b.translation: 战团迅速衰败，许多佣兵开始病急乱投医，苦修者%name%便成了他们抓住的一根救命稻草。混乱之中，有人相信%name%能带领他们赢得荣耀与救赎。几名幸存者脱离%companyname%，陷入疯狂，投身于他那个以残酷自虐求取神恩的教派。在嘶声嚎叫的%name%带领下，这些皈依者漫无目的地游荡，弯着腰，阴沉沉地蹒跚前行，背上只剩一层层血肉模糊的皮。

6ca778c68f44d671fef2.source: {The gods pity men, spurring many, not unlike %name%, to seek their favor. | Illiterate and born to poverty, %name% found refuge in tales of the gods. | Always a man to devour books, it wasn't long until %name% discovered texts of the gods. | Some say the gods speak to us and, if true, they definitely spoke to %name%. | With new cults springing up in the wilds, %name% returned to the familiarity of the gods. | Raised by his firebrand father, %name% spent much of his early years nursing wounds from good floggings. The gods would approve.} {When war came to the land, the gods told him to take part for greater justice. | As cultists spread their vile word like disease on a rat, %name% saw fit to take up arms and battle the heresy. | Straying from his faith, he committed a horrific crime in %randomtown% - finding company with a man. While flagellating himself nightly, he seeks redemption. | Hearing but a mere rumor of a holy place, the pilgrim took up staff and supplies to seek it out. | Now that war has returned to the land, the gods' devotee wished to find out why, through prayer and corporeal means. | A night spent in a cave revealed to the believer that the gods demanded blood. %name% was not one to refuse their beckoning. | After raiders looted the coffers of his church, %name%'s quest was to refill the pure purses.} {As the laws of the universe bend to a world-consuming war, a thaumaturge like %name% might be useful to have around. | He carries a whip with glass-barbed leather. This is not for your enemies, he states, but for purity. Interesting. | He professes to hate evil, but for a few crowns %name% can be persuaded to make anything 'evil'. | This man seeks the difficult road, no doubt why he saw fit to join a mercenary band. | If %name% had the power, you believe he'd purge the entire world. Thankfully, he is a mere man. | Talks of the gods might be a tad irksome, but %name%'s fiery passion lends itself well to the battlefield. | So enamored with the world of the gods, it's not much of a surprise that the pilgrim sees the real one filled with enemies.}
6ca778c68f44d671fef2.translation: {诸神怜悯世人，许多人因此寻求神恩，%name%也不例外。 | %name%出身贫寒，目不识丁，却从诸神的传说中寻得了慰藉。 | %name%向来如饥似渴地读书，没过多久便读到了诸神的经文。 | 有人说，诸神会对凡人说话。若这是真的，他们肯定对%name%说过。 | 新兴邪教在荒野中接连冒头，%name%却回归了自己熟悉的诸神信仰。 | %name%由狂热的父亲养大，早年的许多时日都在养伤——那些伤来自一顿又一顿结实的鞭打。诸神想必很赞许。}{战火烧到这片土地时，诸神告诉他，要为更大的正义投身其中。 | 邪教徒像老鼠传播瘟疫一样散布邪说，%name%便觉得该拿起武器，与异端作战。 | 他曾背离信仰，在%randomtown%犯下“骇人的罪行”——与一名男子相好。如今他夜夜鞭笞自己，寻求救赎。 | 仅仅听到一点圣地的传闻，这位朝圣者便拿起手杖，带上补给，踏上寻访之路。 | 战争再次降临大地，这位虔诚的信徒想通过祈祷与肉身苦修，弄清其中缘由。 | 在山洞中度过的一夜，让这名信徒领悟到诸神渴求鲜血。%name%绝不会拒绝他们的召唤。 | 掠夺者洗劫了教堂的钱箱后，%name%便肩负起使命，要重新填满这只圣洁的钱袋。}{吞噬世界的战争仿佛连天地法则都能扭曲，身边留个%name%这样的神秘行者，也许会有用。 | 他带着一条皮鞭，上面嵌着玻璃倒刺。他说，这不是给敌人准备的，而是为了净化自身。有意思。 | 他口口声声痛恨邪恶，不过只要给几个克朗，就能说服%name%把任何东西都当成“邪恶”。 | 这人专挑难走的路，也难怪他会看上佣兵队伍。 | 要是%name%真有那个本事，你相信他会把全世界都净化一遍。所幸，他不过是一介凡人。 | 他满嘴诸神，或许有点烦人，不过%name%的狂热倒很适合战场。 | 这位朝圣者一心沉醉于诸神的世界，自然会觉得现实世界处处都是敌人。}

02c28914078c4536a646.source: Gamblers tend to have quick reflexes and a higher resolve than their opponents at the card table.
02c28914078c4536a646.translation: 赌徒通常反应敏捷，在牌桌上也比对手更沉得住气。

d6bfe3d469dd884859b7.source: It was perhaps a risk to take a gambler like %name% into your ranks. Now, many days later it's obvious you made the right choice. Last you heard, he was still with the company and uses his earnings to enrich his habits. Rumor has it that, through all his winnings, he's secretly become one of the richest men in all the land. You think it's a bunch of hogwash, but a surprising number of mayors have become suddenly lax on gaming...
d6bfe3d469dd884859b7.translation: 将%name%这样的赌徒收入麾下，或许本身就是一场赌博。如今时过境迁，事实证明你赌对了。最近听说，他仍在战团里效力，把挣来的酬劳继续投入自己的爱好。传闻他凭着赌桌上的连番大胜，已经悄悄成了全境最富有的人之一。你觉得这纯属胡说八道，不过，近来对赌博突然网开一面的镇长，数量还真不少……

5f4b77ac6bbd619a243e.source: %name% the gambler retired from the declining company and returned to his gambling ways. He quickly acquired great debts he could not pay. You saw him begging on a street corner with one of his hands missing and gaps in his teeth. You dropped a few crowns into his tin and said a few words, but he did not recognize you.
5f4b77ac6bbd619a243e.translation: 赌徒%name%离开衰败的战团后，又重拾赌博恶习，很快欠下了无力偿还的巨债。你后来在街角见过他行乞，少了一只手，牙也缺了几颗。你往他的铁罐里丢了几枚克朗，还说了几句话，他却没认出你。

e142733220f27e405715.source: {They say luck is the devil, so just how long can a gambler like %name% play with it? | Everyone gambles, so %name% figured why not do it for money? | Dice, cards, marbles - there are a lot of ways to take a man's money, and %name% knows all of them. | %name%'s got the eyes of a desert snake - and shaping cards is his rattle. | In a world of life or death, taking risks is %name%'s game. | A man like %name% sees everything coming, especially the next card in the deck.} {He supported himself by playing cards from town to town, only leaving after he'd cleaned out their pockets. | But it is a mystery as to how a man decides to take up cards as a lifestyle. | The constant coming and going of mercenaries made for easy targets - until one sore loser ran him off with a bastard sword. | Orphaned by his own birth, he's always scrounged up a living by gambling with others. | When he was a kid, a trickster's cup-game showed him the value in hustling. | When his father fell into gambling debts, he figured the best way to pay them back was to become an even better hustler himself. | After taking all their crowns, towns across the land banned %name% from hustling in a fit of so-called 'religious revival.'} {Now, the gambler seeks to throw his dice into the wind - as well as the mud, taking rank with any outfit that pays. | One has to wonder what a cardplayer is doing not playing cards. Then again, maybe it's good that he sees your group as a smart gamble. | Perhaps years of scamming mercenaries has given him the notion that he could just as easily be one. | Clever and quick-thinking, the cardshaper survives by moving before anyone else does, a skill as useful as any other in this world. | Ironically, a bad play put him into enormous debt with a baron. Now he has to find another way to pay it back. | Wars have sapped most of the fish from his cards games. Instead of waiting around he figured he'd just go ahead and follow them.}
e142733220f27e405715.translation: {人们说运气就是魔鬼，那么%name%这样的赌徒，还能陪它玩多久？ | 人人都免不了赌一把，%name%便想，何不索性靠这个挣钱？ | 骰子、纸牌、弹珠——赢走一个人的钱有许多办法，%name%样样精通。 | %name%的眼神像沙漠中的毒蛇，摆弄纸牌的声音便是他的响尾。 | 在这个非生即死的世道，冒险就是%name%的拿手好戏。 | %name%这样的人总能看穿下一步，尤其是牌堆里的下一张牌。}{他辗转各个城镇，靠打牌谋生，不把当地人的钱赢光，绝不离开。 | 不过，一个人究竟怎么会决定以纸牌为业，仍是个谜。 | 来来往往的佣兵都是好下手的肥羊，直到某个输不起的家伙提着手半剑，把他赶跑。 | 他一出生就成了孤儿，一直靠与人赌博勉强糊口。 | 小时候，一个骗子的猜杯戏法让他见识了出千的妙处。 | 父亲欠下一屁股赌债，他便觉得，最好的还债办法，就是让自己成为一个更高明的赌棍。 | %name%把各地镇民的克朗赢了个精光，镇上便借着所谓“重振信仰”的风潮，纷纷禁止他设赌。}{如今，这名赌徒打算把骰子抛进风里，也抛进泥里：只要给钱，哪支队伍他都肯加入。 | 不禁让人奇怪，一个牌手不去打牌，跑来这里做什么。不过，他觉得押注你的队伍值得一试，或许也是件好事。 | 也许是骗了佣兵多年，让他觉得自己当起佣兵来，也会同样容易。 | 这名老千机灵敏捷，靠着总比别人先动一步才活到今天。在这世上，这本事不比任何手艺差。 | 讽刺的是，一次失手让他欠了某位男爵巨额赌债。如今他得另想办法偿还。 | 战争带走了牌桌上大多数肥羊。与其干等，他索性决定跟着他们一起走。}

87a18b5c895c3390ff65.source: Gladiators are expensive, but a life in the arena has forged them into skilled fighters.
87a18b5c895c3390ff65.translation: 角斗士要价高昂，但竞技场生涯已将他们磨炼成技艺高超的战士。

9dbd4d29c09f8ca41ce5.source: You thought that %name% the gladiator would return to the arenas as you thought he might. However, news from the south speaks of an uprising of indebted and gladiators alike. Unlike previous revolts, this one has viziers swinging from rooftops and slavers being lynched in the streets. The general upheaval is apparently about to sit the once-ringfighter as a legitimate powerbroker in the region.
9dbd4d29c09f8ca41ce5.translation: 你原以为角斗士%name%会重返角斗场。然而，南方传来的消息却是一场由负债者和角斗士共同掀起的暴动。与以往的起义不同，这一次，维齐尔们被吊在屋顶上摇晃，奴隶贩子在街头遭人私刑处死。这场动乱似乎即将把那位昔日的角斗士，推上当地真正掌握权势的位置。

cb04eae91d9dabc5e2a3.source: The call of the crowd was too loud for the gladiator %name%. After your quick retirement from the unsuccessful %companyname%, the fighter returned to the southern kingdoms' fighting arenas. Unfortunately, the wear and tear of his time with mercenaries slowed him a step and he was mortally slain by a half-starved slave wielding a pitchfork and a net.
cb04eae91d9dabc5e2a3.translation: 观众的呼声让角斗士%name%难以抗拒。你从功业未成的%companyname%匆匆退役后，他也回到了南方诸国的角斗场。可惜，多年的佣兵生涯磨损了他的身躯，让他慢了一步。一名饿得半死、手持草叉与网的奴隶，最终要了他的命。

fd1c0716228b8cf31953.source: {The South is littered with slaves of all sorts, called the indebted for their debt to the Gilder. While most find themselves in the fields, a select few are taken to the fighting pits to battle it out. | While northerners do partake in combat tournaments, nothing gets close to the violence and gore of a southern gladiatorial pit. | In the South, rich and poor alike enjoy cheering on the gladiators of the fighting pits. | Southern gladiatorial pits are filled with indebted and voluntary killers alike. | A bloody house of combat and betting, a gladiatorial pit is the one place in the South one may find rich and poor crowded together.} {It was from these ranks %name% came. He rapidly grew through the ranks and managed to buy his way out of the pits and into whatever 'freedom' one could find after such a life. | A crowd-favorite, %name%'s time as a gladiator ended after a 'pardon' by his wealthy sponsors. But in early retirement he found his life unfulfilled. | Successful killers such as %name% can buy their way to freedom, though the bloodlust has yet to leave the man. | %name% was involved in a 'diving' incident and received a year long ban from the pits. | But gladiators like %name% are not just popular with the public, but particularly with the womenfolk. A raunchy tryst with a nobleman's wife led to the fighter being spirited away under the cover of night lest he be castrated. | A pit's most popular fighter is usually a blend of murderous handsomeness, and a man such as %name% was only the former. Dispirited by the lack of fame he thought he had earned, he purchased his freedom and departed the blood sport.} {Gladiators usually cross from fighting pit to fighting pit, so a sturdy, well skilled fighter such as %name% is rare to find in the wild. Yet here he stands, albeit with enough scars to make a flagellant blush. | You've met many a warrior, but rarely one with the particular skillsets of a pit fighter such as %name%. All the clashing in the arenas has made him a clever warrior indeed, and also one with many a scar and injury to match his time there. | There's many pairings in this world, and a gladiator with an untouched body is not one of them. %name% is a skilled fighter, but he earned those experiences with his own blood and body. | An impressive gladiatorial resume such as the one %name% brings hints at a man well versed in killing. The many scars, however, flatly state that his time in the pits came with an irreversible price of their own. | Gladiators such as %name% could be the most skilled fighters in all the land, but the fighting pits are full of games and are designed to bring harm to all who partake. The man is a talented warrior, but he wears the scars and wounds of a career in the arena.}
fd1c0716228b8cf31953.translation: {南方到处都是各色奴隶，因欠着镀金者的债而被称作负债者。他们大多被送去耕田，只有少数被挑进角斗场，彼此搏杀。 | 北方人也举行比武大会，可论血腥残酷，远不及南方的角斗场。 | 在南方，富人穷人都喜欢为角斗场上的斗士欢呼。 | 南方的角斗场里，既有负债者，也有自愿来杀人的家伙。 | 角斗场既是搏杀的血腥场所，也是下注的赌坊。在南方，几乎只有这里能见到富人与穷人挤作一团。}{%name%便出自这群人。他很快脱颖而出，攒钱赎身，离开了角斗场。至于过过那样的日子后还能找到多少“自由”，便是另一回事了。 | %name%深受观众喜爱，后来得到富有赞助人的“赦免”，结束了角斗士生涯。可早早退役后，他却觉得生活空空荡荡。 | 像%name%这样善于杀戮的人，能靠战绩赎回自由，只是嗜血的冲动至今仍未离开他。 | %name%卷入了一桩假赛风波，被禁止进入角斗场一年。 | 像%name%这样的角斗士，不仅深受大众欢迎，更格外讨女人喜欢。他与一位贵族的妻子私通后，只得趁夜被人偷偷送走，免得遭到阉割。 | 角斗场上最受欢迎的人，通常既会杀人，又长得英俊。%name%却只占了前一样。他自认应得的名声迟迟不到，心灰意冷之下，便赎回自由，告别了这场血腥的竞技。}{角斗士通常只是从一座角斗场辗转到另一座，因此像%name%这样强健又老练的斗士，在外面很难遇见。可他此刻就站在这里，只是身上的伤疤，多得足以让苦修者自惭形秽。 | 你见过许多战士，却很少有人拥有%name%这样的角斗士所独具的本领。无数场交锋将他磨炼得精明老到，也留下了与那段岁月相称的伤疤和旧伤。 | 世上有许多天生一对的事物，角斗士与毫发无伤的身体却绝不在其中。%name%武艺精湛，可那些经验都是拿自己的血肉换来的。 | %name%带来的辉煌战绩，表明他深谙杀人之道。可遍身的伤疤也明明白白地告诉你，那些角斗场上的岁月，索取了无法挽回的代价。 | %name%这样的角斗士，或许是全境技艺最精湛的战士。但角斗场里花样百出，处处都在设法让参与者受伤。他很有本事，却也带着整个角斗生涯积累下来的伤疤与创痛。}

8dda7746740431e144fb.source: Gravediggers are used to physical labor and handling the dead.
8dda7746740431e144fb.translation: 掘墓人习惯体力劳动，也习惯与死人打交道。

b38b324f25bdc81c7eff.source: With the great successes of the %companyname%, %name% the gravedigger got continued practice in his trade. As the crowns began to stack, he eventually left the company and returned to the graveyards. Last you heard, he had retired to digging holes again and was happily raising a family of sextons.
b38b324f25bdc81c7eff.translation: 随着%companyname%捷报频传，掘墓人%name%的老本行也一直没闲着。积蓄渐丰后，他终于离开战团，回到了墓园。上次听说，他又开始挖坑了，还在快活地养育一大家子未来的墓园看守。

93a4a404b1826a35bcbc.source: The way you heard things, %name% the gravedigger was one of the last men to leave the %companyname%. With hardly a crown to his name, he slipped hard into drinking and last you heard his body was found in a muddied gully.
93a4a404b1826a35bcbc.translation: 据你听说，掘墓人%name%是最后几个离开%companyname%的人之一。他几乎身无分文，很快沉溺于酗酒。最后的消息是，有人在泥泞的沟渠中发现了他的尸体。

a1c1c0837bb8032b2ef3.source: {%name% got his start as a gravedigger by burying his baby brother. | Putting a sword to his drunken father's neck, %name%'s start in gravedigging was a nasty one. First he buried the crime, and then he buried the lawmen who came around asking questions. | After disease swept through %townname%, %name% was the last man standing. He had to abandon his trade to take up the only thing left: gravedigging.} There's a look in the dead, they say. But there's also a look in those who have seen the dead. %name% has now spent a life and a half {staring at corpses | putting bodies in the ground | digging graves, big ones and small}. To the gravedigger, {death is now but a science | the dead have been better company than the living | earning gold for burying the dead is no new task}. {Employed by a wagon-train, %name% traveled the land and dug it up, too. But one day his burial was suddenly undone. Not by the buzzards or rats, but by the dead itself. Seeing such a sight, and having to bury the same man twice, no doubt compels a swift career change. | Every gravedigger is eyed with suspicion. It wasn't long until his patrons became accusers and the notion of a horrific crime of undead passion drove him from his work. The claims are absurd, but you can't get a read on his pale face. It's like playing cards with the moon. | By now, the man looks as if he could use a change of scenery. Just don't ask him to bury the casualties.}
a1c1c0837bb8032b2ef3.translation: {%name%的掘墓人生涯，始于埋葬自己尚在襁褓中的弟弟。 | %name%把剑架上了酗酒父亲的脖子，就这样血腥地开始了掘墓人的生涯。他先埋掉自己的罪行，随后又埋掉了上门盘问的差役。 | 瘟疫席卷%townname%后，只剩%name%一人活着。他不得不放弃旧业，干起唯一还有活可做的行当：掘墓。}人们说，死人有一种特殊的神情。其实，见多了死人的人也一样。%name%已经花了比一辈子还漫长的光阴，{盯着尸体 | 把尸体放进土里 | 挖掘大大小小的坟墓}。对这名掘墓人而言，{死亡如今不过是一门学问 | 死人比活人更适合作伴 | 靠埋葬死者挣钱，早已不是什么新鲜差事}。{受雇于一支车队时，%name%走遍各地，也挖遍各地。可有一天，他才填好的坟忽然又开了。干这事的不是秃鹫，也不是老鼠，而是死者自己。见过这番景象，还得把同一个人埋上两回，任谁都会赶紧换个行当。 | 掘墓人总免不了招人猜疑。没过多久，原本的雇主就变成了指控者，一桩骇人的恋尸罪名让他干不下去。这些指控荒唐透顶，可你从他苍白的脸上读不出半点端倪，简直像在和月亮打牌。 | 如今看来，他确实该换个环境了。只要别再让他埋葬死者就好。}

d70c4b5ab588d482c769.source: Graverobbers are not faint of heart.

1907a2624eea9e60a2a7.source: Graverobbers like %name% aren't exactly the most well liked men in this world, but all you needed from him was to be a great mercenary and he came through in spades. After you left the business, you learned that the graverobber stayed for the long haul. From what you know, he's now the company's trainer, helping green recruits get up to speed.
1907a2624eea9e60a2a7.translation: 像%name%这样的盗墓人，实在算不上受欢迎，但你只需要他当好佣兵，而他干得相当出色。你离开这行后，听说他一直留在战团。据你所知，他如今已成为战团教官，帮助新兵尽快上手。

2fddb4c53c0d33663550.source: A man like %name% the graverobber came to the company to help escape from his most unlawful and immoral errors, and what better way to do that than killing people for money? Unfortunately, the %companyname% slowly began to fall apart. You learned that %name% eventually left the company and joined with a similar, competing outfit. You're not sure where he is now, and you're not sure whether to be insulted by his betrayal or understand the reasoning behind it. Business is only business, after all.
2fddb4c53c0d33663550.translation: 盗墓贼%name%加入战团，是为了逃开自己那些违法又缺德的往事，而有什么比拿钱杀人更好的出路呢？可惜，%companyname%还是渐渐分崩离析。你后来得知，%name%最终离开了战团，加入了另一支类似的竞争队伍。如今他身在何处，你不清楚；面对他的背叛，你也不知道该感到受辱，还是理解他的理由。毕竟，生意终究只是生意。

ed8347f0ea516251c851.source: {What compels a man to disturb those who have passed away? | With rumors of the dead rising again, perhaps it is but forward thinking to go around digging up graves. | An enemy to moral standards and sensibilities, men who take spades to fresh graves find few allies. | A coward attacks a man when he's down, a graverobber attacks a man when he's really down. | It is trivial how easily a man abrogated by death can be acquired by mere graverobbing. | When it comes to death, worms take the flesh, and time the bones, but graverobbers get the jewels.} {Raised by an abusive mother, %name% found happier coordinance with the dead than the living. | After many lonely nights in hermitry, %name% is said to have taken up dancing with the dead. | %name% romanced beneath the stars, but pale and cold describes more than just the night sky. | For entertainment in a boring life, %name% is known to visit the murky gastines of graveyards. | Swindled by a salesman, %name% found himself digging up graves for loot. So the story goes, anyway. | Once a fine jeweler, dementia drove %name% into crafting a very different style of attire. A toothy necklace chatters at you as he explains.} {The deviancies of such a man may know no bounds, but his for-now warm body could be of use. | He's not right in the head, but maybe he's right with a sword in hand. Maybe. | Disturbing as he might be, desperate times call for desperate recruits. | He wears a plain necklace with a subtle offwhite color best described as 'bone'. | Driven away by an especially mad mob, %name% is one of many outcasts to venture into the world of mercenaries. | The man is quiet, but you can't shut him up around a graveyard. | Hopefully he likes putting cold bodies into graves as much as he likes digging them up.}
ed8347f0ea516251c851.translation: {究竟是什么，会驱使一个人去惊扰逝者？ | 既然传闻死人正在复起，提前四处掘坟，或许也算未雨绸缪。 | 朝新坟挥铲的人，冒犯了道德，也触犯了常情，很难交到什么朋友。 | 懦夫欺负倒地的人，盗墓贼欺负的，则是倒得更深的人。 | 死亡把一个人夺走，盗墓却只消几铲便能把他弄回来，说来真是轻而易举。 | 人死之后，蛆虫取走血肉，岁月消磨白骨，珠宝则归了盗墓贼。}{%name%由一位虐待他的母亲养大，与死人相处反倒比与活人更快活。 | 据说，在隐居中熬过无数孤寂的夜晚后，%name%开始与死者共舞。 | %name%曾在群星下谈情说爱，只是苍白冰冷的，远不止夜空。 | 为给无聊的生活找点乐子，%name%常去墓园那些阴暗荒僻的角落闲逛。 | %name%遭商贩欺骗，落得只能掘坟取财。至少他自己是这么说的。 | %name%曾是个出色的珠宝匠，后来神志失常，开始制作风格迥异的饰物。他解释时，脖子上那串牙齿项链正对着你咔哒作响。}{这人的怪癖也许没有底线，不过他眼下还热乎的身子，倒可能派上用场。 | 他脑子不太好使，没准手里的剑能好使些。没准吧。 | 他或许令人不安，可绝望的年头，也只能招些绝望的兵。 | 他戴着一条朴素的项链，颜色淡淡发白，最贴切的说法，大概就是“骨头色”。 | %name%被一群格外疯狂的暴民赶了出来，成了众多投身佣兵世界的弃民之一。 | 这人平时很安静，可一到墓园附近，就再也闭不上嘴。 | 但愿他喜欢把冰冷的尸体埋进去，能和挖出来一样喜欢。}

f94e197648590625e764.source: Hedge Knights are competitive individuals that excel in fighting man against man with brute strength and heavy armor, but less so in cooperating with others or in swiftness.
f94e197648590625e764.translation: 流浪骑士争强好胜，擅长凭蛮力与重甲单打独斗，却不长于协作，也不够灵活。

b404ab23e7728d0fce99.source: A man like %name% would always find a way. The hedge knight eventually, if not inevitably, left the company and set out on his own. Unlike many other brothers, he did not spend his crowns on land or ladders with which to climb the noble life. Instead, he bought himself the finest war horses and the talents of armorers. The behemoth of a man rode from one jousting tournament to the next, winning them all with ease. He's still at it to this day, and you think he won't stop until he's dead. The hedge knight simply knows no other life.
b404ab23e7728d0fce99.translation: 像%name%这样的人，总能找到自己的路。这名流浪骑士终究还是离开战团，独自闯荡去了。与许多弟兄不同，他既没花钱买地，也没拿积蓄去攀附贵族。他买来了最上等的战马，请最出色的铠甲匠为自己效力。这个巨人般的汉子骑马奔赴一场又一场比武，轻轻松松拿下全部胜利。直到今天，他仍乐此不疲。你觉得他大概要到死才肯停下来，因为流浪骑士只懂得这样过活。

750d5829ab2aedbd3e03.source: %name% the hedge knight eventually left the company. He traveled the lands, returning to his favorite past time of jousting, which was really a cover for his real favorite past time of lancing men off horses in a shower of splinters and glory. At some point, he was ordered to 'throw' a match against a pitiful and gangly prince to earn the nobleman some prestige. Instead, the hedge knight drove his lance through the man's skull. Furious, the lord of the land ordered the hedge knight killed. They say over a hundred soldiers took to his home and only half returned alive.
750d5829ab2aedbd3e03.translation: 流浪骑士%name%最终离开了战团。他四处游历，重拾最钟爱的马上比武。说是喜欢比武，其实他更喜欢在木屑四溅、喝彩如潮之际，一枪把人挑下马。后来，有人命他故意输给一个瘦弱可怜的王子，好为那贵族挣点名声。他却一枪贯穿了王子的头颅。当地领主勃然大怒，下令处死这名流浪骑士。据说，一百多名士兵杀到他家，只有一半活着回来。

7cece8e3a126f22dd709.source: {Some men are born to be feared. Well over six feet tall, %name%'s stature alone is a threatening one. | %name%'s shadow casts over smaller men - and they seem to only further shrink when he walks by. | Standing amongst men like a bear in a suit of armor, %name% earns plenty of double-takes. | Years of brutal combat with his equally huge brothers left %name% a scarred and scary figure.} {The hedge knight has spent many seasons taking his prized horse to jousting tournaments. Unfortunately, a polearm crowned his mount, leaving him without a ride. | A mercenary in the company of himself, the hedge knight wandered for years, doing battle for those who offered the most crowns. | When he cleaved five men with one swing, three of which were on his side, the hedge knight was banned from service in every army in the land. | Ordered to kill a lord's enemies, the hedge knight kicked in the door of a family and slaughtered them all with his bare hands. When the lord refused to pay, %name% killed him, too. | The hedge knight has spent many nights sleeping peacefully beneath a pale moon - and just as many days killing ruthlessly beneath a shining sun.} {Always on the hunt for more crowns, the company of sellswords seemed like a good fit. | Too terrifying to be employed for long, %name% seeks the company of men who will not piss themselves when he grabs a weapon. | Tired of killing jousters and lords, as well as women and children, %name% sees mercenary work as something of a vacation. | War has apparently gotten in the way of %name%'s jousting career. He seeks to amend that problem.}
7cece8e3a126f22dd709.translation: {有些人生来就令人畏惧。%name%身高远超六英尺，光是块头就足够吓人。 | %name%的身影笼罩着那些矮小的汉子，每当他走过，他们仿佛还要再缩上一截。 | %name%站在人群里，像一头披着铠甲的熊，谁见了都忍不住多看两眼。 | 多年来与同样魁梧的兄弟残酷厮斗，让%name%伤痕累累，面目骇人。}{这名流浪骑士曾骑着心爱的坐骑，年复一年参加马上比武。可惜一柄长杆兵器劈中了战马的脑袋，让他失去了坐骑。 | 这名流浪骑士独自一人便是一支佣兵队，游荡多年，谁出的克朗多，就替谁打仗。 | 他一挥武器砍倒五个人，其中三个还是自己人。从此，这片土地上的每支军队都不肯再收留这名流浪骑士。 | 领主命这名流浪骑士除掉仇敌，他便踹开一家人的房门，徒手杀光了他们。领主赖账不肯付钱，%name%连他也一并杀了。 | 这名流浪骑士曾在苍白月色下安眠无数个夜晚，也曾在明亮阳光下无情杀戮无数个白天。}{他总在寻找更多克朗，佣兵战团似乎正合他的心意。 | %name%太过吓人，总受雇不久就被打发。他想找一群不会一看他拿起武器就吓尿裤子的同伴。 | %name%杀腻了比武骑士和领主，也杀腻了妇孺。在他看来，当佣兵简直算是度假。 | 战乱显然妨碍了%name%的比武生涯。他想把这麻烦解决掉。}

3d88de7438a5a96c0017.source: Historians are studious individuals with vast amounts of knowledge, none of it any use on the battlefield.
3d88de7438a5a96c0017.translation: 历史学家勤学博闻，可惜满腹学问在战场上都派不上用场。

39544788ad589d2c886d.source: You did not expect the historian, %name%, to stay in the company forever. He eventually left and it is said he took with him a large trove of scrolls. As it turns out, he was compiling a list of the %companyname%'s achievements. He created a codex of all its accomplishments, enshrining the name of all the mercenaries into the history books for future generations to see. You hope they learn something from your doings.
39544788ad589d2c886d.translation: 你从没指望历史学者%name%会永远留在战团。他最终还是离开了，据说走时带走了一大堆卷轴。后来你才知道，他一直在整理%companyname%的功绩。他将战团的全部成就编纂成书，把每一位佣兵的名字载入史册，留待后人翻阅。你只盼他们能从你们的所作所为中，学到些什么。

732c5168de0b83fb39fb.source: The %companyname% continued its decline and many non-fighters such as %name% the historian saw this as a good time to leave. You tried to keep up with these men, but the historian was particularly easy to find: he left a paper trail. You sought the man out, asking scribes if they had heard of him. They said he was a mere little man writing a tome about how dark, violent, and pointless the life of a sellsword is.
732c5168de0b83fb39fb.translation: %companyname%继续衰败，许多像历史学者%name%这样并非战士出身的人，都觉得该离开了。你试着打听他们的近况，其中最容易找到的就是历史学者——他留下了一路笔墨。你向抄写员们询问他的消息，想找到他。他们说，那不过是个不起眼的小人物，正埋头写一部厚书，讲述佣兵的一生何其黑暗、暴力，又毫无意义。

3e153f74f3e14df20ae4.source: {Always a voracious reader, %name%'s early life consisted of long nights in %randomcity%'s library. | Bullied by his stronger peers, a young %name% retreated into the world of books. | Looking for where man's past truly lies, %name% read books and studied human nature. | With so many changes in the world, %name% decided to help record them. | A quick-learner with a penchant for a good read, %name% sought to envision the world on paper for others. | A scholar of %randomcity%'s small college, %name% records the histories of the world for future generations. | Chilled by dark events in the world, %name% stopped studying plants and began recording human history.} {A proper historian seeks the closest sources he can get, which has brought the man to the company of mercenaries. | After brigands ruined his written works, the man strapped on his boots to carve out new research - personally. | When his professor said his research was rubbish, the historian went out into the world to prove him wrong. | Accused of plagiarism, the historian was kicked out of academia. He seeks redemption in the world of what he studied: war. | Using his position in academia to bed women, eventual scandals and controversies drove the historian from his field, and left him penniless and ready to take on any job. | Bored with reading about adventurers, the historian figured he'd suit up to fashion himself a closer look at the real thing. | With so many mercenary bands floating around, the historian sought to attach himself for some real-life studying.} {%name% has little in common with actual soldiers, but his imaginative mind fancies a good battle nonetheless. | While %name% spent all his life writing, he spent exactly none of it fighting. Until now. | %name% has the itch to record your outfit's travels. He can help by grabbing a sword and suiting up. | A bag of books is hefted over %name%'s shoulder. You suggest a flail as replacement. It's similar, but pointier and stabbier. | %name% is frequently found scribbling notes as he still sees the world with a researcher's eye. | %name% comes with a pocketful of quill pens. The feathers would make for some pretty good arrows. | You can place good faith in %name%'s earnest want to research, but maybe not so much faith in his ability to swing a sword. | %name%'s time with the outfit is to develop a theory, but can he survive the experiments? | You promise %name% that, shall he perish, you will find a way to record his life. He thanks you and hands over his will. It's written in a language foreign to you and you can read absolutely none of it. You smile back anyway.}
3e153f74f3e14df20ae4.translation: {%name%从小就如饥似渴地读书，早年的许多个长夜，都是在%randomcity%的图书馆里度过的。 | 年少的%name%受尽强壮同龄人的欺凌，便躲进了书本的世界。 | 为探寻人类过去的真相，%name%研读书籍，钻研人性。 | 世事变幻如此之多，%name%决定尽一份力，把它们记录下来。 | %name%学东西很快，又爱读好书，便想将世界描绘在纸上，供他人一观。 | 身为%randomcity%一所小学院的学者，%name%为后世记录这世界的历史。 | 世间的黑暗事件让%name%不寒而栗，于是他不再研究植物，转而记录人类的历史。}{称职的历史学者总要尽可能接近第一手材料，因此他来到了佣兵之中。 | 强盗毁掉了他的著作，他便系紧靴子，亲自出门，重新开展研究。 | 教授说他的研究一文不值，他便走向外面的世界，决心证明对方错了。 | 因被指控剽窃，这名历史学者遭到学界驱逐。他想在自己研究的领域——战争之中——洗刷耻辱。 | 他利用学术地位与女人厮混，最终丑闻缠身，被赶出学界。如今他身无分文，什么工作都肯干。 | 厌倦了读别人的冒险故事，他决定穿戴上阵，凑近些亲眼看看真正的冒险。 | 四处游荡的佣兵队伍如此之多，这位历史学者便想加入其中一支，做些实地研究。}{%name%与真正的士兵没多少相似之处，不过他那颗想象丰富的脑袋，倒很向往一场精彩的战斗。 | %name%一辈子都在写作，却从没花过片刻打仗。直到如今。 | %name%迫不及待地想记录战团的旅程。想帮忙的话，他大可以先拿把剑，把甲穿上。 | %name%肩上扛着一袋书。你建议换成链枷，差不多的玩意儿，只是多了些扎人的尖刺。 | %name%常常埋头记笔记，仍旧用研究者的眼光打量这个世界。 | %name%带来了一口袋羽毛笔。那些羽毛拿去做箭，倒是相当不错。 | 你可以相信%name%做研究的诚意，不过对他挥剑的本事，最好别抱太大指望。 | %name%跟着战团是为了构建一套理论，可他能活过那些试验吗？ | 你向%name%保证，万一他死了，你会想办法记下他的一生。他道过谢，将遗嘱递给你。那是用一种你不认识的语言写的，你一个字也看不懂，还是回了他一个微笑。}

He thanks you and hands over his will. It's written in a language foreign to you and you can read absolutely none of it. You smile back anyway.}

ceae46a868bfb3b8ecbe.source: Houndmasters are used to handle dogs of war.
ceae46a868bfb3b8ecbe.translation: 驯犬师熟悉战犬的驯养与指挥。

4e99d18e6402868cb9fb.source: Dogs were not simply 'hounds' to %name%, despite his title as 'houndmaster.' To him, they were the most loyal friends of his life. After leaving the company, he discovered an ingenious way to breed the animals specifically tailored to the desires of the nobility. Wanted a brutish beast for a guard dog? He could do it. Wanted something small and cuddly for the children? He could do that, too. The former mercenary now earns an incredible earning doing what he loves - working with dogs.
4e99d18e6402868cb9fb.translation: 尽管顶着“驯犬师”的名头，对%name%而言，狗却从不只是“猎犬”，而是他一生最忠诚的朋友。离开战团后，他琢磨出一种巧妙的育犬办法，专门迎合贵族的喜好。想要一头凶猛的巨犬看家？他办得到。想给孩子找只娇小可爱的宠物？他也办得到。如今，这位前佣兵靠着自己最爱的事情——与狗打交道——挣下了惊人的财富。

5695eacdcd8e97ad27bb.source: What's merely a hound to one man is a loyal beast to %name%. After leaving the company, the houndmaster went out to work for the nobility. Unfortunately, he refused to let hundreds of his dogs be used as a battle vanguard to be thrown away for some short-lived tactical advantage. He was hanged for his 'traitorous ideals'.
5695eacdcd8e97ad27bb.translation: 别人眼里只是猎犬的动物，对%name%却是忠诚的伙伴。离开战团后，这位驯犬师为贵族效力。不幸的是，他不肯让数百只爱犬充当前锋，白白牺牲，只为换取短暂的战术优势。他因“叛逆思想”被处以绞刑。

3074e519a176c8e9751f.source: Wardogs unleashed by this character will start at confident morale
3074e519a176c8e9751f.translation: 由此角色放出的战犬，会以自信士气投入战斗

1d2e9c3d5dce4443def7.source: {%name%'s fondness for dogs started after his father won a pup in a shooting contest. | When a dog saved him from a bear, %name% dedicated his life to the canine lot. | Seeing a dog stave off a would-be robber, %name%'s fondness for the mutts only grew. | A young, bird-hunting %name% quickly saw the honor, loyalty, and workmanship of a dog. | Once bitten by a wild dog, %name% confronted his fear of canines by learning to train them.} {The houndmaster spent many years working for a local lord. He gave up the post after the liege struck a dog down just for sport. | Quick with training his mongrels, the houndmaster put his dogs into a lucrative traveling tradeshow. | The man made a great deal of money on the dog-fighting circuits, his mutts renowned for their easily commanded - and unleashed - ferocity. | Employed by lawmen, the houndmaster used his strong-nosed dogs to hunt down many a criminal element. | Used by a local lord, many of the houndmaster's dogs found their way onto the battlefield. | For many years, the houndmaster used his dogs to help lift the spirits of orphaned children and the crippled.} {Now, though, %name% seeks a change of vocation. | When he heard word of a mercenary's pay, %name% decided to try his hand at being a sellsword. | Approached by a sellsword to buy one of his dogs, %name% became more interested in the prospect of he, himself, becoming a mercenary. | Tired of training dogs for this purpose or that, %name% seeks to train himself for... well, this purpose or that. | An interesting prospect, you can only hope %name% is as loyal as the dogs he once commanded.}
1d2e9c3d5dce4443def7.translation: {父亲在一次射击比赛中赢回一只小狗后，%name%便喜欢上了狗。 | 一条狗把%name%从熊口下救出来，他便决心将一生献给这些犬类伙伴。 | 亲眼见过一条狗挡住企图抢劫的歹徒，%name%对狗的喜爱更深了。 | 年少的%name%打猎捕鸟时，很快便见识了猎犬的勇气、忠诚与勤勉。 | %name%曾被野狗咬过，为克服对狗的恐惧，他开始学习驯犬。}{这名驯犬师为当地领主效力多年。后来领主仅仅为了取乐便打死了一条狗，他于是辞去了差事。 | 这名驯犬师训练杂种狗颇有一手，便带它们巡回展示，赚得盆满钵满。 | 他在各地斗狗场挣了不少钱。那些杂种狗以凶狠闻名，却又极听号令，能收能放。 | 受雇于差役时，这名驯犬师靠着猎犬灵敏的鼻子，追捕了许多罪犯。 | 当地领主征用了这名驯犬师的许多狗，将它们送上战场。 | 多年来，这名驯犬师一直用自己的狗，给孤儿和残疾者带去慰藉与欢笑。}{不过如今，%name%想换一份营生。 | 听说佣兵的酬劳后，%name%决定试试这份差事。 | 一名佣兵前来买狗，却让%name%对自己也去当佣兵生出了更大的兴趣。 | %name%厌倦了为各种用途训练狗，如今想训练训练自己，好去……嗯，派上各种用场。 | 这是个值得考虑的人选。你只盼%name%能和他曾指挥的狗一样忠诚。}

fa242772e3a5b16ac020.source: Hunters are used to expertly hunt animals with bow and arrow, and traverse the woods on their own.
fa242772e3a5b16ac020.translation: 猎人擅长用弓箭猎杀动物，也习惯独自穿行林间。

94cbdd95547b50ac8277.source: While the %companyname% continued on with great success, %name% the hunter eventually saw fit to leave it all behind.
