He returned to the forests and fields, hunting deer and small game. He rarely showed the grim reality of hunting humans, but you have to imagine he'd just rather stop doing it. As far as you know, he's doing well for himself these days. He purchased a bit of land and helps guide nobles on pricy hunting trips.
94cbdd95547b50ac8277.translation: 尽管%companyname%依旧战功赫赫，猎人%name%最终还是决定把这一切留在身后。他重返林野，追猎鹿群和小型猎物。他很少流露出猎杀同类带来的阴影，但你猜，他大概只是不想再干这种事了。据你所知，他如今过得不错，买了一小块地，还为贵族们的昂贵狩猎之行担任向导。

cbc9679a6a0a2e45c668.source: With the decline of the %companyname% readily obvious, %name% the hunter departed from the company and returned to game hunting. Unfortunately, a hunting trip with a nobleman went awry when the lord was gored through both cheeks by a boar. The hunter, feeling he'd be blamed, shot by the nobleman and his guard and fled through the forests on his own. He has not been seen since.
cbc9679a6a0a2e45c668.translation: 眼看%companyname%的衰落已无可挽回，猎人%name%离开战团，重操打猎的旧业。可惜，在陪一名贵族狩猎时出了意外：野猪的獠牙贯穿了那位老爷的两颊。猎人觉得自己免不了被问罪，便从贵族和卫兵身旁飞奔而过，独自逃进森林。从此，再也没人见过他。

03e35c3fa3378a702190.source: {Without his father around, %name%'s mother taught him how to shoot a bow, and how to feed the rest of his family. | Born in the hinterlands of %randomtown%, %name% has spent much of his life stalking the beasts amongst the trees. | %name% once took a bet to shoot an apple off a pig's head. He missed. With a belly full of bacon, he became determined to never miss again - unless it meant more bacon, of course. | Early in his life, %name% liked to traipse about the forests. When a rabid fox attacked him, he learned to take a bow. When a devilish eagle clawed his face, he learned to shoot it.} {Once employed by local royalty, a disastrous boar hunt ended with a gored baron and all the blame - and blood - on %name%'s hands. | The hunter hid the thought well, but for the longest time he wondered what it would be like to hunt the ultimate game: man. | Sadly, a bad game of peasant-roulette forced the deer hunter into seeking other means of income. | Unfortunately, he is not nearly as good at cooking deer as he is at shooting them. A dinner consisting of undercooked meats poisoned his entire family. His desperation for a new life is understandable. | After an arduous trip to town to sell meats and leathers, he followed the call of mercenary work. | War drove the game out of the forests, and the hunt out of %name%. Now he seeks another line of work. | When his wife fell ill, he could not heal her with hunted meat. Needing to earn crowns to pay for treatment, he took up the vocation of sellswords - or sellbows, as it were.} {Any outfit could use a deadeye such as this man. | Not entirely without faults, %name% is a professional bowman nonetheless. | A quick demonstration is offered: %name% shoots one arrow high into the sky, and with another he knocks it out. Impressive. | %name% looks like he has something to prove - just make sure he does it at range. When first given a sword, he grabbed it at the wrong end. Yes, that end. | The hunter wields his bow like another limb, and shoots his arrows like a preacher does words.}
03e35c3fa3378a702190.translation: {父亲不在身边，%name%的母亲教会他如何拉弓射箭，也教会他如何养活家里其余的人。 | %name%出生在%randomtown%的偏远乡野，一生大半时间都在林间追踪野兽。 | %name%曾与人打赌，要射下猪头上的苹果。他射偏了。吃了一肚子猪肉后，他决心再也不射偏——当然，除非射偏能换来更多猪肉。 | %name%小时候喜欢在森林里闲逛。被一只疯狐狸袭击后，他学会了随身带弓；被一只凶鹰抓伤脸后，他又学会了如何射箭。} {他曾受雇于当地贵族，可一场野猪狩猎酿成大祸，男爵被獠牙刺穿，鲜血和罪责全落到了%name%手上。 | 猎人把这个念头藏得很深，但他早已好奇了许多年：追猎终极的猎物——人——会是什么滋味？ | 可惜，一场倒霉的“农夫轮盘赌”迫使这位猎鹿人另谋生计。 | 遗憾的是，他烹鹿的手艺远不如射鹿。一顿没煮熟的肉，让全家人都中了毒。他迫切想换一种生活，也是情有可原。 | 一趟辛苦的进城卖肉卖皮之行过后，他响应了佣兵招募。 | 战争把猎物赶出了森林，也磨灭了%name%的狩猎兴致。如今，他打算换个行当。 | 妻子患病时，打来的猎物治不好她。为了挣克朗付医药费，他做起了刀头舔血的营生——不过准确来说，他用的是弓。} {任何队伍都用得上这样的神射手。 | %name%虽不是毫无缺点，却确实是名专业弓手。 | %name%随手露了一招：先向高空射出一箭，再用第二箭将其击落。令人佩服。 | %name%似乎急于证明自己，记得让他在远处出手。第一次给他剑时，他竟抓住了错误的那一头。没错，就是剑刃。 | 猎人用弓如使臂指，射出的箭就像传教士嘴里的话一样滔滔不绝。}

5a98197c303ec30fabc1.source: Jugglers need to have good reflexes and hand-eye-coordination for their profession.
5a98197c303ec30fabc1.translation: 杂耍艺人的行当需要敏捷反应与良好的手眼协调。

4b7b732d2f7d91d6ec64.source: %name% the juggler took all his mercenary money and started a traveling troupe of performers. Last you heard, he started an entire theater and puts on a new play a month!
4b7b732d2f7d91d6ec64.translation: 杂耍艺人%name%拿着当佣兵挣来的全部钱财，办起了巡回演出团。最后听说，他已经开了一整座剧院，每个月都会推出新剧！

2899a0934cd7bf2bb737.source: %name% the juggler retired from fighting. He was performing for a gaudy nobleman in the {south | north | east | west} when an act went horribly wrong. Word has it he was thrown off a tower for his mistake, but you prefer to not believe that.
2899a0934cd7bf2bb737.translation: 杂耍艺人%name%告别战斗，在{南方 | 北方 | 东方 | 西方}为一位衣着浮夸的贵族表演时，出了严重差错。据说他因此被扔下高塔，但你宁愿不信这种传闻。

bb9971fdf43a59de7deb.source: {Taught by his step-brother, %name% took up juggling like a sailor to his oars. | Although sneered at by his peers, %name% always loved juggling. | Visited by a troupe of jesters, %name% was most enamored - and eventually taught - by one particularly interesting man: a juggler. | Son to a local lord, %name%'s embarrassing obsession with juggling and entertaining had him exiled from the family line. | %name% didn't juggle just for the sake of it, but to earn the laughter and applause of an audience.} {Unfortunately, there's not many folks to entertain when war is ravaging the land. | But crowds and crowns are sparse in a land of misery and suffering. | But a juggling accident involving adzes and a royal infant had the entertainer running for his life. | So good at flipping swords and daggers, it wasn't long until he was accused of sorcery and driven from his passion. | Sadly, %name%'s skill in juggling led to much jealousy amongst his fellow jesters. They conspired against him - and his poor wrists. | When an assassin killed the lord he was entertaining, the juggler was the first to be accused. He barely escaped with his life.} {Now, %name% seeks a new path, even if death itself has become his audience. | Now, %name% finds respite in the company of equally down-on-their-luck men. | With fast hands and quick reactions, %name% should have no problem hitting his targets. | Juggling knives with his eyes closed, %name% knows exactly where to throw each blade. | There is far more coin in killing than juggling, a sad reality %name% has come to accept.}
bb9971fdf43a59de7deb.translation: {在继兄弟的教导下，%name%学起杂耍来就像水手操桨，得心应手。 | 尽管同伴们嗤之以鼻，%name%始终热爱杂耍。 | 一班丑角来访时，%name%迷上了其中一位格外有趣的杂耍艺人，后来还拜他学艺。 | %name%是当地领主之子，却因痴迷杂耍和逗人取乐，让家族蒙羞，最终被逐出家门。 | %name%耍杂技并非只为耍着好玩，而是为了赢得观众的笑声和掌声。}{可惜，战火蹂躏大地，也没剩多少人还有心情看热闹。 | 可在这片满是苦难的土地上，观众少，克朗也少。 | 一场牵涉扁斧和王族婴儿的杂耍事故，却让他不得不逃命。 | 他抛接刀剑匕首的本领太过高明，没过多久便被指为妖术，被迫放弃了自己的热爱。 | 可惜，%name%的杂耍技艺招来了同行丑角的嫉妒。他们合谋算计了他，也没放过他那双可怜的手腕。 | 刺客杀死了他正在逗乐的领主，这名杂耍艺人第一个遭到指控，好不容易才捡回一条命。}{如今，%name%想另寻出路，哪怕台下的观众已换成死神。 | 如今，%name%在一群同样落魄的汉子中找到了暂时的安宁。 | %name%手快、反应也快，命中目标想必不成问题。 | %name%闭着眼也能抛接飞刀，清楚每一把刀该掷向何处。 | 杀人比杂耍挣钱多得多，%name%已经接受了这个可悲的现实。}

99beaf62202feefc9f94.source: A killer on the run may kill again, and he knows where to aim.
99beaf62202feefc9f94.translation: 在逃杀人犯可能会再次杀人，而且知道该瞄准哪里。

18674e9b824af7b4e740.source: Always a risk taker, you accepted %name% into the %companyname%'s ranks despite him being a killer on the run. It worked in your favor as he proved himself an able and brave sellsword. As far as you know, he is still with the company, thoroughly enjoying every 'business' opportunity it affords him.
18674e9b824af7b4e740.translation: 你一向敢于冒险，明知%name%是在逃杀人犯，仍收他进了%companyname%。这次冒险值得，他证明了自己既勇敢又能干。据你所知，他至今仍在战团里，尽情享受每一次“生意”机会。

54d8c54e86080d4c24f6.source: While many doubted the risk of hiring a killer on the run such as %name%, the man did prove himself a very capable sellsword. Unfortunately, an old life never trails far behind and bounty hunters kidnapped him in the night. You can find his skeleton squatting in a gibbet fifty feet in the air.
54d8c54e86080d4c24f6.translation: 许多人质疑雇用%name%这样的在逃杀人犯是否值得冒险，不过他确实是个出色的佣兵。可惜旧日罪行总会追上来，赏金猎人在夜里掳走了他。如今，他的骸骨蜷缩在离地五十英尺的铁笼里。

5b1da56aab1fb1872ed7.source: {%fullname% has a face that no one desires - one fit for a wanted poster. | With blood on his hands, %name% resembles a man recently described to you by bounty hunters. | %name% looks about ready to join any outfit - or disappear into its ranks. | Upon meeting people, %name% stammers out his name as if reluctant to part with it.} {Recognizing %name% is no hard feat: this man is a known-murderer, the blood of both his cuckolding wife and her lover on his hands. | His eyes are dark and shifting. There is a crime behind them, but also a sense of humanity, as if he knows he has done wrong and is looking to make amends. | Mud stands up to his legs. He's been running for a long time. His hands tremble, too, for his legs run from what his hands have done. | They say he killed his newborn daughter, having always wanted a son instead. | Some believe he struck down a man in self-defense. | Being blackmailed with scandalous information, it's hard to blame the man for what he has done.} {Even if he has done wrong, a party of killers could use a man such as he. But can the man be trusted? | %name%'s eyes skirt from yours. When you ask how he is with a weapon, he mumbles about only having to hit 'the man' once. | A man of %name%'s physique could be useful, but how much can you depend upon a man whose former life was one of being on the run? | The man chamfers on his fingernails like a beaver would a tree. He's jumpy, but maybe that's a good thing in this world. | Mercenary bands are just the thing for a man like him.}
5b1da56aab1fb1872ed7.translation: {%fullname%长着一张谁也不想要的脸——倒是很适合印在通缉令上。 | %name%双手沾血，看起来很像赏金猎人最近向你描述过的某个人。 | %name%似乎什么队伍都肯加入，又像是只想混进去，隐姓埋名。 | 与人见面时，%name%总是结结巴巴地报上名字，仿佛舍不得把它告诉别人。}{认出%name%并不难：他是个出了名的杀人犯，手上沾着不忠妻子和她情人的鲜血。 | 他的目光阴沉而游移，藏着罪行，却也还留着一点人性，仿佛知道自己做错了，正想设法弥补。 | 他两腿沾满泥泞，显然已逃了很久。双手也在颤抖，因为那两条腿一直在替这双手做过的事逃命。 | 据说他一心想要儿子，于是杀死了自己刚出生的女儿。 | 有人认为，他只是为自卫才杀了人。 | 有人拿丑闻勒索他，这样看来，也很难全怪他做出那种事。}{即便他犯了罪，一群靠杀人为生的人，也用得上这样的家伙。但他可信吗？ | %name%躲闪着你的目光。你问他使兵器的本事如何，他含含糊糊地说，自己只打了“那个人”一下。 | %name%这样的体格或许能派上用场，可一个此前一直在逃命的人，你究竟能指望他多少？ | 他啃指甲，活像海狸啃树。他很容易受惊，不过在这个世道，也许是件好事。 | 对他这样的人，佣兵队伍再合适不过。}

0fde2ced4d678d44ae5f.source: You thought %name% a simple peasant when you found him freezing in the wastes of the north. As it turned out, he was very much a King's Guard, not only in title but in action. He fought like a man protecting his liege from the world at large. Thankfully, for a time, that 'liege' happened to be you. Last you heard he traveled to the southern realms and is protecting an upstart nomad king trying to overthrow the local Viziers.
0fde2ced4d678d44ae5f.translation: 你在北方荒原发现%name%时，他冻得奄奄一息，你只当他是个普通农夫。后来才发现，他确实是个国王卫士，不仅有这个名头，也有与之相称的本领。他作战时，仿佛在凭一己之力保护主君，抵挡整个世界。所幸有一段时间，那个“主君”恰好就是你。最近听说，他去了南方，正在保护一位新近崛起的游牧民之王，帮他推翻当地的维齐尔。

11695e398ed7cf36a61b.source: You never truly found out which king %name% supposedly 'guarded' in his days before joining the %companyname%, but it matters not now. After your abrupt retirement, the King's Guard took himself to the southern deserts. He served a Vizier for a time but failed to protect the royal from a concubine's poison. For punishment, %name%'s equipment was melted into a pot and poured down his throat.
11695e398ed7cf36a61b.translation: 在加入%companyname%之前，%name%究竟“保卫”过哪位国王，你始终没弄清，如今也不再重要了。你仓促退役后，这名国王卫士去了南方沙漠。他曾为一位维齐尔效力，却没能挡住一名侍妾下的毒。作为惩罚，%name%的装备被熔成一锅铁水，灌进了他的喉咙。

13ac21ea69037366c48e.source: Lumberjacks are used to hard physical labor. And axes.
13ac21ea69037366c48e.translation: 伐木工习惯了繁重的体力劳动，也用惯了斧头。

a744ff3f568bcf6ab5d6.source: %name% the burly lumberjack eventually left the company to return to the woods. He started a woodcutting business and operates every day of the year. Luckily, timing was on his side: the nobility have recently really gotten 'into' cabins and are paying out crowns left and right to anyone who can build them.
a744ff3f568bcf6ab5d6.translation: 魁梧的伐木工%name%最终离开战团，回到了森林。他开了伐木生意，一年到头都在忙碌。幸好赶上了好时候：贵族们最近突然迷上了木屋，对能替他们建屋的人挥金如土。

473770e7996b9855f9ae.source: %name% the lumberjack had enough of the sellsword's life and returned to woodcutting. Last you heard, he was involved in a tree-falling accident and his body could have been rolled up like a rug the bones were so thoroughly squashed.
473770e7996b9855f9ae.translation: 伐木工%name%厌倦了佣兵生活，回去重操旧业。最后听说，他遭遇了倒树事故，全身骨头被压得粉碎，尸体软得能像地毯一样卷起来。

d911dcf149a266eba441.source: A lumberjack, %fullname% {spent most of his days in the woods, chopping down trees | earned his crowns by chopping trees for firewood | was never seen without either axe or wood on his shoulder | always was a quiet man that prefered the serenity of the woods to the company of people | was eyed by many a young woman for his good stature and strong hands | always used to day-dream he was a knight, swinging his axe not against trees but orcs and trolls}. {A large and sturdy man, working outside came easily to him | He loved his collection of axes, having named every single one after a woman he once knew | He worked hard every day, but it was honest work | Alone in the woods he would talk to the trees and have them tell him which ones would give the best wood | Few men could swing an axe like he did, having a tree fall just like he wanted it | With his large and sturdy build he could carry on his back what other people would be crushed by}. {Like most people, he took on the profession of his father. Yet over the years, it dawned on him that he wanted to see more from the world than the same woods every day. After thinking long and hard, he made up his mind to | His life collapsed on him as his beloved wife died in childbirth. With everything taken from him, he became more and more reclusive, and not even the woods could bring him peace anymore. Just wanting to get away, he decided to | Returning from the woods one day, he saw smoke from afar. His village was burning, the people slaughtered or taken. His home destroyed. Full of anger he set off and decided to | Over time, strange creatures began to appear in the woods. One villager after the other disappared, some moved away. After a long night with no sleep, he decided it was time for him to leave as well. With nothing to live off, he was desperate to | Curious to all the villagers, it seemed %name% lost his interest in the woods with time, speaking of going away every more often if he spoke at all. One fateful day, they saw him volunteer to | One fateful day a tree he fell slew a deer. %name% did not want to waste it and so took it home, only to find himself accused of poaching. Before a sentence was cast he decided to leave the village in haste and attempt to} join a travelling mercenary company.
d911dcf149a266eba441.translation: 伐木工%fullname%{大半日子都在树林里砍树 | 靠伐木制柴挣取工钱 | 肩上不是扛着斧头，就是扛着木料 | 一向沉默寡言，比起与人相处，更喜欢树林的宁静 | 体格健壮、双手有力，惹得许多年轻姑娘侧目 | 总爱幻想自己是骑士，斧头砍向的不是树木，而是兽人和巨魔}。{他身材高大结实，户外劳作不在话下 | 他珍爱收藏的斧头，每把都以曾相识的一位女子命名 | 他每天辛苦劳作，却是凭本事吃饭 | 独自在林中时，他会与树交谈，请它们告诉自己哪些树能出最好的木材 | 很少有人能像他那样使斧，树总能分毫不差地倒向他想要的方向 | 凭着魁梧身板，他能背起足以压垮别人的重物}。{与大多数人一样，他继承了父业。可多年下来，他不愿每天只看同一片树林，想去见识更广阔的世界。深思熟虑后，他决定 | 挚爱的妻子死于难产，他的人生也随之崩塌。失去一切后，他愈发孤僻，就连树林也无法令他平静。他只想远走，于是决定 | 某天从林中归来，他远远望见浓烟。村庄燃烧着，村民或被屠杀，或被掳走，家园尽毁。满怀怒火，他踏上道路，决定 | 渐渐地，怪异生物开始在林中出没。村民一个接一个失踪，也有人搬走。又熬过一个不眠之夜后，他决定自己也该离开。身无长物的他迫切想要 | 让村民不解的是，%name%似乎日渐失去了对树林的兴趣，偶尔开口，也越来越常提到远行。某天，他们看见他主动前去 | 某个倒霉的日子，一棵被他砍倒的树压死了一头鹿。%name%不愿浪费，便将鹿带回家，结果被指控偷猎。还没等宣判，他就匆匆离开村子，打算}加入一支路过的佣兵战团。

547e29fe370cc108d4d6.source: Manhunters are used to hunting down people in the rough environment of the south.
547e29fe370cc108d4d6.translation: 捕奴者习惯在南方恶劣的环境中追捕逃亡者。

a3d569d77f1a3d47c849.source: %name% the manhunter stuck with the %companyname% for a long while after you left it. You haven't gotten much word of the man other than he's found far more income in the world of sellswords than that of hunting down the indebted.
a3d569d77f1a3d47c849.translation: 你离开后，捕奴者%name%又在%companyname%待了很长一段时间。有关他的消息不多，只知道佣兵这行挣的钱，比追捕负债者多得多。

6de24eca9d7f2c6d6ced.source: Upset with how his time in the company of the %companyname% has gone, %name% the manhunter deserted and returned south. It's hard to say what became of him, but the business of tracking and hunting human prey carries endless dangers. The only news you have of him is ancillary to his vocation: that of numerous indebted uprisings with many manhunters being buried alive or fed to a variety of desert-borne creatures.
6de24eca9d7f2c6d6ced.translation: 捕奴者%name%对自己在%companyname%的经历十分不满，便擅自离队，返回南方。他后来如何，很难说清，但追踪、猎捕人类这门营生，危险永无止境。你听到的消息只与他的行当有关：负债者屡次起义，不少捕奴者被活埋，或被拿去喂沙漠里的各种生物。

cd6f2ec4e1e49ccc5502.source: {The large population of slaves, prisoners, criminals, and indebted servants in the south has produced an economy of sellers, buyers, and, given the flighty nature of the product, hunters. | Southern city states must have enormous reserves of labor to fuel their desert-borne economies. While many are born into working tirelessly for Viziers, some must be coerced into a life of servitude. | The deserts so sparse in natural resources, it is often an ample supply of captured criminals and indebted souls which bolsters the southern economy. And the business of hunting down these eventual servants is a prosperous one. | Southern Viziers are so fearful of rebellions that an entire market of Manhunters has emerged to nip them in the bud.} {%name% entered manhunting with a vengeful attitude: his entire family was massacred in a slave uprising. | %name% was once an ordinary caravan guard but turned to manhunting nomads who kept trying to ambush his convoys. Finding more profit in the human trade, he's stuck with it ever since. | %name% is a manhunter with a good nose for tracking criminals, deserters, prisoners of war, and more. You sometimes wonder if he's got a keen sense of smell for fearful sweat. | Once a big game hunter, %name% grew fond of chasing the greatest game of all: man. He is an expert tracker with a nose for sniffing out desperation.} {For %name%, the opportunity of working for a mercenary band simply brings in more consistent work than waiting around for some pressed criminal to get antsy about his chains. | %name% is a rugged, shady individual and it is quite possible that he is just as flighty as the men he sought to hunt down. | Hunters like %name% carry traits and skills that would be useful in a mercenary band, but to some their past may be an ever present slight. Not all manhunters are seen in good light. | Capturing humans for the purpose of labor is frowned upon by many and catching those seeking their freedom equally so. Manhunters like %name% certainly have useful skills, but may rub some the wrong way. | To no surprise, many see men like %name% as opportunistic slugs. If he can make it with the company, it may take time to change the minds of some about his past.}
cd6f2ec4e1e49ccc5502.translation: {南方有大批奴隶、囚犯、罪犯和负债的仆役，由此养活了卖家、买家，以及——考虑到这些“货物”总想逃跑——猎手。 | 南方城邦要维持沙漠中的经济，必须拥有庞大的劳力。许多人生来就得为维齐尔终日劳作，另一些人则要靠强迫，才肯过上被奴役的一生。 | 沙漠物产匮乏，支撑南方经济的，往往是源源不断被捕获的罪犯与负债者。因此，追捕这些未来仆役的生意相当兴隆。 | 南方的维齐尔极度畏惧叛乱，甚至催生了一个专门的捕奴行当，好将反抗扼杀在萌芽之中。}{%name%怀着复仇之心当上捕奴者：他全家都死在了一次奴隶起义中。 | %name%原本只是普通商队护卫，后来开始捕捉那些不断伏击车队的游牧民。发现人口买卖更赚钱后，他就再也没改过行。 | %name%是个捕奴者，尤其擅长追踪罪犯、逃兵、战俘等人。你有时怀疑，他是不是能闻出恐惧的汗味。 | %name%曾猎杀大型野兽，后来却迷上了追逐最难对付的猎物：人。他精于追踪，仿佛能嗅出走投无路者的气息。}{对%name%而言，替佣兵战团做事，比坐等某个受奴役的罪犯厌倦锁链、决定逃跑，差事要稳定得多。 | %name%粗悍而来路不明，或许也和他曾追捕的人一样，随时准备溜之大吉。 | %name%这样的猎手，性情和本领都有佣兵战团用得上的地方。但在某些人眼里，他的过去永远是个污点。并非人人都看得起捕奴者。 | 抓人去当苦力，许多人都不齿；抓捕追求自由的人，也好不到哪去。%name%这样的捕奴者确有可用之才，却难免招人反感。 | 毫不意外，许多人把%name%这样的家伙视为投机钻营的蛀虫。即便他能在战团站稳脚跟，要让某些人不再介意他的过去，也得花上一段时日。}

7923e89de6cd16f50850.source: A good mason is used to physical labor and studying to improve his craft.
7923e89de6cd16f50850.translation: 优秀的石匠既习惯体力劳动，也乐于钻研技艺。

00737840184a5f8afcf2.source: Masonry has its own call, notably a call perfectly cut stones and impossible towers that defy the eye's ability to even shape them against the skies. %name% the mason returned to his old trade and, with all the money he'd made with the %companyname%, he started a reputable business renowned for its ability to construct stone rooms that held the heat during winters and the cool during summers.
00737840184a5f8afcf2.translation: 石工自有一番诱人的魅力，尤其是那些切割得严丝合缝的石块，以及高耸得仿佛不可能建成、让人连映在天际的轮廓都难以辨清的塔楼。石匠%name%重操旧业，用在%companyname%挣下的钱开办了一家颇有名望的工坊，以修建冬暖夏凉的石屋闻名。

40e5bde53984013670ab.source: The %companyname% continued to suffer losses long after you'd left. More and more of the brothers departed the company, a good lot of them returning to old trades. %name% the mason was no different. Sadly, all the time spent fighting had destroyed any steadiness he had left. With hands that wouldn't stop shaking, he could no longer shape stones like he used to. Last you heard, he was hauling rocks as a daytaler instead of shaping them as a mason.
40e5bde53984013670ab.translation: 你离开很久之后，%companyname%仍在不断折损人手。越来越多的弟兄退出战团，其中不少人重操旧业，石匠%name%也不例外。可惜，多年的战斗彻底毁了他原有的沉稳，双手抖个不停，再也无法像从前那样凿石。最近听说，他只能当短工搬运石块，而不能再做雕琢石块的石匠了。

3e6033b0ac6ced49afec.source: {Growing up in %townname%, %name% spent his youth poring over construction books with earnest. | Raised by a guild of tradesmen, %name%'s swift ascent through the field of masonry was of little surprise. | A student of %randomtown%'s esteemed college, %name% graduated with great expectations, and even greater things yet to build. | With a bricklayer for a father, %name%'s entrance into masonry was but the smallest of steps. | Amazed by the regal structures of church and state, %name% fell in love with masonry. | When %randomtown% was in dire need of defensive walls, %name% took to masonry like a very fortunately-timed natural.} {Unfortunately, his time as a mason was short-lived. A church he built collapsed and out of its ruins rose a murderous mob looking for revenge. | Five buildings built, five buildings knocked down. Endless wars made the man's vocation an impossible one. | Betrayed by a fellow architect, the mason bricked his rival inside the walls of his next project. It wasn't long until people started asking questions. | While roofing, the man took a misstep and fell. The ensuing injuries forced him out of his field. | But when a lord demanded he build a horrific dungeon, the mason refused. Now he is banished from ever laying a brick again. | A misplaced blueprint had the mason building the temple of the Davkulians and not the temple of the Davkuliads. Now he says the gods themselves are after him.} {Putting down his hammer and chisel for a hammer and sharpened chisel called a sword, %name% now works in the field of mercenaries. | One day, a poster for a mercenary troop caught his eye. Much like his old buildings, the rest is history. | Years of masonry made the man fit for a life of blood and mud. | %name% finds a flaw in every building he passes. Hopefully he can tune that annoying analysis to the battlefield.}
3e6033b0ac6ced49afec.translation: {%name%在%townname%长大，少年时便埋头钻研营造书籍，十分用功。 | %name%由一群工匠组成的行会养大，在石工这一行崭露头角之快，并不令人意外。 | %name%毕业于%randomtown%一所声名卓著的学院，肩负着很高的期望，眼前还有更宏伟的建筑等待他营造。 | 父亲是泥瓦匠，%name%走上石工这条路，可谓再自然不过。 | 教堂与王室建筑的恢宏气象令%name%惊叹，他就此迷上了石工。 | %randomtown%急需城墙时，%name%投身石工，天赋恰逢其时。}{可惜，他的石匠生涯十分短暂。他建的一座教堂倒塌了，废墟里爬出来的，是一群要找他报仇的暴民。 | 建了五座楼，倒了五座楼。无休无止的战争，让这门营生根本做不下去。 | 遭同行建筑师背叛后，这名石匠在下一项工程中，将对头砌进了墙里。没过多久，人们便开始追问起来。 | 修屋顶时，他一步踏空摔了下来，留下的伤迫使他离开了这一行。 | 一位领主命他修建一座骇人的地牢，他却拒绝了。如今，他被禁止再砌哪怕一块砖。 | 一张放错的图纸，让他把达夫库利亚德派的神殿建成了达夫库利安派的神殿。如今他说，连诸神都在追杀他。}{放下锤子和凿子，换上战锤以及一种磨尖后叫作“剑”的凿子，%name%如今投身于佣兵行当。 | 一天，一张佣兵招募告示吸引了他的目光。余下的事，就像他昔日的建筑一样，都成了历史。 | 多年的石工劳作，让他足以适应浸在血与泥里的日子。 | %name%走过每栋建筑，都能挑出点毛病。但愿他能把这套恼人的审视本领用到战场上。}

15101104b3a968e20fc2.source: Messengers are used to long and tiring travels.
15101104b3a968e20fc2.translation: 信使习惯了漫长而疲惫的旅途。

61a54c5ee842e0e4e264.source: The oddity of having %name% the messenger in your band did not seem so strange after he showed himself to be a killer sellsword. As far as you know, he's still with the company, preferring the march of a mercenary to that of a messenger. You don't blame him: an errand boy must bend the knee to every nobleman he comes across, but in the company of sellswords he'll no doubt get the occasional chance to kill one of them bastards. Not a hard trade off to accept!
61a54c5ee842e0e4e264.translation: 让信使%name%加入战团，起初显得古怪；可等他证明自己是个杀敌好手后，也就没人再觉得奇怪了。据你所知，他仍留在战团，比起替人送信，他更愿意跟着佣兵行军。你很理解：跑腿的见到哪个贵族都得屈膝行礼，而跟着佣兵，偶尔总有机会宰掉其中几个混蛋。这样的取舍，并不难做！

16b6cacb4282435f1325.source: %name% the messenger departed the %companyname% and returned to being an errand boy for the letters of lieges. You tried to find out where the man had gone to and eventually tracked him down - or what was left of him. Unfortunately, "don't shoot the messenger" is not an adage well followed in these fractured lands.
16b6cacb4282435f1325.translation: 信使%name%离开%companyname%，重新替领主们跑腿送信。你曾设法打听他的去向，最终找到了他——或者说他的遗骸。遗憾的是，在这片四分五裂的土地上，“两军交战，不斩来使”并不受人遵守。

fdebe150de3f681c0691.source: {Some men are so important that they require other men to carry their words. %name% is such a man - the latter, that is. | %name%'s shoulders are yoked with bags of mail, the receivers almost certainly dead on arrival. | To escape a life of servitude, %name% took up the vocation of a messenger. | With so many hurrying to find out the status of relatives, %name% has found ample work as a messenger. | %name% once traveled the land as a modest messenger. | Like his father and his father's father before him, %name% took messages across the land for royalty and laymen alike. | Picking up a dead messenger's bags, %name% soon found himself in the role of a would-be messenger. | Once a refugee, %name% figured he might as well deliver letters if he was already wandering the land.} {But making the rounds gets boring. The mailman seeks a new field of work. | Carrying love letters, the would-be adventurer wondered what the hell he was doing. | Claiming to be a budding hero, %name% now believes the task of delivering mail is beneath him. | Rain or sunshine, sure, snow or sleet, sure, but all out war? Maybe another time. | But after opening a letter that would ruin a goodhearted noble, the messenger decided to leave his post. | When robbers made his life hell, %name% figured he'd be better off traveling in the company of armed men. | After sleeping with a mayor's wife, the messenger had a small army on his heels. He figured he'd best slip into a different outfit for his own safety.} {%name% has spent years memorizing messages. Now he'll have to remember keeping the shield wall as arrows rain down on it. | Ironically, %name% has never written anything in his life. | Rolling up his sleeves, %name% boasts he has one last message to give the world. Everybody look out. | Perhaps his joining mercenaries suggests that, indeed, the pen is not mightier than a sword. | %name% has a tendency to repeat everything said to him. Old messenger habits die hard. | Ironically, the well-traveled messenger has probably seen more horrors on the road than most of the men in the outfit. | Few, if any, of %name%'s skills make him ready for combat. But he does have some sturdy legs, hopefully just not for running away.}
fdebe150de3f681c0691.translation: {有些人身份尊贵，连话都要别人替他传。%name%就是这样的人——我是说，替人传话的那个。 | %name%肩上扛满邮袋，等信送到时，收信人八成早已死了。 | 为逃离受人使唤的一生，%name%当上了信使。 | 如此多人急着打听亲人的消息，%name%的信使差事从来不缺活干。 | %name%曾是个不起眼的信使，走遍各地送信。 | 和父亲、祖父一样，%name%为王族和平民传递书信，奔走四方。 | %name%捡起一名死去信使的邮袋，没过多久，自己也成了半个信使。 | %name%曾是难民。他觉得，反正都在四处流浪，何不顺路送些信呢？}{可来回跑腿总会厌倦，这名送信人想换个行当。 | 捧着一封封情书，这个梦想冒险的家伙不禁怀疑，自己究竟在干什么。 | 自称崭露头角的英雄，%name%如今觉得送信实在有失身份。 | 晴天雨天都行，风雪冰雹也行，可要是全面开战？还是改日再说吧。 | 拆开一封足以毁掉一位善良贵族的信后，这名信使决定辞去差事。 | 强盗把他的日子搅得生不如死，%name%便觉得，跟着一群带兵器的人上路，也许更好。 | 睡了镇长的妻子后，信使身后便多了一小队追兵。为了保命，他觉得最好赶紧混进另一支队伍。}{%name%多年来一直在背诵口信。如今他得记住，箭雨落下时千万要守住盾墙。 | 说来讽刺，%name%这辈子从没亲笔写过一个字。 | %name%挽起袖子，夸口说自己还有最后一句话，要传给这个世界。大家可小心了。 | 他加入佣兵，或许正说明笔锋终究敌不过剑锋。 | 别人对%name%说过的话，他总喜欢复述一遍。信使的老习惯，哪有那么好改。 | 说来讽刺，这位走南闯北的信使，在路上见过的可怕事物，也许比战团里大多数人都多。 | %name%的本领几乎没有一样能用来打仗。不过他确实有两条结实的腿，但愿不只是拿来逃跑。}

ca5d173a1a0a569562eb.source: Anyone that's been in the militia will have received at least some basic training in matters of combat.
ca5d173a1a0a569562eb.translation: 任何服过民兵役的人，都至少接受过一些基本战斗训练。

b3ae78a81eba9430c251.source: A former militiaman such as %name% eventually left the %companyname%. He traveled the lands, visiting villages and helping them establish credible militias with which to defend themselves. Finding success in an increasingly dangerous world, %name% eventually came to be a known name, called upon as a sort of 'fixer' to come and ensure these villages would remain safe. Last you heard, he's purchased a plot of land and was raising a family far from the strife of the world.
b3ae78a81eba9430c251.translation: 曾是民兵的%name%最终离开了%companyname%。他走遍各地村庄，帮助村民组建足以自保的民兵队。在这个愈发危险的世道里，他的本领颇见成效，%name%渐渐有了名气，人们常请这位能人出面，替村子解决防务难题。最近听说，他已买下一块地，成家安顿下来，远离了世间纷争。

afaa72d5e8cfd271e1d0.source: %name% left the collapsing company and returned to his village. Back in the militia, it wasn't long until {greenskins | raiders} attacked and he was called to action. It's said that he stood tall, rallying the defense as he slew through countless enemies before succumbing to mortal wounds. When you visited the village, you found children playfighting beneath a statue made in the militiaman's image.
afaa72d5e8cfd271e1d0.translation: %name%离开日渐崩溃的战团，回到故乡，再次加入民兵。没过多久，{绿皮 | 劫掠者}便来犯，他又被召上战场。据说，他昂然挺立，鼓舞众人奋起抵抗，斩杀无数敌人后才因重伤倒下。后来你到访村庄，看见孩子们在一座以他为原型的雕像下嬉戏打闹，模仿着战斗。

bc6c2245beec4c21b27b.source: {A militiaman like %name% is only raised in times of need. | Broke and without work, %name% joined his local militia. | Caught stealing an apple, %name% was pressed into the militia as a form of punishment. | Although a member of the peasantry, %name% was always willing to join the militia and protect his homestead. | War is a hungry beast - militia conscripts like %name% are what feed it.} {While he got proper training, there was rarely enough food to go around for the 'second-rate soldiers'. | Even though he fought just as hard as the professionals, he found himself unable to garner any sort of respect for his work. | Being the bottom rung of soldiering, he quickly realized that it meant his life was expendable. | His weapons were rusted and the armor nonexistent. Unfortunately, enemies were not so kindly under-equipped.} {After a year of traipsing around with shoddy gear, he decided to look for something a bit more to his liking: sellswords. | When a lord sent his entire militia to almost certain doom, %name% realized he had better seek something better if he wanted to live. He took his modest skillset to the field of mercenaries. | Years in an outfit where he couldn't depend on the man next to him drove %name% to find something better. He's not the best soldier you've ever seen, but he is earnest. | When his militia was disbanded, he returned home to find his town had been burned to the ground. One foot already in the door, it only made sense to join one of the numerous mercenary bands roaming the land. | %name%'s modest military garb belies a man who has seen his fair share of training and combat.}
bc6c2245beec4c21b27b.translation: {像%name%这样的民兵，只有在缺人时才会被征召。 | %name%穷困潦倒，又找不到活干，便加入了当地民兵。 | %name%偷苹果时被抓住，作为惩罚，被强征进了民兵队。 | 虽然只是个农民，%name%却始终愿意加入民兵，保卫家园。 | 战争是一头饥饿的野兽，%name%这样的征召民兵就是它的口粮。} {他确实接受过正规训练，可那些“二流士兵”的口粮却往往不够分。 | 尽管他和职业军人一样卖命，却始终没能为自己挣来半分尊重。 | 作为军中最底层的一员，他很快明白了，自己的命随时都可以被舍弃。 | 他的武器锈迹斑斑，身上连件护甲都没有。可敌人并没有好心到也用同样的破烂装备。} {带着劣质装备奔波了一年，他决定找份更合心意的活：当佣兵。 | 领主把整支民兵队送上了一条几乎必死的路，%name%明白，想活命就得另谋出路。他带着那点武艺，投身佣兵行当。 | 多年来，%name%连身旁的同袍都靠不住，这让他决心找一支更好的队伍。他不是你见过最出色的士兵，却足够认真。 | 民兵队解散后，他回到家乡，却发现镇子已被夷为焦土。既然已经半只脚踏进军旅，在游荡各地的众多战团里找一个加入，便顺理成章了。 | %name%朴素的戎装之下，是一个受过不少训练，也经历过不少战斗的汉子。}

eafa43730f6e914ac9a4.source: A miller is used to physical labor.

2dcba5149a169681dbb4.source: %name% the once-miller stayed with the %companyname% for a time, collecting enough crowns to start his own bakery. Last you heard, his sword-shaped desserts have been a hit with the nobility and he makes more money selling to them than he ever did with the company.
2dcba5149a169681dbb4.translation: 曾是磨坊工的%name%又在%companyname%待了一阵，攒够钱后开了自己的面包店。上次听说，他做的剑形甜点深受贵族喜爱，卖给贵族赚的钱比当佣兵时还多。

c70cdd61547f144f501a.source: As the %companyname% fell on hard times, %name% the miller saw fit to go ahead and leave while he could still walk. He helped a nobleman test out a new way of grinding grains with mules and waterwheels working in tandem. Unfortunately, by 'helping' he managed to fall into the contraption and was brutally crushed to death.
c70cdd61547f144f501a.translation: %companyname%陷入困境时，磨坊工%name%决定趁自己还能走路，赶紧离开。他帮助一位贵族试验用骡子和水车共同驱动的新式磨谷装置。不幸的是，“帮忙”途中他跌入机器，被活活碾死。

b7ba319484ddead3dad8.source: {The life as a miller had always been lacking something for %name%, yet the hard work kept him from making any big plans. | Continuing the family tradition, %name% learned the millers trade from his father. | Although just a simple miller, %name% always dreamed about wandering out into the world and bring home tales and pockets full of crowns. | Being a simple fellow, %name% did not mind working hard in the mill every day. | %name% always was more ambitious than other people. While his brother was content with running their family's mill, he could not shake the feeling that he was destined for more.} {One night he was awoken by a loud thunderstorm. Rushing outside, %name% realised that his mill had been ignited by a lightning strike. | When he caught his promised wife in bed with another man, he was furious, battering both of them with a hail of blows. His fists were bruised, people were shouting at him, but the only thing he felt was emptyness where once was his heart. As if in a dream he quickly packed his belongings and set out, never to return. | When his young and lovely wife was found dead, torn apart by wild beasts in the woods, he did not say a word. Silently he packed his belongings and set out into the world, to start a new life somewhere far away. | After hearing wild tales from a hedge knight in the tavern of %townname%, his imagination was running wild with all the possibilities out there in the world waiting for him. | A drought meant business was running slow for him. When %name% was not able to pay his debts any more his life was threatened by ruthless money collectors. He had to disappear.} {Remembering his cousin, %randomname%, who has made a decent living in the mercenary business, %name% decided to do the same. | While looking for opportunities he met a mercenary recruiter who promised him fame and fortune. | Although he does not know the next thing about fighting, %name% is eager to sign up with a mercenary company hooked by the promise of adventure. | Whether by lack of alternatives or by his free will, %name% stands before you now, ready to swear fealty.}
b7ba319484ddead3dad8.translation: {%name%总觉得磨坊主的生活缺了点什么，可繁重的劳作让他无暇谋划别的出路。 | 承袭家业，%name%跟父亲学会了磨坊主的手艺。 | %name%虽只是个普通磨坊主，却总梦想出去闯荡，带着满肚子的故事和满口袋的克朗回家。 | %name%是个朴实的人，并不介意每天在磨坊里辛苦劳作。 | %name%向来比旁人更有雄心。兄弟满足于经营家里的磨坊，他却始终觉得自己注定要成就更大的事业。}{一天夜里，雷暴将他惊醒。%name%冲到外面，才发现磨坊已被雷电引燃。 | 撞见未婚妻与另一个男人同床，他怒不可遏，挥拳将两人一顿痛打。拳头伤痕累累，旁人冲他叫喊，他心里却只剩空荡荡的一片。他像在梦中一样，匆匆收拾行囊，踏上旅途，再也没有回来。 | 年轻美丽的妻子被发现死在林中，尸体遭野兽撕碎，他一句话也没有说。他只是默默收好行李，走向外面的世界，想在遥远的地方重新开始。 | 在%townname%的酒馆听一位流浪骑士讲过惊险的故事后，他便浮想联翩，满心都是外面世界里等待自己的种种可能。 | 干旱让生意冷清下来。%name%再也还不起债，心狠手辣的讨债人开始威胁他的性命，他只得逃之夭夭。}{想起在佣兵行当里过得不错的表亲%randomname%，%name%决定也试一试。 | 寻找出路时，他遇到了一名佣兵招募人，对方许诺能让他名利双收。 | 虽然对打仗一窍不通，%name%仍被冒险的前景勾住，急切地想加入佣兵战团。 | 不论是别无选择，还是出于本心，%name%如今站在你面前，准备宣誓效忠。}

139561078f38f0f07e95.source: A miner will be used to physical labor, but breathing in the dusty air of the mines may have taken a toll on his health over the years.
139561078f38f0f07e95.translation: 矿工做惯了体力活，但多年吸入矿井里的粉尘，可能已损害了他们的身体。

18f39f3b3af6da6662aa.source: %name% the miner never did return to the mines, thankfully. If there's one life that could be worse than that of fighting for a living, it very well may be digging into mountains for a living! Apparently, the miner built a home by the sea, spending the rest of his days peacefully fishing for dinner and enjoying sunrises or some such sappy shite.
18f39f3b3af6da6662aa.translation: 谢天谢地，矿工%name%再也没回矿井。若说还有什么日子比提着脑袋挣钱更糟，那多半就是钻进山肚子里讨生活了！听说他在海边盖了房子，余生安稳地钓鱼做晚饭、看日出，尽过那些肉麻得要命的清闲日子。

3ffce2d824785241939f.source: If there's one life that's more rough than that of being a sellsword, it is that of being a miner. Sadly, %name% returned to that life, going back into the mines to dig out metals and ores to fill some rich man's pockets. A recent earthquake collapsed many such mines. You're not sure if the ol' brother survived, but it's looking pretty grim.
3ffce2d824785241939f.translation: 若说有什么营生比当佣兵还苦，那就是挖矿。遗憾的是，%name%又回到了那种日子，钻进矿井挖出金属和矿石，填满有钱人的口袋。最近一场地震震塌了许多矿井。你不知道这位老兄弟是否还活着，前景却着实不妙。

1d3650b874236de3a4cd.source: {To support a fatherless family, %name% went into the mines at a very young age. | An orphan, the only work %name% could find was working the mines of the earth. | Mining is tough work, the sort of job men like %name% flock to. | Even though his father died in the mines, %name% felt compelled to work in them himself, like most men do where he grew up. | %name% worked in the mines as a family tradition spanning many generations. | Whenever wars start up, miners like %name% are more needed than ever, lest an army wishes to go without steel to wield. | A hardhelm and a pickaxe, the tools %name% has been taking deep into the earth for years.} {But, as always, a mine doesn't last forever, and the miner barely escaped the last collapse. | Sadly, he proved to be the only survivor of a shaft collapse, and there's no way he's digging back in there by himself. | After a tragic mine collapse, the sight of dozens of widows moved the man to think of a different field of work. | Surviving yet another collapse, the man's wife demanded he seek a new line of work no matter what it was. | Bending over and scuttling about in the dark gets old, though, and so the man sought a different vocation. | Working in environments far too dark, the man accidentally killed a coworker. The tragedy pushed him from the field. | After his own son lost his life in the mines, the man left the job forever. | But suffering from relentless coughs, the man felt maybe a career in fresh air would better serve him.} {%name% has the stocky frame of a miner. Unfortunately, he has the lungs of one, too. | He's tough alright, but %name%'s wheezing sounds like rusted blades grinding together.  | You have to wonder if %name%'s lungs have enough metal dust in them to fashion a blade or two. | %name%'s breath could probably ink a chunk of coal. | %name% spent years earning keep for a company store. Now he wants to earn some real coin. | %name% looks forward to pocketing some of that gold he spent years plucking out of the earth. | Annoyingly, %name% points at half your gear - the metal stuff, mostly - and reminds everyone who's responsible for it being there. | %name% has almost catlike vision in the dark. He would have made for a good assassin if it weren't for his damned wheezing. | %name% has cheated death a few times, so why not try it a few times more as mercenary? | %name%'s already had the earth itself out for his head so a few things above the soil don't scare him much. | If darkness truly is death's ambassador, %name%'s already been talking to it for years. | Stupidly brave souls like %name% can definitely find a good register in an outfit such as this. | %name% proudly boasts that, once upon a time, he could play cards in the dark. You don't doubt it. | If %name% can swing a sword as well as a pickaxe, then all is well.}
1d3650b874236de3a4cd.translation: {为了养活失去父亲的一家人，%name%年纪很小就下了矿。 | %name%是个孤儿，唯一找得到的活计就是下井挖矿。 | 挖矿是苦力活，像%name%这样的人却总往里奔。 | 尽管父亲死在矿井里，%name%仍像家乡大多数男人一样，别无选择地走上了同一条路。 | %name%下矿是承袭家业，这一行已经传了好几代。 | 战端一起，像%name%这样的矿工就比以往更加不可或缺，毕竟军队总不能没有钢铁兵器。 | 一顶硬盔、一把镐，这就是%name%多年带进地下深处的家当。}{可矿井终究不会永远牢固，他在最近一次塌方中险些丧命。 | 遗憾的是，他成了一次矿井塌方的唯一幸存者，再也不肯独自挖回那片黑暗。 | 一场惨烈的塌方之后，数十位寡妇的身影让他萌生了改行的念头。 | 又从一次塌方中活下来后，妻子逼他另谋生路，干什么都行。 | 终日弯腰在黑暗中爬来爬去，实在令人厌倦，于是他想换个行当。 | 工作的地方太暗，他失手害死了一名同伴，这场悲剧让他离开了矿井。 | 自己的儿子在矿井中丧命后，他永远告别了这份工作。 | 咳嗽始终不停，他觉得也许换份能呼吸新鲜空气的差事更好。}{%name%有着矿工般敦实的身板。可惜，肺也是矿工的肺。 | %name%确实强壮，可喘息声像生锈的刀片在相互刮磨。  | 你不禁怀疑，%name%肺里的金属粉尘够不够再打出一两把刀。 | %name%呼出的气，大概连煤块都能再熏黑几分。 | %name%辛苦多年，收入都花在矿主的铺子里了。现在他想挣点真正归自己的钱。 | %name%挖了多年黄金，如今盼着能有一些真正落进自己口袋。 | %name%总指着你们的大半装备，主要是金属的那些，提醒大家这都离不开谁的功劳，实在烦人。 | %name%在黑暗中的眼力几乎如猫一般。要不是那该死的喘息声，他倒能当个好刺客。 | %name%已多次从死神手里逃脱，何不当个佣兵，再试上几回？ | 连大地都曾想要%name%的命，地面上那些东西自然吓不太住他。 | 如果黑暗真是死神的使者，%name%已经与它打了多年的交道。 | 像%name%这样勇敢得有些傻的人，在这支队伍里总能找到位置。 | %name%自豪地吹嘘，自己曾经能在黑暗里打牌。你倒不怀疑。 | 只要%name%挥剑的本事和抡镐一样好，那就没问题。}

e391a572a4ae8603c4dc.source: A good minstrel will sing a saga to inspire the men, play the flute to calm them, or entertain them with poetry around the camp fire. A lute is not a weapon, however, and minstrels are often not used to physical labor or bloodshed.
e391a572a4ae8603c4dc.translation: 优秀的吟游诗人能用史诗鼓舞士气，用笛声安抚人心，或在营火旁吟诗取乐。不过鲁特琴毕竟不是武器，吟游诗人通常也不习惯体力劳动或流血厮杀。

d2d385e59e8caf24e3cd.source: Ah, %name%. What an addition to the %companyname%! The minstrel not only became an excellent fighter, but was crucial in keeping the men's spirits high in the toughest of times. A poet and actor at heart, he eventually retired from the company and started up a theater company. He current performs plays for both the nobility and laymen. The minstrel does not yet realize it, but his playful wit and sharp commentary are slowly bringing the classes together.
d2d385e59e8caf24e3cd.translation: 啊，%name%！%companyname%能有他，真是走运！这位吟游诗人不仅成了一名出色的战士，更在最艰难的日子里，帮助弟兄们振作精神。骨子里终究是诗人和演员，他最终离开战团，组建了一支剧团。如今，他为贵族和平民演出戏剧。这位吟游诗人还没意识到，自己诙谐的机锋与犀利的针砭，正在一点点拉近不同阶层之间的距离。

dbb9f6cd2d03448552ec.source: Never a fighter at heart, %name% the minstrel quickly left the declining %companyname%. He and a group of musicians and jesters spend their evenings performing for drunken noblemen. You managed to see one of these performances for yourself. %name% spent much of the time being berated by the inebriated and having half-eaten chicken bones thrown at him. One of the nobles even thought it'd be funny to set a dog loose on one of the jesters. You could see the minstrel's dreams dying in his eyes, but the show went on.
dbb9f6cd2d03448552ec.translation: 吟游诗人%name%心底从来不是个战士，很快便离开了日渐衰败的%companyname%。他和一群乐师、丑角，每晚为喝得烂醉的贵族表演。你也亲眼看过其中一场。大多数时候，%name%都在挨酒鬼们的骂，还不断被啃剩的鸡骨头砸中。一个贵族甚至觉得，放狗去咬某个丑角，会是件很好玩的事。你看得出，吟游诗人眼中的梦想正在熄灭，可演出仍在继续。

460acf6f276aa75ca791.source: "{I can swing a sword and cleave an axe, | One might ask of me a task, | Right with god, but in the left a flask,} {and I say, 'You question a man who wears no mask?'. | and so I have to move quick, but not quite fast.} {Stare down the stuffed bears I did, | Into my frayed pantaloons I bid, | Along the muddy roads my boots skid,} {and so of many things I am rid. | truth! My shameful talent is to - ferociously! - knit.} {So take me along your adventure, | Bring me with your men who clatter and clamber, | Hand me your shield and that thing shaped like my member,} {and let us go and bid fear a farewell to remember! | and let's - oh, ow! I have a splinter! | and may we come, one and all, to a healthy next-winter!}". {The man speaks gibberish. | It rhymes!}
460acf6f276aa75ca791.translation: “{我能挥剑舞大斧， | 有人托我办事务， | 右手奉神左手酒壶，}{我道：‘我这不戴面具之人，何须盘问得这般唐突？’ | 因此脚步须利索，却也不必太仓促。}{我曾怒瞪填草熊， | 我请诸位入我破裤筒， | 泥路脚滑似乘风，}{许多东西离我去，转眼便成空。 | 实话！我的丢人绝技——凶猛地！——舞织针，练编织功。}{带我与你冒险闯， | 带我随众吵吵嚷嚷、爬高上低四处忙， | 给我盾牌，还有那根像我胯下物的棒，}{咱们向恐惧道别一场，叫它永远难忘！ | 然后咱们——哎哟！木刺扎得真够呛！ | 愿咱们人人平安，到下个冬天仍安康！}”{这人满嘴胡话。 | 居然押韵了！}

77ea74af671d8b3a34e0.source: Monks tend to have a high resolve in what they do, but are not used to hard physical labor or warfare.
77ea74af671d8b3a34e0.translation: 修士通常信念坚定，但不习惯繁重的体力劳动或战争。

8a551a6f6743b48580f2.source: %name% the monk retired back into calmer spiritual duties. He is currently out in a mountain monastery, enjoying the quiet while reflecting on his time in the mercenary company. The other monks hate him for fighting and killing, but he's penning a world-changing tome on the balance between peace and violence.
8a551a6f6743b48580f2.translation: 修士%name%退役后，又回到了平静的宗教生活。如今他住在山中修道院里，享受清静，回顾自己的佣兵岁月。其他修士厌恶他的杀戮过往，他却正在撰写一部探讨和平与暴力平衡、足以改变世人观念的巨著。

7af674bbe872fae0b7a5.source: After having a spiritual breakdown, %name% retired from fighting and found home in a monastery. All his fellow brothers and abbots ostracized him for taking part in such a violent venture. Word has it he was eventually exiled when a sexton caught him stealing an offertory.
7af674bbe872fae0b7a5.translation: %name%精神崩溃后告别战斗，在一座修道院安了身。可修士同伴与院长都因他参与过如此暴烈的营生而排斥他。据说，后来有个教堂杂役撞见他偷窃奉献金，他便被逐出了修道院。

c31121debd1d1c470ff7.source: {After raiders murdered his family, %name% retreated into the comforts of religion and became a monk at a nearby monastery. | Often traveling away from his church and fellow monks, %name% spent years preaching to peasantry in remote villages. | %name%, a quiet monk, has spent untold days worshipping the old gods in %townname%'s monastery. | One monk amongst many, %name% used to wander the steepled temples of %randomtown%. | Abandoned on the steps of a monastery, %name% grew up in the company of monks, and soon took to their lifestyle. | Trying to find peace in a land of ruin, %name% became a monk. | Always an unruly child, %name%'s parents handed him over to the local monastery where he was quickly pacified as a monk.} {Unfortunately, his abbot's liking for youth and fleshen things led to a terrible scandal. %name% fled to preserve his life and his faith. | But his faith was irreversibly damaged as a hellacious attack by raiders left men castrated, women raped, and children skewered on spits. | Though a believer in the old gods, the monk could not stand what atrocities his head priest committed in their name. The monk eventually left to seek spirituality on his own terms. | As the world's suffering grew, %name%'s abbot requested that he go out and heal the people of the earth - or kill those who did them wrong. | Cults of death, beasts of nightmare, and men of cruelty. %name% left the halls of his temple to purify them all. | But when a child asked him a faith-shattering question, %name% abandoned his faith, seeking out spirituality by other means. | Unfortunately, prayer did not spare his brothers from a slaughter. %name% realized that his faith was better invested in looking out for himself than muttering to some so-called god. | Always a fiery man, %name% left the safety of the monasteries to go out and 'right' the world. | One of the few literate men around, %name% abandoned his ascetic life to learn more of the world and, hopefully, to cure that which sickened it. | But one night a woman bedded him. He woke with his faith cratered in the crumpled sheets around him. Ashamed, he never returned to his monastery. | But he used his trusted position for ill-gotten gains, stealing from the temple's treasury. It didn't take long for the scandal to drive him out. | Unfortunately, a child accused him of behavior unbecoming of a monk. Nobody knows the truth behind the story, but %name% did not last much longer at the church. | One night, he discovered an awful truth in an old tome. Not long after, %name% quickly left the church, never quite saying what it was that he discovered.} {The man hardly knows a thing about fighting, but he carries the mental fortitude of a mountain standing against a storm. | Years of solitude and prayer have left %name% out of shape, but it is his steeled mind that is of most value. | Perhaps never really content with his life, it's difficult to entirely know why someone like %name% would join a band of mercenaries. | Maybe there are too many devils in the world, or too many inside him, but you don't question why %name% wishes to join a band of sellswords. | Faith won't cleave a greenskin, but it won't have a man like %name% running away from one, either. | %name%'s stated desire to rid the world of 'the unfaithful' is almost scary in its determination. | While %name%'s spirituality is to be commended, the constant mutterings to the old gods are a bit annoying. | While %name%'s hands are better clasped in prayer than around the handle of a sword, few mercenaries have the sense of resolve that he does. | A holy book practically anchored to his wrist, %name% has sought the company of sellswords. | The holy book he carries is thick enough to be used as a shield, but %name% looks absolutely horrified when you say as much out loud. | Perhaps with a romantic view of mercenaries in need of a good spiritual cleansing, %name% seeks to accompany sellswords. | Once having read of warrior priests, %name% now wishes to emulate those brave, unwavering soldiers of faith. | You get the feeling %name% wants release from this sinful world. If that's the truth then he has come to the right place.}
c31121debd1d1c470ff7.translation: {掠夺者杀害了他的家人后，%name%转向信仰寻求慰藉，在附近的修道院当了修士。 | %name%常常离开教堂和修士同伴，多年来一直在偏远村庄向农民传教。 | %name%是个寡言的修士，在%townname%的修道院里度过了无数侍奉旧神的日子。 | 和许多修士一样，%name%曾常在%randomtown%尖塔耸立的神殿中踱步。 | %name%被遗弃在修道院的台阶上，在修士们的陪伴下长大，很快便习惯了他们的生活。 | 想在这片破败之地寻得安宁，%name%成了一名修士。 | %name%自幼顽劣不驯，父母便把他送进当地修道院，他很快就服服帖帖，当上了修士。}{可惜，院长对年轻肉体的偏好酿成了一桩可怕的丑闻。%name%为了保住性命，也保住信仰，逃了出来。 | 可掠夺者的一场地狱般的袭击彻底摧毁了他的信仰：男人被阉割，女人遭强暴，孩子被串上烤叉。 | 虽然信奉旧神，这名修士却无法忍受首席祭司以神之名犯下的暴行。最终，他离开了，决定按自己的方式寻求信仰。 | 世间苦难日增，%name%的院长便命他出门，医治受苦的世人——或杀死那些害他们受苦的人。 | 崇拜死亡的邪教、噩梦般的野兽，还有残忍的人类。%name%离开神殿，要将他们统统净化。 | 一个孩子的问题动摇了他的全部信仰，%name%于是弃了教，转而用别的方式寻求精神寄托。 | 可惜，祈祷没能让他的修士弟兄逃过屠杀。%name%明白了，与其对着某个所谓的神喃喃低语，不如相信自己能照顾好自己。 | %name%向来满腔热忱，他离开安全的修道院，决意去“匡正”这个世界。 | 身为少数识字的人之一，%name%放弃苦修生活，想更深入地了解世界，也希望能治好让它病入膏肓的症结。 | 一夜之间，一个女人上了他的床。醒来时，他的信仰仿佛也碎在了四周凌乱的床单里。羞愧之下，他再没有回过修道院。 | 他却利用受人信任的职位谋取不义之财，偷盗神殿钱库。没过多久，丑闻便迫使他离开。 | 可惜，一名孩子指控他做了有辱修士身份的事。没人知道真相如何，但%name%此后没能在教堂再待多久。 | 一天夜里，他从一本古书中发现了可怕的真相。不久后，%name%便匆匆离开教堂，始终不肯说清自己究竟发现了什么。}{这人几乎不懂战斗，心志却如迎着风暴的山岳般坚定。 | 多年的独居与祈祷让%name%的身子疏于锻炼，不过最有价值的，本就是他坚韧的意志。 | 也许他从未真正满意过自己的生活。像%name%这样的人为何会加入佣兵队伍，很难说得清。 | 或许世上的恶魔太多，又或许他心里的恶魔太多，但你并不追问%name%为何想当佣兵。 | 信仰劈不开绿皮，却也不会让%name%这样的人在绿皮面前转身逃跑。 | %name%声称要将“不信者”从世上除尽，那份坚决几乎令人害怕。 | %name%的虔诚值得称道，只是他老对着旧神念念有词，实在有些烦人。 | 比起握住剑柄，%name%的双手更适合合十祈祷，但很少有佣兵能有他那样的决心。 | 圣书几乎像拴在%name%手腕上一样，如今他带着它来投奔佣兵。 | 他带的圣书厚得足以当盾牌用，不过你一说出口，%name%便露出惊恐至极的神情。 | 或许怀着些浪漫的念头，觉得佣兵正需要好好净化灵魂，%name%想与他们同行。 | 读过战斗祭司的事迹后，%name%如今也想效仿那些勇敢坚定、为信仰而战的勇士。 | 你觉得%name%是想从这罪恶的世界里解脱。若真如此，他倒是来对地方了。}

f2f38779b5a5677e7472.source: The world was too dark for %name% to continue his ways. A talk with a flagellant showed him that the old gods are not happy with man's pursuits of justice through reasonable means. Now the once-monk can be found whipping himself, bleeding righteousness into the world one strike at a time.
f2f38779b5a5677e7472.translation: 世道太过黑暗，%name%无法再沿旧路走下去。与一位苦修者长谈后，他明白旧神并不满意人们用温和手段追求公义。如今，这个曾经的修士不停鞭笞自己，每落下一鞭，都仿佛向世间洒下一滴正义之血。

19568c4aa23b06d3a393.source: Any nomad that survived out in the desert will have some expertise in fighting.
19568c4aa23b06d3a393.translation: 能在沙漠中活下来的游牧民，多少都懂些战斗本领。

2945c6bc578f0d1031b9.source: The nomad %name% left the %companyname% a few months after yourself. He apparently traveled south and now leads what they're calling the 'City on Legs,' a huge band of peoples that roam the deserts. It is apparently so rich and successful a society that the Viziers worry their own people will flock to it.
2945c6bc578f0d1031b9.translation: 你离开数月后，游牧民%name%也离开了%companyname%。听说他去了南方，如今率领着一支庞大的沙漠游牧队伍，人称“会行走的城”。这个群体似乎富足而兴盛，以至于维齐尔们都担心自己的百姓会争相投奔。

dd1dea84a3d1da863296.source: You learned that %name% the nomad departed the company with the hope of finding new plains to roam. Apparently, he got the idea in his head that he would travel far to the north and land cozily with the barbarians there. To his credit, the barbarians and nomads share a similar lifestyle, culture, language, religion, laws, struggles, conflicts, and general appearances aside. The nomad was butchered almost instantly upon entrance to a barbarian encampment and his remains eaten in a warrior ritual.
dd1dea84a3d1da863296.translation: 你得知游牧民%name%离开了战团，想寻找新的原野继续漂泊。显然，他忽然冒出了一个念头：一路北上，去和那里的野蛮人舒舒服服地过日子。平心而论，野蛮人与游牧民确实有相似的生活方式——只要不论文化、语言、宗教、律法、困境、争端，以及大致长相的话。他刚进野蛮人营地，几乎立刻就被宰了，残躯则在一场战士仪式中被分食。

7a342e4febaad1a36f84.source: {Like many southerners, %name% is someone who grew up in the desert, roaming the dunes and waylaying caravans and lost travelers alike. | Born into one of the South's many desert tribes, %name% learned the ways of the sands before he learned anything else. | Nomads pepper the southern deserts and it is in one of these roaming bands that %name% was born. | True nomads are a rare find in the cities of the south and %name% is no different. | You rarely see a nomad outside his element in the dunes of the southern sands, but %name% stands, darkly tanned and gritting himself again.} {However, nomadic politics are a mite complicated. Some event, which the nomad-turned-sellsword refuses to explain, ushered him into the cities looking for work. | A rule of his tribe is that every third son must travel out to see the world and, if he so wishes, return. So, here %name% stands. | Accused of sexual impropriety with a woman not formally gifted to him, %name% was faced with execution or exile from the tribe. His breathing and standing before you hints at which of the two he chose. | Having murdered one of his fellow tribesman over a gambling debt, the nomad was exiled from his tribe. | But a disastrous ambush, which he was responsible for planning, saw him voted out of his particular tribe. | But the nomad wished to see more of the world, to see himself as more than what he could muster within the confines of his tribe, and so he left and ventured to the cities for adventurous work.} {The nomad stands before you every bit of his upbringing: darkly toned, eyes black, hands sanded down. If he's not a warrior already, he presumably could be trained into one with time. | As a man of the unbearable sands of the south, it's no surprise that the nomad is physically ready to take on the tasks of sellswording. Whether the skills are there is another matter entirely. | Men who venture the desert wastes are a hardy lot and %name% is no different. | Nomads such as %name% earn most of their combat experience ambushing caravans. It could be of use in a mercenary band, though frontline work is a fair bit different than waylaying poor merchants. | %name% is every bit of the South as you expect: worn down by the sands, yet standing with the constitution of a man ready to take on the day and all those to come. | %name% is unlikely to be a trained and skilled fighter quite yet, but as a man of the southern wastes there is little doubt that he has the heart and spirit of a warrior.}
7a342e4febaad1a36f84.translation: {和许多南方人一样，%name%生长在沙漠，在沙丘间游荡，伏击商队，也伏击迷路的旅人。 | %name%出生于南方众多沙漠部族之一，最先学会的便是在黄沙中生存。 | 南方沙漠里散布着游牧部落，%name%就出生在其中一支逐地而居的队伍里。 | 南方的城市中很难见到真正的游牧民，%name%也很少踏足那里。 | 游牧民很少离开南方沙丘这片熟悉的天地，可%name%此刻就站在这里，皮肤晒得黝黑，正又一次咬紧牙关。}{然而，游牧部落之间的关系颇为复杂。这个转当佣兵的游牧民不肯解释究竟发生了什么，只说有件事迫使他进城找活干。 | 他部落的规矩是，每家的第三个儿子都要外出见识世界，若愿意，再回来。因此，%name%就站在了这里。 | %name%被控与一名尚未正式赐给他的女子私通，面临处死或逐出部落的选择。他如今还能站在你面前喘气，已足以说明选了哪一条。 | 因赌债杀死一名同族后，这个游牧民被逐出了部落。 | 他负责策划的一场伏击惨败，族人投票将他赶了出去。 | 可这名游牧民想看看更广阔的世界，证明自己能做的远不止部族之内那点事，于是离开家园，进城寻找冒险的营生。}{站在你面前的游牧民，处处都显出他的出身：深色的皮肤、漆黑的眼睛，还有被风沙磨粗的双手。就算还不是个战士，花些时间想必也能练出来。 | 在南方酷烈黄沙中长大，这名游牧民的体格足以胜任佣兵的差事，并不令人意外。至于本领够不够，就是另一回事了。 | 敢闯沙漠荒野的人向来坚韧，%name%也不例外。 | 像%name%这样的游牧民，大多靠伏击商队积累作战经验。这也许对战团有用，不过正面交锋和偷袭可怜的商人，终究大不相同。 | %name%完全是你印象中的南方汉子：饱受风沙侵蚀，却依然站得稳稳当当，随时准备迎接今天，以及此后的每一天。 | %name%眼下大概还算不上训练有素的好手，但身为南方荒漠之子，他无疑拥有战士的勇气与心志。}

005ce4153a3a5b805071.source: %name% doesn't talk much about himself. He just wants to kill orcs and goblins which, given the state of things, makes him a perfect fit for the company. If he's true to his word, he'll leave as soon as the invasion is taken care of.
005ce4153a3a5b805071.translation: %name%很少谈自己的事，只想着杀兽人和地精。眼下的局势让他再适合战团不过。如果他言而有信，等入侵平息，他就会离开。

c6d81564212be0d26ac4.source: After a long talk with a monk, %name% was converted to a more peaceful means of expressing his faith. Now when he picks up a weapon you can be assured it will only be pointed at someone other than himself.
c6d81564212be0d26ac4.translation: 与一位修士长谈后，%name%改用更平和的方式表达信仰。如今他再拿起武器，你可以确信，刀尖只会指向别人，不会再对准自己。

1cac12443cd78060adf2.source: Oathtakers are brave warriors sworn to uphold a strict code, and are no strangers to combat.
1cac12443cd78060adf2.translation: 立誓者是宣誓恪守严格准则的勇士，对战斗并不陌生。

8c3ebaf1bac35c090a9f.source: %name% the Oathtaker stayed with the %companyname%, wielding Young Anselm's skull to proselytize knightly virtues unto the world. Most see him as something of an annoyance, but there is also some charm in a man who believes fully in matters of honor and pride and doing good. Last you heard, he singlehandedly saved a lord's princess from a gang of alley thieves. In celebration, he was wed to the damsel, though rumors abound that she is unhappy in bed, proclaiming that the Oathtaker insists on Young Anselm's skull watching from the corner. Whatever's going on, you're happy that the man is still doing his thing to the fullest.
8c3ebaf1bac35c090a9f.translation: 立誓者%name%留在了%companyname%，捧着小安塞尔姆的头骨，向世人宣扬骑士美德。大多数人觉得他有些烦，但一个全心相信荣誉、自尊与善行的人，也确有几分魅力。最近听说，他独自从一群街巷盗贼手中救出了一位领主的千金。为庆贺这桩功绩，他与那位姑娘成了婚。不过传闻新娘对床笫之事颇有怨言，因为这位立誓者坚持把小安塞尔姆的头骨摆在角落里旁观。无论究竟怎么回事，你都很高兴，他仍在尽心尽力地做着自己认定的事。

0e099f0fc1533c6effe7.source: Once an Oathtaker to the bone, %name% grew disenchanted with his fellow believers and one night had a dream that they were, in fact, the true heretics. He slew every Oathtaker in reach and then fled out, eventually joining the Oathbringers of all people. Last that was heard of him, he reclaimed Young Anselm's skull and smashed it with a hammer. Enraged, his new Oathbringer brothers promptly slew him down. %name%'s corpse was found stabbed over a hundred times, ashy skull fragments powdering a bloodied, madly grinning face.
0e099f0fc1533c6effe7.translation: %name%曾是个彻头彻尾的立誓者，却渐渐对同道心灰意冷。一天夜里，他梦见那些人才是真正的异端。于是他杀死了身边所有能找到的立誓者，逃了出去，最终竟加入了誓言使者。最后一次听说他的消息，是他夺回了小安塞尔姆的头骨，并用锤子将其砸碎。他新结识的誓言使者弟兄勃然大怒，当场将他杀死。人们找到%name%的尸体时，上面已有百余处刺伤，灰白的头骨碎屑洒在那张染血而疯狂咧笑的脸上。

89a3677d2348bc2530ad.source: Peddlers are not used to hard physical labor or warfare, but they do excel at haggling for good prices.
89a3677d2348bc2530ad.translation: 小贩不习惯繁重体力劳动或战争，却很擅长讨价还价。

dac92995dab3c40bda28.source: A man of the sale, %name% the peddler couldn't stay fighting for long. He eventually left the %companyname% to go out and start his own business. Recently, you got word that he was selling trinkets with the company's sigil on them. You specifically told him he can do whatever he wants except just this one thing, but apparently your warning merely fostered the idea in him. When you went to tell him to stop, he slammed a crown-bulging satchel on his rather ornate table, saying it was your 'cut.' He sells those trinkets to this day.
dac92995dab3c40bda28.translation: 小贩%name%终究是个做买卖的人，打不了太久的仗。他最后离开%companyname%，出去经营自己的生意。最近，你听说他在卖刻着战团徽记的小玩意儿。当初你明明特意告诉过他，想做什么都行，唯独不准做这个，结果你的警告反倒给他出了主意。你找上门去，想让他停手，他却把一只塞满克朗的钱袋重重摔在那张颇为华丽的桌子上，说这是你的“分成”。直到今天，他还在卖那些小玩意儿。

d949f42fc00270f08ea4.source: With hard times hitting the %companyname%, many brothers saw fit to return to their old lives. %name% the peddler was no different. Last you heard he got the tar beaten out of him trying to sell stolen wares that 'fell off the wagon' to the very merchant which they originally belonged.
d949f42fc00270f08ea4.translation: %companyname%遭遇困境后，许多兄弟决定重返旧日生活，小贩%name%也不例外。最后听说，他想把一批“从货车上掉下来”的赃物卖掉，偏偏撞上原主，被商人痛打了一顿。

543398a43d81055abfba.source: {House to house, | Once a proud merchant, now | An annoyance to most, | In tough times, everyone has to scrape by somehow, hence why | Not a man of the trades, but instead of trade itself,} %name% is a mere peddler. {He'll dance, he'll sing, he'll boast and he'll act a king, anything to make that sale. | Pushy and unrelenting, his tenacity is admirable. | He'll try to sell off a rusty bucket for a helm once worn by kings. This man will sell anything. | This man will make you crave things you never knew you wanted. No refunds, though. | He used to make a decent living selling {used carts | pots, pans and jars}, until fierce competition drove him out of business - by breaking his arm.} {Marketing himself is what this frail man does best, though few believe his pitch about having 'Great swordsmanship and resolute bravery'. | He supposedly handed out 'coupons' for his services, whatever those are. He's chippy, though, and any outfit these days could use a warm body no matter its real value. | If hired, he promises, you'll get a special discount on a virility enhancing potion. | The man lowers his voice and tells you he's got a great deal on rusted arrow tips, just for you. He looks disappointed at your lack of interest. | This man knows a man who knows a man who knows a man. All three strangers potentially better at fighting than him. | A shame a man can't fight with his words these days. %name% would be unstoppable.}
543398a43d81055abfba.translation: {挨家挨户地叫卖， | 昔日是个体面的商人，如今， | 在大多数人眼里是个烦人精， | 艰难世道，人人总得想办法糊口，因此， | 不会什么手艺，倒很懂买卖之道，}%name%只是个小贩。{他能跳、能唱、能吹，还能装出国王的派头，只要能把货卖出去，什么都肯做。 | 他死缠烂打，绝不松口，那股韧劲倒值得佩服。 | 他能把生锈的水桶当成国王戴过的头盔兜售。这人什么都敢卖。 | 他能让你渴望那些原先压根不想要的东西。不过，概不退货。 | 他曾靠卖{二手货车 | 锅碗瓢罐}过得不错，直到激烈的竞争让他做不下去——对手打断了他的胳膊。}{这个瘦弱的人最擅长推销自己，不过他吹嘘的“剑术高超、勇敢坚定”，没几个人相信。 | 据说他还发过雇用自己的“优惠券”，谁知道那是什么。不过他挺有精神，如今哪支队伍都用得上活人，不论实际有多大用处。 | 他保证，只要雇下他，你就能以特价买到壮阳药。 | 他压低声音，告诉你自己手头有批便宜的生锈箭头，专给你留的。见你毫无兴趣，他显得很失望。 | 他认识一个人，那人认识另一个人，后者又认识第三个人。这三个陌生人，可能个个都比他会打仗。 | 可惜如今不能单凭嘴皮子打仗，不然%name%准能所向披靡。}

da34ab92b9d82730b7ef.source: Poachers tend to have some skill in using bow and arrow to hunt down rabbits and the like.
da34ab92b9d82730b7ef.translation: 偷猎者通常会用弓箭猎取野兔之类的小动物。

381886c793a9030c4726.source: %name%, former poacher, eventually saved enough money to leave the %companyname%. You learned he found a bit of mountain land and works it for a local nobleman. Ironically, his job is to hunt down poachers.
381886c793a9030c4726.translation: 曾经的偷猎者%name%终于攒够钱，离开了%companyname%。你听说他在山中找到一块地，替当地贵族做事。讽刺的是，他如今的工作正是追捕偷猎者。

883309f280647cc3b7eb.source: No longer seeing the point in risking his life for so few crowns, %name% the former poacher put down the sellsword's life and returned to unlawfully hunting deer in the woods. A nobleman once offered you a good satchel of crowns to specifically hunt the man down. You declined the offer, but the writing was on the wall: his days are numbered.
883309f280647cc3b7eb.translation: %name%觉得为了那点克朗冒生命危险已不值得，于是放下佣兵营生，重回林中非法猎鹿。有位贵族曾给你开出一袋钱，指名要你追捕他。你拒绝了，可结局已明摆着：他的好日子不多了。

bde25517b824d88f56df.source: {Interested in the thrill of the hunt, | Looking to support his family, | With a grumbling stomach, | After a long and hard winter that left him without a stock of food,} %name% {set off into the woods in chase of deer | sought wildlife to which, if his skittishness is any indication, he may or may not have had proper claim | ate his fill of all manner of woodland creatures, a well-used bow yoked across his shoulders indicating the means to his meals | took to the woods to hunt game with bow and spear}. Hailing from %townname%, %name% {was, as a poacher, the hunter and the hunted | needed to feed his wife and children back home | sought to support himself, his own hide, and his ever-growling stomach | was poaching, an act of rebellion against the order of things as much as a means to fill his belly}. {Fearful that his pursuits would attract bounty hunters or lawmen, he decided to settle on life as a bow for hire. | Tired of working so hard just to put food on the table, buying a meal with a sellsword's pay just seemed so much easier in his mind. | After a bad hunt led him to a long stay in a lord's dungeon, he'd rather put his neck on the line as a mercenary now than in the noose as a poacher. | Years of lonely hunting wore on the man. Although life as a mercenary is exceedingly dangerous, he'd rather die with company than by himself. | His wife pleaded long that he change his ways lest the whole family pay for his crimes. He stands here now, a testament to who won the argument.}
bde25517b824d88f56df.translation: {迷上了狩猎的刺激， | 为了养活家人， | 肚子饿得咕咕叫， | 熬过漫长严酷的冬天，存粮已空，}%name%{走进树林追猎鹿群 | 开始寻找野味，而从他那副提心吊胆的模样来看，他大概没有正经的狩猎权 | 靠林中各种小兽填饱肚子，肩上那张磨旧的弓，说明了饭食从何而来 | 带着弓与矛进林狩猎}。来自%townname%的%name%{是个偷猎者，既猎杀动物，也被人追捕 | 得养活留在家中的妻儿 | 只想保住自己的命，填饱那只永远在叫的肚子 | 靠偷猎糊口，既是为了填饱肚子，也是在违抗这世道的规矩}。{担心这门营生会招来赏金猎人或差役，他决定安下心，当个受雇的弓手。 | 为了桌上一口饭，竟要如此辛苦，他早已厌倦。在他看来，拿佣兵的酬劳买顿饭，反而容易得多。 | 一次倒霉的狩猎让他在领主地牢里待了许久。如今，他宁愿当佣兵冒死，也不愿再以偷猎者的身份套上绞索。 | 多年独自狩猎，让他疲惫不堪。佣兵的生活固然极其危险，可即便要死，他也宁愿身边有人，而非孤零零一个。 | 妻子苦劝他改行，免得全家替他的罪行受罚。如今他站在这里，足以说明这场争论是谁赢了。}

7218a59b28494f350e11.source: Any raider that survived so far will have some expertise in fighting.
7218a59b28494f350e11.translation: 能在劫掠生涯中活到今天的人，多少都有些战斗本事。

22442d62402761daab2f.source: A former raider, %name% fit in well with the %companyname% and proved himself an excellent fighter. Having saved a veritable mountain of crowns, he retired from the company and returned from whence he came. He was last seen sailing a riverboat toward a small village.
22442d62402761daab2f.translation: 曾是劫掠者的%name%很快融入了%companyname%，也证明了自己是个出色的战士。积攒了堆积如山的克朗后，他离开战团，回到了来时的地方。最后有人见到他时，他正乘着一条河船驶向某座小村庄。

e40ea0d8c7010a67c9ef.source: As the %companyname% speedily declined, %name% the raider departed from the company and went on his own way again. He returned to raiding, taking his greedy violence along the shorelines of river villages. You're not sure if it's true, but word has it that he was impaled with a pitchfork by a stable boy. Word has it that the town hoisted his body parts along the outer walls as a warning to future would-be raiders.
e40ea0d8c7010a67c9ef.translation: %companyname%迅速衰落，劫掠者%name%也离开战团，再次独自上路。他重操旧业，沿着河岸村庄烧杀抢掠，贪婪而残暴。传闻他后来被一个马厩小厮用草叉刺死，镇民把他的残肢挂在城墙外，警告日后胆敢来犯的劫掠者。你不知道这些传闻是真是假。

1e7c1ac22c93af2c1ffd.source: {Living by the shore, %name%'s life was peppered with the spice of sea raiders. As an adult, he joined them in the raiding. | When his family was slaughtered, newborn %name% was taken in by the very raiders who did it. | Born in a faraway place, %name% traveled to this land looking for towns to pillage. | A strong man from a remote part of the land, %name%'s presence here has been hellacious for local residents. | A raider with a strong oar-arm and an even greater axe-arm, %name% is part of the folklore that keeps kids in bed at night. | Part warrior, part criminal, %name% has made a good life as a raider. | %name% decided many years ago to take by force from the weak and feeble whatever he desired, and has made his presence known by raiding caravans and villages ever since. | A poor and starved boy growing up, %name% took to joining robbers and cutthroats out of desperation. For the first time in his life he didn't feel hunger every night, and so he continued to take by force from others what he needed. He learned to fight and to kill without remorse, and before long, he was a monster of a man. | Wearing a lord's boots and a queen's torn dress as a shawl, %name%'s attire reflects his years of raiding well. | The threat that stirs lords in their sleep and rushes housewives beneath beds, %name% is a menacing raider. | The strong take from the weak - that is the order of things that %name% lives by.} {He and his comrades raided caravans and preyed on outlying farms, only to find themselves being attacked for spoils of war one day. A small band of orcs had spotted %name%'s camp and washed it away like a force of nature, scattering the few survivors into every which direction. %name% ran and didn't look behind. | After many years of ill-gotten gains, the man gave up the life after a raid on an orphanage ended with an out of control fire and the deaths of those inside. | A devoted believer in the old ways, %name% desires to die a glorious warrior's death to take his place beside the gods. But slaughtering villagers like cattle won't get the attention of the gods, and so he now looks for a greater challenge. | But while raping and pillaging, %name% was noticed to have a preference for the husbands over the wives. His taste ostracized him from the rest of the warband. | It started with a good raid on a merchant caravan. The few guards were quickly cut down and the fleeing merchant didn't run fast enough - a javelin to his back attested to it. The spoils were rich, but before long there was heated argument about how they were to be shared. By evening, most of the raiders had killed each other. %name% only barely escaped and had nothing to show for his day but a limping leg. | But he always had a soft spot for women, and the constant rape and murder by his comrades pushed the raider away from this lifestyle. | Caught by a lord's guards, the raider barely escaped, instead watching from a hilltop as his comrades were executed. | But one village ambushed his party on a raid, cutting down everyone but himself as he stole a stable horse and escaped certain doom. | While staking out in a forest, the raider's party was attacked by vicious beasts. He fed his own comrade to the foul things just to save his own neck. | But as war tears the world asunder, the raider realized there was less and less to actually pillage. | But as conflicts boil, every village he ran into was either dirt poor or already armed to face other fiends of the world.} {Now, %name% just wants a fresh start, even in the dour field of sellswords. | %name% can't be wholly trusted as a mercenary, but having been in league with brigands and raiders at the very least makes him fit for the work. | The man is not brotherly in the least, but he can wield a weapon like it's one of his missing fingers. | While %name%'s past leaves a bad taste in anyone's mouth, there are even worse out there. | %name% is adept at killing and looting, just make sure those skills are directed toward your enemies. | While a good fighter, %name% is first and foremost loyal to loot. | %name% is here to kill things and take things. For you, this is a good thing. | %name% wears a necklace of ears about his neck, and another necklace adorned with those ears' earrings. Fancy. | %name% is a strong fighter, but he's in good running to be the least-liked individual in your whole party. | The countryside is an alluring, green canvas upon which to build a life. Maybe the raider just wants to settle down. | Wearing clothes tracked with their previous owner's blood, %name% looks strikingly ready for duty. | You get the feeling that %name% is wearing clothes that someone was probably murdered in.}
1e7c1ac22c93af2c1ffd.translation: {%name%在海边长大，生活中从不缺海盗来袭的惊扰。成年后，他却加入了他们，也干起了劫掠的勾当。 | %name%的家人遭到屠杀时，他才刚出生。收养他的，正是杀害他全家的劫掠者。 | %name%出生在遥远的异乡，来到这片土地，就是为了寻找可以洗劫的城镇。 | %name%是个来自偏远地区的壮汉。自从他踏足此地，当地人的日子便如同坠入了地狱。 | %name%划桨的臂膀强壮有力，挥斧时更是凶狠。大人们用这名劫掠者的故事吓唬孩子，让他们夜里乖乖待在床上。 | %name%半是战士，半是恶徒，靠劫掠过上了不错的日子。 | 多年前，%name%便认定，想要什么就该从弱者手里抢。此后，他靠劫掠商队和村庄打出了自己的恶名。 | %name%自幼贫困，饥肠辘辘，走投无路之下投靠了强盗和杀人犯。他平生头一次不用每晚挨饿，于是继续从别人手里抢夺所需的一切。他学会了厮杀，也学会了杀人而不知悔恨，没过多久，便成了披着人皮的恶兽。 | %name%脚蹬领主的靴子，肩披女王撕破的裙裳。这身行头，倒把他多年的劫掠生涯交代得清清楚楚。 | %name%是个凶名在外的劫掠者。他的威胁能让领主从睡梦中惊醒，让妇人慌忙钻到床底。 | 强者掠夺弱者——这就是%name%奉行的世间法则。} {他和同伙袭击商队，劫掠偏远农庄，直到有一天，轮到别人来抢他们的战利品。一小队兽人发现了%name%的营地，如天灾般将其扫平，幸存的几个人四散奔逃。%name%拔腿就跑，连头也没回。 | 他靠不义之财过了多年，直到一次洗劫孤儿院时，大火失控，烧死了里面所有人。此后，他放弃了这种生活。 | %name%笃信古老的教诲，渴望像战士一样光荣战死，前往诸神身旁。然而，像宰牲口般屠杀村民，显然换不来诸神的垂青。如今，他正寻找更值得一战的对手。 | 但在烧杀奸淫之中，同伙发现，比起妻子，%name%更喜欢向丈夫下手。他的癖好让整支战帮都疏远了他。 | 那天开头还算顺利：他们劫下一支商队，轻易砍倒了寥寥几个护卫；逃跑的商人也没能跑远，一根标枪扎进了他的背。战利品相当丰厚，可分赃很快变成了争吵。到了傍晚，大半劫掠者已经自相残杀而死。%name%勉强逃出，忙活一天，除了瘸掉一条腿，什么也没捞着。 | 可他对女人总有几分怜惜，同伙无休止的强奸与杀戮，最终让他离开了这条路。 | 一次，领主的卫兵抓住了这伙劫掠者。他侥幸逃脱，只能站在山头，看着同伙被一一处决。 | 但一次劫村时，村民设伏杀光了他的同伴。他偷了一匹马厩里的马，这才逃过必死之劫。 | 他们藏在森林里踩点时，遭到一群凶兽袭击。为了保住自己的脖子，他把同伴送进了那些怪物的嘴里。 | 然而，战火把世道撕得支离破碎，他渐渐发现，能抢的东西越来越少了。 | 然而，纷争日盛，他遇到的村庄不是穷得一无所有，就是早已武装起来，准备对付这世上的其他恶徒。} {如今，%name%只想重新开始。哪怕是投身佣兵这份阴沉的营生，也比从前强。 | %name%当佣兵未必完全靠得住，但他曾与强盗和劫掠者为伍，至少不缺干这行的本事。 | 这人毫无兄弟情义可言，但武器到了他手里，就像补回了一根缺失的手指，运用得自如极了。 | %name%的过去固然令人不齿，但这世上比他更坏的人也不少。 | %name%精于杀人和抢掠。你只须确保，他把这些本事用在敌人身上。 | %name%虽是个好手，但他首先效忠的，永远是战利品。 | %name%来这里就是为了杀人、拿东西。对你而言，这倒算是好事。 | %name%脖子上挂着一串耳朵，还有另一条项链，串着那些耳朵原先戴着的耳环。真够讲究。 | %name%身手强悍，不过要说谁最可能成为全队最招人厌的家伙，他也名列前茅。 | 乡间一片青绿，仿佛等着人们在上面安家立业的画布。也许，这个劫掠者只是想找个地方安顿下来。 | %name%身上的衣服还留着前任主人的血迹。这副模样，倒显得随时都能上阵。 | 看着%name%的衣着，你总觉得它原来的主人，多半就是穿着这一身被杀的。}

1aef73f60a12448e4208.source: Ratcatchers need to have quick reflexes to catch their prey.
1aef73f60a12448e4208.translation: 捕鼠人需要敏捷的反应，才能抓住猎物。

f5ba2f73050d791225a9.source: %name% the ratcatcher came from stranger stocks, and to stranger stocks he returned. After retiring from the %companyname%, he started a ratcatching company. He was doing wonderful business until it came out that he hadn't been killing any of the rats, but instead stowing thousands of them in a storehouse just outside town. Last you heard, the man was quite content with his new and numerous friends.
f5ba2f73050d791225a9.translation: 捕鼠人%name%出身古怪，最后又回到了古怪的营生中。从%companyname%退役后，他开办了一家捕鼠铺子，生意兴隆得很，直到人们发现，他一只老鼠也没杀，而是把成千上万只老鼠藏在城外的一间仓库里。最近听说，他和那群数不清的新朋友过得十分惬意。

528ed3109d78bc04b681.source: You didn't think %name% would fit in with sellswords, but he proved himself capable. Unfortunately, the %companyname% fell apart and he returned to ratcatching. You got word that his body was found in a sewer utterly covered in nibbling rats. It's said that he had a smile on his face.
528ed3109d78bc04b681.translation: 你原以为%name%不适合佣兵这行，他却证明了自己的本事。不幸的是，%companyname%最终分崩离析，他只好重操捕鼠旧业。后来有人告诉你，他的尸体倒在下水道里，满身都是啃咬的老鼠。据说他脸上还带着笑。

57a4d0f7d527f05cdd35.source: {Catcher of rats, that's the title %name% once preferred. | With perhaps misplaced pride, %name% fashions himself as a man of the sewers. | Bowlegged and scrawny, %name%'s career of hunting rats has seemingly turned him into one.} He grew up in %townname%, surviving {in the alleys | on rat, the fruit of the sewers | alongside the furry and scuttling, as well as some rats}. {For cheap entertainment, his father taught him the ways of snaring tiny rodents | His fallen brother's body was eaten by rats, forging an angry future of rodent-revenge | His mother demanded the finest meats he could find, and she didn't mean from the market}. But %townname% wears on people, and it wore on %name% like a giant, nibbling creature. {Hearing of greater rats in the world | Sensing that there must be more to life than rats | Trusting his rat-whispering skills}, %name% now seeks to {put his shriveled nose, odd gnawing habits, and quick but kind of gross hands to better use. | crush every rat, see them driven before him, and to hear the squeals of their kin. He has a thousand-yard stare and a clenched fist as he tells you this. | perhaps graduate his skills from rats to dogs and maybe humans, so he says. He doesn't appear to know what he's in for, but perhaps it is best to not tell him. | dish up some rat soup, rat salad, rat kebab, rat bread, rat stew, rat chicken, rat wine... after a while, you just stop listening.}
57a4d0f7d527f05cdd35.translation: {捕鼠人，%name%从前最喜欢这个称呼。 | %name%以“下水道里的汉子”自居，那份自豪也许用错了地方。 | %name%罗圈腿，瘦骨嶙峋，多年的捕鼠生涯似乎把他自己也变成了一只老鼠。}他在%townname%长大，{在小巷里勉强维生 | 靠下水道的“出产”——老鼠——活了下来 | 和浑身是毛、四处乱窜的家伙们一起过活，当然，其中也有几只老鼠}。{为了找点不花钱的乐子，父亲教他如何设套捕捉小啮齿动物 | 死去兄弟的尸体被老鼠啃食，自此他便走上了向鼠辈复仇的愤怒之路 | 母亲要他找来能找到的最好的肉，而她指的可不是去市场买}。但%townname%消磨人心，也像一头不断啃咬的巨兽，慢慢啃噬着%name%。{听说世上还有更大的老鼠 | 觉得人生除了老鼠，总该还有别的东西 | 相信自己与老鼠打交道的本领}，%name%如今想{让那只干瘪的鼻子、古怪的啃咬习惯，以及灵巧却有点恶心的双手，派上更大的用场。 | 碾碎每一只老鼠，看它们在自己面前逃窜，再听它们亲族的尖叫。他说这话时攥紧拳头，两眼直直望向远方。 | 把自己的本事从老鼠身上，慢慢用到狗，或许还有人身上。他是这么说的，似乎并不知道自己将面对什么，不过也许还是不告诉他为好。 | 做出鼠汤、鼠肉沙拉、鼠肉串、鼠肉面包、炖鼠肉、鼠肉鸡、鼠酒……听了一会儿，你就懒得再听了。}

1c22f3aa0f207cff19db.source: Refugees lack the conviction to fight for their homes, but they are used to long and exhausting travel by now.
1c22f3aa0f207cff19db.translation: 难民缺乏守卫家园的决心，却已习惯漫长而疲惫的迁徙。

24d972375ff2b83082ac.source: %name% the refugee showed himself to be a natural fighter, but he eventually retired from the %companyname%. Word has it he returned to his home and is currently using all his crowns to help rebuild it.
24d972375ff2b83082ac.translation: 难民%name%展现出天生的战士本领，却最终从%companyname%退役了。据说他回到故乡，正倾尽积蓄帮助家乡重建。

2c4b3ce248824750ed05.source: With the downfall of the %companyname% written plainly on the wall, %name% the refugee split with the company. He used what scant crowns he had left to purchase a set of shoes and returned to his destroyed home to try and rebuild it. While walking home, an illiterate wildman murdered him and ate the shoes.
2c4b3ce248824750ed05.translation: 眼见%companyname%的衰败已成定局，难民%name%离开了战团。他拿所剩无几的克朗买了双鞋，想回到破败的故乡重建家园。返乡途中，一个目不识丁的野人杀了他，还把那双鞋吃了。

6222d93353e57e18d98f.source: {Catastrophes are cheap. | Disease, the ultimate invisible hand. | Win or lose a war, everything is as it has been.} %name% hails from a tiny village that {is now only remembered by spoken word, a generation away from being forgotten. | was destroyed, to put it succinctly. | now stands as a mere footnote, wasting little of the historian's ink. | suffered the world's wrath.} But %name% is a survivor. {He fled the disaster with just the clothes on his back. | His home ablaze, he saved what he could and fled. | After stumbling upon his dead family, he gathered what he could and ran. | War, famine, disease. It's all a blur to him now.} {%name% is merely a man anxious to look ahead rather than behind. | %name% carries little more than a sense of steeled determination, but that is something worth having. | A horrific history scars his body and glazes his eyes, but the man is easily motivated to never experience that past again. | Whatever befell the man's town didn't get him and, judging by the rumors you hear, that's saying something. | The man isn't skilled in martial arts, but he is for damn sure determined to survive. | Whatever vocation he had in the past is now lost. Like many others, he seeks mercenary work to get by in this increasingly bloody world. | One of many refugees you've seen, this man has decided to stop running and start fighting.}
6222d93353e57e18d98f.translation: {灾祸从来不稀罕。 | 疾病，那只最可怕的无形之手。 | 战争赢了也好，输了也好，日子还不是一样。}%name%来自一个小村庄，如今那里{只活在人们的口耳相传中，再过一代便会被彻底遗忘。 | 说得简单些，已经毁了。 | 只配在史书里留下一笔注脚，费不了历史学者多少墨水。 | 已遭尽这个世界的怒火。}但%name%活了下来。{他逃出灾难时，只剩身上那套衣服。 | 家园起火，他抢出力所能及的东西，逃了。 | 意外发现全家已死后，他匆匆收起能带走的东西，拔腿就跑。 | 战争、饥荒、疾病。如今在他脑海中，都只剩模糊的一团。}{%name%不过是个急着向前看、不愿再回首的人。 | %name%几乎一无所有，只剩一股磨炼出来的坚定意志，不过这也很值得珍惜。 | 可怕的往事在他身上留下伤疤，让他的目光变得木然。不过，为了不再重蹈覆辙，他很容易便能鼓起干劲。 | 无论什么毁了他的村镇，都没能要他的命。而从你听到的传闻来看，这已经很了不起了。 | 他不擅武艺，却他妈铁了心要活下去。 | 过去的营生已荡然无存。和许多人一样，他想靠当佣兵，在这个越来越血腥的世道里混口饭吃。 | 他是你见过的众多难民之一，不过这个人决定不再逃跑，而是拿起武器。}

e4e8494e2925125f7306.source: {%name% is no longer disowned by his royal family, yet his allegiance is now with the %companyname%. Despite not returning home to his lineage, you know that deep down he is emboldened by the fact that he is back in his natural bloodline.}
e4e8494e2925125f7306.translation: {%name%已获王室家族重新接纳，但如今他效忠的是%companyname%。尽管没有回去继承家业，你仍知道，重获家族承认让他心底多了几分自信。}

6979cf7261d0fee3e696.source: Retired soldiers tend to have decent experience in warfare, and their resolve is not easily broken. However, their age may have taken a toll on their physical attributes.
6979cf7261d0fee3e696.translation: 退伍士兵通常作战经验丰富，意志不易动摇。不过年龄可能已经损耗了他们的体能。

4fe1e990e9283a240b09.source: %name% retired again, this time from sellswording instead of soldiering. Leaving the %companyname% behind, he built a cabin out in the woods and enjoys the peace and quiet, staying as far away from all the fighting as he can get.
4fe1e990e9283a240b09.translation: %name%又一次退役了，只是这回离开的是佣兵战团，而不是军队。告别%companyname%后，他在林中盖了间木屋，享受宁静，尽可能远离一切厮杀。

2abdb6d242a70ece6636.source: Tired of all the fighting, %name% left the quickly declining %companyname% and went out and built himself a cabin in the woods. Unfortunately, vagabonds attacked. Word has it he was found bleeding out on the floor, surrounded by six dead men and the last man standing, a nervous, broken boy shakily waving a sword at the dying old man.
2abdb6d242a70ece6636.translation: 厌倦厮杀的%name%离开迅速衰败的%companyname%，在林中为自己盖了间木屋。不幸的是，一伙歹徒袭击了他。据说人们发现他倒在血泊中，四周躺着六具尸体。唯一站着的是个惊恐失常的男孩，正颤抖着把剑指向垂死的老人。
