e249dea3717a4d780774.source: Once {a sergeant | a royal guardsman | a dedicated soldier | a respected armsman | a frontliner | a soldier | a footman} in the army of a local lord, %fullname% {retired from service after taking an arrow to the knee | was replaced by an aspiring youngster | was expelled after falling asleep on guard duty | retired after a long and exemplary service | was wounded in combat and forced to retire | grew weary of the battles and bloodbaths, formally ending his service before it ruined his mind | battled the ferocious orc hordes, the campaigns eventually forcing him into retirement}. {He locked his equipment in a chest along with the memories of his duty, intending to never pick up either one again | He shelved both sword and shield in his study as merely relics of a military past | He hung his weapons above the chimney as a silent reminder of the man he used to be | But a new chapter in his life was awaiting him, one where he would not need a sword to get on with his day | With many years of service behind him, he could finally get some peace and quiet | Absent of a military drill's barking, his life never felt so quiet}. {For many years he lived a happy life with his beloved wife, until she died of old age. With nothing else to turn to | Only when finding out that his former comrades were brutally slain in an ambush | Only when hearing rumors of a large invasion about to destroy his homeland, | He tried to live as a farmer for a while, but every day he missed having a good sword in hand and standing in the shieldwall. Finally, | But life outside the army, as it turned out, was not for him, for he felt idle and useless. Finally, | For a time, he felt at ease. But as the land was consumed by warfare, | Time spent away from war was short-lived, as the war soon came to him. It wasn't long until | Living out on a farm, boredom crept at %name%'s wits until, finally,} he picked up arms once more. Although {his best days are long over | not as physically fit as he once was | his constitution is not that of a young man anymore | he is not the brash young fighter he once was | time away from the service has dampened his abilities}, {his swordfighting skills are still enough to beat any young braggart | he still knows how fighting is done on the battlefield | his experience is second to few | he can rely on the combat experience of a lifetime | he is eager to stand amongst brothers | he is eager to find battle again | his itch to find battle is mirrored by his capabilities to actually fight | he still knows a thing or two about holding a shieldwall}.
e249dea3717a4d780774.translation: %fullname%曾是当地领主军中的{一名军士 | 一名王家卫兵 | 一名尽职的士兵 | 一名受人敬重的战士 | 一名前线士兵 | 一名士兵 | 一名步兵}，后来{膝盖中了一箭，便退了役 | 被一名雄心勃勃的年轻人取代 | 因站岗时睡着而被逐出军队 | 在漫长而无可指摘的服役生涯后退了役 | 在战斗中受伤，被迫退役 | 厌倦了战斗与血腥，趁着还没被逼疯，正式结束了军旅生涯 | 与凶猛的兽人群鏖战，连年的征伐最终迫使他退役}。{他把装备连同服役的回忆一起锁进箱子，打算再也不去碰它们 | 他将剑盾放在书房里，只当是军旅往事的遗物 | 他把武器挂在壁炉上方，默默提醒自己曾是什么样的人 | 人生的新篇章正等着他，在那里，每天过日子不必再靠一把剑 | 多年戎马生涯终于结束，他总算能享些清静 | 没了操练时的吼声，他的生活从未如此安静过}。{他与爱妻幸福地度过多年，直到她年老去世。再无别的寄托， | 后来得知昔日战友在一场伏击中惨遭杀害， | 后来听闻大军将至、即将毁掉故乡的消息， | 他试着当过一阵农夫，却每天都怀念握着好剑、站在盾墙中的感觉。终于， | 可事实证明，军队之外的生活并不适合他，他只觉得自己无所事事、毫无用处。终于， | 有一阵，他确实心安了。可当战火吞噬大地， | 远离战争的日子十分短暂，战火很快便找上门来。没过多久， | %name%住在农场，百无聊赖一点点蚕食着他的心神，直到最后，}他再次拿起了武器。尽管{最好的年华早已过去 | 体格不复当年 | 身子已不再像年轻人那般结实 | 不再是当初那个勇猛冒进的年轻战士 | 离开军队太久，本领已有些生疏}，{他的剑术仍足以击败任何年轻的吹牛大王 | 他仍知道战场上的仗该怎么打 | 他的经验仍鲜有人及 | 他仍能依靠一生积攒的作战经验 | 他仍渴望回到弟兄们中间 | 他仍迫切地想再赴战场 | 他渴望战斗，也确实有本事打仗 | 他仍懂得如何守住一道盾墙}。

f911c218180bfd3b2e5b.source: Sellswords are expensive, but a life of warfare has forged them into skilled fighters.
f911c218180bfd3b2e5b.translation: 职业佣兵要价高昂，但戎马生涯已将他们磨炼成技艺高超的战士。

9d6d907dbb0b589c5b8f.source: %name% the sellsword left the %companyname% and started his own mercenary company. As far as you know, it's a very successful venture and he often buddies up with the men of the %companyname% to work together.
9d6d907dbb0b589c5b8f.translation: 佣兵%name%离开%companyname%，另建了自己的战团。据你所知，他经营得相当成功，还经常与%companyname%的兄弟们联手接活。

574558a387b15e3eceed.source: %name% left the %companyname% and started his own competing company. The two companies clashed on opposite sides of a battle between nobles. The sellsword died when a mercenary from the %companyname% stove his head in with a hedge knight's helmet.
574558a387b15e3eceed.translation: %name%离开%companyname%，创建了自己的战团，成了竞争对手。两支队伍在贵族间的战争中分属敌对阵营，最终交锋。%companyname%的一名佣兵抡起流浪骑士的头盔，砸碎了他的脑袋。

7f9efa30011b5bdf72bd.source: {%fullname%'s worked as a sellsword since his father handed down his equipment. | %fullname% can't remember a time when he wasn't a sword for hire. | As a mercenary, %fullname% has never had to look long for work. | The literate talk about letting loose the dogs of war. %fullname% is one such hound. | In war, there is death and profit. %fullname% causes the former to earn the latter. | There has never been a better time for mercenaries like %name% to earn a crown or two. | After his wife ran off with his children, an angry %name% made a steady career as a nasty sellsword. | A decade ago %name% lost everything in a fire. He's been working as a sellsword ever since. | %name% always had the mind for violence and has pursued a long career as a sellsword. | Once dirt poor, %name% has earned a very tidy sum over the years as a sellsword. | %fullname% prefers to keep for himself whence he came, but his reputation as a sword for hire speaks for itself.} {Well experienced, he has traveled in the company of many outfits in his time. | Military campaigns are but notches in his belt. | From work as a lord's bodyguard to being an enforcer for a skeevy merchant, %name% has seen it all. | He once made a living off slaying the wild beasts that encroach on human settlements. | With a grim grin, he boasts he has slain all manner of living creatures. | Through plenty of use, the mercenary has learned a thing or two about weapons you didn't even know existed. | The sellsword is counting how many he has slain to this day and he appears to not be stopping any time soon. | With a sword and shield in hand, the mercenary appears to do what he does best for a living.} {The man is no stranger to the fields of battle. | The man is no stranger to the cruelties of war. | He is used to the harsh realities of mercenary life. | He is said to be a reliable cog in any shield wall. | Some say he can hold a battle line as well as an oak tree. | Rumors abound that the man enjoys the sight of blood. | Without shame, he takes an uneasy pleasure in the misery of others on the battlefield. | Strangely, he seldom joins others around the campfire, instead keeping to himself. | The man loves to tell a good tale about how he killed this thing or that. | Given a chance, the man is quick to showcase a wide variety of fighting styles.} {As long as you have the coin, %name% is yours to command. | A true mercenary, %name% will fight anyone for the right price. | Displaying some fine swordsmanship, %name% says he can run any man through. | With but a hint of a nod, %name% agrees to join you if you have the crowns. | Excited for an opportunity to earn coin, %name% knocks his mug on the table.}
7f9efa30011b5bdf72bd.translation: {%fullname%从父亲手中接过装备后，便一直以受雇作战为生。 | %fullname%已经想不起自己还没当佣兵时是什么样了。 | 作为佣兵，%fullname%从来不愁找不到活干。 | 读书人常说要放出战争的恶犬，%fullname%就是其中一条。 | 战争里既有死亡，也有利润。%fullname%制造前者，换取后者。 | 对%name%这样的佣兵来说，再没有比眼下更好挣克朗的年月了。 | 妻子带着孩子跑了以后，满腔怒火的%name%成了一名狠毒的佣兵，并以此为长久营生。 | 十年前，一场大火让%name%失去了一切。从那以后，他便靠当佣兵过活。 | %name%向来喜欢暴力，也因此在佣兵这一行干了许多年。 | %name%曾经一贫如洗，多年佣兵生涯却让他攒下了一笔可观的钱财。 | %fullname%不愿谈起自己的来历，但他身为佣兵的名声已足以说明一切。} {他经验丰富，曾跟随过许多支队伍。 | 一场场远征，对他来说不过是资历簿上添了几笔。 | 从领主的贴身侍卫，到奸商的打手，%name%什么差事都干过。 | 他曾以猎杀侵扰人类聚落的野兽为生。 | 他带着阴森的笑容，夸口说世间各类活物都死在过他手上。 | 历经无数战斗，这名佣兵连你听都没听过的武器也能说出几分门道。 | 他至今还在数自己杀过多少人，看来一时半会儿也不会停下。 | 剑盾在手，这名佣兵似乎正好靠着自己最擅长的事谋生。} {他对战场早已熟悉。 | 他对战争的残酷早已习以为常。 | 佣兵生涯的严酷现实，对他来说不过是家常便饭。 | 据说，把他放在哪一道盾墙里都靠得住。 | 有人说，他守起阵线来，像棵橡树一样稳。 | 传闻他很喜欢见血。 | 他毫不掩饰地以战场上他人的苦难为乐，让人很不舒服。 | 奇怪的是，他很少加入营火旁的闲谈，总是独来独往。 | 他爱讲故事，讲自己如何杀死这个、弄死那个。 | 只要有机会，他就会迫不及待地展示各式各样的搏杀技巧。} {只要你付得起钱，%name%就听你差遣。 | %name%是个十足的佣兵，价钱合适，谁都能打。 | %name%露了几手漂亮的剑术，说谁挡在面前，他都能一剑刺穿。 | %name%微微点头，表示只要你有克朗，他就愿意加入。 | 听到又有挣钱的机会，%name%兴奋地把酒杯往桌上一磕。}

d4c8d386d22899d1fb30.source: Servants are often not used to hard physical labor.
d4c8d386d22899d1fb30.translation: 仆役通常不习惯繁重的体力劳动。

5ce3c7df417ace15b065.source: As it turns out, %name% the servant had been stowing away every last crown he had earned with the %companyname%. When he had enough, he retired and bought himself some land and slowly worked his way up the social ladder. He died in a comfortable bed, surrounded by friends, family, and loyal servants.
5ce3c7df417ace15b065.translation: 原来仆役%name%一直把在%companyname%挣来的每一枚克朗都存着。攒够钱后，他退役买了地，慢慢爬上社会高处。他最终安然死在舒适的床上，身边围满亲友和忠实仆人。

ae8fb95995f685d12a5f.source: %name% the servant grew tired of the sellsword life and left the company. He returned to serving nobility. When raiders attacked his liege's castle, the nobleman pushed the servant out the door with only a kitchen knife to defend himself with. He was found headless in a pile of broken chairs, a few dead raiders littered around him.
ae8fb95995f685d12a5f.translation: 仆役%name%厌倦佣兵生活，离开战团，重新侍奉贵族。掠夺者袭击城堡时，贵族把他推出门外，只给了一把菜刀防身。后来，人们在一堆破椅子里找到他无头的尸体，身边也倒着几名掠夺者。

4dc72fb70f6b43f9a4eb.source: {Life is difficult. Moreso for some than others. | Some men can fall from grace. Other men have nowhere to fall to, having been born already on the ground. | If life is a throw of dice, maybe some are fools to be men rather than mice.} %name% {was a servant to a decadent lord. | served an abusive family where the kids played with fire. | was kidnapped by brigands and forced to serve their every. Last. Need. | worked feverishly for mad men who looked far too long at the stars.}  He rarely made a mistake about his place in the world. One day, though, his masters {beat him unconscious. When he awoke, he did so in the bed of a benevolent doctor who refused to return him to his 'employers'. Instead, %name% was free to go and his masters were told he had died. | set him free, no questions asked. Not one to dally on ceremony, %name% left in earnest. | invited him to a party. Believing he was a guest, he showed up in his finest attire - a shirt with hemmed sleeves and a billowy set of pantaloons that hid his skeletal frame well. Unfortunately, he was but a show for the party - they gave him a wooden shield and sword, threw him into an arena with a wild boar, and took bets as they watched the horrific spectacle. He barely escaped the 'festivities'.} {%name% has since sworn to never 'serve' someone again. | The man, though now free of his duties, still bears a great deal of humiliation and pain from his long, hard life.}
4dc72fb70f6b43f9a4eb.translation: {人生艰难，而有些人的人生比旁人更艰难。 | 有些人会从高处跌落，有些人却已无处可跌，因为他们生来就在泥里。 | 若人生只是掷骰子，有些傻瓜或许投错了胎，当老鼠都比当人强。}%name%{曾是一位骄奢淫逸领主的仆役。 | 侍奉过一个虐待下人的家庭，连孩子都爱拿火取乐。 | 被强盗绑走，被迫满足他们的每。一个。需求。 | 曾拼命替一群仰望星空太久的疯子干活。}他几乎从没弄错过自己在世上的位置。可有一天，主人们{把他打得不省人事。再醒来时，他躺在一位仁慈医师的床上。医师拒绝将他送回“雇主”手里，反而让%name%自由离去，并告诉那些主人，他已经死了。 | 放他自由，什么也没问。%name%不愿在礼节上耽搁，赶紧离开了。 | 邀他参加宴会。他以为自己也成了客人，穿上最好的行头赴约：一件袖口缝好的衬衫，加一条蓬松宽大的裤子，把瘦骨嶙峋的身子遮得严严实实。可惜，他不过是宴会上的节目。他们给了他木盾和木剑，将他与一头野猪一起扔进场中，边看这出骇人的闹剧，边下注取乐。他好不容易才逃出这场“盛会”。}{从那以后，%name%发誓再不“侍奉”任何人。 | 如今虽已摆脱差役，漫长苦日子留下的屈辱与伤痛，却依然压在他心头。}

f96437a8e38374d196c1.source: {Life is difficult. Moreso for some than others. | Some men can fall from grace. Other men have nowhere to fall to, having been born already on the ground. | If life is a throw of dice, maybe some are fools to be men rather than mice.} %name% {was a servant to a decadent vizier. | served an abusive family where the kids played with fire. | was kidnapped by nomads and forced to serve their every. Last. Need. | worked feverishly for mad men who looked far too long at the stars.}  He rarely made a mistake about his place in the world. One day, though, his masters {beat him unconscious. When he awoke, he did so in the bed of a benevolent doctor who refused to return him to his 'employers'. Instead, %name% was free to go and his masters were told he had died. | set him free, no questions asked. Not one to dally on ceremony, %name% left in earnest. | invited him to a party. Believing he was a guest, he showed up in his finest attire - a shirt with hemmed sleeves and a billowy set of pantaloons that hid his skeletal frame well. Unfortunately, he was but a show for the party - they gave him a wooden shield and sword, threw him into an arena with a wild hyena, and took bets as they watched the horrific spectacle. He barely escaped the 'festivities'.} {%name% has since sworn to never 'serve' someone again. | The man, though now free of his duties, still bears a great deal of humiliation and pain from his long, hard life.}
f96437a8e38374d196c1.translation: {人生艰难，而有些人的人生比旁人更艰难。 | 有些人会从高处跌落，有些人却已无处可跌，因为他们生来就在泥里。 | 若人生只是掷骰子，有些傻瓜或许投错了胎，当老鼠都比当人强。}%name%{曾是一位骄奢淫逸维齐尔的仆役。 | 侍奉过一个虐待下人的家庭，连孩子都爱拿火取乐。 | 被游牧民绑走，被迫满足他们的每。一个。需求。 | 曾拼命替一群仰望星空太久的疯子干活。}他几乎从没弄错过自己在世上的位置。可有一天，主人们{把他打得不省人事。再醒来时，他躺在一位仁慈医师的床上。医师拒绝将他送回“雇主”手里，反而让%name%自由离去，并告诉那些主人，他已经死了。 | 放他自由，什么也没问。%name%不愿在礼节上耽搁，赶紧离开了。 | 邀他参加宴会。他以为自己也成了客人，穿上最好的行头赴约：一件袖口缝好的衬衫，加一条蓬松宽大的裤子，把瘦骨嶙峋的身子遮得严严实实。可惜，他不过是宴会上的节目。他们给了他木盾和木剑，将他与一头野生鬣狗一起扔进场中，边看这出骇人的闹剧，边下注取乐。他好不容易才逃出这场“盛会”。}{从那以后，%name%发誓再不“侍奉”任何人。 | 如今虽已摆脱差役，漫长苦日子留下的屈辱与伤痛，却依然压在他心头。}

61db28012d2d1a6194c0.source: Shepherds are used to physical labor and known to keep the occasional wolf at bay with a sling.
61db28012d2d1a6194c0.translation: 牧羊人习惯体力劳动，也会用投石索赶走偶尔来犯的狼。

d44cf85db5f229a0bad3.source: It was unusual that a shepherd such as %name% ever found his way into a company of sellswords, but he did prove himself an able warrior. With injuries mounting, he eventually retired, returning to a meadow, staff in hand, and herding sheep until his final, peaceful days.
d44cf85db5f229a0bad3.translation: 像%name%这样的牧羊人会加入佣兵战团，本就不寻常，但他证明了自己是个能干的战士。随着伤病增多，他终于退役，手持牧杖重回草场，一直放羊到平静地走完余生。

7bf0a0897f6c7fb9449e.source: You'd think a shepherd would have no place in the company of sellsword and, eventually, %name% agreed. He left the %companyname% not long after you and last you heard he was back to tending his sheep. While most men left the company in poor spirits, %name%'s injuries did not bring down his docile lifestyle of staring at fluffy white critters about as dangerous as a bad dream.
7bf0a0897f6c7fb9449e.translation: 你也许会觉得，牧羊人在佣兵队伍里没什么位置，最终%name%也认同了这一点。他在你之后不久便离开了%companyname%，最近听说，已经回去照看羊群了。大多数人离开战团时都郁郁寡欢，%name%却没有让伤病毁掉自己安宁的生活：整日看着一群毛茸茸的白色小家伙，顶多也就一场噩梦那么危险。

589886978ff49ac3effc.source: {%name% was just a simple shepherd from a simple town, spending many years tending to his flock. | A lovely place like %townname% deserved a lovely shepherd like %name%. | %name% inherited his flock the same day he buried his father. | As a child, %name% stumbled upon a dead shepherd and the listless flock beside him. The boy took up the shepherd's staff and continued his work for many years. | More colorblind than a dog, %name% always enjoyed the company of color-friendly sheep. | When %name% fell from a tower, a flock of sheep broke his fall. He vowed to repay their sacrifice by being the safest shepherd in the land. | %name% found profit in bandying sheep about from one town to the next, selling their coats to tailors and skins to tanners. | Tending sheep was the easiest job %name% could find. | As harmless as the sheep he tends, %name% took to shepherding to find peace in the cruel world. | Never one to find good company amongst humans, %name% preferred the somber sapience of sheep. | Bullied as a child, %name% found peace in tending flocks of sheep. | The playfully obedient sheep of %name%'s life gave him the peace and calm from an otherwise rough upbringing. | Once mistaken for a {prophet | new messiah}, %name% escaped the {religious hordes | angry inquisitors} by disappearing into the vocation sheep shepherding. | Watching {sheep | white blobs of wool} munch on grass all day sounds boring, but to %name% it was bliss. | Enthralled by a sheep herding competition, %name% took to shepherding as a surprisingly competitive vocation. | Always a soft, kind boy, shepherding just made sense to the likes of %name%. | Escaping his abusive {mother | father | sisters | brothers | uncle | aunt}, %name% took the tranquility of being a shepherd.} {Mixed up in a religious conflict between gods followers and cultists, his flock suffered the wrath of those looking for both scapegoats and sacrifices. | Once fending off {brigands | wolves} with his walking stick, the shepherd wondered if maybe he was more physically capable than he once thought. | As time passed, the man felt {as though his vocation had passed him by. | like his heart just wasn't in it anymore.} {He mournfully retired | He hung up his shepherding stick} and sought out other work. | Feeling as though he was seeing the world's beauty but not experiencing it in full, the man decided to abandon shepherding. | When hulking, furry beasts slaughtered his flock, the shepherd was left looking for vengeance. | Sadly, the man's sole companion, a shepherding dog, was killed by {brigands | orcs | wolves}, leaving the peaceful man looking for revenge. | Caught in a loan shark's schemes, though, the shepherd suddenly needed more coin than his flock of sheep could ever provide. | However, the loneliness of his life finally got the shepherd. | But long days and nights by himself wore on the shepherd as they would any man. | But he could not escape the masculinity his father expected of him, and one day put down his walking stick to seek out a manlier vocation. | But one day, textiling while tending, he led every last sheep over a cliff. | But on a rainy afternoon he took one baaa too many: he had to do something beyond just stare at sheep all day. | One morning he awoke covered in sheep's blood, entrails, and bloody, entrails-laden wool. Wolves howled merrily in the distance. As it turned out, he had counted one too many sheep that night. | Unfortunately, rumors of what he did in the privacy of his flock were too embarrassing to face and he had to flee to greener, more accepting pastures. | Sadly, brigands drunk on violence stumbled upon his flock. Bessie, Little Ada, and even the newborn Goatsieg were bloodily dispatched.} {While stopping into town to think things over, %name% stumbled upon a call for mercenaries. With nothing to lose, he is ready to sign up. | The land had no place for a peaceful shepherd. It was time to move on to a new life. | A tiny, blood-rusted bell clings below %name%' neck. It is a relic of another life, and perhaps the sign of a new one. | He swears to still hear the bleating of his flock. For some reason, this does not inspire much confidence in his fighting skills. | Although peaceful as could be, without a flock the man is lost. | While hardly a fighter, the man knows how to keep a tight formation. | %name% knows the stars surprisingly well and can locate a sound in the darkness like a blind dog sniffing a treat. | Walking so much has given %name% sturdy legs, but the most combat experience he has is with a stick. | The world doesn't usually turn to shepherds in its time of need, but this is one very needy world at the moment. | Staring at the shepherd, you wonder just how bad things have gotten for such a man to be standing where he is. | %name% carries almost all weapons like they're walking sticks, and he has a bad habit of whacking the legs of others to move them along. | %name%'s humility is a welcome respite from the usual gungho brethren that become sellswords. | %name% looks like he wouldn't hurt a fly, but with good training you can see to it that he'll hurt a lot more than that. | %name% doesn't carry the murderous conviction of other sellswords, but like any man he can be trained up in all the right ways. | Some of the %companyname%'s men are little better than sheep. Maybe %name% has a place here after all.}
589886978ff49ac3effc.translation: {%name%只是个普通镇子里的普通牧羊人，多年来一直照看着自己的羊群。 | %townname%这样的好地方，就该有%name%这样和善的牧羊人。 | 埋葬父亲的那一天，%name%也继承了羊群。 | 小时候，%name%偶然遇见一名死去的牧羊人，旁边的羊群无精打采。他捡起那根牧羊杖，接过了这份活，一干就是许多年。 | %name%比狗还分不清颜色，因此一直喜欢与颜色简单的羊作伴。 | %name%从塔楼坠下时，一群羊替他垫了底。他发誓，要做全境最让羊安心的牧羊人，报答它们的牺牲。 | %name%赶着羊群往返于各个镇子，把羊毛卖给裁缝，把羊皮卖给制革匠，颇有赚头。 | 牧羊是%name%能找到的最轻松的差事。 | %name%和自己照看的羊一样温顺无害，当牧羊人，只为在残酷世道里找点安宁。 | %name%向来难在人群中找到知己，反而更喜欢羊群那沉静的“智慧”。 | %name%小时候常受欺负，照看羊群却让他找到了平静。 | 童年生活颇为艰辛，活泼而顺从的羊群却给%name%带来了安宁与慰藉。 | %name%曾被误认为{先知 | 新的救世主}，为了躲开{狂热的信徒 | 愤怒的审判官}，他隐姓埋名，当起了牧羊人。 | 整天看着{羊群 | 一团团白毛球}嚼草，听来无聊，对%name%却是莫大的幸福。 | 一场赶羊比赛让%name%着了迷，他就此投身牧羊，没想到这行也有如此激烈的竞争。 | %name%从小温和善良，牧羊对他这样的人再合适不过。 | 为逃离虐待他的{母亲 | 父亲 | 姐妹 | 兄弟 | 叔父 | 姑母}，%name%选择了牧羊人的清静日子。}{卷入诸神信徒与邪教徒的宗教冲突后，他的羊群遭了殃：那些人既要找替罪羊，也要找祭品。 | 一次用手杖击退{强盗 | 狼群}后，牧羊人不禁觉得，自己的身手也许比想象中更好。 | 日子久了，他觉得{自己已不适合这一行。 | 心思已经不在这份活上了。}{他怅然告别牧羊生涯 | 他挂起了牧羊杖}，另寻出路。 | 他觉得自己虽日日看见世界的美，却从未真正体验它，于是决定不再牧羊。 | 巨大而浑身长毛的野兽屠戮了羊群，牧羊人心中只剩复仇的念头。 | 可惜，他唯一的伙伴，那只牧羊犬，被{强盗 | 兽人 | 狼群}杀死了。这个温和的人就此走上复仇之路。 | 可他落入放高利贷者的圈套，忽然欠下一大笔钱，远远超出整群羊所能挣来的数目。 | 然而，孤独最终还是压垮了这个牧羊人。 | 漫长的昼夜独自度过，牧羊人也和任何人一样，渐渐被消磨殆尽。 | 可他始终摆脱不了父亲对男子气概的期待，终于有一天放下手杖，去找更像男子汉的营生。 | 一天，他边放羊边纺织，一不留神，把整群羊都领下了悬崖。 | 一个下雨的午后，他实在受够了那没完没了的咩咩声：总得做点什么，不能再整天盯着羊了。 | 一天早晨醒来，他浑身都是羊血、内脏，以及沾满血和内脏的羊毛。远处，狼群正欢快地嚎叫。看来，那晚他数羊数得太过投入，睡过去了。 | 可惜，关于他私下对羊群做过什么的传闻，实在让人无地自容。他只得逃走，另找一片更宽容、更丰美的牧场。 | 可惜，一伙杀红了眼的强盗偶然撞上了他的羊群。贝茜、小艾达，连刚出生的戈特西格，都被残忍地杀死了。}{%name%进城歇脚、思量出路时，偶然见到一则佣兵招募告示。他已没什么可失去的，准备报名。 | 这片土地已容不下温和的牧羊人，该开始新的生活了。 | %name%颈下挂着一只沾血生锈的小铃铛。那是往昔生活的遗物，也许也是新生活的预兆。 | 他发誓，自己仍能听到羊群的叫声。不知为何，这话实在让你对他的战斗本领提不起信心。 | 他虽然温和得不能再温和，可没了羊群，便彻底失去了方向。 | 虽然算不上战士，他倒知道怎样把队伍聚得紧紧的。 | %name%对星象的熟悉令人惊讶，在黑暗中辨别声音的来处，也像盲犬嗅食一样灵敏。 | 多年的步行让%name%有两条结实的腿，可他大多数搏斗经验，都只用过一根棍子。 | 世道危急时，人们通常不会去向牧羊人求助，可眼下这个世界实在太缺帮手了。 | 看着眼前的牧羊人，你不禁想，局面究竟糟到了什么地步，才会让这样的人走到这里。 | %name%拿什么兵器都像在拄手杖，还有个坏习惯：敲别人的腿，催他们往前走。 | 佣兵里向来多的是好勇斗狠的汉子，%name%的谦和倒让人难得舒心。 | %name%看起来连只苍蝇都不愿伤害，不过好好训练一番，你能让他伤到的远不止苍蝇。 | %name%没有其他佣兵那股杀气，不过和任何人一样，只要方法得当，他也能练出来。 | %companyname%里有些人比羊聪明不了多少。也许%name%在这里还真能找到自己的位置。}

For some reason, this does not inspire much confidence in his fighting skills. | Although peaceful as could be, without a flock the man is lost. | While hardly a fighter, the man knows how to keep a tight formation. | %name% knows the stars surprisingly well and can locate a sound in the darkness like a blind dog sniffing a treat. | Walking so much has given %name% sturdy legs, but the most combat experience he has is with a stick. | The world doesn't usually turn to shepherds in its time of need, but this is one very needy world at the moment. | Staring at the shepherd, you wonder just how bad things have gotten for such a man to be standing where he is. | %name% carries almost all weapons like they're walking sticks, and he has a bad habit of whacking the legs of others to move them along. | %name%'s humility is a welcome respite from the usual gungho brethren that become sellswords. | %name% looks like he wouldn't hurt a fly, but with good training you can see to it that he'll hurt a lot more than that. | %name% doesn't carry the murderous conviction of other sellswords, but like any man he can be trained up in all the right ways. | Some of the %companyname%'s men are little better than sheep. Maybe %name% has a place here after all.}
69908af80eb0461da5ea.translation: {%name%只是个普通镇子里的普通牧羊人，多年来一直照看着自己的羊群。 | %townname%这样的好地方，就该有%name%这样和善的牧羊人。 | 埋葬父亲的那一天，%name%也继承了羊群。 | 小时候，%name%偶然遇见一名死去的牧羊人，旁边的羊群无精打采。他捡起那根牧羊杖，接过了这份活，一干就是许多年。 | %name%比狗还分不清颜色，因此一直喜欢与颜色简单的羊作伴。 | %name%从塔楼坠下时，一群羊替他垫了底。他发誓，要做全境最让羊安心的牧羊人，报答它们的牺牲。 | %name%赶着羊群往返于各个镇子，把羊毛卖给裁缝，把羊皮卖给制革匠，颇有赚头。 | 牧羊是%name%能找到的最轻松的差事。 | %name%和自己照看的羊一样温顺无害，当牧羊人，只为在残酷世道里找点安宁。 | %name%向来难在人群中找到知己，反而更喜欢羊群那沉静的“智慧”。 | %name%小时候常受欺负，照看羊群却让他找到了平静。 | 童年生活颇为艰辛，活泼而顺从的羊群却给%name%带来了安宁与慰藉。 | %name%曾被误认为{先知 | 新的救世主}，为了躲开{狂热的信徒 | 愤怒的审判官}，他隐姓埋名，当起了牧羊人。 | 整天看着{羊群 | 一团团白毛球}嚼草，听来无聊，对%name%却是莫大的幸福。 | 一场赶羊比赛让%name%着了迷，他就此投身牧羊，没想到这行也有如此激烈的竞争。 | %name%从小温和善良，牧羊对他这样的人再合适不过。 | 为逃离虐待他的{母亲 | 父亲 | 姐妹 | 兄弟 | 叔父 | 姑母}，%name%选择了牧羊人的清静日子。}{卷入诸神信徒与邪教徒的宗教冲突后，他的羊群遭了殃：那些人既要找替罪羊，也要找祭品。 | 一次用手杖击退{强盗 | 狼群}后，牧羊人不禁觉得，自己的身手也许比想象中更好。 | 日子久了，他觉得{自己已不适合这一行。 | 心思已经不在这份活上了。}{他怅然告别牧羊生涯 | 他挂起了牧羊杖}，另寻出路。 | 他觉得自己虽日日看见世界的美，却从未真正体验它，于是决定不再牧羊。 | 巨大而浑身长毛的野兽屠戮了羊群，牧羊人心中只剩复仇的念头。 | 可惜，他唯一的伙伴，那只牧羊犬，被{强盗 | 兽人 | 狼群}杀死了。这个温和的人就此走上复仇之路。 | 可他落入放高利贷者的圈套，忽然欠下一大笔钱，远远超出整群羊所能挣来的数目。 | 然而，孤独最终还是压垮了这个牧羊人。 | 漫长的昼夜独自度过，牧羊人也和任何人一样，渐渐被消磨殆尽。 | 可他始终摆脱不了父亲对男子气概的期待，终于有一天放下手杖，去找更像男子汉的营生。 | 一天，他边放羊边纺织，一不留神，把整群羊都领下了悬崖。 | 一个下雨的午后，他实在受够了那没完没了的咩咩声：总得做点什么，不能再整天盯着羊了。 | 可惜，关于他私下对羊群做过什么的传闻，实在让人无地自容。他只得逃走，另找一片更宽容、更丰美的牧场。 | 可惜，一伙杀红了眼的游牧民偶然撞上了他的羊群。贝茜、小艾达，连刚出生的戈特西格，都被残忍地杀死了。}{%name%进城歇脚、思量出路时，偶然见到一则佣兵招募告示。他已没什么可失去的，准备报名。 | 这片土地已容不下温和的牧羊人，该开始新的生活了。 | %name%颈下挂着一只沾血生锈的小铃铛。那是往昔生活的遗物，也许也是新生活的预兆。 | 他发誓，自己仍能听到羊群的叫声。不知为何，这话实在让你对他的战斗本领提不起信心。 | 他虽然温和得不能再温和，可没了羊群，便彻底失去了方向。 | 虽然算不上战士，他倒知道怎样把队伍聚得紧紧的。 | %name%对星象的熟悉令人惊讶，在黑暗中辨别声音的来处，也像盲犬嗅食一样灵敏。 | 多年的步行让%name%有两条结实的腿，可他大多数搏斗经验，都只用过一根棍子。 | 世道危急时，人们通常不会去向牧羊人求助，可眼下这个世界实在太缺帮手了。 | 看着眼前的牧羊人，你不禁想，局面究竟糟到了什么地步，才会让这样的人走到这里。 | %name%拿什么兵器都像在拄手杖，还有个坏习惯：敲别人的腿，催他们往前走。 | 佣兵里向来多的是好勇斗狠的汉子，%name%的谦和倒让人难得舒心。 | %name%看起来连只苍蝇都不愿伤害，不过好好训练一番，你能让他伤到的远不止苍蝇。 | %name%没有其他佣兵那股杀气，不过和任何人一样，只要方法得当，他也能练出来。 | %companyname%里有些人比羊聪明不了多少。也许%name%在这里还真能找到自己的位置。}

0bb9d8f491eb1e0d173a.source: The indebted are a caste of de-facto slaves in the city states, and as such are not hired, but bought, and receive no daily wage.
0bb9d8f491eb1e0d173a.translation: 负债者是南方城邦里实质上的奴隶阶层，因此不是受雇，而是被买下，也没有每日工资。

c77024a865961d9bdaa7.source: %name% the indebted has had a rough life and you've both contributed to that and helped alleviate it in some way. You found him as a slave in the south, far from family and home. You 'hired' him essentially for free and worked him as an enslaved sellsword. After you left the %companyname%, his name was removed from the ledger of indebted and he was for all intents and purposes a free man. He stayed with the company and has been rising through its ranks ever since. You stand at an odd relation to the man. He's never thanked you, nor has he expressed ill.
c77024a865961d9bdaa7.translation: 负债者%name%一生艰难，你既给他添过苦，也在某种程度上减轻过他的苦。你在南方找到他时，他是个远离家人和故乡的奴隶。你几乎没花钱就“雇”了他，让他以奴隶的身份替你卖命。你离开%companyname%后，他的名字从负债者名册上被划去，无论从哪方面说，都成了自由人。他留在战团，自此一步步崭露头角。你与他的关系颇为微妙：他从没谢过你，也从未向你表露怨恨。

a202181c56bc697d9247.source: With your retiring from the unsuccessful %companyname%, %name% the indebted from the north carried on with the company for a time. You got wind that the mercenary band ran into financial troubles and was selling off 'man and material' to make ends meet. It seems %name%'s time with the company presumably ended sometime there, and his time as a slave started again.
a202181c56bc697d9247.translation: 你从功业未成的%companyname%退役后，来自北方的负债者%name%又随战团待了一阵。后来你听说，战团陷入财务困境，正在变卖“人手与物资”维持生计。看来，%name%的佣兵岁月大概就在那时结束，而奴隶生涯又开始了。

3377857086ee7b1d22e5.source: No morale check triggered for non-indebted allies upon dying
3377857086ee7b1d22e5.translation: 死亡时不会使非负债者友军进行士气检定

4d58be0d513c6a9347f3.source: {You can tell %name% is a northerner simply by appearance. And his servitude in the south has come by way of being indebted to the Gilder whom he has transgressed with his faith in the heretical old gods. | %name% bears the features of a northerner, easily capturing the eye of passing men or women. It also happened to catch the attention of a priest who claimed the northerner was indebted to the Gilder and promptly sold the interloper into servitude. | A northerner, %name% was once a soldier sent south on patrol. Lost in the desert, his troop slowly dwindled until he was the last survivor. Manhunters caught him and brought him back from the brink, and of course sold him into servitude once his healed body was worth something. | Despite being a northerner and thus easily spotted, %name% unwisely sought the criminal life and was caught thieving pomegranates from a Vizier's garden. He's lucky to have his head, but now serves as a commodity of labor on the Manhunting markets.}
4d58be0d513c6a9347f3.translation: {只看外貌，就能认出%name%是北方人。他如今在南方服役为奴，是因为信奉异端的旧神，冒犯了镀金者，因而背下债务。 | %name%有着鲜明的北方人相貌，轻易便能吸引过路男女的目光，也碰巧引来一名祭司的注意。祭司声称这个北方人欠了镀金者的债，随即将这位不速之客卖去为奴。 | 身为北方人的%name%曾是一名奉命南下巡逻的士兵。队伍迷失在沙漠里，人手逐渐凋零，最后只剩他一个。捕奴者抓到了他，将他从鬼门关拉回来，当然，等他的身子养好、值几个钱后，就把他卖去为奴了。 | 尽管北方人的外貌十分惹眼，%name%还是不明智地走上了犯罪之路，在偷摘维齐尔花园里的石榴时被逮住。他能保住脑袋已经算走运，如今却成了捕奴市场上一件供人买卖的劳力。}

be4e3a77f77e6c630dfa.source: You purchased %name% as an indebted for almost no gold and continued to pay him a 'slave's wage' for his stay as a sellsword. He did make himself an effective fighter, no doubt believing it was better to be paid nothing and fight to stay alive than be paid nothing and give up and rot. After your departure, you heard that the %companyname% traveled south on a campaign and the indebted got a good chance to exact a fair bit of revenge on a number of enemies in his past. Thankfully, he does not consider you one such person despite having kept him enslaved.
be4e3a77f77e6c630dfa.translation: 你几乎没花钱就买下了负债者%name%，此后他当佣兵期间，也一直拿着那份“奴隶的工钱”。他确实把自己练成了一名得力的战士，想必觉得，同样分文没有，拼命活下去，总好过放弃一切、慢慢腐烂。你离开后，听说%companyname%南下作战，这名负债者得了个好机会，向昔日的不少仇人讨回了公道。所幸，尽管你也曾让他为奴，他并没把你算在仇人之列。

33b84bbc6dca9ea3477d.source: You purchased %name% as an indebted and after your retiring, he went on with the %companyname%. Word of the mercenary band's problems have trickled in, but nothing about the indebted's current situation. Knowing how this world works, he has either been put into the vanguard as fodder or perhaps even been sold off to recoup profits. Either way, the world isn't easy on a sellsword, and it isn't easy on an indebted, and the man is unfortunately both.
33b84bbc6dca9ea3477d.translation: 你以负债者的身份买下了%name%。你退役后，他继续留在%companyname%。战团遭遇困境的消息陆续传来，却没有关于这名负债者近况的只言片语。以你对这世道的了解，他要么被塞进先锋队当炮灰，要么干脆被卖掉，用来回收本钱。无论哪种，世道都不善待佣兵，也不善待负债者，而不幸的是，他两样都占了。

1562e70e15d32d6b5cde.source: {Much of the southern city states float atop the expendable bodies of prisoners of war, criminals, and indebted, throngs of people who have slighted the Gilder or His followers and must 'earn' salvation through hard work. %name% is one such unfortunate soul.} {Like a shocking many, %name% was not always a hunted man. He worked as a traveling merchant until nomads ambushed his caravan. The nomads took him to a Vizier, pretending the man a criminal, and sold him as a hunted man. | Spotted for his handsomeness, %name% was kidnapped off the streets of %randomcitystate% and sold straight to a manipulative Vizier. He does not speak much of what all happened, but there is a sense manual labor was not his sole duty. | So great the religious transgressions of his predecessors, %name% was born into an indebted family, and it is uncertain how far back into his ancestry you must go before a truly free man would be found. | Desperate to save his family from generational debt, %name% sold himself into indentured servitude to ensure his wife and children have a life to live for themselves. | %name% swears he is from the north, but the deserts of the south have left him darkly tanned and, frankly, you've not much reason to believe the words of a former prisoner of war no matter where he's from. | A once sea-farer, %name% spent years as an oarmen traveling from harbor to harbor to drive the goods of opulent merchants. Those who gave him to you stated he has a criminal past in piracy. | %name% was accused of ravishing an old woman and was given the option of execution or lifelong servitude. | Caught stealing from a fruit stall, %name% was pressed into lifelong servitude. | Fornications with 'non-women' led to %name%'s submission to servitude per the rules of the city-state in which he broke the laws. It was either that or become a eunuch, and you can hardly blame him for choosing the hard labor in this case.} {The hardships of his life, rather quaintly, may serve as an excellent cast from which to mold a proper mercenary. | His servitude no doubt made the man formidable in appearance, though it may be hard to say where his mind is at being what is essence an indentured sellsword. | Slaves for warriors are a usual sight in the southern cities and %name% might serve as a useful, albeit enslaved, sellsword yet. | You hope %name% could make a sound sellsword, but you have the feeling his primary allegiance is to that which any man wishes to taste: freedom.}
1562e70e15d32d6b5cde.translation: {南方城邦的繁荣，大半建立在战俘、罪犯和负债者那些可以随意消耗的身体之上。这些人冒犯了镀金者或祂的信徒，必须靠苦役“挣得”救赎。%name%便是其中一个不幸的人。}{和多得令人心惊的同类一样，%name%并非生来就被人追捕。他原本是行商，直到游牧民伏击了商队。他们把他带到一位维齐尔面前，谎称他是罪犯，将他当作捕获的犯人卖了。 | %name%因相貌英俊而被盯上，在%randomcitystate%的街头遭人绑走，直接卖给了一位工于心计的维齐尔。他不愿多谈遭遇，不过听起来，体力活似乎并不是他唯一的职责。 | 因祖辈犯下的宗教罪过太重，%name%生来就是负债者。也不知道要往前追溯多少代，才能在他的祖先里找到一个真正自由的人。 | 为让家人摆脱世代相传的债务，%name%不惜卖身服役，换妻儿能够过上属于自己的生活。 | %name%发誓说自己来自北方，可南方沙漠早将他晒得黝黑。说实话，无论他来自哪里，你都没多少理由相信一个前战俘的话。 | %name%曾经出海谋生，多年充当桨手，往返各个港口，替富商运送货物。把他交给你的人说，他过去干过海盗的勾当。 | %name%被控强暴一名老妇，只能在处死与终身为奴之间做出选择。 | %name%在水果摊行窃时被抓，被迫终身为奴。 | %name%与“并非女人的人”私通，依照他触犯法度的那座城邦的律令，只得服役为奴。另一条路是受阉刑，在这种情况下，你实在很难怪他选择苦役。}{颇为讽刺的是，他一生所受的磨难，也许恰好能成为塑造一名合格佣兵的好底子。 | 奴役无疑将他的外表磨炼得强悍，只是如今换了个实质上仍受奴役的佣兵身份，他心里究竟怎么想，很难说。 | 在南方城邦，让奴隶当战士并不稀奇。%name%或许也能成为一名有用的佣兵，虽然仍是奴隶。 | 你希望%name%能成为可靠的佣兵，却总觉得，他最先忠于的，还是任何人都渴望品尝的东西：自由。}

99070573dd8cb9a97d96.source: Squires usually have received some training in warfare, and often have a high resolve to excel in what they do.
99070573dd8cb9a97d96.translation: 扈从通常受过军事训练，也有很强的上进心。

d2553f94d2aa210fe839.source: %name% the squire eventually left the %companyname%. You've heard that he's since been knighted. No doubt he is sitting happy as a plum wherever he is.
d2553f94d2aa210fe839.translation: 扈从%name%最终离开了%companyname%。你听说他后来被册封为骑士。不管他身在何处，想必正心满意足地过着日子。

7eaf69151e8c2cfc7924.source: The squire, %name%, eventually departed the %companyname%. He intended to return home and become knighted, fulfilling his lifelong dream. Cruel politics got in the way and not only was he not knighted, he was stripped of his squire duties. Word has it he hanged himself from a barn's rafters.
7eaf69151e8c2cfc7924.translation: 扈从%name%最终离开%companyname%，打算返乡受封为骑士，实现毕生梦想。残酷的权斗却毁了一切：他不但没能受封，连扈从的身份也被剥夺。据说他最终吊死在谷仓梁上。

4c806c49f00388a1d357.source: {A young squire, %name% dutifully accompanied his knight to many battles. | Squire to a harsh knight, %name% spent his days running errands for his lordship. | Although a squire, %name%'s life largely meant guarding prisoners of war, much to his chagrin. | Squire to a knight, sure, but %name% mostly cleaned latrines, fed dogs, and got far too much use out of a shinebox.} {One night, strange, shuffling men silhouetted the moonlit horizon. Alarm bells met their moans and an hour later half of %townname% lay in ruin. | While traveling, brigands attacked his lordship's wagon-train. Swords were drawn, heads were halved, and when it was all said and done the squire had failed: everyone he was supposed to protect lay dead. | But one evening a horde of ferocious, furred creatures came down upon his lord's keep. In desperation, %name% let a group of prisoners free, hoping they would aid him in combat. Instead, they slew his lordship and ran off into the night. The squire, bravely, managed to survive, a dozen husky corpses at his feet, but the battle left him alone and without purpose. | Angered by a horrible crime in %townname%, he took matters into his own hands, personally slaying the criminal. A just act, but also an improper one. The young squire was banished for his insubordination. | When a devilish red knight came to %townname% for a duel, %name%'s knight proved far too sick to fight. After downing a mug of liquid confidence, %name% donned his lordship's armor and faced the red knight himself. With a sword slash so fast it rang the very air, %name% slew his opponent down.} {Now there was only one task left for him - to attain knighthood. | Now the squire seeks the company of good men with which to again prove himself worthy of being a knight. | As war ravages the land, there is now plenty of opportunity to put his skills to use. | Though a bit too earnest, there is no doubt the world needs men like %name%.}
4c806c49f00388a1d357.translation: {年轻的骑士侍从%name%尽职尽责，陪同自己的骑士参加过许多战斗。 | %name%侍奉一位严厉的骑士，整日为老爷跑腿办事。 | %name%虽是骑士侍从，大部分日子却都在看守战俘，让他十分郁闷。 | 骑士侍从，说来不错，可%name%干得最多的，还是刷茅厕、喂狗，以及不停地擦靴子。}{一天夜里，月光下的天际出现了诡异的人影，拖着脚步蹒跚而来。警钟与呻吟声交织，一小时后，%townname%便有一半化作废墟。 | 旅途中，强盗袭击了老爷的车队。刀剑出鞘，头颅裂开，等一切结束，侍从已彻底失职：他本该保护的人，全都死了。 | 一天傍晚，一群凶猛的长毛怪物扑向老爷的城堡。绝境之中，%name%放出一批囚犯，盼他们助战。他们却杀死老爷，逃入夜色。侍从英勇奋战，终于活了下来，脚边倒着十几具壮硕的尸体，可那一仗也让他孤身一人，失去了人生的方向。 | %townname%的一桩骇人罪行激怒了他，他便自行出手，亲自杀死罪犯。此举虽出于正义，却越了规矩。年轻的侍从因违抗命令而遭到放逐。 | 一名恶魔般的红甲骑士来到%townname%挑战，可%name%侍奉的骑士病得太重，无法应战。灌下一杯壮胆酒后，%name%穿上老爷的铠甲，亲自迎战红甲骑士。剑刃快得连空气都为之鸣响，%name%一剑斩倒了对手。}{如今，他只剩最后一件事要做：成为真正的骑士。 | 如今，这名侍从想与正派的人为伍，再次证明自己配得上骑士之名。 | 战火蹂躏大地，如今有的是机会，让他施展本领。 | 尽管有些认真过头，这个世界无疑需要%name%这样的人。}

1803fb3e5891ab4ffae3.source: A swordmaster excels in melee combat like no other, but may be vulnerable at range. Age may have taken a toll on his physical attributes and may continue to do so.
1803fb3e5891ab4ffae3.translation: 剑术大师的近战技艺无人能及，却可能容易遭到远程攻击。年龄也许已开始侵蚀他的体能，并且还会继续。

c5e2e79c4748e7b9439a.source: The finest swordsman you'd ever seen, %name% the old swordmaster was a natural addition to the %companyname%. But a man can't fight forever. Despite the company's growing success, it was becoming readily obvious that the swordmaster just could not physically do it anymore. He retired to a nice plot of land and is enjoying some time to himself. Or so you thought. You went out to go see the man and found him secretly training a nobleman's daughter. You promised to keep it a secret.
c5e2e79c4748e7b9439a.translation: 年迈的剑术大师%name%是你见过最好的剑士，加入%companyname%自是如虎添翼。可一个人终究不能永远打下去。尽管战团日益兴盛，剑术大师的身体却越来越明显地吃不消了。他退隐到一片不错的田产上，享受独处的时光。至少你原本这么以为。直到你登门探望，才发现他正在偷偷教一位贵族的女儿练剑。你答应替他保密。

bec9c729847644f88c33.source: A shame that %name% the swordmaster had to spend his twilight years in a declining mercenary company. He retired, stating he just could not physically do it anymore. You think he was just letting the %companyname% down easy, because a week later he slew ten would-be brigands on the side of a road without breaking a sweat. Last you heard, he was training ungrateful princes in the art of swordfighting.
bec9c729847644f88c33.translation: 剑术大师%name%竟要在一支日渐衰败的佣兵战团中度过晚年，实在可惜。他退了役，说身子已经撑不住了。你觉得，他只是想给%companyname%留点体面，因为一周后，他就在路边毫不费力地杀了十个想打劫他的家伙。最近听说，他正在教几个不知感恩的王子练剑。

575e06e98e45d494f697.source: {%name% fights like a fish practices swimming. | %name% isn't just a man's handle, it's a myth. A name used in place of words like war, combat, and death. | To say, 'You move like %name%' is, perhaps, the greatest honor a man can bestow upon a fellow warrior. | %name% is considered to be one of the most dangerous swordsmen to have ever walked the earth.} {Much of his life is founded in myth: stories like how he dismantled a realm by challenging a king and all his guardsmen to a duel - and besting them with one hand. | Supposedly, he fought twenty men in his own garden, slowly picking and pruning his tomatoes with the same blade he was using to kill. | Some say he was left to sea for three-hundred days and there he learned - balancing on a piece of flotsam - how to move, how to fight, and how to survive. | A story goes that his family was murdered and he knew not by whom. Wanting to be ready if he came across those responsible, he taught himself to be good enough with a blade to kill anyone. | Raised by a one-armed father, he first learned how to fight with limitations. By the time he started using both hands he could already kill anybody with just one.} {Unfortunately, time and age have withered %name% into a shell of his former self. | During the orc invasions, %name% managed to kill a dozen greenskins singlehandedly. Sadly, an impossible feat does not come without a price: his sword-hand lost three fingers and his lead foot's achilles was severed. | Sadly, a horde of drunks fell upon his home, each hoping to become infamous by killing the famous swordsman. He slew them all, but not before taking irreversible injuries. | Legend has it that he quarreled with a foul beast of monstrous proportions. He waves the notion away with a fingerless hand and a scarred wink. | While teaching royalty how to fight, a coup that swept the entire realm had him running for his life. | Hired to teach noble heirs fighting skills, it wasn't long until he was embroiled in a web of intrigue and backstabbing, and had to leave as long as he still could.} {Now the old swordsman just looks to spend the rest of his fighting knowledge on the field. | While he's lost his edge, the man is still plenty dangerous and some say he's looking to find a student before he dies. | A master in the martial arts he may be, every movement he makes is echoed by the cracking of old bones. | Depressed and without purpose, %name% now finds meaning in simply blending in with the very men he used to teach. | The man makes it impossible to get through his defense, countering everything offered, but he no longer has the jump in his step to attack back. Admirable, but sad. | Given a sword, the old guard spins and twirls it in an impressive demonstration. When he plants it in the ground, he leans on the pommel to catch his breath. Not so impressive. | The man has been robbed of his athleticism, but his knowledge has turned swordfighting into mathematics.}
575e06e98e45d494f697.translation: {%name%战斗时，就像鱼儿游水一样自在。 | %name%不只是一个名字，更是一则传奇。人们用这个名字代指战争、搏杀与死亡。 | 对一位战士说“你的身手像%name%”，或许就是能给他的最高赞誉。 | %name%被认为是这世上有史以来最危险的剑士之一。}{他大半生都笼罩在传说之中：譬如，他曾向一位国王及其全部卫士挑战决斗，仅凭一只手便将众人击败，让一个王国就此土崩瓦解。 | 据说，他曾在自家菜园里迎战二十个人，一边不紧不慢地摘番茄、修枝，一边用同一把剑杀人。 | 有人说，他曾在海上漂泊三百天，在一块浮木上维持平衡，由此学会了如何移动、如何战斗，以及如何活下去。 | 有个故事说，他的家人遭人杀害，他却不知道凶手是谁。为了有朝一日遇见仇人时能做好准备，他苦练剑术，直到足以杀死任何人。 | 他由独臂的父亲养大，最初学到的，就是如何在受限的条件下作战。等他开始用双手时，单凭一只手，就已经能杀死任何人。}{可惜，岁月与衰老已将%name%消磨得只剩昔日的空壳。 | 兽人入侵时，%name%曾单枪匹马杀死十几只绿皮。可惜，这样的壮举也有代价：他持剑的手失去三根手指，前脚的跟腱也被割断。 | 可惜，一群醉汉闯进他家，人人都想靠杀死这位著名剑士，一举扬名。他把他们全杀了，自己却也受了无法痊愈的伤。 | 传说他曾与一头体型骇人的恶兽搏斗。他只是挥了挥那只没了手指的手，又挤了挤伤痕累累的眼睛，便将这说法轻轻带过。 | 他为王族教授武艺时，一场席卷整个王国的政变，让他不得不仓皇逃命。 | 受雇教授贵族子嗣武艺后，没过多久，他便卷入阴谋与暗算的罗网，只能趁着还能脱身，赶紧离开。}{如今，这位老剑士只想在战场上使尽毕生所学。 | 虽然锋芒已减，他仍是个危险人物。有人说，他想在死前收个徒弟。 | 他或许是武艺大师，可每动一下，老骨头都咔咔作响。 | 心灰意冷、失去目标，%name%如今只想融入那些自己曾教导过的人，在他们之中找到一点人生的意义。 | 他的防守无懈可击，你出什么招，他都能化解，可他的脚步已不够灵活，再无力趁势反攻。可敬，也可叹。 | 给他一把剑，这位老手便能旋转挥舞，演示得令人赞叹。等他将剑插在地上，又得撑着剑首喘口气，这一幕就没那么令人赞叹了。 | 他已失去矫健的身手，却凭毕生所学，把剑术化为了一门精确的算术。}

cfc22c17d558a29284da.source: Tailors are not used to hard physical labor.
cfc22c17d558a29284da.translation: 裁缝不习惯繁重的体力劳动。

b5a4b6670f68f2bd6b9f.source: What was a tailor doing in a mercenary company? A good question, but %name% certainly answered it well by killing so many enemies they could've made an epic tapestry out of story. After a few good years in the company, he eventually left to start up a business creating clothes for nobility. His name is world-renowned, well, the known-world-renowned, and he gets so much business he's making a very different killing these days.
b5a4b6670f68f2bd6b9f.translation: 裁缝跑到佣兵战团里来做什么？这问题问得好，%name%却用行动给出了答案：他杀敌之多，足以把事迹织成一幅史诗挂毯。在战团风光了几年后，他离队开店，专给贵族裁衣。如今他的名声传遍世界，至少传遍了人们已知的世界。生意多得做不完，这回他“杀”的，是顾客的钱袋。

6de5484e54197824bc2c.source: A tailor at heart, it didn't take much to compel %name% to bail from the quickly sinking company. He left to go start a business, but was kidnapped along the way by a group of brigands. When they threatened to kill him, he pretended to be a simple and weak tailor and showed his talents in creating clothes. Impressed, the raggedly dressed outlaws took him into their band. A few days later they were all dead and this 'meek' man walked out of their camp with a bit of red on him. He started his business a week later and is doing well to this day.
6de5484e54197824bc2c.translation: %name%骨子里仍是个裁缝，见战团一天天沉沦，便毫不留恋地离开，打算自己开店。途中他被一群强盗绑走，对方扬言杀他，他便装成老实软弱的裁缝，展示起缝衣的本事。衣衫褴褛的匪徒十分满意，将他收进了伙。几天后，强盗全死了，这位“温顺”的汉子沾着些血走出了营地。又过了一周，他的店开张了，生意至今兴隆。

af6db35b68bc7286b87c.source: {%name% was always curious about fabrics, seeing more science in a linen cloth than {a diviner would in the sands of the desert. | a haruspex would in a toad's entrails. | an alchemist would in a mortar and pestle.} | %name% was always an odd boy growing up, fancying a good silk dress instead of the girl beneath it. | Son to a {mining father | squire | knight | farmhand}, %name%'s turn toward fashioning clothes was a surprise to all. | While %name%'s sisters fancied being warriors and heroes, %name% thought of himself as a future dresser of kings. | %name% spent much of his youth in the company of girls, but not for the reasons one might think. | %name% always fancied animals, particularly how they would look as a good coat or scarf. | As tunics and shirts grew popular, %name% turned to tailoring to make a crown or two. | With a surge in pantaloons popularity, %name% went from being a tanner to a tailor to make more money. | %name% hails from a faraway land where how a man dresses is more important than how he fights. | Tailoring is the science of colors and fabrics, by which standards %name% is renowned. | Good with measuring and calculating, %name% turned his mathematical prowess to tailoring to earn as much as he could. | %name%'s career in tailoring started when his mother pushed him into the vocation to dodge a passing noble's conscription. | %name% took up tailoring to honor his father, a tailor who was killed by an unhappy customer. | Widowed by war, %name%'s mother taught him how to put his hands to better use in tailoring instead of killing.} {When raiders attacked his home, %name% dressed everyone up in clever disguises. The town was destroyed, but not a soul was lost. | He spent many years dressing royalty until a fashion faux pas led his being exiled. | Unfortunately, a man fancying a good fabric, as %name% is wont to do, left the tailor ostracized from many a village. | He tried to make his break in the big cities, but sadly he just could not compete with the other tailors. | When a lord organized an army, %name% handled the clothes, giving the soldiers proper uniforms. | But a fierce competition between tailors led to a linen-wrapped deadman and %name% coincidentally leaving his shop behind. | Sadly, robbers ransacked his shop and, with the wars going on, it would be impossible to restock. | But when he sheared a sheep that did not belong to him, %name% was kicked out of town. | He once choked out a would-be thief with a cord of measuring wire. So he says, anyway. | But dressing unlikeable and unfriendly nobility eventually {bored him. | wore on him.} | Once tasked with making a tunic embroidered with epic feats, %name% wondered what the outside world was really like. | Designing a dress adorned with {epic quests | epic feats}, %name% wondered if maybe he should be the one they wove stories about.} Now the tailor looks for a new life, no matter where it takes him. {Maybe he can dress the unit well, or something. | He's particular and peculiar, peppering everyone with clothing criticisms. | He's no natural soldier, but he appraises a man's attire as if he's about to go to war with it. | The way he measures and calculates for dressing, it's too bad %name% wasn't a siege engineer. | While hardly a soldier, %name%'s earnest love for tailoring is to be admired. | %name%'s knowledge of various cloths is seriously impressive. | A bit on the nimby-pimby side, %name% has the footwork of a swordfighter, but the swordfighting of a soft breeze. | %name% would seem very out of place in a suit of armor, but boy is he going to need one. | As it turns out, %name% can in fact make a silk purse out of a sow's ear. | Don't let his vocation fool you, %name% is more deft with his hands than some {cardsharks | jugglers | pickpockets}. | Tailors don't seem fit for combat, but then again neither do most of the men you run across these days. | A tailor seems ill-fit for combat, yet for some reason you find the finest soldiers in the strangest of places. | With an eye {for calculations | for measuring}, %name% is a lot smarter than he lets on at first glance.}
af6db35b68bc7286b87c.translation: {%name%总爱钻研布料，在一块亚麻布里看见的学问，甚至多过{占卜师从沙漠沙粒里看见的。 | 内脏卜者从蟾蜍肚肠里看见的。 | 炼金术士从研钵和杵里看见的。} | %name%从小就是个古怪孩子，对漂亮绸裙的兴趣，远胜于穿裙子的姑娘。 | 父亲是位{矿工 | 侍从 | 骑士 | 农场工}，%name%却转行裁衣，令所有人都很意外。 | %name%的姐妹梦想成为战士和英雄，%name%却想将来替国王裁衣。 | %name%的少年时光大多混在姑娘堆里，原因却并非旁人想的那样。 | %name%一向喜欢动物，尤其喜欢想象它们变成好外衣或围巾的样子。 | 长衣和衬衫渐渐流行，%name%便做起裁缝，想挣几个克朗。 | 灯笼裤大为流行之后，%name%为了多赚钱，从皮匠改当了裁缝。 | %name%来自遥远的地方，在那里，一个人的穿着比打仗的本事更重要。 | 裁缝讲究颜色与布料的学问，按这个标准，%name%颇有名气。 | %name%擅长测量和计算，便将这份算术本事用在裁衣上，尽可能多挣些钱。 | 为了躲过路过贵族的征兵，母亲催促%name%学做裁缝，他的行当便从此开始。 | %name%学裁缝是为了纪念父亲。父亲也是裁缝，却被一位不满意的顾客杀死。 | 战争夺去了丈夫，%name%的母亲便教他将双手用于裁衣，而非杀人。}{劫掠者袭击家园时，%name%替大家巧妙改装。城镇虽被毁，却没有一个人丧命。 | 他为王室裁衣多年，直到一次衣饰失礼使他遭到放逐。 | 遗憾的是，像%name%这样钟情漂亮布料的男人，在许多村庄都不受待见。 | 他想去大城市闯出名堂，却终究争不过其他裁缝。 | 一位领主组建军队时，%name%负责衣装，给士兵们缝制合适的制服。 | 裁缝之间的激烈竞争最终留下了一具裹在亚麻布里的尸体，而%name%也恰巧在这时丢下店铺走了。 | 遗憾的是，强盗洗劫了他的店铺，战乱之中再也无法补货。 | 给一只不属于自己的羊剪毛后，%name%被赶出了城镇。 | 他曾用量衣绳勒倒一名想行窃的贼，至少他是这么说的。 | 可替那些讨厌又不近人情的贵族裁衣，终于让他{感到厌烦。 | 心力交瘁。} | 受命缝制一件绣着英雄壮举的长衣时，%name%开始好奇外面的世界究竟如何。 | 设计一条饰有{传奇冒险 | 英雄壮举}的裙子时，%name%不禁想，也许自己才该成为织入故事的那个人。}如今，这位裁缝想找一种新的活法，无论它会把自己带向何处。{也许他能让整支队伍穿得体面些吧。 | 他挑剔又古怪，总对大家的穿着评头论足。 | 他虽不是天生的兵，审视衣着时那副架势，却像要和衣服打一仗。 | 看他量尺寸、做计算的本事，%name%没去当攻城工程师，实在可惜。 | %name%虽算不上士兵，对裁缝手艺的那份热爱却值得敬佩。 | %name%对各类布料的了解，着实令人印象深刻。 | %name%有些娇气，步法像个剑客，剑招却软得只抵得上一阵微风。 | %name%披上铠甲大概会显得很不相称，可他确实少不了一副。 | 事实证明，%name%真能拿母猪耳朵缝出丝绸钱袋。 | 别被他的行当骗了，%name%的双手比某些{牌桌老千 | 杂耍艺人 | 扒手}还灵巧。 | 裁缝看起来不适合打仗，不过如今遇到的大多数人也没好到哪去。 | 裁缝似乎不该上战场，可最好的士兵，偏偏常从最意想不到的地方冒出来。 | 凭着{精于计算 | 擅长测量}的本事，%name%比初看起来聪明得多。}

f177e0b0c8199fe71fcc.source: {%name% was always curious about fabrics, seeing more science in a linen cloth than {a diviner would in the sands of the desert. | a haruspex would in a toad's entrails. | an alchemist would in a mortar and pestle.} | %name% was always an odd boy growing up, fancying a good silk dress instead of the girl beneath it. | Son to a {butcher | soldier}, %name%'s turn toward fashioning clothes was a surprise to all. | While %name%'s brothers fancied being warriors and heroes, %name% thought of himself as a future dresser of viziers. | %name% spent much of his youth in the company of girls, but not for the reasons one might think. | %name% always fancied animals, particularly how they would look as a good coat or scarf. | As tunics and shirts grew popular, %name% turned to tailoring to make a crown or two. | With a surge in pantaloons popularity, %name% went from being a tanner to a tailor to make more money. | Tailoring is the science of colors and fabrics, by which standards %name% is renowned. | Good with measuring and calculating, %name% turned his mathematical prowess to tailoring to earn as much as he could. | %name% took up tailoring to honor his father, a tailor who was killed by an unhappy customer. | Widowed by war, %name%'s mother taught him how to put his hands to better use in tailoring instead of killing.} {When nomads attacked his home, %name% dressed everyone up in clever disguises. The town was destroyed, but not a soul was lost. | He spent many years dressing royalty until a fashion faux pas led his being exiled. | Unfortunately, a man fancying a good fabric, as %name% is wont to do, left the tailor ostracized from many a village. | He tried to make his break in the city, but sadly he just could not compete with the other tailors. | When a vizier organized an army, %name% handled the clothes, giving the conscripts proper uniforms. | But a fierce competition between tailors led to a linen-wrapped deadman and %name% coincidentally leaving his shop behind. | He once choked out a would-be thief with a cord of measuring wire. So he says, anyway. | Once tasked with making a tunic embroidered with epic feats, %name% wondered what the outside world was really like. | Designing a dress adorned with {epic quests | epic feats}, %name% wondered if maybe he should be the one they wove stories about.} Now the tailor looks for a new life, no matter where it takes him. {Maybe he can dress the unit well, or something. | He's particular and peculiar, peppering everyone with clothing criticisms. | He's no natural soldier, but he appraises a man's attire as if he's about to go to war with it. | The way he measures and calculates for dressing, it's too bad %name% wasn't a siege engineer. | While hardly a soldier, %name%'s earnest love for tailoring is to be admired. | %name%'s knowledge of various cloths is seriously impressive. | A bit on the nimby-pimby side, %name% has the footwork of a swordfighter, but the swordfighting of a soft breeze. | %name% would seem very out of place in a suit of armor, but boy is he going to need one. | As it turns out, %name% can in fact make a silk purse out of a sow's ear. | Don't let his vocation fool you, %name% is more deft with his hands than some {cardsharks | jugglers | pickpockets}. | Tailors don't seem fit for combat, but then again neither do most of the men you run across these days. | A tailor seems ill-fit for combat, yet for some reason you find the finest soldiers in the strangest of places. | With an eye {for calculations | for measuring}, %name% is a lot smarter than he lets on at first glance.}
f177e0b0c8199fe71fcc.translation: {%name%向来对布料充满好奇，在一块亚麻布上看出的门道，比{占卜者从沙漠黄沙里看出的还多。 | 脏卜师从蟾蜍内脏里看出的还多。 | 炼金术士从研钵和杵里看出的还多。} | %name%从小就是个古怪的孩子，比起姑娘，他更看中姑娘身上那条漂亮的丝裙。 | 身为{屠夫 | 士兵}之子，%name%却转去做衣裳，出乎所有人的意料。 | %name%的兄弟们梦想当战士、做英雄，%name%却觉得自己将来会是维齐尔的制衣师。 | %name%少年时常与姑娘们待在一起，不过原因可不是人们想的那样。 | %name%一直很喜欢动物，尤其喜欢想象它们做成大衣或围巾的样子。 | 长衫和衬衣日渐流行，%name%便做起裁缝，想挣上几个克朗。 | 灯笼裤忽然风靡，%name%便从制革匠改当裁缝，好多挣些钱。 | 裁缝是钻研颜色与布料的学问，以此衡量，%name%颇有名气。 | %name%擅长量尺寸、算数目，便把算术本领用在裁缝活上，想尽可能多挣些钱。 | %name%当裁缝，是为了纪念父亲。他的父亲也是裁缝，却被一名不满的顾客杀了。 | 战争让%name%的母亲失去了丈夫，她便教儿子把双手用来裁衣，而不是杀人。}{游牧民袭击家园时，%name%巧妙地为所有人装扮伪装。镇子虽毁了，却没死一个人。 | 他多年为王族制衣，直到一次穿戴上的失误，让他遭到流放。 | 可惜，一个男人像%name%这样钟情好布料，让许多村子都容不下这个裁缝。 | 他试着去城里闯出名堂，可惜根本争不过其他裁缝。 | 一位维齐尔组建军队时，%name%负责衣装，为征召兵缝制了像样的制服。 | 可裁缝之间的激烈竞争，最终留下了一具裹着亚麻布的尸体，而%name%也恰好在那时弃店离去。 | 他曾用量衣的细绳勒死一个企图行窃的家伙。至少他自己这么说。 | 一次受托缝制绣有英雄事迹的长衫时，%name%不禁好奇，外面的世界究竟是什么样。 | 设计一条绣着{传奇冒险 | 英雄壮举}的裙子时，%name%开始想，也许自己也该成为被人织进故事里的那个人。}如今，这名裁缝想开始新的生活，不论前路通向何方。{也许他能给战团做身像样的衣裳，之类的。 | 他讲究又古怪，见谁都要挑几句穿衣的毛病。 | 他不是天生的士兵，可打量起别人的穿戴来，却像要跟那身衣服开战。 | 看他量体裁衣时那番精打细算的本领，%name%没当攻城工程师，实在可惜。 | %name%几乎算不上士兵，不过那份对裁缝活的真心热爱，倒值得敬佩。 | %name%对各种布料的了解，确实令人印象深刻。 | %name%有点娇气，身法像剑士，挥剑却轻得像阵微风。 | %name%穿上铠甲想必格格不入，可他还真少不了一套。 | 事实证明，%name%真能拿母猪耳朵做出绸缎钱袋。 | 别被他的行当骗了，%name%的手比某些{老千 | 杂耍艺人 | 扒手}还灵巧。 | 裁缝似乎不适合打仗，可话说回来，如今你遇到的大多数人也一样。 | 裁缝看着不适合上阵，可不知为何，最出色的士兵总会在最意想不到的地方被找到。 | %name%善于{计算 | 度量}，比乍看之下精明得多。}

6995f9bcf4955a5922f5.source: A good thief will have quick reflexes and the ability to evade any captors.
6995f9bcf4955a5922f5.translation: 优秀的盗贼反应敏捷，也善于躲开追捕者。

ab5af1a3d253ce69dbea.source: %name% the thief retired from fighting and disappeared off the map. You haven't heard word of the man since, but there are rumors that a certain nobleman had one of his vaults completely drained in a perfectly executed heist.
ab5af1a3d253ce69dbea.translation: 盗贼%name%告别战斗后便消失无踪，你再没听过他的消息。不过传闻某位贵族的一座金库，在一次完美无缺的盗窃中被搬了个精光。

baf27bc63ee3832b53ba.source: %name% the thief read the lines being drawn in the sands and retired from the %companyname% while he still could. He took what money he had made and threw together a crew of thieves and brigands. Last you heard, he pulled off a perfect heist only for one of his partners to stab him in the back and take off with all the goods.
baf27bc63ee3832b53ba.translation: 盗贼%name%看清局势，趁还能走，从%companyname%退役了。他拿积蓄凑起一伙盗贼和匪徒。最后听说，他完成了一场天衣无缝的劫案，却被同伙背后捅刀，卷走了全部赃物。

1dba62015cbebe38e6a1.source: {Raised by thieves on a diet of honeymilk and stolen gold, %name% started life off on the wrong foot. | Raised by a drunken father and an ill mother, %name% was parented straight into a life of thievery. | Born as the sixth-child of an already impoverished family, the budding thief %name% first learned the craft by stealing the last bits of dinner. | Growing up in a family servant to a rich noble, the eventual-thief %name% spent many years staring at royal opulence - and stealing from it. | Taken in by a local orphanage, it wasn't long for %name% to start taking abuse from the lowly orphans. He fell back on thieving to survive. | Orphaned, %name% grew up as a street urchin, his days governed by cutting purses and picking pockets. | While never particularly in need of money, %name%'s jealousy over material things led him to thieving. | The profligacy of the rich amidst crowds of poor always rubbed %name% the wrong way. So he stole from them both and gave to himself. | %name%'s father taught him all there was to know about stealing including, unfortunately, how to backstab. | The church steals with a silver plate. The lords do it with the taxman. So %name% figured why can't he do it with his own two hands? | Impoverished while growing up, %name% took to stealing bread. Well-fed, he soon took to stealing crowns.} {After years of successful stealing, one mistake landed %name% in a dungeon. Thankfully, years of stealing also meant years of lockpicking and he didn't spend long. | But when he was caught trying to steal a temple's chalice, a talk with a priest convinced %name% to perhaps take a different path. | Unfortunately, a smash-and-grab at a local store ended with %name% being caught red-handed. He was soon profiled on posters everywhere, making his work difficult. | Daring to cut the purse of a fat trader, %name% soon found himself nursing a hand absent of a few fingers. He really liked those fingers, too. | %name%'s thievery eventually placed him at the head of an entire guild. But after a dozen failed assassination attempts, the thief realized there was nobody to trust in his line of work. | Partnering up with a beautiful woman, %name% managed to steal from everybody. Too bad the woman stole from him, in the end. | Trying to sell some goods, a trusted fence turned out to be a traitorous informant. One bad pillory experience later and the thief was exiled from %randomtown%. | It was the perfect heist. That's all that is said about it. Now, %name% just needs to lay low. | Tortured by a rival gang, he came to miss a number of teeth, fingernails, and any drive to return to thieving. | His time as a thief came to an end when, arrested, he spent five days pilloried during tomato season. | Naturally, it wasn't long until he went to prison. He doesn't speak of his time there, but it is obvious he wishes to never return. | But one day he learned there are much better ways to spin a blade for a coin than petty thievery. | But his half-brother was captured by a local gang, forcing the thief to find new ways to pay the hefty ransom. | But life as a brigand is not easy. Arrested for eating a chicken that was not his, the man forfeited two fingers and any will to keep thieving. | After a heist went south, the man fingered all his former partners to save his own hide. Now he can never go back to thieving.} {For all you know %name% is just using sellswords to hide behind. Regardless of his reasons, he's still going to have to earn his pay. | You recognize %name% from some posters.  Well, a man who has gotten this far without being caught must have some value. | With one hand, %name% twirls a blade between his fingers. With the other, he snags your purse. Impressive. Now give it back. | Years of thieving have made %name% adept at escaping trouble. | %name% has the skills to be a good mercenary, just be sure to watch your purse while around him. | You can't trust a man like %name%, but that attribute has plenty of company anyway. | Supposedly, somebody once shot an arrow at %name%. They missed, but the thief kept the feathers. | %name%'s effort to join sellswords better not be a scheme to steal from your coffers. | Wanted posters say %name% is considered 'armed and dangerous'. Perfect. | There are plenty of lawmen looking for %name%. Maybe you can get them to join, too.}
1dba62015cbebe38e6a1.translation: {%name%从小由盗贼抚养，喝着蜜乳，花着偷来的金子，人生一开始便走歪了。 | %name%有个酗酒的父亲和患病的母亲，这样的家境把他直接推上了偷窃之路。 | 家里本已穷困，%name%又是第六个孩子。这个小贼最早学会的本事，就是偷走晚饭最后的几口残羹。 | %name%一家在富有贵族家中当仆役。他多年看着贵族挥霍无度，也多年从中顺手牵羊，终于成了惯偷。 | %name%被当地孤儿院收留后，没多久就受到了其他孤儿的欺凌。他只好靠偷窃求生。 | %name%自幼失去双亲，在街头长大，日子离不开割钱袋、掏口袋。 | %name%其实从不怎么缺钱，可对别人财物的嫉妒，还是把他引上了偷窃之路。 | 穷人遍地，富人却挥霍无度，这让%name%怎么看都不顺眼。于是他两边都偷，钱全归自己。 | %name%的父亲教会他偷窃的全部本领，其中很不幸地也包括了如何背后捅刀。 | 教会拿着银盘子偷，领主靠着税吏偷。%name%心想，自己凭两只手偷，怎么就不行？ | %name%小时候穷得叮当响，便开始偷面包。等到吃饱了，很快又开始偷克朗。} {多年行窃无往不利，一次失手却让%name%进了地牢。所幸，多年偷窃也练就了开锁的本领，他没待多久便跑了。 | %name%偷神殿的圣杯时被抓了个正着，与一位祭司的一番谈话，让他觉得也许该换条路走。 | 可惜，%name%砸抢本地商店时被当场逮住。很快，四处都贴满了他的画像，生意便难做了。 | %name%胆敢去割一个胖商人的钱袋，结果没多久，就只能捂着少了几根手指的伤手。偏偏那几根手指，他还挺喜欢。 | %name%靠偷窃一路做到了整个公会的头目。可十几次未遂刺杀过后，他终于明白，干这行谁也靠不住。 | %name%与一个美貌女子搭伙，把能偷的人全偷了个遍。可惜最后，那女人又把他也偷了个精光。 | 他找一个信得过的销赃人出货，没想到对方竟是告密者。吃够了枷号的苦头后，他被逐出了%randomtown%。 | 那是一次完美的盗窃。除此之外，再没人透露半句。眼下，%name%只想避避风头。 | 他遭到敌对帮派拷打，丢了好几颗牙、好几片指甲，也丢尽了重操旧业的念头。 | 他被捕后，赶上番茄成熟的季节，在枷台上足足示众五天。他的盗贼生涯也就此结束。 | 不出所料，他没多久便进了监狱。他不肯说里面发生过什么，但显然再也不愿回去。 | 可有一天，他发现，用刀挣钱还有比小偷小摸好得多的路子。 | 可他同父或同母的兄弟被当地帮派抓走了。为了凑齐高昂的赎金，他得另找财路。 | 可盗贼的日子并不好过。他吃了不属于自己的鸡，被抓之后，丢了两根手指，也彻底丢了继续偷窃的兴致。 | 一次行动失败后，他为保全自己，供出了所有旧日同伙。从此，这一行再也容不下他。} {说不定%name%只是拿佣兵身份作掩护。无论动机如何，该干的活他还是得干，工钱可不能白拿。 | 你在几张告示上见过%name%。不过，一个逃到今天还没被逮住的人，总有些本事。 | %name%一只手在指间转着匕首，另一只手便顺走了你的钱袋。了不起。现在还回来。 | 多年的偷窃生涯，让%name%很擅长脱身避祸。 | %name%的身手足以成为优秀的佣兵，只是和他待在一起时，最好看紧钱袋。 | %name%这样的人信不过，不过这点他倒也不孤单。 | 据说，有人曾朝%name%射过一箭。人没射中，箭羽却被他顺走了。 | 最好别让%name%加入佣兵的打算，变成从你钱箱里下手的诡计。 | 通缉令说，%name%“携有武器，极度危险”。正合适。 | 有不少执法者在找%name%。也许你还能把他们一并招来。}

They missed, but the thief kept the feathers. | %name%'s effort to join sellswords better not be a scheme to steal from your coffers. | Wanted posters say %name% is considered 'armed and dangerous'. Perfect. | There are plenty of lawmen looking for %name%. Maybe you can get them to join, too.}
8aa1e5d9ba7214e172d0.translation: {%name%被一群贼养大，喝着蜜奶、花着赃钱，从一开始便走错了路。 | %name%由酗酒的父亲和患病的母亲养大，就这样被一路推上了偷窃的生涯。 | 家里原本就穷，%name%又是第六个孩子。这个小贼最初练手，偷的是晚饭剩下的那点吃食。 | %name%一家替富商做仆役。他多年望着眼前的奢华糜烂，也从中顺手牵羊，最终成了贼。 | %name%被当地孤儿院收留后，很快便遭到同样落魄的孤儿们欺负，只得靠偷窃活下去。 | 沦为孤儿后，%name%成了街头顽童，整日割钱袋、摸口袋。 | %name%从不怎么缺钱，却因眼红别人的东西而走上偷窃之路。 | 富人在成群穷人中挥霍无度，总让%name%看不顺眼。于是他富人穷人都偷，再把赃物全留给自己。 | %name%的父亲把偷窃的本领尽数传给了他，其中不幸也包括从背后捅刀子。 | 教会用银盘敛财，领主靠税吏搜刮。%name%便想，自己凭什么不能靠这双手？ | %name%自幼贫困，起初偷面包，肚子填饱了，便开始偷克朗。}{多年行窃得手后，一次失误让%name%进了地牢。所幸，偷窃多年也意味着开锁多年，他没待多久就出来了。 | 可当他偷神殿圣杯时被抓住，一名修士与他谈过话后，%name%觉得也许该另走一条路。 | 可惜，一次砸店抢货让%name%被逮个正着。很快，四处的通缉告示上都有了他的脸，生意便难做了。 | 胆敢割一名胖商人的钱袋，%name%很快便只能捧着少了几根手指的手养伤。偏偏那几根手指，他还挺喜欢的。 | 凭着偷盗的本事，%name%最终当上了整个行会的头领。可在躲过十几次刺杀后，他明白，这一行根本没人可信。 | %name%与一位美女搭伙，几乎偷遍了所有人。可惜到头来，那女人又偷走了他的一切。 | 销赃时，一个深受信任的掮客竟翻脸告密。他在枷锁中受尽折磨，随后便被逐出了%randomtown%。 | 那是一次完美的盗窃。除此之外，他什么也不说。如今，%name%只需避避风头。 | 敌对帮派对他施以酷刑，夺走了他的几颗牙、几片指甲，也夺走了他再去偷窃的所有念头。 | 偷窃生涯在他被捕时画上句号：正赶上番茄成熟，他被套着枷在街上示众了五天。 | 自然而然，没过多久，他就进了牢。他不谈里面的经历，但显然绝不想再回去。 | 可有一天，他发现凭刀挣钱的好路子多得很，远胜于小偷小摸。 | 可他同父异母的兄弟被当地帮派抓走，他不得不另找办法，凑那笔沉重的赎金。 | 可盗匪的生活并不容易。只因吃了一只不属于自己的鸡，他便被捕，失去两根手指，也失去了继续行窃的全部兴致。 | 一次行动失败后，他为保住自己，把昔日同伙全供了出来。如今，他再也回不去做贼了。}{据你所知，%name%也许只是拿佣兵当藏身之处。不论动机如何，工钱总得靠他自己挣。 | 你认出了通缉告示上的%name%。嗯，能躲过追捕走到这一步，想必总有些用处。 | %name%一只手让刀刃在指间翻飞，另一只手却摸走了你的钱袋。厉害。现在还来。 | 多年的偷窃让%name%很擅长摆脱麻烦。 | %name%有当个好佣兵的本事，只是在他身边，务必看好自己的钱袋。 | %name%这样的人信不过，不过这点毛病，在队伍里倒也不缺同类。 | 据说，曾有人朝%name%射了一箭。没射中，箭羽却被这贼留了下来。 | %name%想当佣兵，最好别是为了偷你的钱库而设的局。 | 通缉告示说，%name%“持械且危险”。正合适。 | 很多差役都在找%name%。也许能把他们一并招进来。}

763d8f4ddd18dae48407.source: Vagabonds are used to long travels, but don't excel in anything in particular.
763d8f4ddd18dae48407.translation: 流浪汉习惯长途跋涉，却没有特别出众的本事。

af8407b8552a933a20ab.source: Some men were just intended to wander. While his time with the %companyname% went well, %name% the vagabond eventually departed with the company and set off on the roads once more. You've no idea where he's gone, you just know all he's interested in is going.
af8407b8552a933a20ab.translation: 有些人生来就注定漂泊。尽管在%companyname%的日子过得不错，流浪汉%name%最终还是离开战团，再次踏上旅途。你不知道他去了哪，只知道他一心想不断前行。

e83586c629c3da3e9cca.source: As the company fell apart, it's little surprise that a vagabond like %name% chose to leave it behind and return to the roads. Unfortunately, with the world in such a dire state, it did not take long for him to find trouble. His body was found hanging outside a small farming village. A sign nailed to his chest read: 'No Free Rangers'.
e83586c629c3da3e9cca.translation: 战团瓦解时，%name%这样的流浪汉选择离去、重回旅途，并不奇怪。不幸的是，世道如此险恶，他很快便惹上麻烦。人们在一个小农村外发现他被吊着的尸体，胸前钉着木牌：“闲游者免入。”

7b153c82d0c5b9fdf4a9.source: {Pushed out of his town by war, %name% wanders the world as a vagabond. | Lazy and unmotivated, %name% one day put all three of his belongings into a knapsack and hit the road. | Never a strong learner in school, %name% dropped out to wander the earth. | %name% did not have the business acumen to protect his inheritance from debtors, lawmen, and other maleficent men. Now he wanders with the last of his crowns jangling in a pocket. | Life on the road has taught %name% to be a jack of all trades, and a master of none - except walking, of course. | Not quite one for the city, and not quite one for the wild, %name% spends his purposeless days traveling between both. | During his drinking days, %name% managed to gamble away a small fortune. Now homeless, he simply wanders. | When his wife was murdered while he was away, %name% refused to sleep in the house. The man walks the earth, trying to forget the memory. | His son murdered five others. In shame, %name% abandoned his hometown to walk the earth and forget his failures as a father.} {But when a gang of thieves took all he had - including his shoes - he knew he needed yet another change. | But when he came to a literal fork in the road, the man realized he hadn't eaten in some time. His stomach demanded a change in scenery - and diet. | Sadly, the world is not a pleasant place for those who nobody would miss. He was harassed and bullied every day. | After one particularly harsh day trudging through mud, he realized there was no life to be had in walking around. | Strangely, one day he came across his long-forgotten brother he-never-had who said there was plenty of walking to be done for a mercenary outfit - and they'd pay him to do it, too! | Like any good, impulsive man, he flipped a coin on whether or not to try his hand at mercenary work.} {He's not particularly good at anything, but %name% has seen and done a lot, and that's worth at least something. | Mucking about this violent land and surviving with all his limbs is a lot more than some folks can say. | A mercenary band would be but another adventure for a vagabond like %name%. One hopes he survives to write about it. | Through his travels his only weapon was a walking stick. Let's see how he does with something a smidge sharper. | A thief, a scoundrel, a baker, a tailor, %name%'s done it all. Too bad he was never good at any of those things. Maybe it'll be different this time. | The world has been harsh to %name% for many years now. That isn't going to change, but at least he will be with brothers now.}
7b153c82d0c5b9fdf4a9.translation: {战争将%name%赶出家乡，他就此成了四处漂泊的流浪汉。 | %name%懒散又没志气，有一天把全部三件家当往背包里一塞，便上路了。 | %name%上学时就不怎么开窍，后来索性退学，四处游荡。 | %name%不懂经营，没能保住自己的遗产，任由欠债者、差役和其他恶人将它吞光。如今他四处流浪，口袋里只剩最后几枚克朗叮当作响。 | 流浪的生活让%name%什么都会一点，却什么都不精——当然，走路除外。 | 城里容不下他，野外也不完全适合他，%name%便在两者之间来回游荡，漫无目的地度日。 | 酗酒的那些年，%name%把一笔不小的家财赌了个精光。如今无家可归，只剩四处流浪。 | 外出期间，妻子遭人杀害，%name%此后再也不肯在那间屋里睡觉。他走遍天下，想忘掉那段记忆。 | 他的儿子杀了五个人。羞愧之下，%name%离开故乡，浪迹天涯，想忘掉自己做父亲的失败。}{可一伙贼抢光了他的全部东西，连鞋都没留下，他便知道，自己还得再换种活法。 | 可有一天，他在路上真捡到一把叉子，才想起自己已经很久没吃东西。肚子要求他换个地方，也换换饭食。 | 可惜，对那些死了也无人惦念的人，世界从不友善。他每天都受人骚扰、欺凌。 | 在泥泞中跋涉了格外艰难的一天后，他明白，光靠四处走路，实在过不出什么日子。 | 奇怪的是，一天他遇见了一个早被自己忘光、实际上压根没有的兄弟。对方说，佣兵战团有的是路让他走，而且还给钱！ | 和任何一个说干就干的汉子一样，他抛了枚硬币，决定要不要去当佣兵。}{%name%没什么拿手本事，可见得多、做得也多，这总归值点什么。 | 在这片暴力横行的土地上混来混去，还能四肢齐全地活着，已经比不少人强了。 | 对%name%这样的流浪汉而言，佣兵战团不过是另一场冒险。但愿他能活着将它写下来。 | 一路走来，他唯一的武器就是手杖。给他换个稍微锋利些的，看看会怎样。 | 贼、无赖、面包师、裁缝，%name%什么都干过。可惜，哪一样都没干好。也许这回会不同。 | 这世界多年来一直苛待%name%，以后也不会改变，不过至少，如今他身边有了弟兄。}

6c35ea9012744b9eb8cc.source: Wildmen are used to the hard life of the wild where only the strong prevail. They are less used to the life of cities, where the astute and deceitful rule.
6c35ea9012744b9eb8cc.translation: 野人习惯荒野的艰苦生活，那里只有强者能够生存。他们却不适应城市，那里是精明者和骗子的天下。

9ded21b7075e56957bca.source: While the %companyname% visited a town for rest and recuperation, a local princess took a shine to %name% the wildman. He was 'purchased' for a large sum of gold and given to the noblewoman. You went and visited the man recently. For dinner, he sat at a kingly table, grinning goofily and mimicking the nobles around him as best he could. His new and inexplicable wife adored him, and him her. When you said your goodbyes, he offered you a heavy golden crown off the top of his head. It weighed heavy with traditions and ancient histories. You said it'd be best if he kept it. The wildman shrugged and walked off, spinning the circlet around a finger.
9ded21b7075e56957bca.translation: %companyname%到一座城镇休整时，当地一位贵族千金看上了荒野人%name%。有人花大价钱把他“买”下，送给了那位贵族小姐。最近，你去看过他。晚餐时，他坐在一张国王般气派的餐桌旁，咧嘴傻笑，尽力模仿周围贵族的举止。他那位来得莫名其妙的新婚妻子爱极了他，他也爱极了她。告别时，他从头顶摘下一顶沉甸甸的金冠，想送给你。那顶王冠承载着厚重的传统与久远的历史，你说还是他留着好。荒野人耸耸肩，转身走开，将那顶金冠套在手指上转个不停。

fac37ba81a2434ae64ab.source: %name% the wildman stayed with the fragmenting %companyname% for a time and then, just like that, he was gone. The company went out looking for him in a forest, eventually finding some sort of crude note: an enormous pile of crowns next to a dirt-drawing of the %companyname% and some of its members, all of them being hugged by a big, literal stick figure with a goofy smile on its face. There was also an offering of a dead, half-eaten rabbit.
fac37ba81a2434ae64ab.translation: 荒野人%name%在日渐分裂的%companyname%又待了一阵，随后就那么突然消失了。战团进林子找他，最后找到了一封粗陋的“信”：一大堆克朗旁边，泥地上画着%companyname%和几个成员，一个硕大的火柴人把他们全抱在怀里，脸上挂着傻乎乎的笑。旁边还留着一份赠礼——一只死了、被啃掉一半的兔子。

70ecc79873bf78f6dbe1.source: {For some, the wild is a refuge. | It is said that man is born with the wilderness in him, and that he does wrong by turning his back on it. | Civilization is a stain, one prolonged arming of every next-generation to better battle the ultimate enemy: Mother Nature herself. | In a time of war, it's not surprising that many once again seek refuge in the wild. | Some people flee from town to town. Others stop in between, disappearing into the tranquil forests.} {%name% once found a safe register amongst the trees, but that time is over. | Once a mysterious figure to hunters - the famed masskewatsthat - %name% now returns to civilization for reasons unknown. | %name%'s got the hands of a blacksmith, but the hygiene of a pigsty. | Maybe it was spurned love, or maybe just war, but %name% has spent the last decade far from the rest of mankind. | Possibly a poacher who settled where he hunted, %name%'s lived amongst the trees for untold years. | With cleverly stitched garb, %name%'s atavistic appearance perhaps belies a past as a tailor or tanner.} {There is an obvious language barrier with the wildman, but for some reason he seems very willing to fight. Let's hope his newfound 'calling' doesn't have a darker purpose behind it. | Colorful and permanent ritual rites circle about his body. When asked why he wishes to join a band of mercenaries, he hoots and, with a crooked finger, replicates one of his fleshen arts across the sky. | Wounds, old and fresh, dot his already mottled body. And they are not superficial - this man had been fighting something fierce in the wild. | One has to wonder if the calamities which chased him into the forests have come to chase him back out. | Judging by his wild grunting, it's doubtful he's here to rejoin civilization. | Years as a recluse haven't made the man forget what a few crowns can get you. The question is, why did he come back? | He has the strength to wrestle a boar - and his many scars makes you wonder if perhaps he did.}
70ecc79873bf78f6dbe1.translation: {对有些人来说，荒野就是避难所。 | 据说，人天生便带着一分野性，背弃它，便是走上歧途。 | 文明是一块污迹，不断武装一代又一代的人，让他们更善于对抗终极的敌人：大自然母亲本身。 | 战争年代，许多人重新躲进荒野，并不令人意外。 | 有些人从一座城逃往另一座城，还有些人停在途中，消失于静谧的森林。}{%name%曾在林间找到安全的栖身之处，可那样的日子已经结束。 | %name%曾是猎人眼中的神秘身影，也就是传说中的“马斯奎沃茨萨特”。如今，他不知为何又回到了文明世界。 | %name%有一双铁匠般的手，身上的干净程度却和猪圈差不多。 | 也许是失恋，也许只是战争，%name%过去十年一直远离人群。 | 或许原本是个干脆在猎场安家的偷猎者，%name%已在林间生活了不知多少年。 | %name%衣着原始，针脚却颇为巧妙，或许这副野人模样，掩盖了一段裁缝或制革匠的过去。}{与这个荒野人交流显然很困难，可不知为何，他似乎很愿意打仗。但愿这份新找回的“使命”背后，没有更阴暗的目的。 | 他身上环绕着五颜六色、永不褪去的仪式印记。问他为何想加入佣兵队伍，他便嗷嗷叫着，弯起一根手指，在空中描摹自己身上的某个图案。 | 他本已斑驳的身躯上遍布新伤旧疤，而且绝不是些皮外伤：这人在荒野里，显然曾与凶狠的东西搏斗。 | 不禁让人怀疑，是否当初将他逼入森林的灾祸，又追进林子，把他逼了出来。 | 听他那粗野的哼声，很难相信他是来重新融入文明的。 | 多年离群索居，也没让他忘记几个克朗能换来什么。问题是，他为何回来？ | 他力气大得足以与野猪角力，而满身的伤疤也让你怀疑，没准他真干过。}

d9210fe84ac7263147c9.source: Witchhunters tend to have some martial experience, and their resolve often remains unbroken even in the face of unspeakable horror.
d9210fe84ac7263147c9.translation: 猎巫人通常有些战斗经验，即使面对难以言喻的恐怖，意志也往往不会动摇。

de00ed85a36e5a9a668e.source: %name% the witchhunter eventually heard word of evil spreading in northern villages. He departed the %companyname% and has been burning those horrid witches at the stake ever since.
de00ed85a36e5a9a668e.translation: 猎巫人%name%终于听说邪恶正在北方村庄蔓延。他离开%companyname%，此后便一直将那些可怕女巫送上火刑柱。

737063bbb6a9eb565a3c.source: Word of evil spreading in the north drew %name% the witchhunter from the company. He departed with stakes, vials of strange liquids, and a lot of kindling. A month later a peasant found him wandering the northern wastes with his eyes gouged out and his mouth sewn shut. He had a strange symbol ironed into his chest and when the peasant touched it both men exploded.
737063bbb6a9eb565a3c.translation: 邪恶正在北方蔓延的传闻，让猎巫人%name%离开了战团。他带着木桩、装满古怪液体的小瓶，还有大量引火物，踏上旅途。一个月后，一名农夫发现他在北方荒原游荡：双眼被挖去，嘴也被缝住，胸口还烙着一个奇异的符号。农夫伸手一碰，两人便同时炸开了。

9af2f7fefc95f60ca40a.source: {%name% appeared one day in %townname%, some say upon request {of the local council | of a local priest}. | %name% has a reputation of showing up where things out of the ordinary happen and being out and about at the darkest part of the night. | Being a quiet and grim man, %name% has the tendency to make other people feel uncomfortable around him, even afraid. | The name of %name% is known in many a village, for he has travelled the land to wherever his talents are needed the most.} {A Witchhunter he calls himself. With his assortment of exotic tools he has a great deal of experience in getting people to confess in agony their sinful liaisons with demons and devils under terrible torture. | He refers to himself as a Witchhunter, but only superstitious fools would believe this and fall for his preposterous tales. | A Witchhunter he calls himself, and he claims to have seen horrors from beyond that would drive a lesser man insane. | After his arrival in %townname%, rumors spread that he was on the hunt for devil worshippers and creatures of the night, but no one knew what the real purpose of his visit was. | In %townname% he killed an elderly woman and was thrown into the dungeon. As it turned out, the woman was responsible for the abduction and death of 3 infants, and so he was set free again. | For nights on end he sat in %townname%'s pub, silently studying every patron like a bird of prey circling above, his crossbow never far away. It didn't sit well with the residents  but they didn't dare approach him.} {By now most of the local folks want %name% to be gone rather sooner than later and would happily see him join a travelling mercenary company. | It seems that whatever his mission was is now accomplished and so %name% offers his service as a mercenary. | It is somewhat obvious that %name% is not easily scared and he also knows how to handle a crossbow. Nobody was therefore surprised as he approached a mercenary company that was hiring. | Now, a mercenary company would be just the tool he needed to fulfill his personal quest against the evil from the world beyond. | Most people would be glad to get rid of him.}
9af2f7fefc95f60ca40a.translation: {一天，%name%出现在%townname%，有人说他是应{当地议事会 | 当地一名祭司}的请求而来。 | %name%向来以出没于怪事发生之处闻名，还常在夜色最深时四处活动。 | %name%寡言而阴沉，总让身边的人感到不安，甚至害怕。 | 许多村子都听过%name%的名字，因为他走遍各地，哪里最需要他的本领，他就去哪里。}{他自称猎巫人，带着一整套奇异的工具，极有经验，知道如何用酷刑折磨人，逼他们在惨痛中承认自己与恶魔、魔鬼有染。 | 他自称猎巫人，可只有迷信的傻瓜才会相信，才会被他那套荒唐的故事哄住。 | 他自称猎巫人，说自己见过彼岸的恐怖之物，足以让心志稍弱的人发疯。 | 他来到%townname%后，传言四起，说他正在追捕恶魔崇拜者和夜行的怪物，却没人知道他此行的真正目的。 | 他在%townname%杀了一名老妇，被关进地牢。后来查明，那女人曾绑架并害死3名婴儿，他才获释。 | 接连许多夜晚，他坐在%townname%的酒馆里，默默审视每一位客人，如盘旋高空的猛禽，弩始终放在伸手可及之处。居民们心里不安，却又不敢上前。}{如今，当地大多数人都巴不得%name%早些离开，很乐意看他加入一支过路的佣兵战团。 | 无论任务是什么，似乎都已完成，于是%name%提出以佣兵的身份效力。 | 很明显，%name%不容易受惊，也懂得使弩。因此，他找上一支正在招人的佣兵战团时，没人感到意外。 | 如今，一支佣兵战团恰好能成为他所需的工具，助他完成对抗彼岸邪恶的个人使命。 | 大多数人都很乐意甩掉他。}

984a0c4746cf4fbae6f8.source: This character's armor has been sprayed with a Lindwurm's acidic blood, which is now slowly eating away at it for another [color=
984a0c4746cf4fbae6f8.translation: 此角色的护甲溅上了林德蠕龙的酸血，正被缓缓腐蚀。效果还将持续[color=

8a87d537d5d4229ba38e.source: ]20%[/color] of head armor is lost each turn
8a87d537d5d4229ba38e.translation: ]20%[/color]头部护甲损失，每回合生效一次

f975009342f6843163a5.source: ]20%[/color] of body armor is lost each turn
f975009342f6843163a5.translation: ]20%[/color]身体护甲损失，每回合生效一次

1fec11ff03d7c76e6a38.source: 's body has been sprayed with acid

dd9e095e83f8c0b1a728.source: Go, go, go! This character has an adrenaline rush and will act again before his opponents come next round.
dd9e095e83f8c0b1a728.translation: 快！快！快！此角色的肾上腺素激增，下轮将抢在敌人之前行动。

bb0a5504faedbfe07b1a.source: This character's eyes have mutated to respond faster and more drastically to low light environments. As a result, they have night vision nearly on par with their sight during the day.
bb0a5504faedbfe07b1a.translation: 此角色的双眼发生了变异，在昏暗环境中反应更快、对光线更敏感。如今，他的夜间视力已与白昼时相差无几。

05bff1b4e12901b61133.source: Further mutations will cause a longer period of sickness
05bff1b4e12901b61133.translation: 进一步变异会延长患病时间

90d389660a2121090ec2.source: This character's body has mutated in such a way that their fight-or-flight response is altered. In high stress situations, their limbic system is simply refused resources for flight, making them effectively unbreakable in the battle line.
90d389660a2121090ec2.translation: 此角色的身体发生了变异，改变了本能的战逃反应。在极度紧张的情况下，他的神经系统无法为逃跑提供支持，因此即使身处战线，也几乎绝不会溃逃。

c99bb04846185819002c.source: Can not be reduced to Fleeing morale, only Breaking
c99bb04846185819002c.translation: 士气最低只会降至“崩溃”，不会进入“溃逃”状态

9acbdff35008cbc5dbaf.source: This character has taken antidote and is immune to any kind of poison for another [color=
9acbdff35008cbc5dbaf.translation: 此角色已服下解毒剂，能够免疫所有毒素。效果还将持续[color=

f792ad8016ddba64589b.source: This character has consumed a particularly powerful stimulant. While the delivery mechanism itself is revolutionary, the drug itself is not as powerful as the grandeur of its name suggests.
f792ad8016ddba64589b.translation: 此角色服下了一剂强效兴奋药。给药方式虽堪称革新，药效却没有那夸张的名字听起来那么神奇。

c883223f5e5b909be2af.source: With the company's glorious battle standard nearby, this character feels compelled to push onward and spit danger in the face.
c883223f5e5b909be2af.translation: 战团光荣的旗帜就在身旁，令此角色鼓起勇气，迎着险境继续前进。

c66a93c691c6167b5dd1.source: KILL!!! This character is in a mushroom-induced trance-like rage and only wants to crush and destroy anyone in his path, with little regard for their own safety. CRUSH!!! DESTROY!!!
c66a93c691c6167b5dd1.translation: 杀！！！此角色在蘑菇的作用下陷入了恍如梦境的狂怒，只想碾碎、毁灭挡在面前的一切，丝毫不顾自身安危。碾碎他们！！！毁灭一切！！！

775de2c98db598c57b02.source: Will be gone after 1 more battles

3d959e90e110b8f0011b.source: This character is bleeding profusely from a recently received wound and will lose [color=
3d959e90e110b8f0011b.translation: 此角色新近的伤口正在大量流血，每回合将损失[color=

7137cd2e488d81fbdd83.source: had his bleeding wound quickly close thanks to his unnatural physiology
7137cd2e488d81fbdd83.translation: 凭借异于常人的体质迅速止住了流血

4cb8977dc8b52cce94e9.source: With a captain nearby that provides guidance and pushes forward, this character has temporarily increased Resolve.
4cb8977dc8b52cce94e9.translation: 附近有队长指挥并带头向前，令此角色暂时提升了决心。

8b55fc3da3a82b8d7c59.source: Thanks to a cocktail of psychoactive substances, this character's senses are heightened and their reflexes sharpened, along with a tendency to show paranoid behavior.
8b55fc3da3a82b8d7c59.translation: 多种影响精神的药物增强了此角色的感官，使其反应更加敏捷，也让他变得多疑。

655833fbb05abb63857b.source: Will be gone after 1 more battle

1d3fa9ea77765a069e69.source: This character has been charmed. He no longer has any control over his actions and is a puppet that has no choice but to obey his master. Wears off in [color=
1d3fa9ea77765a069e69.translation: 此角色受到了魅惑，已无法控制自己的行为，只能像傀儡一样听从施术者的命令。效果将在[color=

51ddf3c9bd0009ef5a1e.source:
[/color] turn(s).

The higher a character's resolve, the higher the chance to resist being charmed.
